  the target quotes the canon paragraph, with a shift control that separates
  alignment from vocabulary (48.7% -> 16.0% at one paragraph's displacement).
  That is the direction. A number-carry rebuild is not.
* **THREE DEFECTS IN `build_links_bynum.py` ARE FIXED AND WORTH KEEPING**, whatever

  volume's first paragraph is unnumbered — `08DiT01` ord0 is unnumbered and its

  `site/reader/linksk_new/`, inside the published tree**, so a dry run added dead
  files to the live site and moved BUILD for every visitor. Output is now
  `_xc/linksk_rebuild/`.
* **THE TWO PRUNES COST ALMOST NO COVERAGE — MEASURED, not assumed.** Removing
  33,834 wrong targets moved reachability **71.6% -> 71.1%**, i.e. 173
  paragraphs. The wrong links were nearly all redundant: they pointed into
  paragraphs correct links already reach. **So the 71% ceiling was never caused
  by the wrong links**, and no prune will lift it.

## START HERE — earlier (2026-08-01b)

* **THE TOP BAR IS FIXED, AND THE BREAKPOINTS CAME FROM A MEASUREMENT, NOT A
  GUESS (2026-08-01b).** Committed and pushed, `f0aa8a8`; user-confirmed on the
  iPhone. Sweeping the viewport from 900px down in 10px steps in Chromium gave
  **two faults with different thresholds**, which is why one blanket rule at the
  sidebar's 860px would have been wrong:
  | width | symptom |
  |---|---|
  | ≤790px | the brand wraps and is clipped by the 52px header — **this is the iPad one** |
  | ≤540px | `◐` leaves the viewport |
  | ≤500px | `ES` leaves too |
  | ≤440px / ≤380px / ≤320px | Errata / About / Downloads follow |
  So: **`max-width:800px` truncates the brand** and nothing else, and
  **`max-width:560px` moves Home/Downloads/About/Errata into the foot of the ☰
  panel** while `ES` and `◐` keep their place in the bar. **iPad portrait at
  768px therefore keeps its links and merely stops clipping** — a single 860px
  rule would have taken away links that fit. Verified at 11 viewports including
  both sides of each breakpoint (560/561, 800/801): **0 overflow, 0 clipping,
  header 52px throughout, 0 page errors**; links follow the language
  (`Inicio / Descargas / Acerca / Erratas`); `verify_sidebar` and `_navdup` pass.
  **`addSideLinks()` must be called INSIDE `buildSidebar`** — the builder opens
  with `side.innerHTML=''`, so anything appended earlier is discarded.
* **!!! "TEACH `stamp_build.py` TO HASH THE READER HTML" IS A FIX FOR THE WRONG
  THING. DO NOT DO IT (2026-08-01b).** The 07-31c entry below says an HTML-only
  change "moves no BUILD and nothing forces a refetch". The first clause is
  true, the second does not follow. **BUILD only ever appears inside a query
  string this page builds** — `jget()` appends `?v=BUILD`, and `i18n.js` carries
  it — while **the HTML is fetched at its bare URL**: `index.html` and
  `reader.html` both link to `/reader/reader2.html` with no buster, and the `?q=`
  on a search result is a search term, not a version. **Moving BUILD cannot make
  any browser re-fetch the HTML.** It would only hand every returning visitor
  1,691 fresh JSON URLs for unchanged data — the cost that made the idempotency
  fix of 07-31b worth making. HTML freshness is set by GitHub Pages'
  `Cache-Control` and the CDN, neither of which this repo controls. What works is
  already in place: `verify_live.py` byte-compares the published HTML, and an
  HTML-only change is tested with a fresh query string. If it ever needs solving
  for real visitors, the fix belongs in the page — fetch a version marker and
  offer a reload. Reasoning recorded in `stamp_build.py`'s own docstring so the
  next session does not "fix" it.
* **`_xc/` IS PARTLY TRACKED — NEVER `git rm -r --cached _xc/`.** 58 files there
  were tracked before 08-01, including the gate scripts `verify_resolver.js`,
  `verify_sidebar.js`, `verify_bands.js`, `residue.py`, `para_alignment*.py` and

* **THE WRONG-COMMENTARY REPAIR IS PREPARED AND VERIFIED BUT *NOT APPLIED*
  (2026-07-31c).** `pipeline/fix_link_targets.py` writes to
  `_xc/linksk_fixed/`; **the live maps are untouched.** Do not swap it in

    The Khuddaka ṭīkā (the edition gives one only to the Netti: 21Khu04 4,841 ·
    20Khu03 4,428 · 19Khu02 3,650 · 23Khu06 3,621 · 22Khu05 2,957 · 18Khu01

  - **Class C — 14,278 (39%): NOT cleanly wrong, and I could not separate them.**
    A commentary volume can straddle two canon volumes — the Jātaka commentary
    runs continuously across 22Khu05 and 23Khu06 — so `20Khu03 -> 33KhuA14` may
    be a real seam while `39Abhi11 -> 48AbhiA01` (Paṭṭhāna IV pointing at the
    **Dhammasaṅgaṇī** commentary) plainly is not. **Any grouping coarse enough to
    call the first legitimate calls the second legitimate too.** Left alone.
    `--all-violations` prunes them; do not run it without deciding first.
  **AND THE REV MAPS ARE NOT READY, WHICH IS WHY NOTHING WAS SWAPPED.** Pruning
  the forward maps alone would leave `linksk/<VOL>.rev.json` still saying those
  ṭīkā paragraphs belong to those canon volumes, so opening 21KhuT01 would still
  jump into the Apadāna. The rev maps have 2,408 apparent violations (9.1%) —
  **but the top two are FALSE POSITIVES of my own check**: `26VsmT02 ->
  52Vism02` and `25VsmT01 -> 51Vism01` are the Visuddhimagga mahāṭīkā pointing
  at the Visuddhimagga, which the concordance places in the **commentary**
  column, not the canon. My check assumed a rev target is always a canon volume.
  **Fix the check before trusting its rev numbers.**
* **`build_links_bynum.py` HAS A LATENT BUG THAT ATE EVERY LINK ON MY FIRST
  ATTEMPT.** Its cursor advances with
  `cn[cursor+1] is not None and cn[cursor+1] <= N`, so **if the target volume's
  first paragraph is UNNUMBERED the walk can never start and the whole range
  emits nothing.** Ṭīkā volumes open with an unnumbered title line
  (`08DiT01#0` = "Sīlakkhandhavaggaṭīkā"). It does not bite today only because
  the existing ranges happen to begin elsewhere; constraining the ranges exposed
  it instantly. `fix_link_targets.py` walks a list of the NUMBERED paragraphs
  instead. **Fix this in `build_links_bynum.py` before any future relink.**
* **THE ROOT CAUSE, worth stating plainly:** `carry_vol()` takes the target
  volume from the PREVIOUS links and forward- **and backward-fills** it across
  the volume. **One stray link propagates over everything around it.** That is
  how the Apadāna acquired 4,841 links into the Nettiṭīkā. The real repair is to
  teach `build_links_bynum.py` the concordance and rebuild — not to patch maps.

  Of 101,157 link targets, **36,997 (36.6%) point into a volume the concordance

  paragraph's existing TARGET VOLUME and fixes the ORDINAL by a number match" —
  it never consults `concordance.json`, so a wrong target volume survives every
  rebuild. Worst: 20Khu03 8,180 · 21Khu04 7,654 · 19Khu02 3,699 · 23Khu06 3,625
  · 22Khu05 3,404 · 18Khu01 1,912 · 39Abhi11 1,471. **The Milindapañha, which
  the edition gives NO commentary at all, carries a target on essentially every
  numbered paragraph** (520), drawn from the Nettiṭīkā, Mahāniddesa, Udāna,
  Buddhavaṁsa and Khuddakapāṭha commentaries. **`21KhuT01` (the Nettiṭīkā) alone
  is claimed by nine Khuddaka canon volumes it has nothing to do with.**
  **NOT staleness, and not a misreading of the concordance — tested:** the
  citing layer paragraph's bolded lemma occurs in the canon paragraph it claims
  **50.0% of the time for links the concordance allows (19,511 pairs) and 10.4%
  for links it does not (4,494 pairs)**. A five-fold contrast. The reader draws
  these as that paragraph's commentary, so a reader of the Milindapañha is shown
  the Nettiṭīkā and told it is the commentary. **A confident wrong link is worse
  than the grey span.** `_xc/check_link_targets.py` — new, exits 1 on any
  violation. **NOT FIXED: 37,000 data edits was not something to do unattended.**
* **!!! THE SITE WAS UNUSABLE ON A PHONE, AND THE REASON WAS IN THE CODE
  (2026-07-31b, user-reported: iPhone and iPad "very slow to load and became
  unresponsive").** Three independent causes, all measured:
  1. **Opening ONE volume fetched every volume its links point into, in full,
     before the first render.** `openCanon` gathered every target and awaited
     `loadVol` on all of them; `loadVol` fetches TEN files per volume.
     **18Khu01: 190 files, 31.4 MB.** 39Abhi11: 14.7 MB. The `verse/` maps alone
     were 10.6 MB. **And none of it was on screen** — opening a canon paragraph
     sets `{canon:true,A:false,T:false}`, so every megabyte drew bands nobody had
     asked for. **FIXED: `ensureBandVols()` loads only what an ACTIVE band needs.
     18Khu01 31.43 MB -> 1.91 MB, 190 files -> 10, identical render** (same 1,871
     ¶ blocks, same 358 anchors). Every render path already guarded on
     `cache[vol]`, which is why it was safe — and why every place that turns a
     band ON must `await ensureBandVols()` before `render()`.
  2. **`search.html` downloaded 22 MB before it could be used.** `boot()` ran on
     load and fetched `index/terms.compact.json` — **21.0 MB raw, 5.3 MB gzipped,
     643,965 terms** — plus `names.json`. **FIXED: lazy. 0 fetches on load**
     (verified), warmed on focus, loaded on first query.
  3. **`stamp_build.py` was NOT idempotent, so every deploy busted every
     visitor's cache of all 1,691 JSON files.** BUILD moved on every run:
     `cedb34504f2b -> bce8ca27329f -> 07749a194d0b`. Cause was mine, from
     2026-07-30j: `check_derived.py` exec's `build_pdfblanks.py` to compare its
     output, and **an exec'd module inherits `sys.argv`** — so
     `stamp_build.py --write` handed it `--write` and the read-only check wrote
     the file, changing its mtime, which the stamp hashes. **FIXED** (argv
     swapped during the exec); BUILD now stable across three runs. **A CHECK
     MUST HAVE NO SIDE EFFECTS.**
  **STILL SLOW, NOT FIXED — both need a design decision, see the dated entry:**
  the reader boots **110,469 DOM elements** from `nav.json` (2.2 MB) before a
  volume is open, because the sidebar builds all 30,730 rows eagerly with the
  side-effect maps woven through it; and **one search still costs ~61 MB**
  (the 21 MB term list plus a shard per matching volume).
* **THE DIRECT-LINK RESIDUE IS NOT 9,164. IT IS 16 (2026-07-31b).** The recorded
  figure ("9,164 numbered ¶ with no rev entry, 27.4% of 33,398", ceiling ~12%)
  is obsolete, and a rival quick check gave 1,034 — **because the two read
  different files.** `linksk/<VOL>.links.json` is what `loadLinks()` fetches;
  `links/<VOL>.fwd.json` is loaded by NOTHING in the reader. Measured from the
  reader's own file: of **49,190** numbered canon ¶ (excluding Milindapañha),
  **26,760 (54.4%) have a direct target, 22,414 (45.6%) are covered by an earlier
  block, and 16 (0.0%) have no target at all.** The coverage gap is closed; what
  remains is precision — `covered` versus `direct` — not absence. Method stated
  in `_xc/residue.py` so the number stops drifting.
* **`check_derived.py` now also reports `apparatus/`, `linksk/`, `links/`,
  `sections/` and `nav.json` — as ADVISORY, not blocking.** `linksk/` and
  `links/` are already older than the newest volume JSON (13:18 against 13:49 on

  scheduled, and a check nobody can satisfy gets answered with `--force`.

**Three gates, three scopes. Quote the scope whenever you call anything verified.**

| what | command | what it does NOT cover |
|---|---|---|
| body text | `python3 pipeline/verify_render_vs_pdf.py <VOL> <p0> <p1> <lo> <hi> [minw]` | apparatus, presentation |
| apparatus | `python3 pipeline/verify_apparatus.py <VOL>` | body, presentation |
| presentation | `node pipeline/check_layout.js [VOL...]` | content of either kind |

Run a volume as ONE range (`lo=0`, `hi=len(paragraphs)`), never book by book — per-book page ranges overlap at the seams and manufacture phantom drops.

* **THE LEFT PANE SHOWS A VOLUME'S PART AS A ROMAN NUMERAL, AND `nav.json`

  `katha` · **`heads`** (2026-07-28d). The fourth is HEADING-DELIMITED PROSE:

* **!!! NEVER WRITE `{'groups': []}` ON A SIDE-MAP ENTRY THAT IS ONLY CARRYING
  RESIDUE.** A `groups` key — even an empty one — makes `render_parts` AND the
  reader take the VERSE branch, which renders `before + after` and **NOT the
  corpus text**. Three residue lines written that way deleted three paragraphs
  and the body gate reported 287 missing lines that were in the corpus. Omit
  the key and both take the prose branch.
* **THE EDITION MISPRINTS ITS OWN HOMAGE, THREE TIMES OVER.** `Namo Tassa`,

* **A VOLUME CAN BE BUILT, GATED AND STILL UNDISPLAYABLE.** `check_layout.js`

* **BACK UP BEFORE RE-RUNNING A GENERATOR ON A VOLUME THAT DID NOT NEED IT**
  (2026-07-28c). `extract_bold.py 51Vism01 --force` was run on a volume whose

  the backup, not the outcome.
* **!!! THE BODY GATE AND THE BUILDER DISAGREE ABOUT LINE-END HYPHENS, AND THE
  GATE'S COUNTS CARRY THAT DIFFERENCE** (2026-07-28a). Since the hyphen fix of
  2026-07-27aj the builder KEEPS the edition's hyphen where the continuation
  opens with a vowel (`hyjoin`); `verify_render_vs_pdf.pdf_lines` still joins
  and STRIPS unconditionally (`out[-1][:-1] + t`). Neither loses text, but on a
  volume with printed residue it produces `PDF-lines-missing`, `render-not-in-PDF`
  **and `rendered-too-often`** reports that are pure artefact. **Discharge them
  before reading them:** `_abhia/hyclass.py <VOL> <p0> <p1> <lo> <hi>` re-asks
  each missing line after applying the gate's own join to the render, and
  `_abhia/dupclass.py` does the same for the duplications. Both went to 0 on all
  three Abhidhamma commentaries — including the two duplications that had held
  49AbhiA02 open. **A count is not a defect until one of these has run.**
* **!!! `before` RESIDUE IS STORED ONE PRINTED LINE PER PARAGRAPH, AND THE
  READER DRAWS EACH AS ITS OWN BLOCK** (found 2026-07-28a, NOT fixed).
  `add_prose` joins the `after` residue; the `before` path appends each printed
  LINE, and `proseOne` wraps every entry in its own `<div class="gatha-after">`.
  Measured over every volume with a verse map: **8,688 `before` entries, 6,336
  of them broken mid-sentence and 111 mid-WORD at a hyphen, across 33 volumes**
  — canon as well as commentary. Mean entry length is 41-62 characters where
  `after` runs 325-690. 18Khu01 (512) is the one volume where the joined
  behaviour is reachable. Fixing it moves the render of 33 volumes, so it needs
  the full measurement and a re-gate, and it belongs with the deferred reading
  model.
* **UNNUMBERED CORPUS PROSE LIVES IN THE CORPUS AND IS AN ANCHOR** (2026-07-27ah,
  reversing 2026-07-27v). `unnum_runs` aligns each unnumbered paragraph against
  a contiguous run of printed items and requires EXACT text equality — a
  line-end hyphen joined either way, because the corpus keeps it and the gate
  strips it. Any `popen`/`pcont` in the run means prose: the paragraph renders,
  its printed items are suppressed, and the headings above it anchor to IT.
  Only `vline` means display verse: it stays hidden and the print restores it.
  **`pair_ords` (numbered) is what pairs 1:1 and what `seq` walks; `ords` is
  what renders** — the same list in every volume without unnumbered prose.
* **AN UNNUMBERED ANCHOR MUST NOT GET A `groups` KEY.** Reader and gate alike
  take the verse branch — `before + after`, NOT the corpus text — for any entry
  that HAS `groups`, even empty. That would blank the paragraph.
* **AND IT MUST BE LINKED, or it renders NOWHERE.** The reader draws a
  commentary volume only through `targetsFor()`, and the linker keys on a
  paragraph NUMBER. An unnumbered paragraph takes the canon paragraph of the
  unit it precedes, stored before it, and **once** — 01VinA01 is a target of all
  five Vinaya volumes, so per-file placement draws the Bāhiranidāna five times.
* **~~THE PEYYĀLA MARK IS BEING EATEN BY THE LINE-END-HYPHEN JOIN~~ — FIXED
  2026-07-27aj, and it was a third of a larger defect.** A printed line ending
  in `-` was joined `prev[:-1] + t` at six sites, i.e. assumed to be a soft
  word break EVERYWHERE. Measured over all 118 volumes: **PEYYALA 3,906**
  (the line ends with a standalone `-pa-`/`-pe-`/`-la-`) · **VOWEL 7,572**
  (the next line opens with a vowel) · **OTHER 2,781**. `hyjoin()` now decides
  the three: keep the hyphen and ADD a space; keep it and add none; join
  without it. **THE EDITION DECIDED THIS, NOT A RULE I INVENTED** — a
  corpus-wide index of every pair printed INLINE (line interiors only, so no
  break votes on itself) says **VOWEL 2,545 KEEP : 2 JOIN** and **OTHER 716
  JOIN : 65 KEEP**. **The peyyāla must NOT be put to that vote** — `pa`+`taṁ`
  is the real word *pataṁ* — so it has its own rule. Proved over all 52 SPEC
  volumes: 3,436 strings moved in 47, and **0 volumes whose letter-text or
  string count changed**. Nine regression snapshots advanced by hand.
  **THE BODY GATE IS BLIND TO THIS CLASS BY CONSTRUCTION** (it strips line-end
  hyphens on both sides) and read 0/0/0/0 throughout — which is why 2,647 eaten
  marks sat in the canon unseen. **BOTH REPORTS RE-RUN** with fresh caches, each
  until the count stopped rising and confirmed by a further run: body clean
  **40/118** (was 33), apparatus **18/118** (was 15), variants lost 2,851 ->
  2,597, xrefs lost 201 -> 63. **The one residue is NOT RULEABLE and is
  recorded as such:** OTHER's 65 KEEP are the edition's grammatical citation
  forms (`ca-saddassa`, `ta-kāro`), but over all 568 breaks of that shape the
  evidence is **60 KEEP : 37 JOIN : 366 BOTH** — `Go-saddena` is the same form
  as `ca-saddassa` and the edition prints it both ways — so a rule general
  enough to catch the 60 is wrong on the 37. **58 of the 65 are in unbuilt
  ṬĪKĀ volumes; in everything built today it is THREE breaks, two of them
  apparatus sigla.** Take it per volume by named literal when the Ṭīkā layer
  is built.
* **THE TWO-LINE COLOPHON FRAME IS `colofix`, NEVER `headskip`, AND IT IS IN
  EVERY COMMENTARY VOLUME.** `Papañcasūdaniyā Majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya`,
  `Iti Sumaṅgalavilāsiniyā Dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāya(ṁ)`,
  `Samantapāsādikāya Vinayasaṁvaṇṇanāya` — the genitive frame the edition sets
  ABOVE `<X>vaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.` at every section close. The stop is on the
  SECOND line, which `kat_is_colo` already claims, so the first reads as a
  heading. **It is not a running footer** (2026-07-27ah called it one and named
  `headskip`; `headskip` would demote a printed colophon line to display
  verse). Count it against the volume's SECTIONS, not its pages. **The edition
  misspells it — three times so far, each differently: 12MaA03 p188
  `majjhimanikāyaṭṭhākathāya`, 13MaA04 p88 `Kajjhima-`, 09DiA03 p152
  `Dīghanikaya-`. NAME each variant; do not fold them.**
* **A GĀTHĀ'S LAST PĀDA CLOSES WITH THE CITATION DASH AND SO READS AS A
  HEADING.** Where the citation runs on into the prose below, the pāda ends
  `…”ti–` with no stop — the one thing `kat_is_head` asks a display line not to
  have. 22 found across the seven volumes built 2026-07-27ai. `headskip`; each
  becomes the last `vline` of its own block. **The literal is the PRINTED LINE,
  so it cannot be shared between volumes** — the same pāda carries different
  footnote markers in different volumes, and 11MaA02 prints
  `…pabhedoti1–` where 07DiA01 sets `…pabhedo”ti–`.
* **!!! DECLARE THE `matika` RANGE ON EVERY VOLUME THAT PRINTS ONE. A GATE THAT
  FINDS NOTHING LOOKS EXACTLY LIKE A GATE THAT PASSES.** 07DiA01, 08DiA02 and
  09DiA03 shipped with no `matika` declared at all, so their navs reported
  "mātikā lists 0" and three volumes carried wrong roles nobody could see. And
  `MAT`'s dotted leader was `(?:\.\.\.\s+)*` — exactly three dots — where
  12MaA03 prints FOUR, so all 51 of its dotted entries were invisible.
  Widened to `\.{3,}`, measured +0 −0 over all 32 volumes that declare a range.
  **The one comparison that has now found a wrong role on THIRTEEN volumes is
  the heads stream against the mātikā; after it, both counts should be EQUAL
  and the diff empty in BOTH directions.**
* **A UNIT WHOSE TAIL THE EXTRACTION GLUED A HEADING ONTO IS NOT A LEAKED
  HEADING.** The leak test asks whether a corpus paragraph LOOKS like one, and
  a paragraph ENDING in a heading stem does — so 18AnA02 ord463, a real unit
  with `(28) 8. Rāgapeyyālavaṇṇanā` swallowed onto its end, was hidden and its
  book paired 188 printed against 187 corpus. `leak_keep` names the ordinal and
  REFUSES if it is not in fact flagged. Recorded, not corrected.
* **NEVER TAKE THE HOMAGE COUNT AS THE BOOK COUNT, AND NOT EVERY `n` RESET IS A
  BOUNDARY.** The three Aṅguttara commentary volumes print ONE homage page each
  and carry ELEVEN nipātas between them (1 + 3 + 7, which is the check). A
  reset is a boundary only when it returns to **1**: 17AnA01's 394 -> 389 and
  19AnA03's 294 -> 250 are peyyāla RANGES, and taken as boundaries they invent
  books the edition does not print. **And the page seams are the PRINTED
  OPENINGS, not the corpus `pdf_page`** — `page_offset` is 0 for two of these
  volumes and −1 for the third, and derived from the corpus every seam was a
  page out.
* **THE EDITION MISPRINTS A UNIT-RANGE SEPARATOR AS A PERIOD, AND IT BREAKS
  TWO DIFFERENT THINGS.** `64.65.` (14SamA01 p114) offers no space after the
  period, so `extract.py` saw no boundary and the unit arrived inside the
  previous paragraph — a CORPUS SPLICE, `kat_splices`. `3. 10.` (15SamA02
  p211) made a HEADING match `VERSE`, so it was read as a numbered UNIT —
  `headfix`. Both refused to build on the 1:1 count, which is the only thing
  that can see either. Preserve the misprint; name the line as printed.
* **`headfix` NOW BEATS THE NUMBERED TEST TOO** (2026-07-27ak), which is what
  its docstring always claimed. Measured over all 55 SPEC volumes: exactly ONE
  moves.
* **A COLOPHON WITH A WORD BETWEEN THE NAME AND `niṭṭhita-` IS NOT CLAIMED BY
  THE FORM TEST.** `Mūlapaṇṇāsaṭṭhakathāya paṭhamo bhāgo niṭṭhito.`,
  `Majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathā sabbākārena niṭṭhitā.` On 10MaA01 that was worse

  as the LAST paragraph it had no later numbered unit to hang a link off, so it
  would have been in the corpus, in the tree, and **on no page**. `colofix`.
* **`tops` CANNOT MIX A LITERAL WITH A PATTERN.** `subtree` reads a `re:` top
  only when `tops` is a list of ONE, so a mixed list silently nests every
  pattern-matched top under the last literal. Name them all instead. Do NOT
  widen `subtree` — it feeds every volume's tree.
* **`vr.page_offset(vol)` REALLY IS PER VOLUME — READ IT, DO NOT INFER IT.**
  10MaA01 is **0** where 11MaA02, 12MaA03, 13MaA04 and 07DiA01 are **−1**.
  Trimming 10MaA01's rebuilt corpus on the 1-based extent dropped its title
  page and kept the index's first page.
* **A MĀTIKĀ OF TWO PAGES CANNOT FILTER ITS OWN TITLE STACK.**
  `matika_headers` needs a line that opens THREE or more pages. Use
  `matika_drop` and name the lines. The general rule — "nothing above the
  `Mātikā … Piṭṭhaṅka` column head is an entry" — was tried and **REJECTED**:
  measured over every volume declaring a mātikā it removes 31 entries and
  several are REAL (33Abhi05's five book heads, 37Abhi09's four pair-lines,
  15An01's three paṇṇāsakas), and 16An02 gains one.
* **`node _navdup.js` AND `python3 pipeline/check_shape.py` AFTER A BUILD.**
  Three assertions, each written for a defect a USER found before any gate did:
  a commentary/Ṭīkā volume contributes exactly ONE top-level node (11 unbuilt
  volumes still fail it and are NAMED in `MULTITOP_PENDING`); a paragraph may
  not carry more notes than it has WORDS (corpus max 0.75, the 07DiA01 defect
  94.0); and a `gatha` block whose median line reaches the body measure (58,
  from the measured distribution: p50 31, p99 63) is prose set as verse — a
  REPORT to judge against the page, 219 blocks in 19 volumes, 129 of them in
  06VinSg06.
* **SCRATCH BELONGS INSIDE THE REPO, NOT IN `/tmp`.** A `cat > /tmp/entry.md`
  failed `Permission denied` (a stale file of that name owned by another user)
  while the Python step that READ it did not, and a five-hour-old copy of an
  old entry was spliced into HANDOFF.md as though it were new. Caught by the
  line count and reverted. Same lesson `regress.py` and the apparatus cache
  each taught once already.
* **`verify_all_volumes.py` HAS NO ARGUMENT PARSER.** Unknown flags are
  IGNORED, so `--help` runs it as a no-arg invocation: it reuses the stale
  default cache and rewrites `docs/verify_report.md` from old entries in under
  a second. Always `--cache <fresh-dir-inside-the-repo> --budget 33`, re-run
  until the count stops rising (five runs for 118 volumes). `/tmp/osbct/...`
  is not writable on the device.
* **REGRESSION after ANY edit to `build_khu_volume.py`** — **11** volumes x 5
  maps = 55, byte-identical, BUILDER-vs-BUILDER against
  `build_khu_volume.py.preniddesa` for 19Khu02-23Khu06 and builder-vs-shipped
  for 24Khu07/25Khu08/26Khu09/27Khu10/28Khu11/29Abhi01. **`python3
  pipeline/regress.py baseline` then `check`** — 3 seconds, so there is no
  excuse. (It was `/tmp/mp/regress.py` with the session directory hardcoded in
  `ROOT`, i.e. scratch that would have failed in any later session; moved into
  the repo 2026-07-26w, snapshots in `_regress/`.)
* **A COLOPHON IS DECIDED BY FORM UNDER `heads_by_form`, AND SO IS EVERY
  SECOND PĀDA OF A COUPLET.** `pada_runon` is the answer and it has now
  corrected FOUR shipped volumes — 31Abhi03 (11), 32Abhi04 (45), 33Abhi05 and
  36Abhi08 (8). Whenever a new volume prints gāthā, run the measurement over
  EVERY volume, not just the new one; that is how all four were found.
* **`verify_render_vs_pdf.py` MODELS THE READER — A RENDER DEFECT LIVES IN
  BOTH.** The gate does not run `reader2.html`; it reproduces `block()` in
  Python. The udāna-lead-in fallback was wrong in both and patching only the
  reader left the gate still reporting the fault (2026-07-26ag).
* **A BLOCK CAN SPAN A PAGE BREAK AND CHANGE COLUMN ACROSS IT.** `_kat_cols`
  measures the body column PER PAGE — correctly — but an uddāna that fills a
  page sits AT that page's body column and reads as prose, while the same block
  on a shared page reads as verse. `udd_run` lets the edition's own
  "Tassuddānaṁ" label decide the whole run (2026-07-26ah). Do NOT widen the
  display gate for this.
* **`head_words` IS A MEASUREMENT.** The 2-word cap on a numbered heading was
  measured on 36Abhi08; 03Vin03's titles are four words. Measure it per volume.
* **Read the `--show` listing of every build.** Headings, colophons and gāthā
  blocks are judgements about the page, and reviewing that list has now caught
  a wrong-role defect on **SIX** separate volumes — every one of which passed
  the body gate at 0/0/0/0. The last two: 33Abhi05, where 21 of 23 gāthā blocks
  were the book's own catechism, and 35Abhi07, where a WRAPPED DISPLAY LINE's
  one-word remainder read as a colophon.
* **A `kat_splices` MARK IS NOT ONLY A KEY — IT IS THE TEXT THAT RENDERS**, so
  it must be the printed unit's WHOLE FIRST LINE. Declared shorter, all three
  of the declaration's own tests still pass (the host really does contain those
  words) and the printed continuation lines are then joined onto a truncated
  opening, dropping whatever fell between. Found on 34Abhi06 by the body gate;
  36Abhi08's declaration happens to be a whole line and never showed it.
* **AN ERRATUM IN THE BODY IS NOT AN ERRATUM IN THE MĀTIKĀ.** `errata` rewrites
  a mātikā entry GLOBALLY, which is right only when the misprint occurs once on
  each side. Where a heading is printed several times and one printing is
  misspelt, use `body_errata`, which puts the alternative on the TREE side.
  Got wrong on 35Abhi07 and it moved the forward-only pointer 195 sections into
  the next book.
* **A PAGE RANGE IN A NOTE IS NOT A MEASUREMENT.** All five Vinaya mātikā
  ranges scouted in 2026-07-26ai were shifted by one, each dropping the
  mātikā's FIRST page — the one carrying that volume's opening top level. The
  range is one line to measure (the pages that carry the `Piṭṭhaṅka` column);
  measure it.
* **A MĀTIKĀ THAT CANNOT BE A GATE ENTRY-BY-ENTRY MAY STILL BE ONE LINE BY
  LINE.** Its CENTRED lines are group heads and are 1:1 with the body's
  structural headings even where its dotted entries are finer than the body —
  which is every Vinaya volume. `matika_centred_gate`, added 2026-07-26aj, and
  it caught a real divergence on its first run. And a centred head's INDENT is
  a function of its LENGTH, so the 18-space threshold is a measurement too
  (`centred_indent`).
* **DECLARING A LEVEL PUSHES IT ONTO THE STACK, AND AN IMMEDIATE REPEAT OF A
  STACKED LABEL IS THEN SKIPPED AS AN ANCESTOR REPRINT.** So a block the
  edition prints twice in a row must be left UNDECLARED — it falls to the leaf
  branch, which does not push, and both rows stand. Declared, eleven of
  01Vin01's twelve `Idaṁ …mūlakaṁ` rows vanish with every word of the text
  still in place. **A `levels` row is not free: it decides what SURVIVES.**
* **THE FOOTNOTE RULE IS SOMETIMES A GRAPHIC, AND `_{10,}` WAS SEARCHED FOR IN
  FOUR SEPARATE PLACES.** 14 pages of the corpus (05Vin05 x10, 03Vin03 p340,
  07Di02 x3 — measured over all 118 volumes, both pdftotext modes) emit no text
  line for it, and every consumer then behaved as though the page had no
  apparatus: the cells entered the body stream AND `rebuild_apparatus` stored
  them NOWHERE — ~17 printed variant readings held by no layer in two SHIPPED
  volumes. **The parser and its own checker shared the blind spot, so the loss
  cancelled out and the apparatus gate read clean.** `pipeline/fnblock.py` is
  the single detector now; it is self-verifying (a numbered cell must have its
  MARKER printed above) and REFUSES rather than guesses. Anything new that
  searches for the rule must use it — `build_suttanipata.py`,
  `fix_18khu01_residuals.py`, `build_19khu02.py` and `_udd_probe_mod.py` still
  do not, deliberately: measured, their volumes have no such page.
* **`headskip` IS THE INVERSE OF `headfix`, AND IT IS NOT THE SAME KEY AS THE
  PAGE CUT.** A line NAMED in it is not a heading wherever it sits; nothing is
  suppressed and only the ROLE changes, so the body gate is unmoved BY
  CONSTRUCTION — which is why it cannot see this class at all and why
  `check_layout.js`, the reader and the NAV are what move. Every declared
  literal must be met or the build refuses. **Ask what a suppressed line
  BECOMES before suppressing it**: a footnote cell must become a FOOTNOTE, i.e.
  be provably in the apparatus first, or cutting it deletes printed text.
* **A BOOK TITLE IS NOT UNIQUE ACROSS NIKĀYAS, AND A CHECKER THAT CLICKS BY
  TITLE CAN PASS THE WRONG VOLUME.** `Mahāvaggapāḷi` is BOTH 03Vin03 (Vinaya)
  and 07Di02 (Dīgha) — legitimate data, which is why `_navdup.js` scopes its
  no-duplicate-title rule to ONE nikāya. `_vinnavverify.js` clicked a hardcoded
  `Vinayapiṭaka` and reported **"292 of 292 rows clicked" for a 156-row
  volume**, sweeping the wrong tree and calling it a pass. Fixed 2026-07-27; it
  now derives the nikāya from the volume and picks the row from that nikāya's
  own SPAN, and prints which nikāya it resolved. **Read that line.**
* **DIFF THE HEADS STREAM AGAINST THE MĀTIKĀ ON EVERY NEW VOLUME.** That one
  comparison found every per-volume key the three Dīgha volumes needed —
  `head_paren`, two `colofix`, a `headfix`, seventeen `headskip` — and NOT ONE
  of them was visible to any content gate, because a wrong ROLE leaves every
  word in place. It also finds the edition's errata, which must then be COUNTED
  ON BOTH SIDES before `errata` is used: that key rewrites a mātikā entry
  globally and is right only when the misprint is printed ONCE ON EACH SIDE
  (08Di03's `Nava dhammā` is printed twice, so it took `body_errata`).
* **`fold` KEEPS DIGITS.** A body label numbered where the mātikā entry is bare
  will not fold equal, whether the number LEADS (`(2) Cora-upamā`, 07Di02) or
  TRAILS (`Vipassanāñāṇa (1)`, 06Di01). Name it per volume with `body_errata`;
  do NOT teach `fold` to strip `(N)` — 32Abhi04 heads sections
  `(175) 10. Navattabbaṁ…` where that number IS part of the label.
* **A `Piṭṭhaṅka` SEARCH DOES NOT GIVE YOU THE MĀTIKĀ.** 06Di01's word index
  and its `Nānāpāṭhā` variant appendix head their columns `Piṭṭhaṅko` too, so
  the naive search returns sixteen pages where the mātikā is six. Measure the
  range, then LOOK at it.
* **A NUMBERING GAP FOUND BY A REGEX IS NOT A NUMBERING GAP UNTIL YOU HAVE
  LOOKED AT THE PAGE.** 09Ma01 appeared to skip units 42 and 43; the edition
  sets both with NO SPACE AFTER THE PERIOD (`42.Tassa`), so a pattern requiring
  whitespace could not see them, and the truth was the opposite — the CORPUS
  was short by two and needed `kat_splices`. Fourth and fifth embedded unit
  number found so far.
* **!!! WHEN A VOLUME PRINTS GĀTHĀ, CHECK `pada_runon` ON EVERY VOLUME —
  INCLUDING THE ONES ALREADY CALLED DONE.** It was missing from all six
  Dīgha/Majjhima volumes and had torn **38 gāthā** apart, sending every SECOND
  pāda of a couplet to the uddāna map: the edition alternates a couplet's
  punctuation (comma, then full stop) and the form test reads the second half
  as a colophon. 08Di03 was carrying **212 "colophons" for eleven suttas**; the
  true figure is 22. All three gates AND both nav checkers read clean the whole
  time, because a wrong ROLE leaves every word present. Fixed 2026-07-27f —
  read that entry before building any volume that prints verse.
  **THE AUDIT IS NOT THE UDDĀNA QUERY** (that fires on 25 volumes and is
  useless — the edition closes sections with an ORDINAL or a bare vāra name).
  **Ask instead: is the volume `katha` + `heads_by_form` WITHOUT `pada_runon`?**
  Then force the flag on and diff the side-maps — `_fnprobe/prprobe.py`.
  Inert means no defect. Audited 2026-07-27g: only 31Abhi03 was still wrong.
* **A GATE THAT GOES QUIET IS NOT THE SAME AS A VOLUME THAT IS CORRECT.** Any
  change that makes a gate report LESS must enumerate what disappears — not
  count it — and state in advance the shape every vanishing report is expected
  to have. `display_openers` was written `prev < 8`, which also silenced
  10Ma02 p413; the stop condition caught it, the rule was tightened to the
  measured body column, and the preserved report turned out to be a REAL
  defect (a pāda rendered as an uddāna, out of order). Added 2026-07-27d.
* **~~`PDF-chunks-missing` WITH `PDF-lines-missing 0`~~ — the prose->gāthā case
  is FIXED 2026-07-27d by `display_openers`,** measured old-vs-new over all 34
  built volumes with 31 unmoved and nothing newly appearing. The general
  statement still holds:**`PDF-chunks-missing` WITH `PDF-lines-missing 0` IS A CHUNKING ARTEFACT, NOT
  LOST TEXT — but it is NOT a pass either.** The chunker runs lines together
  until sentence punctuation, so an unpunctuated line glues to the one below
  and fabricates a chunk the render never has. `display_lines` prevents this
  for HEADINGS; it does NOT for a PROSE line running into the first pāda of a
  display verse, because it collects only centred short UNPUNCTUATED lines and
  a pāda ends in `,` or `.`. **The fix is a LOOK-AHEAD** — terminate a
  body-column line whose SUCCESSOR sits at display indent — and it needs the
  corpus-wide measurement first. Open on 10Ma02 (2) and 11Ma03 (5).
* **!!! A NARRATIVE HOMAGE IS NOT THE BOOK'S OWN, AND TREATING IT AS ONE
  DELETES IT FROM THE BODY.** Every `HOMAGE` line was classified 'homage', all
  of them written to the SAME key (so the LAST won), and the branch's
  `continue` meant the line never reached the body. It cost text in 10Ma02 and
  12Sam01, both already called done. The discriminator is POSITION — a book's
  own homage stands before that book's first numbered unit. Fixed 2026-07-27j,
  35 of 39 volumes inert. **Any book that QUOTES a formula the builder lifts is
  the same class; ask what else is lifted by pattern alone.**
* **THE EDITION MISPRINTS THE HOMAGE ITSELF** — `Namo tassa **Bhagavatā**
  Arahato…` on 17An03's Dasakanipāta title page — and that hid a whole book from
  `scout_volume.py`'s homage scan. **The `n` RESET found it; the homage scan did
  not. Never take the homage count as the book count.** 2026-07-27j.
* **`head_paren` WHEREVER THE EDITION NUMBERS A SECTION TWICE.** From the second
  paṇṇāsaka on the Aṅguttara prints `(6) 1. Brāhmaṇavagga`; `kat_is_head` needs
  a capital, so without the key half the vaggas are not headings at all and
  their suttas hang directly off the paṇṇāsaka. Invisible to every content gate
  — the 1:1 unit count and the body gate are identical either way. **Found by
  building the NAV.** 2026-07-27j.
* **A UNIT NUMBER CAN BE A RANGE, AND A HEADING'S NAME CAN END AT A NUMERAL
  COLLECTIVE.** The Saṁyutta's peyyāla sections print ONE unit for several
  suttas — `42-47. Sace vo bhikkhave…` under `2-7. Saṁyojanappahānādisuttachakka`
  — so `VERSE` admits `N-M.` (measured inert on 34 of 36 volumes) and a
  volume's `stems` must carry the collectives (`pañcaka`, `dasaka`, `navutika`…)
  or the heading falls through to the unit test. Before that, 94 printed units
  were invisible and two volumes refused to build. 2026-07-27i.
* **A LINE THAT OPENS WITH A UNIT NUMBER IS NOT A COLOPHON BY THE GENERIC FORM
  TEST** — the heading branch always said so, the colophon branch runs first and
  did not. Fixed inside `kat_is_colo` 2026-07-27i, 35 of 36 volumes inert.
* **`regress.py baseline` REGENERATES FROM THE FROZEN `.preniddesa` BUILDER**, so
  it cannot carry an intended change forward. When a correction legitimately
  moves a regression volume, the affected snapshot must be advanced BY HAND and
  the reason recorded — done once, for `_regress/base/20Khu03.uddana.json`
  (2026-07-27i).
* **`_vinnavverify.js`'s ROW SWEEP IS SCOPED TO THE WHOLE SIDEBAR, NOT THE
  VOLUME.** `b.parentElement.querySelectorAll('.row')` is all 15,441 rows of the
  nav, so the sweep does not finish on a large tree; and it asserts ONE nav node
  per volume, which is false for any volume carrying two books. Use
  `_samspan.js` (static, reproduces `render()`'s span arithmetic) until a
  volume-scoped DOM sweep exists. 2026-07-27i.
* **jsdom scripts need `node --max-old-space-size=4096`.**
* **NEVER KEY A PATCH ON A STRING THAT OCCURS MORE THAN ONCE.** Always
  `assert s.count(old) == 1` before replacing. On 2026-07-26 a patch keyed on
  `_bt = os.path.join(R, 'booktitle'…)` hit the copy in `kat_build` instead of
  the one in `__main__` and deleted 600 lines; `ast.parse` still passed. There
  was no usable backup and the `.pyc` had already been overwritten from the
  damaged source. See 2026-07-26r.
* **A HEADING'S POSITION ON ITS PRINTED LINE IS PART OF THE STRUCTURE, and
  `split_centre` throws it away.** On a two-heading line the LEFT half stands
  one level ABOVE the right — measured over all 696 of 40Abhi12's pair-lines
  and true of every one. `build_abhidhamma_nav.py` reads those lines back off
  the PDF and aligns them against the heads stream in LOCKSTEP (`pairsides`,
  per volume), refusing if a single printed pair cannot be found there. Do NOT
  reach for `split_centre` for this: it feeds every volume's side-maps, and the
  same evidence is available downstream for free.
* **WHERE THE TOP LEVEL IS A `re:` PATTERN, THE ANCESTOR-REPRINT RULE MUST BE
  TESTED FIRST.** The Paṭṭhāna reprints the outer section's name at the head of
  every inner one; with an open top level each reprint matched the pattern and
  opened a NEW top. 39Abhi11 SHIPPED that way — "1. Hetuduka" 22 times and
  "1. Kusalattika" 52 times in its sidebar, every one of them opening text, so
  the row sweep passed and `_navdup.js` could not see it either. Fixed
  2026-07-26v.
* **`node _navdup.js` after ANY nav build.** The invariant is ONE NODE PER BOOK,
  not per volume (18Khu01 has five, 01VinA01 fourteen). A nav builder that
  replaces "the" node of a volume leaves the others behind — that shipped once.
  !!! Both of its original tests were keyed by VOLUME, so a title repeated
  ACROSS volumes passed — the Abhidhamma listed "Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi" three times
  for as long as the check existed, and a USER found it, not the check. It now
  also requires no two book nodes anywhere in a nikāya to share a title, and —
  added 2026-07-26v for the reprint defect above — **no two ADJACENT SIBLINGS
  anywhere in any tree may share a label** (10,972 rows checked). A label
  repeated NON-adjacently is left alone: the edition really does make a second
  and third pass over the same tikas or dukas, and those passes are not
  contiguous, so each needs its own node. The two adjacent repeats that ARE the
  edition's own are NAMED in the file, not admitted by widening the rule.
* **A WORK PRINTED IN SEVERAL BHĀGAS GETS ONE NODE PER BHĀGA, labelled as the
  edition labels it** ("Jātakapāḷi (Paṭhamo bhāgo)", "Paṭṭhānapāḷi (Catuttho
  bhāgo)") — read off that volume's own title page, never invented. Every row
  then lies inside ONE volume and so opens a reading pane instead of only
  expanding, which is the standing `render()` limitation.
* **A nav row that opens nothing, or opens its parent's whole text, is a SPAN
  bug, not a data bug.** THREE shapes have now shipped: a node whose NEIGHBOUR
  shares its ordinal, a node keyed the same as its parent, and a LAST CHILD
  that inherits a parent end EQUAL TO ITS OWN START (found on 28Khu11 by the
  row sweep; fixed with `if(en!=null && en<=st) en=st+1`). `_nettiverify.js`
  and `_milindaverify.js` click every row of their volume; do the same for a
  new one — it is the only thing that finds this class.
* **Some checkers now take an argument so they fit a short command budget:**
  `_khu01verify.js <book>…` and `_milindaverify.js data|rows [from to]`. With
  no argument both run everything. Run in parts, an assertion about a book that
  part did not render WILL fail — read the parts together.
* **A 0/0/0/0 means no BODY TEXT is missing, duplicated or spliced. It says
  nothing about the apparatus, and nothing about whether the page LOOKS right.**
* **`pipeline/scout_volume.py` BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE on a new volume** —
  `extent` (where the text really is), `corpus` (n-runs, resets, book field),
  `geometry` (the page's shape and whether any display line carries a comma),
  `pair` (WHERE the printed stream and the corpus differ, by page), `page`.
  Added 2026-07-26ae after the same measurements had been hand-rolled as
  session scratch three times.
* **THE PDF DECLARES ITS OWN TEXT EXTENT — read it, don't guess it, AND DO
  NOT TRUST IT BLINDLY.** `verify_all_volumes.declared_range(vol)`, from the
  `Subject` metadata, for 116 of 118 volumes; validated against all eleven
  hand-measured Khuddaka ranges. **!!! 33Abhi05 IS THE FIRST VOLUME WHERE IT IS
  WRONG** — it declares "content 10 + text 265" but the front matter is ELEVEN
  pages (1-based p11 carries the roman folio "viii"), so the whole range is
  shifted by one and the volume's real extent is 0-based `11 275`. The declared
  LENGTH was right; the offset was not. **CHECK THE FOLIO, not just the
  figure** — and check BOTH ENDS: the first read of this volume corrected the
  head and left the tail, which cost the Saccayamaka its last printed unit.
  `page_range()` now prefers `build_khu_volume.SPEC`'s measured extent where
  the volume has one (2026-07-26ac); the two agree on nineteen of twenty.
* **BOTH SWEEP CACHES WERE EXISTENCE-ONLY UNTIL 2026-07-26y** — no mtime check
  at all, in `verify_all_volumes.py` (whose docstring claimed otherwise) and in
  `verify_apparatus.py --all` (whose cache path was hardcoded to
  `/tmp/osbct/appcache` and was found holding 118 entries from an earlier
  session). Both now invalidate an entry when any input it depends on is newer,
  and both take `--cache DIR`. A no-argument invocation still rewrites the
  report from whatever the default cache holds, so pass `--cache` and read the
  count.

**Governing lesson.** Side-maps built by splitting the corpus text inherit every corpus defect. Build them from `pdftotext -layout` of the printed edition and map onto corpus ordinals; never edit the corpus. `pipeline/build_19khu02.py` (whole volume, four books) and `pipeline/build_suttanipata.py` (one book) are the worked templates.

**A second lesson, from 19Khu02.** Two checks that share an input are ONE check. Both "independent" confirmations of that volume's book boundaries read the corpus `book` field, and both were wrong the same way. Before calling something confirmed two ways, name the two inputs.

**Page numbers: `pdf_page` is NOT a pdftotext index, and its offset is not the same in every volume.** Use `vr.page_offset(vol)`, which measures it. The harness's own `<p0> <p1>` arguments ARE 0-based `\f` indices — 19Khu02's text is pages 17-451 printed, so pass `16 450`.

## THE PAGE INDEX WAS STALE, THE SIGLUM PARSER WAS CAPPED AT SEVEN CHARACTERS, AND THE COMMENTARY AND ṬĪKĀ MAPS ARE NOW COMPLETE (2026-07-30i)

Full write-up in `claude/pageindex_stale_and_xc_maps_completed.md`.

### What was asked, and what was actually in the way

The task was to extend `XC_COMM` to the Khuddaka commentaries using
`concordanciatextos.pdf`. Two things had to be fixed first, both defects in
already-shipped work.

**1. `site/reader/pageindex.json` predated the volume rebuilds.** Dated
2026-07-23; the volumes were rebuilt on the 27th-29th and the page audit of
2026-07-29t rewrote `printed` in all 118. 65 volumes disagreed. Of 28,263
resolving xrefs, **3,774 landed on the wrong printed page and none on the
right one.** The rebuilt index is self-checked: 29,581/29,581 entries point at
a paragraph carrying that page. This also made the mapping verification usable
at all — before the rebuild, `Jātaka-Ṭṭha` scored 59.6% on the page-range test
and `Khuddakapāṭha-Ṭṭha` 40.9%, purely because the index was missing those
volumes' front pages. After: 100% and 100%.

**2. The parser dropped every siglum longer than seven characters** — 1,995
citations, more than the entire 1,810 "unresolved" residue that this task was
scoped against. See the START HERE block.

### The mapping, and how it was checked

Volume numbers are the edition's own: `concordanciatextos.pdf`, aṭṭhakathā
column 20-52 and ṭīkā column 1-26, cross-checked against each volume's own
title page, where the bhāga names the part (`Jātakaṭṭhakathā (Sattamo bhāgo)`
= 42KhuA23). Then verified twice more, because a printed table can be misread:

* **Page-range fit** — every cited page must fall inside the target volume's
  printed page range. 100% on 14 of 19 commentary works; 99.4% Netti, 99.3%
  Kaṅkhā, 99.8% Visuddhi, 97.5% Itivuttaka, 86% Cariyāpiṭaka. **Every miss is a
  parse artefact** (`Cariyā-Ṭṭha 9, 324` read as vol 9) and every one of them
  **fails safe to the grey span shown today**.
* **Lemma on the cited page, against a control** — the citing note's own lemma
  should occur on the cited page of the right volume and not of a wrong one.
  **35% hit against 1% for a control volume of the same layer** (573 citations
  with a usable lemma). The control near zero is what gives the test power.

### The maps

| map | what it holds |
|---|---|

## THE CENTRED GATE WAS PARTLY BLIND IN SIX VOLUMES — AND I DESTROYED nav.json FINDING OUT (2026-07-30e)

### !!! FIRST, THE DAMAGE, AND IT WAS MINE

A read-only probe (`_tika/cmin_sweep.py`) imported every `build_*_nav.py` to read its
`SPEC`. **`pipeline/build_nav.py` has no `main()` and no `if __name__` guard — its whole
body is module-level — so importing it REBUILT `site/reader/nav.json` from scratch**,
replacing 2.16 MB and **28,612 gated tree rows with 0.53 MB and none**, and printing a
cheerful `wrote nav.json 519 KB` while it did so.

**THIS WAS THE SECOND TIME.** `site/reader/nav.json.damaged_by_29probe` (527,683 bytes,
2026-07-29) is the same file destroyed the same way by the same kind of probe.

Recovered in full: `nav.json.bak26vsmt02` (the last pre-image, 12:01) + one re-run of
`build_lasttika_nav.py 26VsmT02 --write`. Verified **138 volumes, 28,722 tree rows,
`_navdup` PASS** — the count is 110 higher than the backup because the backup predates the
26VsmT02 node it was taken before. The damaged file is kept as
`nav.json.damaged_by_cminsweep`.

**FIXED SO IT CANNOT RECUR:** `build_nav.py` now REFUSES TO BE IMPORTED —

```python
if __name__ != '__main__':
    raise ImportError('build_nav.py is a SCRIPT: importing it rewrites '
                      'site/reader/nav.json and drops every gated tree...')
```

and `cmin_sweep.py` no longer imports anything that writes: it `ast.parse`s each builder,
**strips every top-level bare CALL** (which is exactly the `A.main()` / `main()` at the
foot of each file, the only thing in them that writes) and execs the rest. Assignments and
defs still run, so the SPEC comes out complete.

### THE FINDING ITSELF

`matika_lines` reads a centred mātikā line as one indented **at least 18 spaces**. A
centred line's indent is a function of its LENGTH — a long group head centres further
LEFT — so the reader was skipping long ones entirely. `centred_indent` already existed for
this and the five Vinaya canon volumes already declare 14; nobody had swept for the rest.

Measured against each volume's OWN declared indent (the first run of the sweep compared
against the bare 18 and overstated the loss — 8 volumes, 20 heads):

```
volume     builder                            centred seen -> at 12
17AnA01    build_anguttara_atthakatha_nav.py       6 ->   7
19AnT02    build_anguttara_tika_nav.py            19 ->  22    (three pair-lines)
15SamA02   build_samyutta_atthakatha_nav.py       47 ->  48
16SamA03   build_samyutta_atthakatha_nav.py       73 ->  77
14Sam03    build_samyutta_nav.py                  99 -> 104
52Vism02   build_vism_nav.py                       9 ->  12
```

**Six volumes, 17 printed group heads the gate never saw.** A gate that cannot see an entry
cannot refuse it — 2026-07-29's lesson (*"a gate that finds nothing is indistinguishable
from a gate that passes"*) in a new place.

### AND THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION IT RAISES: NO READER HOLE

The tree is built from the BODY's headings; the mātikā only checks it. So each of the 17
was resolved separately against `nav.json` and `sections/` (`_tika/cmin_reach.py`):
**15 of 17 were in the tree all along.** The two that were not are both non-sections:

* `17AnA01` `Ekakanipāta Aṅguttaraṭṭhakathā` — **the mātikā's own title line**, printed
  ONCE in the whole file, over the mātikā itself. `matika_drop`.
* `14Sam03` `10. Cattuttha-āmakadhaññapeyyālavagga` — **the edition's own slip**. The body
  heads `10. Catuttha-` and closes it `Catuttha-āmakadhaññapeyyālavaggo dasamo.`;
  `Cattuttha-` occurs once, in the mātikā. Two witnesses against one. Added to that
  volume's existing `errata` map — which already carried FOUR centred errata, so this is a
  fifth of the same kind — and to `data/errata.json` as **E067**, 57 → **58**.

All six now declare `centred_indent: 12` (where the count stabilises; **no dotted entry
leaks in** — checked on every volume that declares a mātikā range) and all six gates pass
seeing everything: 6/6, 16/16, 38/38, 76/76, **94/94**, 12/12. Nodes rewritten, `_navdup`
PASS, BUILD **`1b6ead6ab910`**.

## THE CORPORA ARE CLEAN — 38 GLYPH SUBSTITUTIONS IN 27 VOLUMES, AND A VERDICT OVERTURNED (2026-07-30d)

`_charcensus/census.py` over all 118 corpora now returns:

```
distinct 0 | occurrences 0 | volumes touched 0
```

It returned 89 places in 49 volumes this morning. Nothing was guessed to get there.

### !!! THE REGISTER'S OWN VERDICT ON ITS THREE HARDEST CLASSES WAS WRONG

This is the finding, and it is worth more than the fixes. The register had written off
`Ù`, `ò` and `−` — 29 of the 89 places — because it had asked *what does this character
stand for* and got no consistent answer:

| class | the verdict this project published | what is true |
|---|---|---|
| `Ù` | MIXED — do not apply without a page check | a NEIGHBOURHOOD fault; settled |
| `ò` | MIXED — do not apply without a page check | a NEIGHBOURHOOD fault; settled |
| `−` | *"a substitution table cannot repair this; the passages must be reset from the page"* | repairable at WORD level, with witnesses up to 112 volumes |

**The character was never the whole fault.** Where the vowel degraded, the retroflex or the
doubled stop beside it degraded with it — so a single-character substitution produces a word
that does not exist, and looks like evidence that the class is unresolvable:

```
vòṭthānasammutiṁ -> vuṭthānasammutiṁ    0 volumes   <- ò->u alone
                 -> vuṭṭhānasammutiṁ    1 volume    <- ò->u AND ṭth->ṭṭh
patÙmaṇḍitaṁ     -> patimaṇḍitaṁ        0 volumes   <- Ù->i alone
                 -> paṭimaṇḍitaṁ       18 volumes   <- Ù->i AND t->ṭ
```

Read as a WORD instead, the `−` class — the one declared unfixable — is the best-witnessed
of all: `ñāṇaṁ` in **112** of 118 volumes, `ārammaṇaṁ` **97**, `viññāṇaṁ` **96**,
`daṭṭhabbo` **89**, `akaraṇato` **69**, `māṇavo` **69**. Twelve of the fourteen corpus
places are witnessed outright; the other two by their halves (`padaṭṭhāna` 57 +
`kāraṇattā` 46; `ārammaṇādhipatipaccaya` 6).

### THE METHOD: THE CORPUS IS ITS OWN LEXICON

The decisive test for a proposed emendation is **how many of the 118 volumes print the
emended word**. This is not a dictionary — the project instructions bar a lexicon as a
source of analysis — it is the edition being asked about its own usage. A reading printed
in 112 volumes is not a conjecture. A reading printed in 0 is refuted, however plausible
the character substitution behind it looked.

`_charcensus/propose.py` derives the candidate and reports the witness count. It does not
apply anything.

### WHAT WAS APPLIED

`_charcensus/apply_fixes.py --write` — a **declared table of 38 rows**, each
`(volume, from, to, witness, min_volumes)`, which **refuses on any mismatch**. 38
substitutions in 27 volumes; 162 of 182 register sightings now carry `apply_from`/`apply_to`.

Dissenting places were applied as they read, not as the majority reads:
`Aòjalī`→`Añjalī` (20Khu03, a proper name in an uddāna) is ñ where the class is u;
`PavesanapavÙṭtha`→`…pavuṭṭha…` (07ViT07) is u where the class is i; 22Khu05's `(Sī, Ù)`
was left alone, because it is a **variant siglum and not a letter**.

Also settled: `⎯` (U+23AF) → `–` in 04Vin04, on the count that the volume prints `–` 216
times and `⎯` twice; and `é`, which was MIXED for the right reason and the wrong
conclusion — two places, two readings, two fixes (`passémi`→`passāmi` 07Di02,
`viharāmé`→`viharāmi` 15An01).

### THE 20 UNAPPLIED SIGHTINGS ARE NOT OPEN FAULTS

17 are PDF-text-layer sightings of matter **the corpus never carried** — `¥` ×8 (all-capital
title lines), the combining-dot places ×7 (NFC, not a wrong glyph), `−` ×1, `Ù` ×1
(02Vin02's `PiÙṭhaṅkā`, in a word index). 3 are **SUBSUMED**: `buddhañān−ṁ` is broken across
a line in the printed text layer, so the builder rightly refused the declaration — and the
shorter `ñān−ṁ`→`ñāṇaṁ` row repairs the place anyway, because it is a substring. Corpus
verified: 18AnT01 reads `buddhañāṇaṁ`, and carries no U+2212 at all.

`register.py` now DERIVES the applied count from the entries rather than believing the
proposal's own `applied` field. That correction alone moved the published figure from
**165** to **162** — the earlier number was generated before the three subsumed rows were
cleared, and it flattered the work by three.

### !!! THE REGRESSION HARNESS NEEDED A NAMED EXEMPTION, AND WHY THAT IS HONEST

`pipeline/regress.py` compares against the baseline builder
`build_khu_volume.py.preniddesa`, which contains **0** occurrences of `GLYPH_ERRATA` — it
has no register mechanism at all and can never reproduce an applied glyph fix. Re-baselining
fixed 26Khu09; it could not fix 20Khu03, whose uddāna and verse maps carry
`Aòjalī`→`Añjalī`. Rather than weaken the comparison, two named exemptions were added:

```python
EXEMPT = {('20Khu03', 'uddana'): 'applied glyph erratum Aòjalī -> Añjalī; '
                                 'the baseline builder has no register',
          ('20Khu03', 'verse'):  'same place, same reason'}
```

`regress check` prints `EXEMPT …` on every run and reports `53/55 … 2 exempt (named above)
[OK]`. **An exemption that is printed is a different thing from a test that was loosened.**

* body gate 18AnT01 8/6/16 (the known hyphen class), 19AnT02 0/1/0/0 (the declared splice)
* all 27 touched volumes' side-maps rebuilt, every one `[OK]`

and verified identical on paragraph count, character count and page range; one paragraph

**The pre-image directory is `_fnprobe/corpus_pre/`.** Use `&&`, and check the directory first.

### !!! A HEADING IS NEVER A QUESTION

`kat_is_head` under `heads_by_form` asks for a capital, six words or fewer, no comma and no terminal
stop — and a QUESTION MARK is not a terminal stop. The edition quotes catechetical prose at a
display indent, and three such lines were shipped as headings:

```
19AnT02 p295   Katamo ca puggalo dhammappamāṇo dhammappasanno?      (Puggalapaññatti, quoted)
02ViT02 x2     Tattha katamaṁ kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṁ?  (Vibhaṅga, quoted)
```

Measured over every shipped side-map that holds headings: **exactly three entries anywhere end in
`?`, and all three are these.** So the rule takes nothing else. 02ViT02 rebuilt: body gate
5/4/10/0 -> **4/4/8/0**.

### !!! AND A FALSE COLOPHON CLASS THAT REACHED TWENTY-FIVE SHIPPED VOLUMES

`kat_is_colo`'s form (1) accepts an **unindented** line when `NIDCOLO` and `NIDSECT` both hit — the
words being "decisive on their own". Both are SUBSTRING searches, and both can land inside ordinary
words. 19AnT02 p170 sets the body line

```
samudāyo samāsattho. Chaṭṭhakāmāvacaradevaggahaṇaṁ paccāsattinayena.
```

— `chaṭṭh` opens *Chaṭṭhakāmāvacara…*, `vagg` sits inside *de-**vagg**-ahaṇaṁ* — four words, a
terminal stop, no comma. It was pulled out of ord168 and rendered as an **uddāna block at the foot
of the sutta**, 20 render parts below where it belongs. Found by the body gate's MISSING-CHUNK arm,
which is the only arm that could: every printed LINE was present.

Swept over all 94 `heads_by_form` volumes (`_tika/colofallback.py`, `_tika/colofallback2.py`): **85
lines are claimed by that unindented arm. 46 of them open with a LOWERCASE letter**, which makes
them the continuation of a wrapped body line — a colophon names a section and is always capitalised,
so no real one can be there. Guarded, and every one of the 46 verified back into the body
(`_tika/colomoved2.py`: 46 contiguous in the render, 0 in any uddāna block). **25 volumes move**:

## THE PAGE LINK WAS WRONG ON 40 VOLUMES, AND THE GANTHĀRAMBHA WAS DRAWN NOWHERE (2026-07-29t)

All user-reported, from two screenshots. Four defects, one feature, and one that had already been
fixed earlier the same day without anyone noticing why.

### !!! THE `printed` LABEL WAS RIGHT EVERYWHERE; THE PDF LINK WAS NOT

`reader2.html` wrote `<a href="…/<VOL>.pdf#page={pdf_page}">p.{printed}</a>`. `pdf_page` is the
index among NON-BLANK pages (2026-07-29p), not the index in the file, so the anchor is short by
the number of blanks above it.

`_tika/pageaudit.py` reads the running header of the page each paragraph claims and compares,
over every volume: **78 exact, 40 with a wrong link, 0 with a wrong `printed`.** Worst 40Abhi12
**+11**, 19AnA03 +6, 24AbhiT03 +5, 18Khu01 +5. So `p.52` was the right number and it opened the
wrong leaf — exactly what was reported.

**Fixed without touching the corpus**, which is the 2026-07-29q decision.
`pipeline/build_pdfblanks.py` writes `site/reader/pdfblanks.json` (67 volumes, 2 KB) and both
readers add the blanks back in `truePdfPage()`. **Verified**: the reader's formula reproduces
the independently measured true page on 170 of 170 sampled paragraphs across 40Abhi12, 05ViT05,
13MaT01 and 08DiT01.

### THE PAGE RULE, IN ALL 118 BOOKS

Requested from buddha-dhamma.net's older `reader.html`, which draws `── page N ⧉ ──` whenever
the printed page changes. Now in `reader2.html` too, emitted inside `block()` — the one place
the columns, single and tabs paths all go through — and tracked **per volume**, because in the
columns view three volumes' blocks interleave and one shared counter would make each suppress
the others' page turns. `check_layout.js` over canon, commentary and ṭīkā: **0 layout issues.**

### ...AND THE BADGE NOW CARRIES THE RANGE, BECAUSE ONE PARAGRAPH CAN SPAN 50 PRINTED PAGES

In the canon a paragraph is 0.4 printed pages long and `p.N` says everything. In the Ṭīkā it does
not: **08DiT01 ord12 runs from printed p.62 to p.111**, and a badge reading `p.62` swallows
forty-nine pages. `pipeline/build_pagespan.py` measures each paragraph's LAST page by locating
its closing words in the printed text and writes `pagespan.json` — **17,106 paragraphs in 114
volumes**, and the badge reads `p.62–111`.

It is self-checking three ways and **leaves a paragraph out rather than guess**: the closing
words must occur on exactly one page at or after the paragraph's own start, that page must not
precede the start, and it must not pass the next paragraph's start. 4,246 fall out and keep their
single-page badge, which is never wrong. Two things it had to learn: the tail is tried at three
lengths because the last 60 characters can straddle the page break itself, and a page whose
header carries no readable folio takes its number from the nearest page that has one — 06Di01
went from 142 unresolved to 3, the Ṭīkā to 0 and 1.

### FOUR VOLUMES DREW THEIR OWN NAME TWICE IN THE SIDEBAR

`build_abhidhamma_nav` wraps a volume's tops in a book node so a BHĀGA can carry its work's plain
name under the bhāga label — `Mūlapaṇṇāsaṭīkā` under `Mūlapaṇṇāsaṭīkā (Dutiyo bhāgo)`. Where the
two names are the SAME the sidebar drew the name twice, one nested under the other:
**14Sam03, 08DiT01, 11DiT04, 12DiT05.** Collapsed in the READER, because it is a display
question, and safe to collapse only because the wrapper's key is the node's own `first` in all

### !!! WHY THE GANTHĀRAMBHA OPENED AT UNIT 3 ON PRINTED PAGE 52

The reported symptom: clicking `Ganthārambhakathāvaṇṇanā` showed the Pāḷi from unit 3, not from
page 1. The cause is nameable and it was already gone by the time it was asked about.

**A LINK THAT POINTS AT A HIDDEN ORDINAL RENDERS NOTHING.** `targetsFor()` filters targets whose
volume hides them (2026-07-27af). Before today, canon `06Di01#0` pointed at `08DiT01#0` — the
volume's TITLE LINE `Sīlakkhandhavaggaṭīkā`, which the build hides — so that block drew empty and
the first ṭīkā the reader could draw was unit 3, on printed p52. **Fifty-one printed pages of the
Ganthārambha and Nidāna were in no page of the site.**

The Dīgha rebuild of 2026-07-29r fixed it as a side effect: the corpus now starts at printed p1
instead of p34, and `_tika/relink_tika.py`'s pass 2 placed ord2-ord5 under `06Di01#0` with ord6
direct. Measured before/after from the session backup:

```
BEFORE  06Di01#0 -> ['08DiT01#0']                                   (hidden — drew nothing)
NOW     06Di01#0 -> ['08DiT01#2','#3','#4','#5','#6']               (printed pp1-34)
```

**The general case was then swept.** 2,422 canon paragraphs still have their WHOLE commentary or
ṭīkā block on hidden ordinals — 38Abhi10 1,052, 39Abhi11 531, 37Abhi09 354, 40Abhi12 341,
36Abhi08 144, all pointing into 50AbhiA03 and its neighbours. **No Ṭīkā volume is affected any
more.** This is the same 2,432 the link-rebuild note has carried since 2026-07-29o, now located.

### !!! AND THE CACHE-BUSTER WAS A HAND-TYPED CONSTANT THAT NOBODY BUMPED

Reported as "Ganthārambhakathāvaṇṇanā still starts on page 52" AFTER the fix had shipped. The
reader was new; the data it loaded was not. **The header gave it away — `08DiT01 · 303 ¶` where
the rebuilt volume has 315.**

`jget()` fetches every JSON as `url + '?v=' + BUILD`, and `BUILD` was
`'2026-07-28u-frontscroll'`, last touched by hand on 2026-07-28u. **Every data change since then
kept the same URL**, so a returning browser served the previous build's corpus indefinitely: all
seven Vinaya Ṭīkā, all five Dīgha, all three Majjhima, every relink, every apparatus rebuild,
`pdfblanks.json` and `pagespan.json`. And `reader.html`, `search.html`, `errata.html` and
`downloads.html` had **no cache-buster at all** — every fetch a bare URL.

`pipeline/stamp_build.py` DERIVES the stamp from the data: it hashes the name, size and mtime of
all 1,609 JSON files under `site/` and rewrites `BUILD` in all five pages. Any rebuild moves it
and **no rebuild can fail to**. A fresh checkout moves the mtimes and so moves the stamp once,
which costs one cache miss and is the safe direction to err in. **Run it LAST, after every
builder and before deploying.**

### NEW FILES

```
_tika/pageaudit.py            does the page link open the right leaf?  118 volumes
pipeline/build_pdfblanks.py   -> site/reader/pdfblanks.json   the blanks to add back
pipeline/build_pagespan.py    -> site/reader/pagespan.json    each paragraph's LAST printed page
pipeline/stamp_build.py       rewrites BUILD in all five pages from the data's own hash
```

Reported again once the first fix shipped: `Mūlapaṇṇāsaṭīkā I` with `Mūlapaṇṇāsaṭīkā` nested

10DiT03, 11DiT04, 12DiT05, 13MaT01, 14MaT02** — and the wrapper's key is the node's own `first`
in all ten, so nothing becomes unreachable.

### !!! THE EDITION SETS ONE UNIT NUMBER ALONE ON ITS OWN LINE, FLUSH RIGHT

15MaT03 printed p13:

```
    4                           Majjhimanikāya
                                                                        3.
    Kārakabhāvanti paṭipattiyaṁ paṭipajjanakabhāvaṁ. Mayampi nāma gihī
```

The `3.` stands at **indent 79** and its unit's first words begin on the NEXT line at indent 0.
The numbered rule wants `N.` and its text on one line, so **the extraction saw no unit there at
all** and the whole of unit 3 arrived inside the paragraph carrying n=2. The printed side does
see it, which is how the 1:1 count found it: **333 printed against 332 corpus**. 36Abhi08's
class — `41.Nevavipāka…` with no space — reached from the other side, and `kat_splices` answers
it. The declaration verifies itself: it refuses unless the host really carries n=2, really

### THREE DEFECTS IN THE MACHINERY, ALL FOUND BY BUILDING

**1. `head_build` CRASHED ON A `unit` ITEM IN THE RESIDUE.** A `unit` item carries its number in
`it[1]` and its text in `it[2]`, so `txt` is an INT there. The key already read `it[2]`; the
residue branch did not, and 07ViT07 — the first `heads` book whose printed stream holds numbered
units the corpus does not — raised `'int' object has no attribute 'strip'`. 05Kankha and
36KhuA17 never reached it because every one of their units is located. **Fixed and MEASURED:
both of those volumes rebuild BYTE-IDENTICAL on all five side-maps, 12/12 files**, and
`pipeline/regress.py check` is **55/55 across 11 volumes**.

**2. NOTHING COULD CREATE A `booktitle` MAP FOR A VOLUME WITH NO NAV NODE.**
`build_booktitles.py` anchors a book's first ordinal from `nav.json`; `build_khu_volume.py`'s
own derivation only RE-ANCHORS a map that already exists (`if os.path.exists(_bt)`). New file
`_tika/booktitles_tika.py` reads the stacks off the printed title pages with the builder's own
walk, anchors each on the book's first NON-HIDDEN ordinal, and **REFUSES if the map already
exists**. It also learned one thing: **a book need not open on a title page** — 01ViT01,
04ViT04 and 06ViT06 seam mid-page, `Verañjakaṇḍavaṇṇanā` being a centred head at the top of an
ordinary text page — so a stack that overruns is accepted as the head line alone, and ONLY when
that line is the book's own SPEC title.

**3. THE LEAK TEST FLAGGED THREE REAL UNITS IN 03ViT03.** New probe `_tika/unitdiff.py` walks
the printed numbered stream against the corpus `n` stream 1:1: books 0, 2 and 4 agree **number
for number**, 173/173, 210/210, 74/74, with no divergence anywhere — so hiding any of the three
takes an ordinal the printed side still emits a unit for. `leak_keep: (145, 433, 607)`.
ord145 `10. Chandaṁ adatvā gamanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā` IS a heading, but a NUMBERED one at indent
14, and `kat_items`' numbered rule takes precedence over the generic form test — **so the
PRINTED side reads it as unit 10 too.** Both sides are consistent, the role is wrong on both,
and it is recorded rather than corrected.

## THE VINAYA ṬĪKĀ SEAM FOUND, THE SEVEN REBUILT — AND `pdf_page` DRIFTS IN 40 SHIPPED VOLUMES (2026-07-29p)

### THE SEAM IS A PROPERTY OF THE WORK'S FIRST VOLUME, AND THE OLD EXPECTATION WAS WRONG

02ViT02-06ViT06 were measured the way 2026-07-29n asked: where the first numbered unit falls
against the extent, then the pages around it read. The result **refutes** the standing
expectation that 02ViT02 and 03ViT03 carry 01ViT01's `heads`/`katha` seam.

```
                     first anchor   pages before it        books
01ViT01  16-475      p209/210        194  (42%)            heads p16-209  | katha p210-475
02ViT02  10-457      p12               2  ( 0%)            katha p10-457
03ViT03  22-517      p23               1  ( 0%)            katha p22-517
04ViT04  10-371      p76              66  (18%)            heads p10-47   | katha p48-371
05ViT05  19-340      p20               1  ( 0%)            katha p19-340
06ViT06  28-612      p71              43  ( 7%)            heads p28-56   | katha p57-612
07ViT07  22-510      --                --                  heads p22-139  | heads p140-510
```

**The reason is nameable.** The Ganthārambhakathā + Bāhiranidānakathā prelude opens a WORK. It
therefore stands in that work's FIRST volume only: 01ViT01 (Sāratthadīpanī I), 04ViT04
(Vimativinodanī I) and 06ViT06 (Vajirabuddhiṭīkā, one volume for the whole work) have it;
02ViT02, 03ViT03 and 05ViT05 are dutiya-/tatiyabhāga and open straight into commentary.

**!!! AND THE SEAM IS NOT THE FIRST NUMBERED ANCHOR.** On 04ViT04 the Bāhiranidāna closes on
p47 and `Verañjakaṇḍavaṇṇanā` is a centred head on p48, but the numbered stream does not begin
until **p76** — 28 pages later, and it opens at `2.`, not `1.`. On 06ViT06 the same shape:
seam p57, first anchor p71. Both shipped corpora began at **exactly that first anchor** (p76
and p71), which is all `extract.py` could see. Checked against each volume's own printed
mātikā: 04ViT04's `Verañjakaṇḍavaṇṇanā` group opens before its first child
`Paṭhamajjhānakathāvaṇṇanā` at printed 71 = pdf p80, and the Bāhiranidāna's last child
`Ācariyaparamparakathāvaṇṇanā` is printed 32 = pdf p41.

The extents are hand-measured at both ends in `_tika/EXTENTS.md`; the seams, the book heads and
the numbering resets are in `_tika/VINAYA_TIKA_SEAMS.md`.

### THE READERS ARE A SPEC QUESTION, NOT A REBUILD ONE

`_khua/rebuild.py` takes `<VOL> <LO> <HI>` and nothing else. The reader name (`heads`/`katha`/
`verse`/`niddesa`) is not one of its inputs — `rebuild_corpus.py` always restores unnumbered
prose and always bounds it by the printed headings, and `derive()` keys each paragraph by its
INDEX (`VOL#i`), never by its unit number. So the seam feeds the **SPEC**, step 6, and a
volume whose unit numbering overlaps itself cannot collide in the corpus.

### THE SEVEN REBUILT, AND FOUR OF THEM KEPT THE WORD INDEX ON THE FIRST PASS

```
          shipped        rebuilt   pdf_page       lost   back matter left
01ViT01     23 ¶  ->        45 ¶   15..474   mono   0    0
02ViT02    314 ¶  ->       344 ¶   10..457   mono   0    0
03ViT03    648 ¶  ->       671 ¶   22..515   mono   0    0
04ViT04    280 ¶  ->       302 ¶   10..371   mono   0    0

06ViT06    814 ¶  ->       860 ¶   28..609   mono   0    0
07ViT07     22 ¶  ->       420 ¶   22..508   mono   0    0
```

`lost` is shipped paragraphs whose text is not in the rebuilt corpus: **0 on all seven.** Every
corpus now reaches its volume's own closing colophon — in `text` or, where the extractor
classifies it as one, in `headings` (`_seam/ends2.py`, no `ABSENT`). Character census over all
seven: **clean**, one residual `Ù` in 07ViT07, a known-unsettleable place from 2026-07-29l, not
new. Coverage 0.970-1.015 (below).

**The first pass was wrong on four of them and the cause is the next section.** With the trim
given the TRUE extent, 01ViT01 kept 2 index paragraphs (1,319 ch), 03ViT03 2 (4,043), 05ViT05
3 (5,937) and 06ViT06 5 (2,820) — **and 01ViT01 lost its first body page**, because the same

### !!! `extract.py` NUMBERS `pdf_page` AFTER DROPPING BLANK PAGES, AND 40 OF 118 SHIPPED VOLUMES ARE WRONG

```python
pgs=[p for p in (split_page(x) for x in raw_pages(pdf)) if p]   # blanks dropped HERE
for i,p in enumerate(pgs,1): p['pdf_page']=i                     # numbered AFTER
```

`pdf_page` is therefore not the PDF's page index but the index among NON-BLANK pages, and every
blank verso shifts every later page down by one.

**Measured, not inferred.** `_seam/offsetsweep.py` takes 13 paragraphs spread through each
SHIPPED corpus and locates each one in the PDF by its own opening words, skipping any probe
that is ambiguous rather than guessing. Over all 118:

```
78 volumes exact      40 volumes WRONG
40Abhi12 +11   19AnA03 +6   24AbhiT03 +4   18Khu01 +4   05ViT05 +3
05Kankha +2 and thirteen more at +2      twenty at +1
```

34Abhi06, which has no blank page at all, returns +0 on all 13 probes — the clean control that
says the method is measuring the defect and not itself.

**The blanks are the versos the edition sets before a new book**, so the drift is worst in
exactly the multi-work volumes and it lands at the seams. This is also why 07ViT07's rebuild
recorded `pdf_page 22..508` for a body that ends on p510 (2026-07-29o): the corpus content was
right and the page number was two short.

**IT IS NOT FIXED.** The fix is one line, but it moves `pdf_page` on 40 shipped volumes whose
SPEC page ranges, nav and `sections/` maps are all keyed to the present numbers, and those
volumes are gated against the current state. **That is the user's decision, not mine.** Until
it is taken, convert any true page range before using it as a trim or a gate bound:
`python3 _seam/trimbounds.py <VOL>:<LO>:<HI>`.

### THE COVERAGE RATIO MEASURE IS FIXED, AND THE SEVEN SCREEN CLEAN

2026-07-29o named the cause — the printed-side measure cut each page at the first line
beginning `___`, and the edition also prints a short decorative rule between vaṇṇanā sections
— but left the measure alone. `_seam/ratio2.py` now requires a rule of **>=40 characters** and
takes the **LAST** one on the page, so a decorative rule mid-page cannot end the body.

```

          05ViT05 0.970  06ViT06 0.987  07ViT07 0.995      (was 1.204)
controls  29KhuA10 0.997  34Abhi06 1.005  35KhuA16 1.011  51Vism01 1.045
```

## THE BRACKET COLOUR FOLLOWED THE RENDER SLOT, NOT THE LAYER — 40 VOLUMES DREW THE PĀḶI GOLD (2026-07-29o)

**Reported by the user from the reader, not by any gate.** A commentary or ṭīkā
volume opened from the Contents tree drew its paragraph bracket, its paragraph
number and its verse numbers in `--canon` gold — the Pāḷi colour — instead of
`--comm` teal / `--tika` purple. The P/A/T layer chips were right; only the text
was mis-coloured.

**Cause.** `openKey()` resolves a non-canon paragraph to its canon counterpart
through the reverse map. Where the clicked paragraph has none, it falls back to
rendering that volume STANDALONE, and it does so by setting `kind='canon'`
(reader2.html:510) — the render slot, not the layer. `block()` then took its
class from `kind`: `'para'+(kind==='canon'?' canon':' l-'+kind)`. So every
paragraph of a standalone-rendered commentary came out `.para.canon`.

**Fix.** Colour follows the VOLUME'S LAYER, never the render slot. `block()` now
derives `lk = LAYERKIND[VOLLAYER[vol]] || kind` and uses `lk` for the bracket
class, the paragraph number (`pn k-*`) and the two verse-number sites.
`uddanaHTML()` — which hardcoded `class="para canon pali"` and `pn k-canon` for
every restored `plain` block — takes the layer kind as a second argument. And
`.rowline.hot .para` reset `border-color` on all four sides while only `.canon`
put its own back, so an A/T bracket went grey under the cursor; `l-A`/`l-T` rules
added. Seven edits, `site/reader/reader2.html`, backup `.bak_bracketcol`.

**Extent, measured before and after** (`_tika/bracketsweep.js`, which opens every
non-canon volume the way the tree does and counts bracket classes). Over the 101
non-canon nav entries:

| | volumes drawing a canon bracket |
|---|---|
| BEFORE | **44 entries / 40 distinct volumes** — 01VinA01, 04VinA04, 05Kankha, 06VinSg06, 07DiA01, 10MaA01, 11MaA02, 17AnA01, 23KhuA04, 43KhuA24, 44KhuA25, 46KhuA27, 47KhuA28, 48AbhiA01, 49AbhiA02, 50AbhiA03, 51Vism01, 52Vism02, 03ViT03, 04ViT04, 05ViT05, 06ViT06, 07ViT07, 09DiT02, 10DiT03, 16SaT01, 18AnT01, 22AbhiT01, 24AbhiT03, 25VsmT01, 26VsmT02 |
| AFTER | **0** |

07DiA01 alone went 330 `.para.canon` → 330 `.para.l-A`. The rest of the layer —
volumes whose paragraphs DO resolve to a canon counterpart — was already right,
which is why nothing flagged: the gates assert content and role, never colour.

**Not a regression:** `check_layout.js` returns the same verdict on 18Khu01,
09Ma01, 06Di01, 07DiA01, 50AbhiA03 (PARTIAL 76%, pre-existing) and 51Vism01
(REFUSING — no reverse map, pre-existing, identical on the backup).

**Open:** no gate asserts colour. `check_layout.js` already knows
`LAYERSEL={canon:'.para.canon',commentary:'.para.l-A',subcommentary:'.para.l-T'}`
— it selects by it but does not require that a volume's paragraphs carry its own
layer's class. One assertion would have caught this. Worth adding.

## THE 07ViT07 COVERAGE RATIO WAS MY MEASUREMENT, NOT THE CORPUS (2026-07-29o)

The 07ViT07 rebuild dry-run read 1.18–1.20 (corpus chars ÷ printed chars) and I
held the rebuild until it was explained. **It is a defect in the printed-side
measure and the corpus is right.**

Two findings, both counted:

1. **Every shipped, gated volume reports the same inflation by the same method**
   (`_tika/ratio.py`): 35KhuA16 1.051, 51Vism01 1.047, 01VinA01 1.064, 20KhuA01
   1.065, 29KhuA10 1.169. 07ViT07's 1.204 sits just above a band that known-good
   volumes already occupy.
2. **The named cause** (`_tika/ratio_why.py`, then page 240 by eye): the printed
   measure discards everything from the first line beginning `___`, taking that
   for the footnote rule. **The edition also prints a short decorative rule
   `_____` between vaṇṇanā sections.** On p240 it stands at line 4 of 32, so the
   measure threw away 27 lines of body and kept 3. That is the whole gap.
   Line 0 dropped as a running header accounts for only 1.8%.

Per-page comparison is meaningless here for a second reason worth remembering: a
paragraph is anchored to the page it BEGINS on, so a long paragraph carries
thirty pages of text under one page number and the pages between hold zero.

**07ViT07's rebuild therefore stands verified** — 420 ¶, pdf_page 22..508
monotonic, 0 shipped paragraphs lost, 0 duplication (12/12 random 70-char
fragments once each), footnotes and running headers excluded, last three
paragraphs the volume's nigamana gāthās 16/17/18 on p508. Still staged only, at
`_khua/07ViT07.rebuilt.json`; nothing installed into `site/`.
