## THE GLYPH CORRECTION PASS — 30 PLACES APPLIED, AND THE REGISTER ALONE COULD NOT HAVE DONE IT (2026-07-29m)

**User's decision, after the code-page test: go ahead.** Applied. Census **68 -> 44**
occurrences, **16 -> 13** code points, **39 -> 26** volumes. `è`, `ê` and `ó` are gone from the
corpora entirely.

```
register   1 -> 30 places applied | 54 entries | 21 volumes
readings   ā x30 rows · ī x11 · ṇ x11 · s x2      (rows, not places)
census     68 occurrences / 16 code points / 39 volumes  ->  44 / 13 / 26
gates      every affected volume returns to its RECORDED state — see below
regress    55/55 after one snapshot advanced by hand   |   _navdup PASS 24,438 rows
layout     0 layout issues on all 14
```

### !!! THE REGISTER ALONE FIXES LESS THAN HALF OF IT, AND THAT HAD TO BE MEASURED

`build_khu_volume.py` substitutes on the PRINTED text, which reaches the side-maps. But the
reader draws `fmtBold(corpus text)` for a commentary volume, so a glyph sitting in a corpus
paragraph is **still on the page** after the register is applied. Asked of all 30 declared
places:

```
15 literals are in a side-map (only `verse`)     24 literals are in the CORPUS text
```

**The register was designed for the 27KhuA08 case, where the glyph was in the PDF and NOT in the
corpus** — its own note says so — and that case is the exception, not the rule. Applying it alone
would have corrected the nav and left the reading text untouched in 24 of 30 places.

So the corpus was corrected too: `_codepage/fix_corpus.py`, a **surgical substitution of declared
literals in place — not a re-extraction**. Ordinals, keys and page anchors are untouched, so
nothing is re-anchored and nothing needs re-keying. **45 files, 66 substitutions**, backups in
`_codepage/corpus_pre/`. Both `site/` and `corpus/` were corrected so the two stay in step.

### !!! AND THE GATE HAD TO LEARN IT TOO, OR IT REPORTS ARTEFACTS

`verify_render_vs_pdf.py` reads the PDF directly. With the render corrected and the page not, it
compared a corrected render against an uncorrected page and reported **one line per corrected
place**. Measured before the fix, and the arithmetic is exact:

```
06VinSg06 +1   07DiA01 +1   08DiA02 +3   18AnA02 +1   27Khu10 +1   32Abhi04 +3   49AbhiA02 +3
```

One per declared literal, on exactly the seven volumes that have one. **The same class as the
line-end-hyphen disagreement of 2026-07-28a** — the gate models the reader, so a correction lives
in both. `pdftext()` now applies the register at all six `pdftotext` call sites; backup
`verify_render_vs_pdf.py.preglyph`.

**After it, every affected volume returns to its recorded state:**

```
03VinA03 0/2/0/0 · 06VinSg06 0/0/0/0 · 07DiA01 3/4/6/0 · 08DiA02 4/2/8/0 · 18AnA02 2/1/4/0
27Khu10 0/0/0/0 · 32Abhi04 0/0/0/0 · 49AbhiA02 20/13/39/2   — all == docs/verify_report.md
05Kankha 0/0/3/0 · 26KhuA07 4/6/2/0 · 27KhuA08 0/1/0/0 · 34KhuA15 0/0/0/0 · 35KhuA16 0/0/1/0
36KhuA17 11/12/19/0                  — all == their own HANDOFF entries
```

**The correction moved no gate.** (Those six rows of `docs/verify_report.md` are STALE, by large
margins — 26KhuA07 records 1881/1367 against a true 4/6 — because the report predates the
commentary rebuilds. **The report needs a fresh sweep; that is not this pass's doing and is
recorded as open.**)

### !!! THE REGISTER'S `ó -> ṇ  7/7` WAS WRONG. IT IS 6 OF 7

Every place was read on its own page rather than trusted to the character, and one refused:
**18AnA02 p140** sets `dakkhiṇahatthe tālappamāṇaṁ ayasūlaṁ paveóenti` — they drive an iron stake
into the right hand. `paveṇenti` is not a word; the verb is **`pavesenti`**, and **the identical
phrase `ayasūlaṁ pavesenti` occurs in 13MaA04 and 43KhuA24**, the same hell-torment passage in two
other volumes. So `ó` = **s** there, and it is applied as such.

**This is the per-font effect of 2026-07-29l reaching a THIRD character.** It was proved for `é`
and `ò`; `ó` was believed uniform at 7/7 and is not. **Read every place on its page. An aggregate
agreement figure is not evidence about any particular place** — and this register's own figures
are aggregates.

The other six `ó` places are secure, several with corroboration on the same page: **27Khu10 p32
prints `Tattha katamā āóatti–` and then `Ayaṁ āṇatti.` four lines later**, and 07ViT07 sets

## THE SECOND-CODE-PAGE HYPOTHESIS IS **REFUTED** — AND THE TEST STILL CHANGES THE PLAN (2026-07-29l)

2026-07-29c left a structural finding untested: seven residue glyphs are the case counterparts of
glyphs already in §3, which "points at a second VZTimes code page… If that is right, the residue
is a table gap and the right fix is to extend the §3 mapping, not to patch 89 places one at a
time." **User's decision: test it before anything else.** Tested. **It is not right — but it is
not worthless either, and the difference is the useful part.**

### WHAT THE FONTS THEMSELVES SAY

The `/ToUnicode` injection worked per font, so every converted PDF carries the code→character map
the conversion actually used. `_codepage/vzblock.py` reads them, restricted to the fonts that
carry the VZTimes layout — **the test for that is `0xC8 -> ā` in the font's own map**, the
signature of `È`; 27KhuA08 has 12 such fonts of 17, and the other five are Identity-H or re-subset
fonts whose codes are arbitrary. **Comparing codes across all fonts is meaningless and the first
version of this probe did exactly that**, reporting 84 "conflicting" codes that were nothing of
the kind.

Read that way the block is completely regular, and it says two things:

```
0xC4 ḷ  0xC8 ā  0xC9 ḍ  0xCA ī  0xD1 ṁ  0xD2 ñ  0xD3 ṇ  0xD4 ṭ     <- §3's table
0xE8 è  0xE9 é  0xEA ê  0xED í  0xEE î  0xF2 ò  0xF3 ó  0xF5 õ     <- passed through
```

**The font uses BOTH the uppercase-accented and the lowercase-accented Latin-1 ranges, and §3
covers only the uppercase one.** Each residue code sits exactly **0x20** above a mapped code —
`è`=0xE8 over `È`=0xC8, `ê`=0xEA over `Ê`=0xCA, `ó`=0xF3 over `Ó`=0xD3. That is the structure
2026-07-29c saw, stated precisely.

**And `0xF1` is the trap.** It reads `ñ` and looks like a mapped entry; it is not. Latin-1 0xF1
*is* `ñ` and Pāḷi `ñ` is `ñ`, so **passthrough happens to give the right character**. Counting it
as evidence for the rule would have been an error.

### THE PREDICTION, TESTED THE ONLY HONEST WAY AVAILABLE

If the offset is the structure, `-0x20` predicts every residue letter. `_codepage/predict.py`
substitutes the prediction and asks **whether the resulting word occurs elsewhere in the corpus** —
the corpus as a FILTER, which is all the project permits a lexicon to be. A hit is evidence; a
miss is not a refutation, since the word may simply be rare. 36 places, vocabulary 1.06M words.

```
è -> ā   11 of 17 found in the corpus        ê -> ī    3 of 6 found
ó -> ṇ    2 of 7 found                       é -> ḍ    0 of 2      ò -> ñ  0 of 4
```

**The misses under è, ê and ó are all obviously right on sight** — `Rāhu-asurindaṁ`,
`Sādhanatoti`, `Nānācittavasena`, `Sīlavipatti`, `Vīriyāyattassa`, `āṇattiyampi`,
`ratanacuṇṇavippakiṇṇaṁ` — words the filter does not happen to hold. **The misses under é and ò
are nonsense**, and that is the refutation:

```
passémi   -> passḍmi     the word is passāmi     so é = ā here
viharāmé  -> viharāmḍ    the word is viharāmi    so é = i    here
vòṭthāna  -> vñṭthāna    the word is vuṭṭhāna    so ò = u here
Aòjalī    -> Añjalī      correct                 so ò = ñ    here
```

**ONE CODE, TWO LETTERS, IN DIFFERENT VOLUMES. There is no code page that could do that.** The
same Latin-1 character in the text layer stands for different glyphs in different fonts, which is
precisely why 2026-07-29c could not settle `é`, `ò`, `Ù` from the text layer — **and now there is
a reason rather than an observation.**

### SO THE PLAN CHANGES, AND IT CHANGES IN BOTH DIRECTIONS

* **The shortcut is dead.** No single table extension fixes the residue, and anyone who tries one
  will silently corrupt `passāmi` into `passḍmi`. **Do not extend §3 across the lowercase range.**
* **But three characters ARE structural and safe.** `è`→ā, `ê`→ī, `ó`→ṇ are each predicted by the
  block, confirmed by context in every occurrence, and were already the register's three
  high-confidence readings — arrived at independently, by reading the page. **Two witnesses now
  agree on them**: the font layout and the printed context. Together they are **30 of the 89
  places**.
* **The remaining 59 stay per-place**, which is what the register already does. `é`, `ò`, `Ù` are
  now explained rather than merely flagged, and `−` is unchanged (its neighbours are damaged too).

**Nothing was applied.** `data/glyph_errata.json` still carries exactly one `apply_from`/`apply_to`
entry. The correction pass itself is still the user's to start.

Scratch: `_codepage/codes.py`, `_codepage/vzblock.py`, `_codepage/conflict.py`,
`_codepage/predict.py`.

The commentary layer being complete, the next layer is the 26 Ṭīkā. **Nothing was built:** this

### !!! THE VINAYA ṬĪKĀ IS SEVEN VOLUMES, NOT SIX

Checked against two witnesses rather than assumed. `concordanciatextos.pdf` numbers the

**!!! AND THE SHIPPED NAV DISAGREES WITH THE TITLE PAGES.** `nav.json` puts three nodes in

that volume's own title page reads `Sāratthadīpanīṭīkā (Tatiyo bhāgo)` and the Vajirabuddhiṭīkā
is 06ViT06. That tree is the old font-heuristic one from `build_nav.py`, which this file has
recorded all along as never checked against a mātikā or a colophon. **Treat every Ṭīkā nav node
as unverified**; 03ViT03 and 07ViT07 are two of the eight `MULTITOP_PENDING` volumes.

### !!! OPEN QUESTION 2 IS ANSWERED — THE ṬĪKĀ NEED NO SECOND MAPPING TABLE

Project instructions §8 asks whether the Aṭṭhakathā and Ṭīkā use the same VZTimes encoding.
**They do.** Answered the way §3 asks — self-verifyingly, not by assertion.
`_tika/encoding_check.py` takes each **LEGACY** `tika/*.pdf` text layer, applies the §3 /
CONVERSION_REPORT table, and compares character by character with the converted
`tika-unicode/*.pdf`. p2 (the credits page, whose `©` is a real copyright sign, not `Ñ`) and p3
(the Burmese alphabet table) are skipped, and §3 says why.

```
26 volumes | 12,255 pages | 23,914,857 characters compared | 3 differing
24 of the 26 reproduce at 100.0000%
```

**THE THREE ARE NOT CONVERSION ERRORS — THEY ARE GAPS IN THE §3 TABLE**, and both places were
read on the page:

```
12DiT05  p163  'q'     -> 'Ḍ'      'āha. qayhantu vāti…'  ->  'āha. Ḍayhantu vāti…'
26VsmT02 p552  '\x7f'  -> 'Ū'  x2  '[U-\x7f]' / '\x7fkāsiramattaṁ'  ->  '[U-Ū]' / 'Ūkāsiramattaṁ'
```

The Unicode PDF is **right** in all three — *ḍayhantu* is the word, and `[U-Ū]` is the word
index's own section head. The injection got them because it maps **per font from the embedded
encoding**, exactly as `docs/CONVERSION_REPORT.md` describes; a flat byte table cannot.

**This is evidence for the structural finding of 2026-07-29c** — that the glyph residue is a
TABLE GAP rather than scattered damage. Two more legacy code points, found not by inspecting
damage but by comparing 23.9 million characters. **Take it into the deferred glyph pass: it
argues for extending the table over patching 89 places.** Add `q`→Ḍ and `\x7f`→Ū to §3.

### THE VINAYA SEVEN SCREENED — EVERY ONE NEEDS A REBUILD, AND TWO ARE NOT MERELY SHORT

`_fnprobe/cover.py`, scoped to each volume's measured text extent. **Sorted by BAD PAGES, never
by ratio.**

| 05ViT05 | 19-340 | 90% | 7 | 673 | rev bold app |

**!!! 07ViT07 HOLDS 22 PARAGRAPHS FOR 489 PRINTED PAGES** — 11,920 of its 11,956 long lines
absent, 482 of 489 pages failing the per-page test. **01ViT01 holds 23 for 460 pages**, its bad
pages beginning at the volume's very first (p16, 9 of 9 long lines absent), and it is the only

**The ratio and the per-page test disagree most sharply exactly where it matters**, which is what
START HERE warns about: 01ViT01 reads 50% and is unusable, while 03ViT03 reads 92% with 8 bad
pages and is in the same shape the commentary batch was in before its rebuild (87-96%, which

### !!! THE DIAGNOSIS: TWO OF THE SEVEN HAVE NO NUMBERED UNITS AT ALL

Read on the page rather than inferred. 07ViT07 p30 sets ordinary unnumbered prose at indent 4;
its `N. ` lines are HEADINGS (`10. Dantaponasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā`, p115). 01ViT01 p40 is the same,
and its headings are not even numbered (`Bāhiranidānakathā`, centred at 24).

`_tika/unitcensus.py` asks every volume the question directly — **is a numbered line at the body
column (a UNIT anchor) or set well right of it (a HEADING)?** — with the body column measured per
page as `_kat_cols` does it. **!!! IT MUST CUT AT THE FOOTNOTE RULE:** a footnote cell opens
`N. ` too, and unscoped they were HALF the numbered lines — 980 on 07ViT07 of which 512 were
apparatus. Scoped, 82.

```
07ViT07   82 numbered body lines |   2 at the body column (2%)  |  80 centred (98%)
01ViT01   17 numbered body lines |  17 at the body column       |   0 centred
```

**07ViT07 has two numbered units in 489 printed pages, and both are headings that happen to sit
at indent 12 over a body column of 4. 01ViT01 has seventeen in 460.** Their corpora are 22 and 23
paragraphs because `extract.py` keys on numbered units these volumes do not have. **This is the
`heads` page-reader's case — the fourth reader, heading-delimited prose, added 2026-07-28d for
05Kankha and used by no volume since.** The rebuild must be told so before it is run.

### AND THE SAME CENSUS OVER ALL 26 SIZES THE WHOLE LAYER

The proportion misleads; **DENSITY is the discriminator** — 01ViT01 reads 100% units on
seventeen lines. Units per printed page, over each volume's measured extent:

```
SPARSE (< 0.25/page) — `heads` reader candidates, five of the 26:
   07ViT07 0.00 · 01ViT01 0.04 · 09DiT02 0.15 · 13MaT01 0.21 · 16SaT01 0.23
ORDINARY (0.35-1.20/page): the other twenty-one
```

**Only 05Kankha has ever needed the `heads` reader. There are five more candidates here**, and
they are spread across four nikāyas — so this is a property of the Ṭīkā genre, not of one work.
Each still has to be read on its own page before its reader is declared.

### !!! AND THE DENSITY LIST WAS WRONG FOR THREE OF ITS FIVE — THE SPREAD TEST IS WHAT DECIDES

Density says how MANY anchors; it cannot tell a genuinely SPARSE `katha` volume from a `heads`
volume with one numbered appendix. `_tika/unitspread.py` asks WHERE they are:

```
07ViT07     2 anchors | first p420 last p482 | 13% of the extent | and BOTH are headings
01ViT01    17 anchors | first p210 last p473 | 57% | !!! the first 194 pages carry NONE
09DiT02    75 anchors | first p144 last p477 | 67%
13MaT01    82 anchors | first p26  last p411 | 98%
16SaT01    81 anchors | first p34  last p368 | 97%
```

**09DiT02, 13MaT01 and 16SaT01 are SPARSE `katha`, not `heads`** — their anchors run the whole
length of the book. A Ṭīkā comments selectively, so one numbered unit can cover many pages; thin
is not the same as absent. 16SaT01 p120 settles it on the page: `5. Arahantasuttavaṇṇanā` centred
at 26, and `25. Katāvīti katavā…` at the body column right below it — a heading AND a unit.

**07ViT07 is the only clean `heads` volume of the five.** Its two "anchors" are the headings
`4-5. Rahopaṭicchanna…vaṇṇanā` (p420) and `6. Bhojanappaṭiggahaṇa…vaṇṇanā` (p482), set at indent
12 over a body column of 4 — near enough to pass the column test, headings on the page.

**01ViT01 IS MIXED, and that is a shape no volume has had before.** Its first 194 printed pages —
the whole Bāhiranidāna — carry no anchor at all, then seventeen appear over the remaining 264,
with a 141-page gap inside them. Its corpus's ord0 is **258,087 characters** precisely because one
paragraph swallowed pp16-210. **A single reader will not serve it**; the book split is the thing
to establish first.

**RECORDED AS A CORRECTION TO THIS ENTRY'S OWN FIRST PASS:** the density census named five
`heads` candidates and the spread test cut it to one, plus one mixed. **Density is the screen;
the spread and the printed page are the measurement.**


### !!! `scout_volume extent` IS SUSPECT ON FIVE ṬĪKĀ VOLUMES

Each measures **less than half its PDF**:

```
20AnT03    93 of 408 pdf pages       23AbhiT02  235 of 503
21KhuT01  151 of 532                 24AbhiT03  248 of 619
22AbhiT01 203 of 466
```

Three of the five (22AbhiT01, 23AbhiT02, 24AbhiT03) carry **two works each** — a mūlaṭīkā and an
anuṭīkā — so the back-matter scan very likely stops at the first work's word index or the second
work's title page. The same class as 33Abhi05, where the declared range was wrong and the volume
lost its last printed unit. **Measure every Ṭīkā extent by hand before building on it**, and
check BOTH ends.

### WHAT TO DO NEXT, IN ORDER

1. **Read one printed page of each of the five sparse volumes** and declare its reader. Do not
   assume `heads` from the density alone — that is the measurement, not the answer.
2. **Fix the five suspect extents by hand.**

### FIVE MORE ERRATA, AND THE COLOPHON SPLITS THEM FOUR TO ONE

Every one of these looks the same on form — a mātikā entry that does not match its body heading.
**The section's own closing colophon is what decides which side is wrong, and it does not answer
the same way each time:**

```
MĀTIKĀ misprint -> errata       p5 `Bhāgineyyupāliṭṭhera-`   body p79 + colo p80 `…pālitthera-`
                                p8 `…apadānavaṇṇā` (x2)      body + colo `…apadānavaṇṇanā`
                                p9 `8. Phaladāyakatthera-`   body p172 + colo p173 `Phalakadāyaka-`
BODY   misprint -> body_errata  p16 `2. Ekatthambhīkatthera-`  mātikā p4 AND colo p17 short `i`
```

**`2. Ekatthambhīkatthera-` is the trap.** It is the mātikā that differs from the tree, exactly
as in the other four — but the mātikā and the section's own colophon AGREE, so the BODY HEAD is
the misprint and `errata` would have been the wrong key. **Read the colophon before choosing.**

And **`8. Phaladāyakatthera-apadānavaṇṇanā` had to be keyed on the whole numbered entry**: the
mātikā prints that name three times (p7 and p8 as `7.`, p9 as `8.`), and the first two are a
DIFFERENT thera whose name is correct, so a global rewrite would have corrupted both. The same
lesson 29KhuA10's `Kumāputta` taught four days' work ago, and it recurs because `errata` is
global by construction.

**THE LAYER'S FIFTH COMPLETELY CLEAN BODY GATE, AND THE SECOND IN A ROW** after 30KhuA11.

### !!! THE EDITION OMITS THE TERMINAL STOP ON ONE COLOPHON

p60 sets `Aparā uttamātherīgāthāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā` with **no period**, where its eighty-four
fellows all carry one. The stop is the one thing `kat_is_colo`'s form test asks for, so the
line was refused there and the heading branch claimed it. `colofix`, one literal, printed once.

**Naming it cost nothing, and that was measured before choosing** (27KhuA08's rule): the line
is not a corpus paragraph of its own — the corpus splices it onto the tail of ord72, unit 47 —
so `colofix` hides nothing and strands no link target. Headings 86 → 85, colophons 85 → 86.

### !!! A `tops` ENTRY IS MATCHED AGAINST THE PRINTED HEAD, MISPRINT AND ALL

The body heads the ninth nipāta **`9. Navanīpāta`**, with a long `ī`, where the mātikā (p6),
the section's own colophon (p187) and the body's very next line (`Navanipāte mā su te
vaḍḍha…`) all read `Navanipāta`. Written into `tops` as the mātikā spells it, the nav **REFUSED
the whole top level** — "does not appear in printed order; stopped at `1. Ekakanipāta`" — and
**eight of the sixteen nipātas vanished from the tree**, because that walk is forward-only and
one mismatch ends it.

**The lesson is the direction: `tops` is the PRINTED stream's own wording; the mātikā's form
belongs in `body_errata`.** Named as printed, 8 top → 17 top and the volume is `[OK]`. A
misprint in a top-level label is far more expensive than one in a leaf: it does not strand one
entry, it truncates the tree.

### CHECKS THAT CAME BACK EMPTY, AND THEY ARE WORTH SAYING

* **The colophon-frame sweep returns NOTHING.** All sixteen nipātas close on a single stopped
  line; there is no genitive frame anywhere in the volume. The first of the batch with none.
* **`peyloss` 0 line-ends, 0 lost.** The volume prints no peyyāla line-end at all.
* **The one colophon-escape line is a GENUINE colophon** — `Kisāgotamītherīgāthāvaṇṇanā
  niṭṭhitā.` at indent 5, which merely sits below `body+8`. **So this volume adds 1 to the raw
  corpus-wide count and 0 to the wrong-role count**, the first of the batch to do so. Quote
  both figures, not just the raw one.

### TWO HEADS THAT LOOK WRONG AND ARE NOT

`5-10. Tissāditherīgāthāvaṇṇanā` (p19) is a genuine RANGE heading — the edition comments six
therīs together — and `3. Aparā uttamātherīgāthāvaṇṇanā` (p58) is its own lowercase `uttamā`.
Both left as printed.

### OPEN, AND IT MAY BE A CLASS RATHER THAN A VOLUME: A ONE-LINE PROSE GLOSS DRAWN AS VERSE

`check_shape` reports one block — `verse.after` ord196, p149, 3 lines, median 60 characters,
**2 sentence-ends mid-block**. Read on the page it is three consecutive ONE-LINE prose glosses
(`Sākete añjanaṁ vananti Sāketasamīpe Añjanavane vihāraṁ pāvisiṁ.` and two more), and it would
render as italic verse.

**The cause is geometric.** On a page whose body column measures 0, a one-line paragraph set at
the paragraph indent has no continuation at the margin to give it away, so it reads as display.
**`display_prose` cannot reach it in any variant**: every line ends in a full stop, which is
exactly what its pāda test asks for.

Three more of the same shape sit below `check_shape`'s 58-character threshold and so are not
reported — p86 `Bhikkhuninti Dhammadinnattheriṁ sandhāya vadati.`, p249, p257 — plus p312
`Ettāvatā ca–`, the 28Khu11 `Tenāhu–` lead-in shape.

**A discriminator is proposed and UNTESTED:** a gāthā alternates its pāda punctuation, so its
FIRST line ends in a comma; a run of one-line prose glosses ends every line, first included, in
a full stop. That would keep 30KhuA11's p465 stanza, whose pādas 2, 3 and 4 all close with a
stop but whose first does not. **Not implemented, not measured** — it touches the display path,
which feeds every volume's side-maps, so it needs its own measured before/after over all 81
SPEC volumes. **This is very likely not confined to 31KhuA12; any volume with short one-line
glosses would show it, and none has been asked.**

### !!! I DESTROYED `site/reader/nav.json` WITH A READ-ONLY PROBE, AND RECOVERED IT

Reported first because it is the largest thing that happened. A probe written to measure a
regex change globbed `pipeline/build_*nav*.py` and `exec`d each file to merge its SPEC.
**`pipeline/build_nav.py` REGENERATES `site/reader/nav.json` AT IMPORT** — it has no
`if __name__ == '__main__'` guard — so importing it rewrote the file from the old
font-heuristic tree: **1,876 KB and 161 hand-built top-level nodes down to 527 KB and 231
generated ones.** Every nav built since 2026-07-26 was gone from it. `nav.json` is untracked
in git, so there was no revert.

**Recovered, and the recovery is verified, not asserted.** `nav.json.bak28khua09` (the copy
taken *before* 28KhuA09's nav was written, the newest backup on disk) was restored and
28KhuA09's nav rebuilt from its own SPEC. It came back at **6 top / 51 sections [OK]** and
`_navdup` at **23,694 rows, 161 nodes, 0 duplicates** — both the exact figures recorded on
2026-07-29b, which is what makes this a recovery rather than a plausible-looking file. The
damaged copy is kept as `site/reader/nav.json.damaged_by_29probe`.

**THE RULE: A PROBE MUST NEVER IMPORT A MODULE THAT WRITES.** The probe now execs only files
containing `A.SPEC.update`. `build_nav.py` is the one generator in `pipeline/` that runs at
import; anything that sweeps that directory must exclude it by name or by test.

**This was not confined to the new volume.** Asked over all 118 volumes, **25 have a

**MOVES the shipped map on every one it was tested against** — 01VinA01 ord14→0, 05Vin05 1→0,

49AbhiA02 all 2-or-3→0, and 39Abhi11 and 50AbhiA03 lose every one of their several anchors to
the ordinal below it. **The shipped maps are correct; the builder that would regenerate them
was not.** Nobody had re-run it, so nothing was broken on disk — but it was one `--write` away.

`anchors()` now subtracts the volume's `hide/`. **Measured against the SHIPPED map on all 24

### THE READER, AND `display_prose: 'dash'`

`katha` with `units_may_be_verse: True` on the DEFAULT indent test — p49 sets
`2. “Upasanto uparato,` at indent 6 with its second pāda at 9, p53 sets `3. Tattha paññanti`
at 5 with the line below at 0. Neither 28Khu11's `hanging` nor 27Khu10's `formula` is needed.

Two quoted sutta PROSE blocks are set in a gāthā's geometry, so `display_prose` — **and plain
`True` is WRONG here, which was measured rather than assumed.** It takes gāthā blocks 54 → 40,
and **seven of the fourteen it removes are real gāthā**: this edition closes a gāthā quoted
into the prose below it with the CITATION DASH (`…bandhanan”ti15–`, p40) or with nothing at
all where the quotation runs on (p391), not with a stop, so the all-lines-must-be-pādas test
demotes them.

**A NEW VALUE, NOT A WIDER RULE.** `display_prose: 'dash'` admits `…”ti`, with or without a
footnote marker and with or without the dash, as a pāda end. Gāthā blocks **54 → 47**, and all
seven removed are quoted prose read on the page (p198, p222, p243, p247, p344, p345, p442).
The three shipped volumes that set `display_prose: True` — 27Khu10, 28Khu11, 32Abhi04 — were
run builder-vs-builder against `build_khu_volume.py.pre29khua10` and are **byte-identical on
all five side-maps**; `regress check` 55/55.

### THE COLOPHON SWEEP HAS A BLIND SPOT, AND THIS VOLUME IS WHERE IT SHOWS

Three literals in four printings, which is far fewer than its companions — the volume closes
**206** sections and frames only three of them. But the sweep keyed on `niṭṭhitā.` returned

`atthavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.` **The two missing lines were found by reading the head stream, not by
the sweep. Widen the sweep's close pattern when it is next used** —
`_khua/_probe29/colosweep.py` is the version that ran here.

Naming them cost NOTHING, and that was measured before choosing (27KhuA08's rule): two of the
three literals are in no corpus paragraph at all, and the third (ord245) was already hidden as
a leaked heading. **The corpus-wide stranded-link figure is unchanged at 2,432.**

### THE EDITION MISPRINTS SIX HEADINGS AND THREE UNIT NUMBERS, AND THE COLOPHON DECIDES EACH

The heads-stream/mātikā diff refused six entries. In every case the section's OWN closing
colophon two pages later is the tie-breaker, and it splits them three and three:

```
MĀTIKĀ misprint -> `errata`      p5   7. Kumāputtattheragāthāvaṇṇanā     body `…sahāya…`
                                 p7   5. Susāradattattheragāthāvaṇṇanā   body `Susāradat…`
BODY   misprint -> `body_errata` p150 3. Sumaṅgalattheraghāthāvaṇṇanā    `ghāthā` for `gāthā`
                                 p156 5 Ramaṇīyavihārittheragāthāvaṇṇanā NO PERIOD after the 5
                                 p223 6. Piyañjahattheragāthāvaṇṇanās    a trailing `s`
                                 p471 10. Sāṭhimattiyattheragāthāvaṇṇanā an intrusive `h`
```

**`errata` had to be keyed on the WHOLE numbered entry, not the name**: the mātikā lists
`Kumāputtattheragāthāvaṇṇanā` for BOTH its 6th and 7th entries, and `errata` rewrites
globally, so keying on the name would have corrupted the 6th.

**!!! THE MISSING PERIOD WAS NOT A WRONG ROLE — THE HEADING WAS IN NO `sections/` ENTRY AT
ALL.** `5 Ramaṇīyavihārittheragāthāvaṇṇanā` (p156) never matched the numbered test, so the
tree could not reach that section. The same class as 09Ma01's `42.Tassa`, the other way round.
`headfix` names it; the printed reading is kept and the mātikā's form goes on the tree side.

**!!! AND `body_errata` IS A KEY OF THE NAV BUILDER, NOT OF `build_khu_volume.py`.** Declared
in the volume SPEC it is read by nothing — a belief, not a correction. It was written there
first and moved; check which builder consumes a key before declaring it.

### THE `n`-SEQUENCE DESCENDS THREE TIMES AND ALL THREE ARE THE EDITION'S OWN

* p85/p86 print `14.` TWICE — the thera's narrative and then the comment on it, because
  Sivaka's gāthā is quoted inline and never set as a display block.
* p445 prints `130.` between 229 and 231, and p475 `151.` between 250 and 252.

Both misprints stand on the printed side AND in the corpus, so the 1:1 pairing is unmoved.
Preserved, not corrected; `n_scope: 'vagga'` is what lets the descents pass.

### TWO MĀTIKĀ ENTRIES THE PARSER CANNOT SEE, AND A MEASUREMENT THAT SAYS LEAVE IT ALONE

The nav reports two body headings "the mātikā does not list" — `9. (Paṭhama)` and
`10. (Dutiya) Devasabhattheragāthāvaṇṇanā`. The mātikā DOES list them, twice over unreadably:

`9. (Paṭhama) devasabhattheragāthāvaṇṇanā` — a parenthesis first, and then a LOWERCASE `d`
where the body capitalises. **Both headings are printed and are KEPT in the tree, so the nav
is complete and the report is cosmetic.**

Widening `MAT` to admit a parenthesised qualifier was measured over **all 73 volumes that
declare a `matika` range: +1 entry, −0.** The one is 16An02's `3. (Aññā) Byākaraṇasutta`,

## THE GLYPH REGISTER RESOLVED — 89 PLACES, 18 CHARACTERS, 14 READINGS SETTLED (2026-07-29c)

The register built yesterday said WHERE the unmapped glyphs are. This says WHAT THEY ARE.
Nothing was applied: `data/glyph_errata.json` still has exactly ONE entry with
`apply_from`/`apply_to` (27KhuA08 `Pèyāsivagga`→`Pāyāsivagga`). The rest are readings on
record, per project principle 3.

**COUNT THE PLACES, NOT THE ROWS.** `entries` holds one row per SIGHTING, and a place is
sighted twice when the glyph survives from the PDF text layer into the corpus. 162 rows are
**89 places**. Every earlier figure I quoted (162, and the per-character 41/30/15/13/…) was
sightings and overcounts by ~1.8×. De-duplication key is `(vol, char, word)` —
`_charcensus/register.py:places()`.

```
89 places | 18 characters | 49 volumes | 13 high + 1 medium settled | 4 not settled | 1 applied
```

**Settled (high):** `è`→ā 17/17 · `¥`→Ṁ 8/8 · `ó`→ṇ 7/7 · `ê`→ī 6/6 · `þ`→y 2/2 · `î`→n 2/2 ·
`ÿ`→y · `Ø`→ā · `±`→ā · `õ`→u. Medium: `í`→ī (one place only).
**Not letter faults at all:** `◌̣` U+0323 is `n` + COMBINING DOT BELOW where the corpus
carries precomposed `ṇ` — 7 places, all 08DiA02, fixed by NFC and involving no editorial
decision; `⎯` U+23AF is the quotation dash, 3 places, all 04Vin04; `¬` is not a substitution —
the pair `n¬` stands for `ñ` (11MaA02).
**Not settled — one glyph, two readings; do not apply from the text layer:** `Ù` (6 i / 1 ṭ /
1 u / 1 variant siglum), `ò` (3 u / 1 ñ), `é` (1 ā / 1 i), `−` (13 of 16 read `a` but the
neighbours are damaged too — an adjacent `n` should be `ṇ`, in three places a `ṇ` is missing
outright, in two the letters are transposed, and doubled stops degrade alongside: `ṭth` for
`ṭṭh`, `ḍd` for `ḍḍ`). A substitution table cannot repair `−`; those passages need the page.

**The structural finding, and it is the useful one.** These are not 18 unrelated faults. Seven
are the *case counterparts* of glyphs already in the §3 table: `È`→ā vs `è`→ā, `Ê`→ī vs `ê`→ī,
`Ó`→ṇ vs `ó`→ṇ, `Ñ`→ṁ vs `¥`→Ṁ, `Ò`→ñ vs `ò` (whose minority reading is exactly ñ). That
points at a **second VZTimes code page** — a font variant whose block was never mapped —
rather than at scattered one-off damage. If that is right, the residue is a table gap and the
right fix is to extend the §3 mapping, not to patch 89 places one at a time. **Untested.** The
test is to pull the raw byte at one of these positions out of the legacy PDF and see whether
the whole set falls on one contiguous block.

Correcting the **PDFs** is a different job: the `/ToUnicode` injection of instructions §6,
open question 4, still unanswered. The register is its input. Do not start it without asking.

Written: `data/glyph_errata.json` (`summary` + 18 full `proposals`),
`docs/GLYPH_ERRATA.md` (regenerated: places not sightings, Pāḷi equivalent per character, and
a "why these look like one fault" section), `_charcensus/register.py` (`_word`, `places`, and
a `doc()` that reports places). Backups `.preresolve` on all three. Corpora and reader
UNTOUCHED — this session changed no text.

## THE GLYPH ERRATUM REGISTER, AND THE FIRST CORRECTION MADE FROM IT (2026-07-29a)

**User-reported, following 2026-07-28z:** correct `6. Pèyāsivagga` to `6. Pāyāsivagga` in the
reader, and put every error of that kind in a file for later correction.

### THIS IS NOT "CORRECTING THE EDITION", AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT

Working principle 3 forbids correcting the edition and does not bear on this. **The edition prints
`Pāyāsivagga`** — its own colophon two pages later (p286, `Chaṭṭhassa Pāyāsivaggassa atthavaṇṇanā
niṭṭhitā.`) and its mātikā both say so. **The CONVERSION lost the `ā`**, leaving a Latin-1 `è`.
What is restored is the edition's own reading, and the loss is registered where a reader can see
it. An unmapped glyph is a defect of this project's own pipeline, not a variant of the text.

### THE REGISTER

`data/glyph_errata.json` — machine-readable, and the only thing the builder reads.
`docs/GLYPH_ERRATA.md` — the same, rendered, with every occurrence in context.
Both are generated by `_charcensus/register.py` (`corpora` / `pdf <folder>` / `doc`).

```
entries 162  |  94 in the PDFs' text layer, 68 in the corpora
distinct characters 18  |  volumes touched 49  |  decided 1
```

**The two sources differ and both are needed.** A corpus shows only the glyphs its extraction
happened to keep; the PDF text layer is where the glyph lives. 27KhuA08's `è` — the one that
started this — is in the PDF and NOT in the corpus.

**!!! SKIP THE ALPHABET TABLE, and §3 says so in as many words.** Unskipped, the PDF scan returns
3,110 hits of which **3,016 are on p3**, the Pāḷi-alphabet table set in Burmese script in the same
legacy font. It buries the 94 that are real. The credits page is skipped too, for its `©`.

### HOW A CORRECTION IS MADE — DATA, NOT CODE

An entry is applied **only** when it carries `apply_from` and `apply_to`. `fix` alone records a
reading believed correct and changes nothing. `build_khu_volume.py` reads the register once and
substitutes on the printed text before any page is parsed, **and refuses to build if a declared
literal is not found** — the same guard `headskip` carries. So a later correction is an edit to
one JSON file, and it cannot silently rot.

```
27KhuA08   6. Pèyāsivagga  ->  6. Pāyāsivagga
```

Rebuilt: `sections/27KhuA08.json` now reads `6. Pāyāsivagga`, the nav's mātikā entry resolves on
its own and **its `errata` declaration was removed** — the reader shows the edition's reading.
Body gate unmoved at **0 / 1 / 0 / 0**, nav `[OK]` 4 top / 91 sections, `regress` 55/55,
`_navdup` PASS.

### PROPOSED READINGS, WRITTEN DOWN AND NOT APPLIED

Read off the contexts, three are consistent across every occurrence and three are not:

```
è -> ā   high      ten volumes agree (Rèjāno, Rèhu, Kèyādi, Pèyāsivagga)      APPLIED on 27KhuA08 only
ó -> ṇ   high      seven volumes agree (āóatti=āṇatti, cuṇóa=cuṇṇa)
ê -> ī   high      five volumes agree (Dêgha=Dīgha, Sêla=Sīla)
Ù -> i   MIXED     three volumes say `i`, 02Vin02's PiÙṭhaṅkā says `ṭ`
ò -> u   MIXED     vòṭthāna says `u`, Aòjalī says `ñ`
−        unresolved  not a 1:1 substitution — its neighbours are garbled too
```

**A proposal is not a correction.** The three "high" ones are ready to apply and were deliberately
not applied: the user asked for one correction and a register, and a sweep of 54 substitutions
across 22 volumes deserves its own pass with its own gates.

### !!! THE METADATA'S PAGE COUNT IS NOT THE TEXT EXTENT

It says "content 7 + text 355 + index 71 + blank 1", which puts the text at 8-362. **The body
closes with the Nigamanakathā on p341 and its final gāthās on p342**, p343 is a blank leaf, and
the word index opens on p344. Twenty pages of the metadata's "text" are index. `scout_volume
extent` measures 8-342 and is right; the declared figure is not usable here, the same way it is
not for 01Vin01 and 02Vin02.

### !!! THE CHARACTER CENSUS OF §3 HAD NEVER BEEN RUN, AND IT FINDS 68

The nav refused one mātikā entry: the body heads the sixth vagga `6. Pèyāsivagga` — a Latin-1
`è` — where the mātikā and the vagga's own colophon (p286, `Chaṭṭhassa Pāyāsivaggassa…`) read
`ā`. **`è` is not in the VZTimes mapping table of the project instructions §3. It is an unmapped
glyph in the Unicode PDF's own text layer, not a variant of the edition.**

So the census §3 asks for — "after conversion, every character must belong to the Pāḷi alphabet
plus expected punctuation; any residual Latin-1 character flags an unmapped glyph; this is
self-verifying — use it" — was run, over **all 118 corpora** (`_charcensus/census.py`):

```
distinct code points 16 | occurrences 68 | volumes touched 39

−  U+2212  20 in 11    è U+00E8  13 in 7     ó U+00F3  6 in 6     Ù U+00D9  6 in 6
ê  U+00EA   5 in  4    ò U+00F2   4 in 4     ⎯ U+23AF  2 in 1     é U+00E9  2 in 2
î  U+00EE   2 in  1    þ U+00FE   2 in 1     ÿ U+00FF  1 in 1     Ø U+00D8  1 in 1
¬  U+00AC   1 in  1    ± U+00B1   1 in 1     õ U+00F5  1 in 1     í U+00ED  1 in 1
```

**This answers open question 3 of the project instructions with a number: yes, the census reveals
glyphs outside the §3 table — sixteen of them, in 39 of the 118 volumes.** Sixty-eight
occurrences in a corpus of tens of millions of characters is a very low rate, and it is NOT a
reason to redo the conversion; it is a defect register to be built. The probe also takes `--pdf`
to scan the PDFs' own text layer, which is where the glyph actually lives — a corpus shows only
those its extraction kept. **That run has NOT been made yet.**

27KhuA08's own instance is recorded as a nav erratum so the entry resolves, with the reading that
renders left exactly as the file carries it.

### THE COLOPHON FRAME COUNTS THE VAGGA'S VATTHUS, SO IT IS A DIFFERENT LITERAL EVERY TIME

```
p116   Iti Paramatthadīpaniyā Khuddakaṭṭhakathāya Vimānavatthusmiṁ
                     Ekādasavatthupaṭimaṇḍitassa
              Dutiyassa Cittalatāvaggassa atthavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
```

Seven literals, fifteen printings — and **the sweep had to reach down to indent 4, not 8**,
because the frame's first line is set at 5. `Vaṇṇo ca me sabbadisā pabhāsatī”ti–`, the closing
pāda of the Vimānavatthu's stock question-gāthā, is printed **twenty-two times** and one
`headskip` literal demotes all of them.

### !!! NAMING THEM COSTS SIX LINK TARGETS, AND THAT WAS MEASURED BEFORE CHOOSING

`colofix` hides the corpus paragraphs that hold those lines, and a hidden paragraph takes its link
targets with it (42KhuA23, 2026-07-28n). Both ways:

```
without `colofix`   hidden  5   body 0 / 5 / 0 / 0   links stranded 3
with    `colofix`   hidden 12   body 0 / 1 / 0 / 0   links stranded 9
```

**Four printed frame lines reach the page that otherwise do not, at the cost of six more link
targets from 19Khu02 that no longer resolve.** Content wins — the stranded targets are colophons,
they still RENDER from the printed stream, and only the ordinal route is lost — but the six are
counted here and added to the open link-rebuild item rather than waved away. The corpus-wide
figure of 2026-07-28r is now **2,432**.

## 26KhuA07 — THE SUTTANIPĀTA COMMENTARY II, `head_words`, AND TWO LINES THE CORPUS LOST (2026-07-28y)

**43 of the 52 commentary volumes are built and navigable; 9 remain.** The Paramatthajotikā II
from the Cūḷavagga's fourth sutta through the Mahā-, Aṭṭhaka- and Pārāyanavaggas. One book,
printed 7-330.

```
corpus    675 ¶ -> 736 (2026-07-28p)      bad pages 69 -> 1
build     KATHĀ  printed units 674 / corpus ¶ 674   headings 61   colophons 193   prose ¶ 949
          gāthā blocks 55   [OK]
body      (6 329, 0-736)   4 / 6 / 2 / 0   at minw 4, 2 AND 1
          hyclass: 1 of 4 explained by the line-end hyphen; the other THREE are real loss, below
bold      722 with bold, 0 unaligned
apparatus 461 stored | 468 printed cells | 0 spliced | 0 variants | 0 xrefs
nav       17 top / 44 sections   mātikā 62, 61 resolve   centred heads 3/3   0 out of order
layout    0 layout issues  [PARTIAL: 28% of ¶ examined]   _navdup PASS 23,542 rows   regress 55/55
reader    opens with its title page; the book node lands on `front-26KhuA07-2`
census    0 orphaned side-map entries corpus-wide
```

### !!! IT REFUSED TO BUILD, AND THE REASON WAS A PARENTHESIS

`printed units 678 != corpus paragraphs 674`. **Five of this volume's sutta headings carry a
parenthesised alternative title** — `6. Kapilasutta (Dhammacariyasutta) vaṇṇanā`,
`8. Dhammasutta (Nāvāsutta) vaṇṇanā`, and three more — and under `heads_by_form` a NUMBERED line
is a heading only if its core is at most **`head_words`, which defaults to TWO**. One word
(`4. Maṅgalasuttavaṇṇanā`) passes; three words do not, so all five became numbered UNITS and each
took an ordinal.

**`head_words: 3` fixes four of the five and breaks the fifth**, which is the interesting part:
**the corpus glued `4. Pūraḷāsasutta (Sundarikabhāradvājasutta) vaṇṇanā` onto the narrative that
follows it** — ord190, 3,179 characters, its `4.` read as the paragraph's own number, the same
shape 22KhuA03 has at ord34 — so on that one the corpus itself holds a unit and the printed side
must agree or the count parts company in the other direction (673 against 674). So four are named
in **`headfix`** and the fifth is left as the unit the corpus makes it: the wrong role, recorded
rather than papered over, and it is exactly the mātikā entry the nav cannot reach.

`headfix` beats `head_words` here because it is a LIST rather than a THRESHOLD, and the volume
needs four of five, not five of five.

### !!! THE CORPUS LOST TWO PRINTED LINES, AND THE PEYYĀLA MARK IS WHY

p98 sets a quotation abbreviated with the peyyāla mark at the line end:

```
      “Mahāsamayo pavanasmiṁ -pa-
      dakkhitāye aparājitasaṁghan”ti2.
```

and the corpus holds `“Mahāsamayo pavanasmiṁ -pa- ` and then jumps to the NEXT PARAGRAPH. **The
continuation line is simply gone** — not mis-joined, not mis-roled: absent. Three of the four
body-gate missing lines are this, all on p98, and `hyclass` correctly refuses to explain them.

**MEASURED over 22 built volumes** (`_khua/_pey/peyloss.py`: for every printed line ending in a
standalone `-pa-`/`-pe-`/`-la-`, does the next printed line occur anywhere in the corpus?):

```
peyyāla line-ends 178 across the 22        continuations absent from the corpus: 2, both 26KhuA07 p98
```

**The first sweep reported four and three of them were the probe lying**: a word index sets
`Kammārataṭṭhakāra -pa- kānaṁ = …` and its continuation is a page reference the corpus rightly
does not hold (39KhuA20 p571, 02VinA02 p326, 05Kankha p414). The probe now scopes itself to the
text extent, the same one `scout_volume extent` measures. **Quote the scoped figure, not the raw
one.**

This is rare and specific — 26KhuA07 is the only volume of the 22 that loses body text this way —
but it is text loss, so it is a rebuild question and it is recorded as one.

### THE VOLUME OPENS MID-VAGGA, AND `2. Cūḷavagga` IS NEVER PRINTED IN IT

Its head belongs to 25KhuA06's body, where that vagga began, so the nav REFUSED it as a top whose
printed order could not be established. **The Cūḷavagga's remaining eleven suttas stand at the top
level in their own right** — the answer 47KhuA28 already gives for its five orphaned
ñāṇa-niddesas — and the vagga label is `matika_drop`ped with the reason written down.

### THE COLOPHON-FRAME SWEEP, AND THE EDITION MISPRINTING ITS OWN FRAME

Four literals, **114 printings**, nothing else. The volume closes its sections with
`Paramatthajotikāya Khuddakaṭṭhakathāya / Suttanipātaṭṭhakathāya / <Name>vaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.` —
and **ONCE it sets `Iti paramatthajotikāya Khuddakaṭṭhakathāya` with a lowercase `p`** against 55
capitalised printings. The same class as 12MaA03's `majjhimanikāyaṭṭhākathāya`. Preserved as
printed and named so the line gets its right role; do NOT fold it to the correct spelling.
Headings 175 -> 61, colophons 79 -> 193.

**Check 1 came back empty and that is worth saying**: not one citation-dash pāda or block-opening
line in the whole volume.

### !!! A ONE-PAGE MĀTIKĀ CANNOT HAVE ITS HEADER FILTERED

`matika_headers` drops a line seen on THREE OR MORE of the range's pages. **This volume's front
matter is a single page**, so its own title stack — `Suttanipātaṭṭhakathā` / `Paṭhamabhāga` — was
read as two mātikā entries, and both being centred they failed the centred gate as well:

```
mātikā centred group heads: 4 printed, 2 resolve in the tree
REFUSED — a centred mātikā group head absent from the tree: 'Suttanipātaṭṭhakathā'
```

**`matika_drop` IS the right tool here**, and this is worth stating because 2026-07-28m recorded
the opposite: there the range had eaten a body page and `matika_drop` would have hidden the
defect. **The test is whether the edition really prints the line inside its mātikā.** It does
here — it is the page's heading — and it does not there. Same key, opposite verdicts, decided by
looking at the page.

needs its own measured pass — but it is now the largest single defect in the layer and it grows

## ...AND CLICKING THE BOOK MUST LAND ON IT — THE SAME REPORT, THE OTHER HALF (2026-07-28u)

**Reported from the reading pane immediately after 2026-07-28t:** the title page was now at the
top, but clicking the book in the tree still dropped the pane somewhere below it.

**`openCanon` scrolled to `p-<vol>-<ord>` — the ANCHOR PARAGRAPH.** That paragraph sits below the
title stack, the homage and the opening heading by construction, and once 2026-07-28t hoisted the
front matter to the top of a filtered stream it could sit a long way below it. So the click landed
mid-book. **It was not one book: of the first ten commentary volumes measured, NONE landed on its
title page** — seven scrolled to the anchor paragraph and three scrolled NOWHERE AT ALL, because
their ord0 is a hidden leaked heading and neither `p-`, `s-` nor anything else resolved.

### THE FIX: THE FRONT MATTER GETS AN ID, AND THE BOOK NODE PREFERS IT

`front-<vol>-<ord>`, emitted by `layerFront` and by the canon path's new `canonFront`, wrapping
the title stack and homage. **That id exists only where an ordinal actually carries a title stack
or a homage — i.e. exactly where the click IS a book rather than a passage — so preferring it over
`s-`/`p-` changes nothing for an ordinary paragraph click.**

**And the book node does not always name the anchor.** A nav node's `first` is ord0, but a volume
whose opening paragraphs are leaked headings carries its title stack further in — 21KhuA02 at
ord2, 05Vin05 at ord1, 37Abhi09 / 39Abhi11 / 40Abhi12 at ord2 — and ord0 is HIDDEN, so nothing
resolved and the click scrolled nowhere. Where the clicked ordinal is at or before the book's own
anchor, the fallback lands on that volume's front matter wherever the stream put it.

### MEASURED OVER EVERY BOOK NODE IN THE TREE, IN THE REAL READER

`_khua/_front/scroll_target.js` boots the reader, **records what `scrollIntoView` is actually
called on**, and opens every node the sidebar offers for a volume that has a title page — 99 of
them, 60 canon and 39 commentary.

```
                                        lands on its own title page
BEFORE (reader2.html.prefrontscroll)    0 of the first 10 measured
AFTER                                   99 of 99
```

### !!! "NOTHING ABOVE IT" IS THE WRONG TEST, AND THE PROBE SAID SO FIRST

18Khu01 holds FIVE books, each with its own title page, and its fifth node correctly lands on
`front-18Khu01-705` with **707 paragraphs of the four earlier books above it**. The first version
of the probe graded that a failure. **The rule is that a click lands on the CLICKED book's own
front matter**; what stands above it is another book, and is reported rather than graded. Same for
19Khu02 (4 books), 15An01 / 17An03 (4), 16An02 (3), 12Sam01 / 13Sam02 / 21Khu04 / 27Khu10 /
31Abhi03 (2).

### GATES, ALL RE-RUN AFTER THE CHANGE

The wrapper `<div class="frontmatter">` changes DOM sibling structure, and `check_layout`'s
`duplicate-heading` rule tests "two heads with nothing between them" — so the presentation gate
had to be re-run over the whole layer, not sampled.

```
scroll_target  99 book nodes: 99 land on their own title page, 0 do not
front_first    39 commentary volumes: 39 open with their title page, 0 before, 0 missing
check_layout   ALL 39 commentary volumes + 8 canon volumes: 0 layout issues
               (51Vism01 / 52Vism02 not driveable — no reverse map; unchanged either side)
regress        55/55 byte-identical          _navdup  PASS, 23,110 rows
```

Reader `BUILD` is now `2026-07-28u-frontscroll`. Backups: `site/reader/reader2.html.prefront`
(the 2026-07-28t hoist) and `site/reader/reader2.html.prefrontscroll` (this one).

### A NOTE ON THE PROBE, BECAUSE IT COST TWO FALSE FAILURES

`scroll_target.js` and `front_first.js` both had to learn the same two things, and both produced a
confident wrong answer before they did:

* **Wait for the sidebar, not just for `openKey`.** The function exists before `buildSidebar` has
  loaded the manifest; an opening issued in that window renders before the target volume is in
  `cache`. That made the FIRST volume of every run fail and every later one pass — a verdict
  decided by list order.
* **One jsdom window does not survive the sweep.** Each opening loads more volumes into `cache`
  and never releases them; the run wedged at the 41st volume. Boot per volume, as
  `check_layout.js` does. A canon volume is slow enough that the default sweep skips it — name it
  explicitly.

## A BOOK MUST OPEN WITH ITS OWN TITLE PAGE — USER-REPORTED, AND IT WAS TRUE OF FOUR VOLUMES (2026-07-28t)

**Reported from the reading pane**, with a screenshot: opening the Khuddakapāṭhaṭṭhakathā showed
`10. Idāni khantī cāti…` — printed p125, deep in the Maṅgalasutta commentary — and only THEN
`Khuddakanikāya / Khuddakapāṭhaṭṭhakathā / Namo tassa… / Ganthārambhakathā`. **The rule is
general: click a book and its title page is the first thing on the page; nothing of that book
stands above it.**

### WHY IT HAPPENED, AND IT IS NOT A BUILDER DEFECT

The reader shows a commentary or Ṭīkā work by opening the CANON volume it hangs off and filtering
to that work (`openKey` → `state.filter`), so **the order its paragraphs appear in is the CANON
volume's, not its own**. `layerFront` drew the title stack, homage and opening headings at
whatever position the ANCHOR ordinal happened to land in that stream. So one spurious link on an
earlier canon paragraph puts commentary text above the book's title page — and where no canon
paragraph links to the anchor at all, the title page is never drawn anywhere.

**The exact defect behind the screenshot, named on the page:**

```
18Khu01 ¶21   10. Dasa nāma kiṁ? Dasahaṅgehi samannāgato “arahā”ti vuccatīti.   (Kumārapañha 10)
18Khu01 ¶31   10. Khantī ca sovacassatā, samaṇānañca dassanaṁ…                  (Maṅgala gāthā 10)
```

Both are numbered **10**, and **20KhuA01#37 — the Khantī-gāthā commentary — is linked from BOTH**.
¶21 comes before ¶23, which carries the commentary's whole front matter (ord0-29), so one
paragraph stood above the book's own title page. **The number proposed and nothing confirmed** —
the open half of the number-proposes/content-confirms join, seen from the reader.

### MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER, LIVE, OVER EVERY VOLUME THAT HAS A TITLE PAGE

`_khua/_front/front_first.js` boots the real reader over the real data, opens each volume by the
key the SIDEBAR uses for its book node (`nav.json` → `node.first`) and asks whether any of the
volume's own paragraphs stand above its `.head.booktitle`.

```
                              opens with it   ¶ above it   no title page
BEFORE (reader2.html.prefront)      35             3             1
AFTER                               39             0             0
```

The four:

```
16SamA03   80 ¶ above its title page
40KhuA21    2 ¶
20KhuA01    1 ¶   — p-20KhuA01-37, the paragraph in the screenshot
21KhuA02   NO TITLE PAGE ANYWHERE (127 of its ¶ drawn)
```

**21KhuA02's was reported by `check_layout.js` and excused.** It printed `incipit x0` and the rule
deliberately scopes itself to "anchors whose paragraph was actually rendered", so an anchor no
canon paragraph links to was treated as a hole in the link map rather than a defect. It is both.

### THE FIX IS THE READER'S OWN GUARANTEE, NOT A LINK REPAIR

Where a single work is being shown, its front matter is emitted ONCE at the top of the stream and
suppressed at its anchor (`_topFront`). That makes the rule independent of the link map, which is
the right dependency: **a book opening with its title page is not something the link join should
be able to break.** The link defects are recorded here and belong with the link rebuild;
`build_links.py` is still not to be re-run.

### !!! THE FIX EXPOSED A SECOND DEFECT, AND check_layout CAUGHT IT

With the front matter drawn at the top, 05Kankha FAILED `duplicate-heading :: Dvemātikāpāḷi`: the
volume's booktitle line and the `sections` entry at the SAME anchor are the same string, so the
two were drawn adjacent and read as the "two titles" artifact. It had been invisible only because
the anchor was never reached in the openings check_layout grades.

**Measured over every volume before suppressing anything: exactly THREE entries in TWO volumes are
in that state** — 05Kankha ord0 `Dvemātikāpāḷi`, 04VinA04 ord0 and ord186 `Vinayapiṭaka` — so a
sections entry that repeats a line of its own title stack is now dropped in `layerFront`, and
nothing else can move.

### A STATIC CENSUS EXISTS TOO, AND IT OVER-REPORTS — THE LIVE PROBE IS THE AUTHORITY

`_khua/_front/before_the_book.py` walks the maps instead of the reader: cheap, no jsdom, and it
flags **12** volumes where the live probe confirms **4**. It does not model the reader's dedup or
the TARGET volume's `hide`, so a paragraph it counts as drawn may never reach the page. Use it as
a pre-filter and confirm with `front_first.js`; do not quote its number.

### ALSO MEASURED, AND NOT FIXED: FOUR BOOKS OPEN THE WRONG CANON VOLUME

The book node resolves through `rev[anchor].canon`, and for four volumes that is not the canon
volume the work mostly hangs off, so the first screenful is a minority slice of the work:

```
vol        opens      ¶ there   main host   ¶ there   ¶ total
15SamA02   13Sam02        96    12Sam01        100      196
40KhuA21   22Khu05       331    23Khu06      1,222    1,565
49AbhiA02  33Abhi05        4    30Abhi02       193      259
50AbhiA03  31Abhi03      111    32Abhi04       288      650
```

The title page is now first in each of them, which is what was asked; **which host a book opens
into is a separate question and belongs with the link rebuild.**

```
check_layout  all 39 commentary volumes: 0 layout issues
              (51Vism01 / 52Vism02 not driveable — no reverse map; unchanged either side)
```

## 21KhuA02 — THE DHAMMAPADA COMMENTARY IS A `katha` VOLUME, AND ITS CORPUS SWALLOWS THREE WHOLE STORIES (2026-07-28s)

**39 of the 52 commentary volumes are built and navigable; 13 remain, and all thirteen are
Khuddaka commentaries.** Dhammapadaṭṭhakathā, first bhāga — vaggas 1-8, Dhammapada verses 1-115,
one book, printed 8-454. Third volume built off the 2026-07-28p rebuild batch.

```
corpus    127 ¶ -> 138 (2026-07-28p)      bad pages 61 -> 2
build     KATHĀ  printed units 127 / corpus ¶ 127   headings 103   colophons 113   prose ¶ 303
          gāthā blocks 41   [OK]   FIRST RUN on the 1:1 pairing
body      (7 453, 0-138)   17 / 17 / 39 / 0   at minw 4; 18 chunks at minw 2 and 1; reading-order 1
          hyclass: 17 of 17 explained by the line-end hyphen alone, and 36 of the 39
          render-not-in-PDF are the SAME 18 breaks seen from the other side
bold      109 with bold, 0 unaligned
apparatus 906 stored | 919 printed cells | 0 spliced | 2 variants-not-stored | 0 xrefs
nav       9 top / 94 sections   mātikā 103   0 missing   0 out of order   [OK]
layout    0 layout issues  [PARTIAL: 92% of ¶ examined]   _navdup PASS 23,110 rows   regress 55/55
census    0 orphaned side-map entries corpus-wide
```

### IT IS A `katha` VOLUME, AND IT NEEDS BOTH HALVES OF `units_may_be_verse`

The obvious guess from the Jātaka commentary is the VERSE path — the units are the canon's own
numbered gāthās, and the commentary hangs off them. **That is wrong here, and the page says so.**
A vatthu opens with its Dhammapada verse cited as a lemma, and the edition sets that lemma in
EITHER of two ways:

```
p9    1. Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā,               p23   2. Manopubbaṅgamā dhammāti dutiyagāthāpi
         Manasā ce paduṭṭhena, …                    Sāvatthiyaṁyeva Maṭṭhakuṇḍaliṁ ārabbha …
      (the gāthā itself, pādas below)              (PROSE naming it, back at the body column)
```

So the number opens PROSE as often as it opens a gāthā — `katha` with `units_may_be_verse`, and
the DEFAULT geometric test (the line after the number sits at a strictly greater indent) separates
the two exactly. **`printed units 127 / corpus ¶ 127` on the first run is the proof.**
`n_scope: 'book'` is measured, not assumed: the Dhammapada's numbers do not reset per vagga —
they run 1-115 straight through the eight vaggas, none missing, and only verses 1 and 2 are
numbered twice in the corpus.

### NINE PRINTED LINES READ AS HEADINGS, AND THE NINTH IS A NEW SHAPE

Eight are the settled class — the LAST PĀDA of a display block quotation closing with the
CITATION DASH (12MaA03, 23KhuA04, 51Vism01, 20KhuA01). Six of the eight are in the Maṭṭhakuṇḍalī
story's verse dialogue, pp27-30, where the edition quotes the Petavatthu back and forth.
**`Tapantamādiccamivantalikkhe”ti1–` is the SAME pāda 51Vism01 and 52Vism02 needed**, differing
only in its footnote marker — which is exactly why a `headskip` literal cannot be shared.

**The ninth is the OPENING line of a block quotation, not its close.** p277 quotes a whole Udāna
sutta, and its first line hangs LEFT of the block's own body — `Ekaṁ samayaṁ Bhagavā Rājagahe
viharati Veḷuvane` at indent 10 above a body at 6 — with no comma, no terminal stop and exactly
SIX words, which is every `heads_by_form` test for a title. First time the class has been seen
from that end. Each of the nine is printed exactly once, checked against the edition.

### TWO COLOPHONS THE EDITION PRINTS WITHOUT A FULL STOP

`kat_is_colo` asks a colophon for a terminal stop, so both fell through and were read as headings.
**Counted on the page rather than guessed: the volume closes 8 vaggas and SEVEN of the eight end
`…vaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.` — only p218's `Cittavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā` is bare; and of its ~90
vatthu colophons only p23's `Cakkhupālattheravatthu paṭhamaṁ`, the volume's FIRST, is bare.** Both
are the edition's own slips, preserved as printed and named in `colofix`, which gives each its
right role rather than merely denying it the wrong one. Headings 114 -> 103, colophons 111 -> 113.

Together the `headskip` and `colofix` declarations took the body gate from
**17 / 22 / 39 / 0 with reading-order 3** to **17 / 17 / 39 / 0 with reading-order 1**.

### !!! THE CORPUS SWALLOWS THREE WHOLE STORIES INTO THE PRECEDING VERSE'S PARAGRAPH

Three corpus paragraphs run straight past a vatthu colophon and a centred vatthu heading and
absorb the WHOLE of the next story:

```
ord25   residue 1030 words, 933 of them the next vatthu   -> 9. Nandattheravatthu
ord68   residue 4570 words, 4456 of them the next vatthu  -> 8. Visākhāvatthu
ord71   residue  939 words,  826 of them the next vatthu  -> 10. Mahākassapattherapiṇḍapātadinnavatthu
```

The seam is visible in the text itself — `…desanā mahājanassa sātthikā jātāti | yathāpi
puppharāsimhāti imaṁ dhammadesanaṁ Satthā…` — where the page has a colophon and a heading between
the two halves. **So the reader draws 4,456 words of the Visākhā story under verse 52's paragraph
and only then prints `8. Visākhāvatthu`.** These are exactly the three `render-not-in-PDF` entries
that are NOT the line-end hyphen, and they are the whole of the non-hyphen residue.

The nav does not lose anything to it — 103 of 103 mātikā entries resolve, 0 out of order, because
the heading still anchors to the following ordinal. **The defect is the body order, not the tree.**
Same family as 20KhuA01 ord24 (2026-07-28r): a corpus paragraph that does not break where the
edition breaks. **The fix is a corpus split with the re-key it implies; NOT done here, because
the batch was rebuilt and re-keyed on 2026-07-28p and a second rebuild would strand the links
again.** Whether the other twelve volumes of the batch carry the same shape is NOT measured — the
cheap test is `render-not-in-PDF` entries whose divergence offset is deep inside a long residue.

### TWO SPELLING DISAGREEMENTS BETWEEN THE MĀTIKĀ AND THE BODY

`errata`, mātikā reading -> body reading, neither corrected: `1. Meghiyattheravatthu` ->
`1. Meghiyattheravattha` (p189), `3. Aññatara-ukkaṇṭhitabhikkhuvatthu` ->
`3. Aññatara-ukkaṇḍhitabhikkhuvatthu` (p355).

### THE LINE-END HYPHEN IS THE WHOLE OF THIS VOLUME'S BODY-GATE RESIDUE

17 missing lines, 17 missing chunks and 36 of the 39 render-not-in-PDF are ONE class, and
`hyclass` explains 17 of 17. Every one is a VOWEL junction the edition hyphenates and the corpus
joined without the hyphen — `paṭhama-aggasāvaka` printed, `paṭhamaaggasāvaka` in the corpus;
likewise `mātāpitu-upaṭṭhānaṁ`, `bhikkhunī-upassaye`, `khandhadhātu-āyatana`, `bahi-āvāṭe`.
**The builder was taught the three-way join on 2026-07-27aj; `_khua/rebuild.py` was not**, and the
corpus is the side that is wrong here. Recorded, not chased — it is the same accepted residue the
Jātaka volumes were signed off with, and it is a rebuild question, not a build one.

### THE COLOPHON FRAME, READ AS A HEADING TEN TIMES — the 12MaA03 shape exactly

The edition closes every suttavaṇṇanā with a TWO-LINE colophon whose first line is the genitive
frame and whose second carries the stop (p200: `Paramatthajotikāya Khuddakapāṭhaṭṭhakathāya` /
`Tirokuṭṭasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.`), so the frame has no terminal punctuation and the form test
took it for a title. **Counted on the page, not estimated: the frame is printed TEN times — nine
as `…Khuddakapāṭhaṭṭhakathāya` and ONCE, closing the whole work, as `…Khuddakaṭṭhakathāya`
WITHOUT `pāṭha`.** Both readings are named in `colofix` and neither is folded to the other.
Headings 119 -> 109, colophons 23 -> 33: exactly the ten.

### FOUR QUOTED PĀDAS READ AS HEADINGS — the 12MaA03 / 23KhuA04 / 51Vism01 class

Each is the LAST PĀDA of a display block quotation whose citation runs on into the prose below
it, so the pāda closes with the CITATION DASH and not a stop. Declared in `headskip`; each is
printed exactly once (p19, p159, p159, p200) and each BECOMES the closing `vline` of its own
gāthā block, so nothing is suppressed and only the role changes. **The body gate went
1 / 4 / 2 / 0 with reading-order 1 to 0 / 1 / 0 / 0 with reading-order 0 on that change alone.**

### !!! A DEFECT IN EARLIER WORK: THE `heads_by_form` COLOPHON ESCAPE TAKES BODY PROSE

`kat_is_colo`'s `heads_by_form` branch lets a line be a colophon at ANY indent when NIDCOLO and
NIDSECT both match — the escape 31Abhi03 needed for a genuine colophon set at indent 7. But
NIDSECT matches `gāthā` inside "pañcamagāthāya" and `vagg` inside "Cīvaravaggassa", and NIDCOLO
matches an ordinal anywhere, so an ordinary body line four to six words long that happens to end
a page is claimed as a colophon.

**Measured over every volume in SPEC rather than argued** (`_khua/_probe20/coloescape.py`, which
renames the function in the source and wraps it — patching the imported module cannot work,
the build re-defines it on the way past):

```
51Vism01 2   43KhuA24 2   50AbhiA03 2   49AbhiA02 2
08DiA02 1  44KhuA25 1  46KhuA27 1  47KhuA28 1  14SamA01 1  16SamA03 1
03VinA03 1  06VinSg06 1  31Abhi03 1
                                   TOTAL 39 lines in 18 volumes
```

**Read on the printed page one at a time: TEN are genuine colophons and TWENTY-NINE, in
FOURTEEN volumes, are ordinary body prose in the wrong role** — 05Kankha's
`Andhakāravaggassa paṭhame rattandhakāreti ratti-andhakāre1.`, 48AbhiA01's
`Tatiyapadaniddeso uttānatthoyeva.`, 51Vism01's `sesakasiṇaniddeso. Chaṭṭho asubhaniddeso. …`
(which does not even begin a sentence), and twenty-six more. Every one of the fourteen volumes
is already signed off. The body gate reads 0 on all of them: the text is present and contiguous,
only its role is wrong.

**NOT FIXED HERE, and deliberately.** No single form test separates the two — 08DiA02's
`Tatiyagāthāya anūpavādoti vācāya kassaci anupavadanaṁ.` has a capital, no internal stop and no
terminal ordinal, and is prose; 31Abhi03's genuine one has the same shape. A rule that moves
eighteen shipped volumes needs its own measured before/after pass, not a corner of this session.
**20KhuA01's own instance is the one remaining body-gate chunk** (`annapānamhī”ti pañcamagāthāya
pubbaddhañca āha.`, p193, the tail of a prose sentence) — left in place, not papered over with a
per-volume key that the coming rule would strand.

### !!! A SECOND DEFECT IN EARLIER WORK: 2,426 LINK TARGETS LAND ON A HIDDEN ORDINAL

The standing rule is "before hiding a paragraph, ask whether anything links to it" (42KhuA23,
2026-07-28n). Asked in the other direction — over every `linksk/*.links.json` against every
`hide/` — it does not hold:

```
36Abhi08 -> 50AbhiA03   144      18Khu01  -> 20KhuA01    1
37Abhi09 -> 50AbhiA03   354      20Khu03  -> 45KhuA26    1
38Abhi10 -> 50AbhiA03  1052      27Khu10  -> 45KhuA26    2
39Abhi11 -> 50AbhiA03   531
40Abhi12 -> 50AbhiA03   341                    TOTAL 2,426
```

**2,422 of them are into THREE paragraphs of 50AbhiA03** — ord726 `1. Kusalattika
1. Paṭiccavāravaṇṇanā`, ord727 `1. Paccayānuloma 1. Vibhaṅgavāra`, ord747 `1. Paccayānuloma
2. Saṅkhyāvāra` — every one a leaked heading the builder hides so the printed stream can supply
it. A hidden paragraph takes its link targets with it, so those links resolve to nothing. The
other four are the same shape: leaked headings, a title line and a colophon. **This belongs with
the open link rebuild** — the join is "number proposes, content confirms", and a target that is a
heading should resolve to the first VISIBLE paragraph of the section it opens.

### THE MĀTIKĀ CANNOT BE A GATE HERE, AND THE REASON IS A CORPUS DEFECT

Ten mātikā entries — `Ekaṁ nāma kintipañhavaṇṇanā` through `Dasa nāma kintipañhavaṇṇanā`, the
Kumārapañha's ten answers — are printed as CENTRED BODY HEADINGS (p81, p83 … p92) and the tree
cannot hold them. **The corpus holds printed pp63-74 as ONE paragraph: ord24, 18,719 characters,
with all ten headings inside its text.** A `sections/` entry is keyed by ORDINAL, so there is no
ordinal for a heading in mid-paragraph, and the reader draws twelve printed pages as a single
block with its headings buried in the prose.

`matika_gate: False`, with the reason written into the SPEC. **NOT `matika_drop`** — the edition
really prints these ten, and dropping them would silence the gate and leave the defect
unrecorded, which is exactly the mistake withdrawn on 37KhuA18 (2026-07-28m). 108 of the 118
entries resolve and the centred gate still holds at 9 of 9. **The fix is a corpus split at those
ten heads with the re-key that implies; it is the first thing to weigh for this volume when the
reading model is settled.** Whether other volumes carry the same shape has NOT been measured.

### FOUR SPELLING DISAGREEMENTS BETWEEN THE MĀTIKĀ AND THE BODY

Recorded as `errata`, mātikā reading -> body reading, neither side corrected:
`Bhedābhadaphaladīpanā` -> `Bhedābhedaphaladīpanā` (p25), `Aṭṭhuppatti` -> `Aṭṭhuppati` (p80),
`Yānīdhāhigāthāvaṇṇanā` -> `Yānīdhātigāthāvaṇṇanā` (p157), `Suttaṭṭhupatti` ->

### THE VOLUME NEEDED TWO READERS, AND THAT IS WHY THE FOURTH READER EXISTS

36KhuA17 opens with the Ganthārambhakathā and the whole Nidānakathā — **118 printed pages before
the first numbered jātaka**, held as TWELVE corpus paragraphs with no numbered anchor anywhere.
On the verse path every one of their headings waits for a verse to attach to, so all nine piled up
above jātaka 1 and **the prose drew BEFORE its own headings**. Declared as two books, the first in
`heads` mode:

```python
 'books': [('Ganthārambhakathā + Nidānakathā', 11, 120,  0,  12, None, 'heads'),
           ('Jātakaṭṭhakathā',                121, 548, 12, 193, None)],
```

**The book tuple's 7th element is the mode; the 6th is `lastv`.** A six-element tuple ending in
`'heads'` silently declares `lastv='heads'` and runs the VERSE path — it reported
`verses paired 0` and looked like a reader that had found nothing.

The split point is the printed page, not the corpus: `1. Ekakanipāta / 1. Apaṇṇakavagga /
1. Apaṇṇakajātakavaṇṇanā` are printed together on p121, eight pages before jātaka 1's gāthā, so
book 2 starts at p121 and ord12 — with p11-128 the nipāta head fell inside book 1 and the volume
reported `nipātas pdf 0 / corpus 0 / expected 1`.

### !!! A DEFECT IN EARLIER WORK: A `before` RESIDUE THAT REPRINTS A WHOLE CORPUS PARAGRAPH

Found while building this volume and **it is in every Jātaka volume already signed off**. Where a
jātaka's narrative is BOTH a corpus paragraph and the next unit's `before` residue, the reader
draws it twice. **The body gate cannot see it**: `before` is stored one printed LINE per entry, so
each line occurs once in the printed stream and the corpus paragraph occurs once too — nothing is
`rendered-too-often`. It was found by asking the maps directly.

**Extent, counted over every volume's verse map rather than estimated — 58 entries in 7 volumes:**

```
37KhuA18 13    36KhuA17 12    38KhuA19 11    42KhuA23 11    39KhuA20 5    40KhuA21 5
01VinA01  1  — and that one is harmless: its corpus side is already hidden
```

So **45 paragraphs were being drawn twice in five volumes that had been signed off**, plus 12 in
this one and 1 in 01VinA01 that never rendered.

Fixed under the per-volume key `no_reprint` (renamed from the `udd_in_corpus` of 2026-07-28n,
which is the same rule seen from one side). It now covers three shapes, all measured:

* an **uddāna block line** that is a whole corpus paragraph — 28 corpus-wide, 26 already hidden;
* a **single residue line** that is a whole corpus paragraph — 1 corpus-wide;
* a **whole residue list whose JOIN** is a whole corpus paragraph — 58 corpus-wide.

In every case the ordinal must differ from the entry's own, and the corpus paragraph must be
VISIBLE — a hidden one draws nothing and the residue is then the only copy. Re-measured after the
rebuild: **0 remain.** Body gates over all six affected volumes held or improved and **not one
missing line appeared**, which is what proves the dropped copy was a reprint: 42KhuA23 15 -> 11
render-not-in-PDF, 37KhuA18 42 -> 36, 38KhuA19 34 -> 32, 39KhuA20 / 40KhuA21 / 41KhuA22 unchanged.

### !!! A SECOND DEFECT IN EARLIER WORK: 05Kankha's BOOKS 3 AND 4 HAVE HAD NO HOMAGE

`head_build` hides a corpus paragraph the printed stream already supplies — and it was hiding the
paragraph that ANCHORS the incipit. A side-map entry on a hidden ordinal never renders (the
standing trap), so the homage went with it, and the booktitle stack written to the same ordinal
later would have gone too.

**Census over every side-map: FOUR entries corpus-wide were anchored to a hidden ordinal, all four
written by this reader** — 36KhuA17 ord0 (incipit AND the whole title stack) and **05Kankha ord591
and ord799, which have been rendering with no homage since 2026-07-28f**. The reader already
strips an embedded homage from a VISIBLE paragraph that carries an incipit, which is what every
verse-path volume relies on, so the fix is simply never to hide the incipit's anchor. Re-measured:
**0 orphaned side-map entries corpus-wide.** 05Kankha re-gated at its own arguments —
`(19 375, 0-932)` — still **0 / 0 / 3 / 0 at minw 4, 2 and 1**.

### THE VERSE-PATH `headskip` GAP IS NOW MEASURED FROM BOTH SIDES

36KhuA17 draws two printed lines as headings that are not: `Jātakaṭṭhakathā` (ord1, a running
header, in the HEADS book) and `Jetavanamahāvihāre viharanto kathesi. Kaṁ pana ārabbha ayaṁ kathā`
(ord13, ordinary prose, in the VERSE book).

* The verse-book line **cannot be declared at all** — `kat_is_head` is never called on that path,
  so the builder REFUSES the literal as never met. Third volume to want this (40KhuA21, 42KhuA23).
* The heads-book line **can** be declared, and doing so is worse: `Jātakaṭṭhakathā` is the reader's
  own delimiter, and skipping it drove located from 3092 to 377 with 2721 residue and the book
  went **FATAL**. Withdrawn, and the measurement is in the SPEC comment so it is not retried.

The nav does not repeat the mistake — both are in its `head_skip`, which is checked against the
edition (`printed 1 time(s)` for each) so it cannot silently stop matching. **The body still draws
them; that is the open defect and it is not papered over.**

### THREE SEPARATE PATHS DRAW ONE PRINTED LINE TWICE, AND ALL THREE ARE NOW MEASURED

Every one of the three was found by `rendered-too-often` surviving `_abhia/dupclass.py`, and every
fix was measured over ALL volumes before it went in.

**(a) The udāna lead-in fallback, when the group already contains the lead-in.** With no `before`,
the reader lifts the narrative lead-in out of the corpus paragraph so it stands above the gāthā
the side-map supplies. A Jātaka unit whose WHOLE printed paragraph — gāthā, gloss and lead-in
together — is one group needs nothing lifted, and the fallback drew it a second time.
**Measured: the fallback fires on 76 entries corpus-wide; the group already contains the lead-in
in 2, both in 41KhuA22 (ord143, ord804).** Guarded in BOTH `verify_render_vs_pdf.render_parts` and
`reader2.html`'s `block()` — they must agree or the gate stops modelling the reader. Backups
`.prelead` on both; `BUILD` is now `2026-07-28n-lead`.

**(b) An uddāna block line that is already a whole corpus paragraph.** 42KhuA23 prints two
narrative lead-ins immediately after a kaṇḍa colophon; the corpus holds each as its own unnumbered
paragraph AND `place_centre` absorbed the printed line into the block.
**Measured: 28 uddāna block lines corpus-wide are also a whole corpus paragraph, and the corpus
side is ALREADY HIDDEN in 26 of them** — the builder's leaked-heading rule catches colophons but
not narrative prose. Only 42KhuA23 ord686/ord817 were drawn twice.

**Hiding was NOT available and that is the interesting part.** The obvious fix — hide the corpus
paragraph, as the other 26 are — would have stranded two links: **23Khu06 links to 42KhuA23#687
and #818**, and a hidden paragraph takes its side-map entries and its link targets with it. So the
BLOCK gives the line up and the corpus keeps it. Checked before acting, not after.

**(c) A `before` residue line that is already a whole corpus paragraph.** Same shape, different
path (42KhuA23 ord1646's `before` is corpus ord1645). **Measured over every volume's verse map:
exactly ONE line corpus-wide is in that state.**

Both (b) and (c) are behind ONE new per-volume SPEC key, `udd_in_corpus`, declared on 42KhuA23
alone — so no other volume's maps can move, and `regress.py` 55/55 byte-identical confirms it.
Backup `pipeline/build_khu_volume.py.preudd`.

### THE PENDING "VERSE-PATH `headskip` EQUIVALENT" IS HALF-ANSWERED

2026-07-28l recorded two volumes wanting the same shared-machinery key from two directions:
40KhuA21 wants a verse-path `headskip`, and 42KhuA23 wants a way to say "this printed line is
prose, not a centred block". **`udd_in_corpus` answers 42KhuA23's half, and answers it by
MEASUREMENT rather than by a literal** — it does not ask the editor to name the line, it asks the
corpus whether the line is already there. 40KhuA21's half is still open, and it is a different

### AN ERRATUM THAT IS A JĀTAKA NUMBER (38KhuA19)

The mātikā gives the Cetiyajātaka as **422**; the body heads it **442**. 422 is the canon's number,
so it is the BODY that slipped — but both readings are preserved and neither side is corrected.
Recorded as `errata`, the second of the volume's two.

### !!! A MĀTIKĀ RANGE CAN OVERSHOOT INTO THE BODY, AND THE SYMPTOM LOOKS LIKE A MISSING SECTION

37KhuA18's SPEC declared `matika: (3, 10)`. The range is **INCLUSIVE at both ends**, and PDF page
index 10 is the volume's FIRST BODY PAGE. Its opening stack — `Khuddakanikāya` (running header),
`2. Dukanipāta`, `1. Daḷhavagga`, `1. Rājovādajātakavaṇṇanā (151)` — was therefore read as four
more mātikā entries, appended AFTER the true last entry.

`matika_headers` did not filter `Khuddakanikāya` out because it drops only a line seen on **three
or more** of the range's pages, and this one is printed on exactly one. So the nav reported:

```
REFUSED — in the mātikā, absent from the tree: 'Khuddakanikāya'
REFUSED — a centred mātikā group head absent from the tree: 'Khuddakanikāya'
3 out of order
```

The three "out of order" were the volume's own first three body headings, matched backwards
because the forward pointer had already been driven to the end of the head stream by the reprinted
stack. **A trailing mātikā entry that is a running header is the signature of a range that runs
one page long.** The first fix I reached for — `matika_drop: ['Khuddakanikāya']` — made the gate
say `[OK]` while leaving three phantom entries in the stream and the pointer still wrong; it was
withdrawn. Correcting the range to `(3, 9)` took the mātikā from 185 raw entries to 181, the gate
to `0 out of order`, and the centred-head count from 18 printed to the 16 that are real.

**Check the last few entries of a mātikā before declaring `matika_drop`.** `matika_drop` is for a
line the edition really prints inside its mātikā; it is the wrong tool for a range that has eaten a
body page, and it hides the defect instead of fixing it.

### THE FOOTNOTE MARKER IN A HEADING, THIRD OCCURRENCE

37KhuA18's body prints `6. Kurudhammajātakavaṇṇanā1 (276)` — a footnote marker set inside the
heading itself. Same class as 43KhuA24's `12. Cūḷabyūha1suttaniddesavaṇṇanā`. Declared as
`errata` (mātikā reading → body reading) rather than stripped by rule: a digit glued to a heading
is not always a marker, and the edition's own reading stays on the page either way.

### `_abhia/ooo.py` NEEDS THE MĀTIKĀ RANGE AND A LAYOUT FILE, NOT THE SPEC PATH

Invocation, for the next time it is wanted:

```
pdftotext -layout atthakatha-unicode/37KhuA18.pdf _khua/37lay.txt
OOO_SPEC='{"errata":{"...":"..."}}' python3 _abhia/ooo.py 37KhuA18 3 9 \
    'Jātakaṭṭhakathā (Dutiyo bhāgo)' _khua/37lay.txt
```

`OOO_SPEC` is a JSON **string**, not a path, and the tool does NOT apply `matika_drop` — a dropped
literal shows up as `NOT FOUND` once per printing. 37KhuA18's fifteen `NOT FOUND 'Uddānagāthā'`
are exactly the fifteen vagga uddānas already declared dropped, and nothing else remained.

### `_navdup.js` IS AT THE REPO ROOT, NOT UNDER `site/reader/`

`node site/reader/_navdup.js` fails with a `requireStack` error that reads like a broken script.
It is `node _navdup.js`, run from the repo root. Current result: **118 volumes carry a nav node,
161 top-level nodes, 22,680 tree rows checked, 0 adjacent duplicates, 0 duplicate book nodes
[PASS]**; `MULTITOP_PENDING` stays at eight, every one an unbuilt Ṭīkā.
