### !!! `headskip` IS A KATHĀ-PATH KEY AND THE VERSE PATH HAS NO EQUIVALENT

40KhuA21 renders two lines of ordinary prose as headings: `Khantivādijātaka Mātaṅgajātaka
Bharujātaka Sarabhaṅgajātaka` (p104) and `Imassa panatthassa dīpanatthaṁ Khantivādijātaka1`
(p124) — the commentary telling the reader which other jātakas to recite at that point. The
`jātaka` stem takes them into `HEADTXT`.

**Declaring `headskip` made the builder REFUSE**: `headskip literal(s) never met as a heading in
40KhuA21`. That is the guard working exactly as designed — `kat_is_head` consults `headskip` and
the verse path never reaches it. The declaration was withdrawn and the defect RECORDED instead:
both lines are present, in printed order, and no text is lost; only their role is wrong.

### AND 42KhuA23 HAS THREE REAL DUPLICATIONS — **THIS VOLUME IS NOT SIGNED OFF**

`rendered-too-often 3`, and unlike 49AbhiA02's these **survive `dupclass.py`**: applying the
gate's own line-end join leaves all three standing.

```
rendered 2x, printed 1x:  taṁ sutvā mahāsatto pitarā saddhiṁ sallapanto imaṁ gāthamāha
rendered 2x, printed 1x:  tato nāgarājā mahāsattaṁ disvā gāthamāha
rendered 2x, printed 1x:  mahāsatto pana paṭinivatto atha naṁ puṇṇako āha
```

Traced: each printed lead-in line is placed in the `uddana` side-map after one paragraph **and is
also the next corpus paragraph's whole text** — `ord817 [udd]` and `ord818 [text]` hold the same
sentence. So the reader draws it twice, once as a centred block and once as prose. Three
instances in 1,690 paragraphs; **no text is lost, but the render is wrong and the volume should
not be called clean.**

### TWO VOLUMES NOW WANT THE SAME SHARED-MACHINERY FIX

40KhuA21 wants a verse-path `headskip`; 42KhuA23 wants a way to say "this printed line is prose,
not a centred block". They are the same key from two directions: **a per-volume literal that
demotes a line the verse path has mis-typed.** One volume asking is not evidence; two is. It is
still shared machinery and still needs measuring over all 40 canon volumes plus the built
commentary ones before it goes in — but it is now a named piece of work rather than a suspicion,
and the four remaining Jātaka volumes will probably raise it again.

Also noted, not chased: 42KhuA23's bold map has **5 unaligned paragraphs**, the first non-zero
`unaligned` in this layer. Every other volume this week returned 0.

**This is the first commentary volume `check_layout.js` has reported as `ok` rather than PARTIAL** —

### THE READER QUESTION, ANSWERED ON THE FIRST TRY

Every commentary volume so far has been `katha` — a number opening prose — or, once, `heads`. The
Jātaka commentary is neither. **Its units are the QUOTED GĀTHĀS carrying the canon's own verse
numbers, pādas set below the number, with the commentary's prose hanging off them** — which is the
`verse` reader, the same one 22Khu05 and 23Khu06 take, with `n_scope: 'nipata'`.

Declared that way it paired **6/6/6 nipātas and 1149 verses at the first attempt, with 0 corpus
splices repaired and 0 corpus paragraphs never matched.** The nipāta count came from the printed
heads — 10. Dasaka, 11. Ekādasaka, 12. Dvādasaka, 13. Terasaka, 14. Pakiṇṇaka, 15. Vīsati,
continuing the earlier volumes' numbering.

**SEVEN VOLUMES TAKE THIS SHAPE: 36KhuA17 to 42KhuA23 are Jātakaṭṭhakathā I-VII**, so this is
nearly a third of everything that remains and the recipe for all seven is now proven rather than
guessed. Their nipāta counts and ordinal bounds still have to be read off each volume's own
printed heads — that is the only per-volume work.

### THE GATE'S 19 CHUNKS ARE CONTIGUITY, NOT LOSS

`PDF-lines-missing` is 7 and `hyclass.py` explains all 7. `rendered-too-often` is 0. The 19
chunks and 22 reverse entries are corpus paragraphs that join text the printed page separates —
the Jātaka's own long narrative running through a verse block — and they sit in the same band as
48AbhiA01 (19-25 / 48) on a volume of comparable size. **No text is lost and nothing is
duplicated.**

### THE RECIPE IS NOW ROUTINE, AND WORTH STATING AS ONE LINE

`scout extent` → `_khua/rebuild.py <VOL> <LO> <HI>` → write the corpus → SPEC (`katha`,
`heads_by_form`, `pada_runon`) → build → booktitle → REBUILD → body gate → `hyclass.py` on
whatever it reports → `corpus_pre` + `relink_abhia.py` → `extract_bold --force` → `rebuild_apparatus
--write` → heads-vs-mātikā diff → nav → `_navdup` / `regress` / `check_layout`.

Neither volume needed a new SPEC key and neither needed the fourth reader: **`katha` paired
printed units to corpus paragraphs 1:1 in both**, 92/92 and 209/209, which is the check that the
rebuild restored the right things and nothing else.

### THE REBUILD, AND WHAT THE SHIPPED CORPUS ACTUALLY HELD

The volume's word index runs **70 printed pages**, and the shipped corpus carried 232 paragraphs
of it — two of them NUMBERED, so they counted as body units
(`1. 331; Saṁ-Ṭṭha 2. 41)  236  (Khu 2. 344)  284 …`). At the other end it was missing printed
pp328-330, the closing uddāna gāthās and the nigamana. `_khua/rebuild.py` LOADS `_abhia/rebuild.py`
and swaps its output directory rather than copying it, so there is still one implementation.

**The re-key needed a hand-made baseline and it is worth knowing why.** `relink_rebuilt.py`
asserts that the old corpus is exactly the new one's NUMBERED paragraphs; here old is 205 and new
numbered is 203, because the two back-matter paragraphs were numbered and are now gone. Checked
first that **no link anywhere targets ord203 or ord204** — 164 distinct link targets, the highest
being ord202 — and then wrote `_fnprobe/corpus_pre/47KhuA28.json` as the first 203 paragraphs.
203/203 re-keyed, 0 mismatches. `extract_bold --force` 201 with bold, 0 unaligned (backed up
first this time). `rebuild_apparatus` 602 stored -> 529 anchored, **0 unanchored**, and the gate
then reads 529 against 535 printed cells with **nothing lost**.

### WHAT THE VOLUME NEEDED

Two `colofix` literals — the frame `Saddhammappakāsiniyā Paṭisambhidāmaggaṭṭhakathāya` eight
times and the closing `Saddhammappakāsinī nāma` — and two `headskip` citation-dash pādas. One of
them, `Tapantamādiccamivantalikkhe”ti3–`, is the `Padumaṁ yathā kokanadaṁ` verse Mahāpanthaka
gives Cūḷapanthaka: **the second volume this session to need that same verse**, after 52Vism02.
The literal differs between them (`…likkheti2–` there, `…likkhe”ti3–` here) — the printed line
including its footnote marker, which is why these can never be shared between volumes.

**Nothing else. The mātikā was fully covered at the first attempt: 77 entries, 0 with no head.**

### THE NAV'S TOP LEVEL IS NOT UNIFORM, AND THAT IS THE PAGE'S DOING

This volume opens IN THE MIDDLE of a vagga — 46KhuA27 ends inside the Mahāvagga's Ñāṇakathā — so
the mātikā's first five entries are that kathā's remaining ñāṇa-niddesas, numbered **68 to 72-73**
continuing its own count, and only then do the Mahāvagga's kathās 2-10 begin. The two later
vaggas ARE printed as centred heads. The tops follow the page rather than normalising it.

**The level-1 pattern had to be widened and the child counts are what caught it.** Written
`\S*kathāvaṇṇanā$` it missed `6. Paṭisambhidākathā` and `7. Dhammacakkakathā`, which the edition
sets without the `-vaṇṇanā`, and both fell a rung — the Yuganaddhavagga showed **8** children
where its mātikā lists **10**. Widened to `\S*kathā(?:vaṇṇanā)?$` it reads 10, and their own
sub-counts (Paṭisambhidākathā 4, Dhammacakkakathā 2) match the mātikā too. The tops are consumed
before the level test, so the vagga-1 kathās that share the shape are unaffected.

### TWO PRINTED HEADINGS `HEADNUM` CANNOT READ, AND WHY THE NAV FOUND THEM

The nav REFUSED twice before it passed, and both refusals were real:

* `1 -pa- 4. Methunadhammasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā` (p312) writes the **peyyāla into the range**.
* `8-9-10. Sikkhamāna-ummaddāpanādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā` (p371) is a **triple range** where every
  other heading in the volume gives a pair — and the volume's own mātikā gives the pair,
  `8-10.`, for this one too.

Neither number is a form `HEADNUM` accepts, so each was read as BODY TEXT, located into its
paragraph and never became a section. Nothing was lost and the body gate stayed 0/0/3/0 — **only
the nav's mātikā gate could see it**, which is the third time this project has been able to say
that. `headfix` names both; the readings are untouched and the range difference is an erratum.

### THE LAYER QUESTION IS SETTLED, AND THE FACTS ARE THE EDITION'S OWN

Printed p20 opens **`Dvemātikāpāḷi`** — the two pātimokkhas, each with its own homage title page,
**46% of the printed body** — and printed p102 opens `Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī-aṭṭhakathā`, which is what
the cover titles the whole volume (`Bhikkhupātimokkhapāḷiyā ceva Bhikkhunipātimokkhapāḷiyā ca
Saṁvaṇṇanābhūtā`). **Censused: the Dvemātikāpāḷi appears NOWHERE in the 40 canon volumes** — the
probe is the uposatha `Sammajjanī padīpo ca` verse, found in none of them. So this resource holds
that canonical text only inside a commentary-layer volume.

**DECIDED: the volume stays in the `commentary` layer** — that is what it is as published — **and
the nav names the two halves for what they are, so the provenance is visible.** `manifest.json`
carries one layer per volume; making it per-book is a separate, scoped change and was NOT made.

### THE FOURTH READER: `mode='heads'`, HEADING-DELIMITED PROSE

The other three readers all pair a printed ANCHOR against a corpus paragraph. This volume has
FIVE numbered units in 275 printed pages, and in its first two books the mismatch runs the other
way because the pātimokkha's SIKKHĀPADA numbers are read as unit numbers. **So the anchor is the
text itself:** a printed body line is located in the corpus paragraph that contains it, searching
**forward only** from the last paragraph already located — the printed stream and the corpus run
in the same order, which is both why forward-only is correct and what disambiguates a repeated
line.

MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN (`_kankha/probe2.py`, `probe4.py`): 383 printed headings, **383
anchored, 0 unanchored**; 8,996 of 8,999 printed body lines located; 930 corpus paragraphs, 927
touched, and the 3 that are not are the two homages and one leaked colophon.

**IT REFUSES RATHER THAN SKIPS.** An untouched corpus paragraph that is not a homage, heading or
colophon is reported by ordinal, and more than 2% of a book is FATAL. All four books report **0**.

### A RULE MEASURED AND THEN REJECTED

With the book bounds WRONG, one ten-character printed line (`veditabbaṁ.`) matched a paragraph
past the one it belonged to, and the forward pointer could never come back — **121 of book 4's 131
paragraphs were lost to a single short line.** The obvious fix is a minimum key length below which
a line may not move the pointer. Swept over 0/12/16/20/24/30/40 with the bounds CORRECTED it
changes nothing at all — 3 untouched and 3 residue at every value. **The defect was the bounds,
not the line, so the rule is not in.**

### THE BOOK BOUNDS WERE WRONG AND HAD BEEN SINCE THE SPEC WAS FIRST WRITTEN

`251/593/802` against the true `251/591/799`: out by two at the second seam and three at the
third, because the ordinals were taken from the page ranges rather than from the corpus paragraph
that carries each homage. It also ran to ord932, taking in **ord930-931, which are the printed
WORD INDEX** (`Padānukkamo Piṭṭhaṅko`, `Akatasahāyaṁ 295 …`). Now `backmatter: [930, 931]`.

### THREE FIXES THAT ARE NOT ABOUT THIS VOLUME

* **!!! `{'groups': []}` ON A RESIDUE ENTRY DESTROYS THE PARAGRAPH.** An entry carrying a `groups`
  key — even an EMPTY one — makes both `render_parts` and the reader take the VERSE branch, which
  renders `before + after` and NOT the corpus text. Written that way, this volume's THREE residue
  lines replaced the three paragraphs they were attached to and **the body gate reported 287
  printed lines missing that are in the corpus.** Without the key both take the prose branch and
  the gate goes to 0. The note about `[]` being truthy in JS has been in `render_parts` since
  26Khu09; this is the same trap from the writing side.
* **THE EDITION MISPRINTS ITS OWN HOMAGE FOR THE THIRD TIME.** `Namo Tassa` and `Bhagavatā` were
  the first two (2026-07-27j, where the misprint hid a whole book); this volume sets
  `SammāsamBuddhassa` with a capital B in THREE of its four books, so three of its four homages
  were being drawn as body prose. `HOMAGE` widened by one character class. **MEASURED old-vs-new
  by rebuilding every one of the 57 volumes that has side-maps: byte-identical**
  (`_kankha/homage_measure.py`).
* **`split_centre` was missing from the new reader.** 05Kankha sets
  `1. Musāvādavagga      1. Musāvādasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā` seven times; taken whole they rendered as
  one heading with a run of spaces in the middle. Fixed inside `head_build`, which is reached only
  by this volume.

### THREE THINGS ABOUT THIS VOLUME THAT ARE NOT IN ANY OTHER

**1. THE SECTION COLOPHON IS THREE OR FOUR LINES, NOT TWO.** Every other volume in the layer sets
a two-line frame with the stop on the second. Here:

```
Iti sādhujanapāmojjatthāya kate Visuddhimagge
[Samādhibhāvanādhikāre]
<X>niddeso nāma
<ordinal> paricchedo.
```

so up to three lines read as headings instead of one. Eleven `colofix` literals. **Only nine of
the eleven paricchedas need them** — the first two set `<X>niddeso nāma <ordinal> paricchedo.` on
ONE line with its stop, and the edition changes the setting after the Dhutaṅganiddesa and never
changes back. Two of the nine are the edition's own slips, PRESERVED as printed:
`Anussatikammaṭṭhānaniddesonāma` drops the space, and `Samādhiniddeso nāma4` carries a footnote
marker.

**2. A PRINTED HEADING WITH A COMMA IN IT.** `Sīlasaṁkilesa, vodāna` (p48) is one centred head for
two topics, and the volume's own mātikā lists it that way. `HEADTXT` is `[^,]*` by construction —
the comma rule is what keeps ordinary prose out of the heading test — so it can never be reached.
`headfix` names it. First of its kind in 22 volumes.

**3. !!! THE EDITION NUMBERS A SECTION HEADING IN SOME PARICCHEDAS AND NOT IN OTHERS.** The mātikā
numbers all 100 of its entries; the body prints the Sīlaniddesa's eleven sections UNNUMBERED
(`Sīlasarūpādikathā`) and the Dhutaṅganiddesa's fourteen NUMBERED
(`1. Paṁsukūlikaṅgakathā`), and goes on alternating. That is a typesetting inconsistency, not 99
misprints, and 99 `errata` would have buried the one entry that really is one.

**NEW GATED KEY `matika_unnum`** in `build_abhidhamma_nav.entry_folds`: also try the mātikā entry
with its leading `N.` removed. **MEASURED OLD-vs-NEW OVER ALL 33 VOLUMES THAT DECLARE A `matika`
RANGE (`_vism/measure.py`, seven nav modules): the two runs are BYTE-IDENTICAL, md5
`c605b75b…`** — it is off everywhere else by construction, and this proves it rather than
asserting it.

The evidence that it is a convention and not a way of hiding misprints: **with the number allowed
for, the mātikā and the heads stream are identical POSITION FOR POSITION, 100 against 100, with
exactly ONE difference** — `17. Pañcakajjhānakathā` against the body's `Pañcakajjhānaṁkathā`
(p163), an `ṁ` the word does not take. That is the volume's single `errata` entry; neither side is
corrected.

### THE NAV, AND THREE INDEPENDENT WITNESSES THAT IT IS RIGHT

`tops` are the eleven paricchedas — which ARE printed as centred headings, numbered 1..11 with no
gap — plus `Nidānādikathā`, which sits above the first pariccheda in both the mātikā and the body
and belongs to no niddesa. `levels` is two rungs deep because the printed mātikā is.

1. **Every top's child count equals its own mātikā group**: 11, 14, 7, 17, 10, 4, 7, 5, 5, 5, 3 —
   88 sections, plus 12 tops, is the 100 the mātikā lists.
2. **All 11 centred group heads resolve in the tree** (`matika_centred_gate`).
3. **The edition's own colophons close 11 of the 12 tops, and all 11 are in the tree.** Only
   `Nidānādikathā` has no colophon, so it is the one not testable that way.

An earlier attempt made the paricchedas `books` with ordinal bounds, on the belief that they were
never printed as headings — read off the colophons and the running headers. **That was wrong and
the child counts caught it**: the book version gave 12/15/8/18/… , one too many everywhere,
because the niddesa heading itself was being counted as a section of the book it opens. The tops
version reproduces the mātikā exactly.

### AN EDITION ERRATUM, RECORDED AND NOT CORRECTED

**`292.` is printed TWICE and `294.` is never printed.** Censused over all 364 paragraphs: the
numbers run 1-364, ord291 and ord293 both carry 292, and 294 occurs nowhere. The two cancel, which
is why the count comes out at exactly 364 and the build paired 364/364 at the first attempt — the
`katha` path pairs by position and keeps `n` only as a cross-check, which is the whole reason it
survived. ord293 is the Samādhiniddesa's opening paragraph (printed p336,
`Idāni āruppānantaraṁ ekā saññāti…`), i.e. **the duplicate falls exactly at a pariccheda
boundary.** The original reading stands; nothing is renumbered.

### !!! A GAP IN MY OWN METHOD, CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT

I re-ran `extract_bold.py 51Vism01 --force` **without taking a backup**, on a volume whose corpus
had NOT been rebuilt — so there was no cause to re-run it at all, and `extract_bold.py` had been
modified on 2026-07-27 22:01, after the shipped map was written on 07-23. The old map was
therefore gone and the change could not be diffed.

Closed the only way left: `13MaA04` and `09DiA03` both carry 07-23 maps and unchanged corpora, so
they were backed up and re-run under the current script. **Both byte-identical.** The 07-27 change
added the `--sections-only` path and does not move `.bold.json`, so 51Vism01's regenerated map is
the map that was there. **Back up before re-running a generator on a volume that did not need it.**

### WHAT IS OPEN ON THIS VOLUME

* **The presentation gate REFUSES it: `51Vism01 is in layer commentary and has no reverse map — the
  reader has no route into it`.** Expected and not a defect in this build — the Visuddhimagga
  comments on no single canon text, so no canon paragraph links to it. It is the link-coverage
  ceiling in its purest form, and it means **this volume is built, gated and currently
  undisplayable.** 52Vism02, 25VsmT01, 26VsmT02 and 09DiT02 are in the same position.
* **`rebuild_apparatus` was NOT run** — the corpus was not rebuilt, so the hold stands. Its dry run
  anchors 833 where 1017 are stored, a net loss of 184, so running it here would destroy data. But
  1017 stored against **843 printed cells** is itself a question nobody has asked: **more notes are
  stored than the page prints.** Recorded, not touched.
* `check_shape` rises from 310 blocks in 32 volumes to **352 in 33**: 51Vism01 contributes 42 of
  its 138 gāthā blocks. Proportionate to the layer (49AbhiA02 19 of 59, 02Vin02 16 of 79) and the
  same `display_prose` question, not a new defect.

### WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT THE PLAN

**A corpus rebuild is now the DEFAULT first step for a commentary volume, not an exception.** The
recipe already has it; what changes is the expectation. Two volumes skip it. And every rebuild
drags its three ordinal-keyed side-maps with it — links, bold, apparatus — as 2026-07-28a found
the hard way when all three Abhidhamma commentaries were left stale.

The two OK volumes are the natural next targets: **51Vism01** (the Visuddhimagga, 370 pages, no
rebuild needed) and **05Kankha**, whose corpus is fine and whose remaining obstacle is the
heading-delimited-prose reader and its layer question — the two are unrelated problems and the
screen has just removed one of them from 05Kankha's path.

### OPERATIONAL NOTE

**Background processes do not survive between device shell calls here** — `setsid nohup … &`
starts and is killed before the next call. Both sweeps are resumable by design
(`--budget SECONDS`, per-volume cache), so drive them in foreground chunks under the shell
timeout instead; `verify_all_volumes.py` took ~18 chunks of 8s and `verify_apparatus.py --all`
~13.

### !!! 49AbhiA02'S TWO `rendered-too-often` ARE NOT FABRICATIONS — READ ON THE PAGE

The previous entry refused to sign the volume off until those two duplications were read on the
printed page. They have been, and **both are printed repetitions of a formula, not fabrications**:

* `manasikārabahulīkāro, ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā` is printed **three** times — pp265, 266 and
  266 of the Bojjhaṅgapabba — once each for the pīti-, passaddhi- and samādhi-sambojjhaṅga.
* `sambojjhaṅgassa (bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya) bhāvanāya pāripūriyā` is printed **twice**, for the
  sati- and the upekkhā-sambojjhaṅga.

The gate said "printed 0×" and "printed 1×" because **the gate joins a hyphenated printed line to
the next and STRIPS the hyphen** (`out[-1][:-1] + t`), so the printed line the render holds —
which begins mid-word after `yoniso-` or `upekkhā-` — does not exist in the gate's printed stream
at all. `_abhia/dupclass.py` applies the gate's own join to the render and the count goes to
**0 duplications**.

### THE SAME MECHANISM EXPLAINS EVERY MISSING LINE IN THIS BLOCK — AND IT IS THE GATE, NOT THE TEXT

`_abhia/hyclass.py` asks, of each printed line the gate reports missing, whether the render holds
it once the gate's own line-end join is applied. Measured:

    48AbhiA01   12,790 printed lines,  23 reported missing,  23 explained,  0 not explained
    49AbhiA02   14,342 printed lines,  20 reported missing,  20 explained,  0 not explained
    50AbhiA03   13,449 printed lines,  20 reported missing,  20 explained,  0 not explained

**The builder and the body gate disagree about line-end hyphens.** Since the fix of 2026-07-27aj
the builder KEEPS the edition's hyphen where the continuation opens with a vowel (`hyjoin`); the
gate still strips it unconditionally. Neither loses text — but the gate's counts on any volume
with printed residue carry this class, and the two scratch tests above are how such a report is
discharged. **Do not read a `PDF-lines-missing` or `rendered-too-often` count on a rebuilt-corpus
volume without running them first.**

### !!! A DEFECT IN EARLIER WORK: `before` RESIDUE IS STORED ONE PRINTED LINE PER PARAGRAPH

Found while chasing the missing lines above, and it is **corpus-wide, not confined to this block**.
`add_prose` joins the `after` residue into paragraphs; the `before` path appends each printed LINE
as its own entry, and `reader2.html`'s `proseOne` draws every entry as its own
`<div class="gatha-after">`. So a printed paragraph in `before` renders as one block PER PRINTED
LINE, several of them ending in a dangling hyphen mid-word.

Measured over every volume with a verse map (`before` entry counts, and how many do not end in
sentence-final punctuation):

    total before entries          8,688
    broken mid-sentence           6,336
    broken mid-WORD at a hyphen     111
    volumes affected                 33   (canon AND commentary: 01Vin01, 03Vin03, 05Vin05,
                                           14Sam03, 15An01 … 48AbhiA01 2,015, 49AbhiA02 1,274)

Mean entry length tells the same story: `after` runs 325-690 characters a paragraph across every
volume, `before` runs 41-62 — one printed line. 18Khu01 is the single exception (512), so the
joined behaviour is reachable.

**NOT FIXED HERE.** It is shared machinery and the standing rule is to measure over every volume
before touching it; and a fix moves the render of 33 volumes, so every one of them has to be
re-gated. It is the next piece of work on the reading model, and it belongs with the deferred
reading-model item rather than ahead of it.

### THE TOP LEVEL IS A DIFFERENT SHAPE IN THREE OF THE ELEVEN BOOKS

The printed mātikā says which, and it is not uniform:

* most nipātas divide into PAṆṆĀSAKAS, and those are the tops;
* the **Sattaka** and **Ekādasaka** nipātas have none and go straight to VAGGAS;
* the **Ekakanipāta** has neither — twenty divisions, of which three carry inner vaggas of their
  own (`14. Etadaggavagga`, `15. Aṭṭhānapāḷi`, `16. Ekadhammapāḷi`) and the rest carry
  suttavaṇṇanās directly.

**In every book the tops run 1..N with no gap**, which is what proves none was dropped.

**!!! THE EKAKANIPĀTA'S LIST COULD NOT BE TAKEN FROM THE HEADS STREAM.** Its stream reprints
`14. Etadaggavagga`, `15. Aṭṭhānapāḷi` and `16. Ekadhammapāḷi` above EACH of their inner vaggas —
the ancestor-reprint pattern `subtree` already skips — so taking the stream's distinct
vagga-shaped heads in printed order put `14. Etadaggavagga` FIRST and lost 15 and 16 entirely,
because neither is named `…vagga`. Read off the MĀTIKĀ instead, where the twenty run in order.

### TWO HEADINGS ON ONE LINE, HIDDEN BY `head_paren`

19AnA03 p1737 sets `(6) 1. Nīvaraṇavagga       1. Āvaraṇasuttavaṇṇanā`. With `head_paren` on,
`kat_is_head` claims the WHOLE line before the `_is_double_head` branch can see it, so the vagga
and the suttavaṇṇanā arrived as one heading and the mātikā reported `1. Āvaraṇasuttavaṇṇanā`
absent from the tree. **A CENSUS, not a discovery one at a time**: over all three volumes exactly
ONE heading line carries a 3-or-more space run — 17AnA01 none, 18AnA02 none, this one this.
`split_literals`, whose key is matched with **internal whitespace COLLAPSED**, so the declaration
need not reproduce the run of spaces `pdftotext` happens to emit.

```
19AnA03  7 books  Pañcaka, Chakka, Sattaka, Aṭṭhaka, Navaka, Dasaka, Ekādasaka
```

**1 + 3 + 7 = the Aṅguttara's eleven nipātas, which is the check that none was missed.**

**NOT EVERY RESET IS A BOUNDARY.** 17AnA01's only reset is a BACK-STEP, 394 -> 389, whose
paragraph reads `389-401. Iddhipādesu chandaṁ…` — a peyyāla RANGE. 19AnA03 ord171 is the same
shape (294 -> 250). A reset is a boundary only when it returns to **1**; taken as boundaries these
two would have invented books the edition does not print.

**AND THE PAGE BOUNDARIES ARE THE PRINTED OPENINGS, NOT THE CORPUS `pdf_page`.** Derived from the
corpus they were a page out at every seam and the 1:1 count refused: `page_offset` is **0** for
17AnA01 and 18AnA02 and **−1** for 19AnA03. Located instead by finding each nipāta's own first
line (`N. Xnipātassa paṭhame …`). 18AnA02's Tikanipāta ends on 1-based p266, its Catukkanipāta
opens on p268, and **p267 is blank**.

### !!! A REAL UNIT WAS BEING HIDDEN AS A "LEAKED HEADING", AND IT DELETED A PRINTED UNIT

18AnA02 ord463 is unit `264-273. Kammapathavaggepi dasapi kammapathā lokiyalokuttaramissakāva
kathitā.` — with the NEXT heading, `(28) 8. Rāgapeyyālavaṇṇanā`, swallowed onto its END, because
that heading opens with `(` and the extraction does not break there. The leaked-heading test asks
whether a corpus paragraph LOOKS like a heading, and a paragraph **ending** in a heading stem
does: `kat_is_head` returned True, the paragraph was hidden, and the book paired 188 printed
against 187 corpus.

**`leak_keep` names the ordinal and REFUSES if it is not in fact flagged**, so the declaration
cannot rot into a lie about the corpus. The divergence is RECORDED, not corrected — the same
treatment `unnum_spanning` gives 01VinA01 ¶14. Inert by construction everywhere else (empty
default); `regress.py` 55/55 confirms.

Backup: `pipeline/build_khu_volume.py.preleakkeep`.

## THE SAṀYUTTA-AṬṬHAKATHĀ IS COMPLETE — THREE OF THREE, AND THE EDITION MISPRINTS A RANGE SEPARATOR TWICE (2026-07-27ak)

```
vol       books  units/¶         body gate (minw 4/2/1)  layout           nav
14SamA01    1    254/254         1/1/2/0                 ok   246 ¶ 97%   12 top / 291 keys
15SamA02    2    188/188 112/112 0/0/0/0                 PART 196 ¶ 65%    2 top / 351 keys
16SamA03    2    156/156 233/233 0/0/0/0                 PART 286 ¶ 74%    2 top / 479 keys
```

`_navdup.js` PASS on 19,526 rows; `regress.py` 55/55; `check_shape` 0 apparatus failures.
Apparatus 0 spliced / 6, 7, 3 variants / 0 xrefs (not rebuilt — no corpus was rebuilt here).
**The two PART verdicts are the standing caveat, not a defect**: a commentary volume's
presentation verdict covers only its LINK-COVERAGE fraction, and both report **0 layout issues**
over the part they can see.

**The bhāga division is the EDITION'S and does not follow the canon's.** 14SamA01 is the
Sagāthāvagga alone; 15SamA02 and 16SamA03 carry TWO books each. Three independent witnesses agree
on that, which is why it was not assumed: the cover (`Nidānavaggapāḷiyā **ca** Khandhavaggapāḷiyā
**ca** saṁvaṇṇanābhūtā`), the HOMAGE pages (1-based 20 and 248; 24 and 176), and the corpus `n`
RESET (ord188 246->1; ord156 420->1).

### !!! THE EDITION MISPRINTS A RANGE SEPARATOR AS A PERIOD, TWICE, AND EACH COST A DIFFERENT THING

The Saṁyutta commentary runs suttas together and numbers them `62-63.`, `1-2.`, `3-6.`. Twice it
sets a PERIOD where the hyphen belongs, and the two failures are not the same:

* **14SamA01 p114 `64.65. Catutthe kiṁsu saṁyojanoti…`** — its own neighbour four lines above
  reads `62-63. Dutiye…` and the heading over it reads `4-5. Saṁyojanasuttādivaṇṇanā`.
  `extract.py`'s PARA wants `\.\s+` and `64.65.` offers no space, so the extraction saw NO
  BOUNDARY and the whole unit arrived inside the paragraph of n=62. **A CORPUS SPLICE**, and the
  same key 36Abhi08's `41.Nevavipāka…` took: `kat_splices`, whose `mark` is the printed unit's
  WHOLE FIRST LINE because that mark is also what renders.
* **15SamA02 p211 `3. 10. Suvaṇṇanikkhasuttādivaṇṇanā`** — the mātikā reads `3-10.` and the
  neighbour reads `1-2. Suvaṇṇapātisuttādivaṇṇanā`. Here the stray period made the line match
  `VERSE`, so it was read as a numbered UNIT rather than a HEADING. **A WRONG ROLE**, and the
  book paired 189 printed against 188 corpus and refused to build.

**Both misprints are PRESERVED** (working principle 3) — `mark` and `headfix` name the line
exactly as the edition sets it. Neither is corrected.

### `headfix` DID NOT MEAN WHAT ITS DOCSTRING SAYS, AND NOW IT DOES

`headfix`'s stated meaning is "a line NAMED here IS A HEADING WHEREVER IT SITS". That was false of
a NUMBERED line: the first heading branch is guarded by `not (m and heads_by_form)`, so a literal
matching `VERSE` could never reach it, and the numbered-heading branch below it has no `headfix`
clause at all. 15SamA02's misprinted heading is exactly that case — and it also fails the
numbered branch's `'.' not in core` test, because of the very misprint being named.

**MEASURED TWICE BEFORE APPLYING.** First by inspection: only FIVE volumes carry a `headfix` at
all, and of their literals only two match `VERSE` — 26Khu09's `5. Virāgatathā`, whose volume is
not `heads_by_form` so this branch cannot reach it, and 38Abhi10's `2. Paccayapaccanīya
2. Saṅkhyāvara`, which the `_is_double_head` branch above already claims. Then by building every
SPEC volume old-vs-new, all five side-maps: **55 volumes, and exactly ONE moves — 15SamA02.**

Backup: `pipeline/build_khu_volume.py.preheadfixnum`.

### THE TWO STANDING CLASSES, FOR THE NINTH, TENTH AND ELEVENTH TIME

* **The colophon frame** — the Sāratthappakāsinī's, in both forms (`Sāratthappakāsiniyā
  Saṁyuttanikāyaṭṭhakathāya` and `Iti Sāratthappakāsiniyā…`), plus the WHOLE WORK's closing
  colophon `Sāratthappakāsinī nāma` in the last bhāga. `colofix`.
* **A gāthā's last pāda closing with the citation dash** — six across the three volumes, checked
  on the page. `headskip`. **16SamA03 prints none, and that is a measurement, not an omission.**
  `Nāgo tādi pavuccate tathattā”ti–` is the SAME pāda 10MaA01 quotes, and it carries a footnote
  marker there and none here — which is exactly why the literal is the printed line.

### SEVENTEEN EDITION ERRATA, JOINED AND NOT CORRECTED

Each printed once in the body and once in the mātikā, so `errata` is right and `body_errata` is
not — 5 in 14SamA01, 4 in 15SamA02, 8 in 16SamA03. Two of 16SamA03's are the edition's own
TYPOGRAPHY rather than a spelling: the body sets `6. Dutiyakāmabhūsutta2 vaṇṇanā` and
`4. Mettāsahagatasutta2 vaṇṇanā` with the FOOTNOTE MARKER inside the heading, which splits
`suttavaṇṇanā` in two, and `fold` keeps digits so the sides cannot meet unnamed. A third simply
truncates: p2386 sets `5-6. Jīvakambavanasamādhisuttādivaṇṇan`, the final `ā` unprinted.

### `head_paren` ON 16SamA03 — FOURTEEN VAGGAS THAT WERE NOT HEADINGS AT ALL

The nav REFUSED with `'(6) 1. Avijjāvaggavaṇṇanā'` in the mātikā and absent from the tree.
`kat_is_head` wants a capital and a line opening `(` never reaches it, so the heading did not
exist in the stream. With `head_paren` the tree gains **fourteen** — `(6) 1. Avijjāvaggavaṇṇanā`
and `(7) 2. Migajālavagga` through `(19) 4. Āsīvisavagga` — every one a real printed vagga whose
suttas had been hanging off the saṁyutta directly. Sections 463 -> 477. Same key and same cause
as the Aṅguttara's `(6) 1. Brāhmaṇavagga` (2026-07-27j); **invisible to all three content gates**,
because a wrong role leaves every word in place.

### THE TOPS ARE NAMED, AND THE NUMBERING IS THE CHECK

Each book's saṁyuttas are named rather than patterned, because the edition heads some
`N. Xsaṁyutta` and others `N. Xsaṁyuttavaṇṇanā`, and `tops` cannot mix a literal with a pattern.
**Each list runs 1..N with no gap** — that is what proves none was missed: 10, then 13; 10, then
12. Four levels throughout (saṁyutta > vagga > suttavaṇṇanā > sub-kathā), which the printed mātikā
states itself by indent.

14SamA01's mātikā sets `3. Vittasuttavaṇṇanā.` with a stray terminal stop; `MAT`'s name group is
`[^.]*?`, so the entry is dropped and that section is simply not checked — 290 entries where the

## THE LINE-END HYPHEN WAS ONE JOIN WHERE THE EDITION USES THREE — 11,463 OF 14,267 WERE WRONG (2026-07-27aj)

Six sites in `build_khu_volume.py` joined a printed line ending in `-` as
`prev[:-1] + t`, i.e. **assumed a soft word break everywhere**. Measured over all 118 volumes,
that is true of a fifth of them. The other four fifths were deleting a character the edition
prints.

```
class                                                 count    what the join must do
PEYYALA  the line ends with a standalone -pa-/-pe-/-la-  3,906  keep the hyphen AND add a space
VOWEL    the next line opens with a vowel                7,572  keep the hyphen, add no space
OTHER    everything else                                 2,781  join without it  (unchanged)
                                                       ------
                                                       14,267
```

### THE EDITION DECIDES THIS ITSELF, AND IT WAS ASKED

Not a rule about vowels that I invented — a lookup. **Pass 1** (`_hyphen/index.py`) built a
corpus-wide index over all 118 volumes of every hyphenated pair and every un-hyphenated whole word
printed **INLINE**, taken only from line interiors so that **no line break can ever vote on
itself**: 25,024 hyphenated pairs, 730,413 words. **Pass 2** (`_hyphen/decide.py`) looked up both
candidates — `X-Y` and `XY` — for every one of the 14,267 breaks:

```
class      KEEP    JOIN    BOTH    NONE     decided        verdict
VOWEL     2,545       2      42   4,968     2,547/7,557    99.92% KEEP
OTHER        65     716     379   1,454       781/2,614     91.7% JOIN
```

**A vowel junction keeps its hyphen: 2,545 to 2.** That is the edition's own orthography —
`pathavī-ādīsu`, `catu-iriyāpatha`, `sakadāgāmi-anāgāmi`, `Mahā-aṭṭhakathāyaṁ` — a hyphen written
so a vowel meeting a vowel is not misread as one long one. **And OTHER really is soft
hyphenation, 716 to 65**, so the old behaviour was right there and is kept; its 65 KEEP are the
edition's grammatical citation forms (`ta-kāro`, `taṁ-saddassa`, `na-kāro`) plus apparatus sigla.

**!!! THE PEYYĀLA MARK MUST NOT BE PUT TO THE VOTE.** `-pa-` is a COMPLETE TOKEN carrying its own
closing hyphen, so it is decided by its own rule. Asked, the word index votes JOIN on 146 breaks —
because `pa` + `taṁ` is the real word *pataṁ* and `pa` + `hoti` is *pahoti*. A lookup that can be
right for the wrong reason has to be fenced off from the cases it cannot see.

### A FLAW IN MY OWN EVIDENCE, CAUGHT BY ITS OWN NUMBERS

The first index added a hyphenated token's **concatenation** to the word set as well, so every
KEEP case was also its own counter-evidence and read as BOTH: VOWEL came out 6 KEEP / 66 BOTH.
Rebuilt with only un-hyphenated tokens as join-evidence, the same 72 cases read **71 KEEP /
1 BOTH**. The verdict did not change; its confidence went from 6 decided cases to 2,547.

### WHAT MOVED, AND THE ONE INVARIANT THAT MATTERS

Old builder against new, **every one of the 52 SPEC volumes** (`_hyphen/hyenum.py`):

```
52 volumes measured, 0 errored
3,436 strings moved across 47 volumes; 5 unmoved (19Khu02, 21Khu04, 22Khu05, 23Khu06, 05Kankha)
volumes whose LETTER-TEXT changed, or whose string COUNT changed:  0
```

That second line is the whole safety argument: with every hyphen and space removed, the old text
and the new text are **character for character identical in all 52 volumes**, and no block split
or merged. The change can only move hyphens and spaces, and it is proved to have done only that.

```
29Abhi01  … phasso hoti -paavikkhepo hoti -pa-.   ->  … phasso hoti -pa- avikkhepo hoti -pa-.
13Sam02   … yena Bhagavā -paekamantaṁ nisinno     ->  … yena Bhagavā -pa- ekamantaṁ nisinno
03VinA03  … Vaṇṇapiṭakaaṅgulimālapiṭaka…          ->  … Vaṇṇapiṭaka-aṅgulimālapiṭaka…
```

### THREE VOLUMES CARRY POST-BUILD STEPS AND WERE NOT BLINDLY REBUILT

Checked before rebuilding anything (`_hyphen/safe.py`): for each volume, is what is on disk plain
builder output? **49 of 52 yes.** The three that are not:

* **19Khu02** — its shipped `sections` carries the 36 Guttilavimāna demotions the NAV builder makes
  afterwards. **It does not move at all**, so it was left alone; a blind rebuild would have
  dropped them.
* **05Kankha** — has no side-maps; does not move.
* **04VinA04** — its shipped `sections` carries a `Vinayapiṭaka` entry above each of its two books
  that the builder does not produce, and it moves 49 strings. Rebuilt, the two entries spliced
  back, and the result checked letter-for-letter against what was on disk before.

### THE NINE REGRESSION SNAPSHOTS, ADVANCED BY HAND

`regress.py baseline` regenerates from the frozen `.preniddesa` builder and so cannot carry an
intended change forward. Nine of the 55 maps move — 20Khu03/24Khu07/25Khu08/26Khu09/27Khu10/
28Khu11/29Abhi01 `verse`, 28Khu11/29Abhi01 `uddana` — every one a byte-size **increase**, which is
what restoring a character looks like. `_hyphen/advance.py` **REFUSES** to advance any snapshot
whose letter-text moves, and all nine passed. 55/55 again after. (Second time a snapshot has been
advanced by hand; the first was `20Khu03.uddana.json`, 2026-07-27i.)

### RE-GATED

```
peyyāla marks eaten          2,647 in 46 files  ->  0 in 0 files
regress.py check             55/55
_navdup.js                   PASS, 18,405 rows
check_shape.py               0 apparatus failures; 243 blocks in 23 volumes, unmoved
check_layout.js              29Abhi01, 01Vin01, 40Abhi12, 12MaA03, 07DiA01 — all ok
body gate                    UNMOVED on every volume run: 12MaA03 0/0/0/0, 29Abhi01 0/0/0/0,
                             01Vin01 0/0/0/0, 13MaA04 2/2/3/0, 10MaA01 10/9/22/0,
                             11MaA02 4/3/8/0, 07DiA01 3/4/6/0, 08DiA02 4/2/8/0, 09DiA03 4/7/8/0
```

**The body gate not moving is the confirmation, not a disappointment.** It strips line-end hyphens
on both sides, so it is blind to this class BY CONSTRUCTION — it could not see the defect and it
cannot see the repair. That was the whole reason 2,647 eaten peyyāla marks sat in the canon
unnoticed: the parser and its own checker shared the blind spot, exactly as they did for the
graphic footnote rule (2026-07-26ak). **01Vin01's `PDF-reading-order 2` was checked against the
old builder and is identical either side — pre-existing, not introduced.**

### BOTH CORPUS-WIDE REPORTS RE-RUN, AND BOTH IMPROVED

Fresh caches (`_vcache_hy`, `_appcache_hy`), re-run until the count stopped rising and then
confirmed by a further run returning the same number — five runs for the body, seven for the
apparatus.

```
body       clean 33/118 (2026-07-27d)  ->  40/118
apparatus  clean 15/118 (2026-07-26ai) ->  18/118
           notes 69,103 -> 69,663 | spliced 124 -> 116
           variants lost 2,851 -> 2,597 | xrefs lost 201 -> 63
```

**Do not attribute this to the hyphen change.** The body gate is blind to the class by
construction and read identically either side of it; the movement is the accumulated effect of
everything built since those figures were taken — the Saṁyutta, the Aṅguttara, twelve commentary
volumes, and the two apparatus rebuilds. What the re-run establishes is that both reports are now
CURRENT, which they had not been.

### THE ONE THING LEFT IN THIS CLASS — MEASURED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT RULED

OTHER's **65 provably-wrong joins** are the edition's grammatical citation forms: `ca-saddassa`
"the word *ca*", `ta-kārādivacanaṁ` "the letter *ta*". The obvious move is to name the form —
right side opens `sadda-`/`kāra-` — and **it does not survive its own measurement**
(`_hyphen/form.py`). Over all 568 breaks of that shape:

```
KEEP  60      JOIN  37      BOTH  366      NONE  105
KEEP  ca-saddassa · ādi-saddenapi · nu-saddo · gāma-saddena · ha-kārā
JOIN  Go-saddena · Mūla-saddassa · hetupaccaya-saddehi · Kaṁsa-saddo · anurūpa-saddo
```

**The JOIN cases are the same grammatical form as the KEEP cases.** `Go-saddena` is "by the word
*go*" exactly as `ca-saddassa` is "of the word *ca*" — and the 366 BOTH say the edition prints
`ca-saddo` and `casaddo` interchangeably. **The edition is inconsistent here, so no rule can be
right**, and one general enough to catch the 60 would be wrong on the 37. Flagged, not guessed.

**And it is almost entirely a future problem: 58 of the 65 are in ṬĪKĀ volumes, none of which is
built.** In everything built today it is **THREE** breaks — `04VinA04 ta-kārādivacanaṁ`,
`07Di02 I-potthakesu`, `07DiA01 Khuddakapāṭha-Ṭṭha` — and two of those three are apparatus
SIGLA (`I` = Iṅgalisa, `Khu-Ṭṭha` a cross-reference), which sit in footnote cells, not body text.
**Take it when the Ṭīkā layer is built, per volume and by named literal, not by rule.**
* `_hyphen/global.json` (17 MB) and the per-volume caches are the measurement's working set and can
  be regenerated by `index.py` / `decide.py`; they are scratch, inside the repo.

Backup: `pipeline/build_khu_volume.py.prehyphen`.

`_navdup.js` PASS on 18,405 rows; `regress.py check` 55/55; `check_shape.py` **0 apparatus
failures corpus-wide**. Apparatus rebuilt for the two volumes whose corpus was rebuilt:
10MaA01 732 → 755 notes (12 variants lost → 0), 11MaA02 863 → **734** (the store was

### 1. !!! THE MĀTIKĀ GATE HAD NOTHING TO GATE ON, IN TWO DIFFERENT WAYS

**A gate that finds nothing is indistinguishable from a gate that passes.** Two causes, both
found by declaring 12MaA03's mātikā:

* **`MAT`'s dotted leader was written `(?:\.\.\.\s+)*` — exactly three dots.** 12MaA03 sets
  **four** (`1. Kandarakasuttavaṇṇanā       ....   ....      1`), so not one of its 51 dotted
  entries matched and the nav reported "mātikā lists 5" — its centred vagga heads alone — while
  reporting every real entry as a body heading the mātikā does not list, the exact inverse of the
  truth. Widened to `\.{3,}`. The change can only ADD entries, so the risk runs the other way: a
  volume passing today could start failing. **MEASURED OVER ALL 32 VOLUMES THAT DECLARE A
  `matika` RANGE in any nav SPEC in the repo** (`_maa03/matregex.py`) — Vinaya, Dīgha, Majjhima,
  Saṁyutta, Aṅguttara, Abhidhamma and the four commentary volumes — **every one is entry for
  entry identical, +0 −0.**
* **07DiA01, 08DiA02 and 09DiA03 declare no `matika` at all, and all three print one.** They
  shipped that way. Declaring it found a wrong ROLE in every one — see §2.

Backup: `pipeline/build_abhidhamma_nav.py.premat4dot`.

### 2. THE COLOPHON FRAME — A CLASS ACROSS THE WHOLE LAYER, AND IT IS **NOT** `headskip`

2026-07-27ah called `Papañcasūdaniyā Majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya` a **running footer**
("~50 times, once per page turn… not body text, so suppressing it deletes nothing") and named
`headskip` for it. **Looked at on the page, that is wrong on both counts.** It is the FIRST LINE
of the two-line colophon the edition sets at the close of every suttavaṇṇanā (0-based p14):

```
        Papañcasūdaniyā Majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

                 Kandarakasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
                             _____
```

The stop is on the SECOND line, which `kat_is_colo` already claims, so the first carried no
terminal punctuation and the form test took it. It occurs 49 times because the volume closes 50
suttas, **not because pages turn** — the running headers are `Majjhimapaṇṇāsaṭṭhakathā N` and
`N Majjhimanikāya`, and neither is read as a heading. **`colofix` gives it the right role rather
than merely denying it the wrong one** — exactly what 08Di03 already says of
`Tīhi vaggehi paṭimaṇḍito sakalo`, and the same literal class as
`Samantapāsādikāya Vinayasaṁvaṇṇanāya`, in `colofix` since the Vinaya commentary was built.
**`headskip` would have demoted a printed colophon line to display verse.**

The frame is printed in every volume of both commentaries, and **the edition misspells it three
times, each differently — all three preserved and named, none corrected** (working principle 3):

```
12MaA03 p188  Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhākathāya   lowercase m, ṭṭhā for ṭṭha
13MaA04 p88   Papañcasūdaniyā Kajjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya   K for M
09DiA03 p152  Sumaṅgalavilāsiniyā Dīghanikayaṭṭhakathāya  short a in nikaya
```

### 3. THE CITATION-DASH PĀDA — the same class, on every volume of both commentaries

A gāthā whose citation runs on into the prose below closes its LAST PĀDA with the **citation
dash** instead of a stop, which is the one thing `kat_is_head` asks a display line not to have.
Twenty-two of them across the seven volumes, every one checked on the page; each BECOMES the last
`vline` of its own block. **The literal is the printed line, so it cannot be shared between
volumes** — the same pāda carries different footnote markers in different volumes
(`Idañca me dhīra mahāvimānan”ti2–` in both 07DiA01 and 10MaA01, but
`Tasmā hi amhaṁ daharā na mīyare”ti5–` there and `…ti1–` here), and 11MaA02 prints
`Dasadhā byañjanabuddhiyā pabhedoti1–` with **no closing quote** where 07DiA01 sets
`…pabhedo”ti–`.

The proof that the dash is the whole cause is inside 12MaA03: the second of its two gāthā is
printed TWICE, and the p58 printing closes `Ko me imaṁ puttamakāsi evan”ti.` **with** the stop and
was never read as a heading.

Not counted. With each volume's five maps laid end to end in ordinal order and the line-end hyphen
resolved both ways, every REMOVED line must occur in the new text and every ADDED line in the old
(`_diaA/account.py`, `_maa03/rolesenum.py`):

```
12MaA03   137 removed / 18 added   0 unaccounted, and each added line a PURE JOIN of removed ones
07DiA01    82 removed / 11 added   0 printed text lost, 0 invented
08DiA02     3 removed /  1 added   0 / 0
09DiA03     0 removed /  0 added   4 role moves only
```

**12MaA03's was much more than a wrong role.** The false heading at p63 had pushed the whole
Mātaṅga narrative (printed pp57-59) into ord45's `verse.before` bucket, which holds the printed
stream **unjoined** — so ~160 printed lines were being drawn with hard line breaks and **8 gāthā
were buried inside them**. Only ordinals 44 and 45 changed. Its body gate went **0/2/0/0 →
0/0/0/0**: the two chunking artefacts *were* that defect.

Heads streams: 12MaA03 108 → 56, 13MaA04 121 → 65, 10MaA01 123 → 98, 11MaA02 82 → 43,
07DiA01 141 → 127, 08DiA02 155 → 152, 09DiA03 156 → 147. **Every one now equals its printed
mātikā exactly, in both directions.**

### 6. A COLOPHON THE FORM TEST CANNOT SEE — and on 10MaA01 it was worse than a wrong role

`kat_is_colo` form (1) wants the section name and `niṭṭhita-` **adjacent**. The edition writes
`Mūlapaṇṇāsaṭṭhakathāya **paṭhamo bhāgo** niṭṭhito.` (10MaA01 p414) and
`Majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathā **sabbākārena** niṭṭhitā.` (13MaA04 p292) with a word between them, so
neither is claimed.

On 10MaA01 that line fell through to the body and became a **visible unnumbered corpus
paragraph** — and being the LAST paragraph it had no later numbered unit to hang a link off, so
`relink` reported `no later numbered paragraph is linked; NOT placed`. **It would have been in
the corpus, in the tree, and on no page.** `colofix` hides it and `uddana/` draws it, which is
what 07DiA01's `Niṭṭhitā ca terasasuttapaṭimaṇḍitassa Sīlakkhandhavaggassa` already does.
13MaA04's is the same class and is left as a one-line `uddana` block beside `Papañcasūdanī nāma`,
because 09DiA03 has the identical shape — consistent with the layer, and recorded rather than
keyed round.

### 7. THE TWO CORPUS REBUILDS

**10MaA01 — and the recipe's one-line test is confirmed wrong on it.** Its corpus's first
`pdf_page` and its body's first printed page are BOTH 18, and 23 printed pages were missing
anyway, because the first paragraph is ANCHORED to p18 while the TEXT of pp18-46 is absent. **An
anchor is not coverage.** The per-page measurement is what finds it:

```
188 -> 197 ¶ after trimming 97 back-matter ¶      coverage 89% -> 94%
pages with MORE THAN HALF their long lines absent   22 -> 0
every one of the 188 shipped paragraphs survives text for text; pdf_page monotonic 17..414
```

**11MaA02 — the first mid-volume gap in the layer, and `rebuild_corpus.py` handles it.** Its
corpus ran ¶239 (`pdf_page` 310) straight to ¶240 (317): printed pp311-316, six pages of the
Brahmanimantanika narrative, in no paragraph at all. **Position in the volume is irrelevant to
the mechanism** — the restored `else` opens an unnumbered paragraph wherever the numbering stops,
and the flush-at-headings bound applies the same. Four unnumbered paragraphs recovered, anchored
pp312-314 and running through 316.

```
249 -> 256 ¶ after trimming 162 back-matter ¶     coverage 92% -> 93%
pages with MORE THAN HALF their long lines absent   5 -> 0
```

**!!! `pdf_page`'s OFFSET REALLY IS PER VOLUME, and it bit the first trim.** `vr.page_offset`:
10MaA01 **0**, 11MaA02/12MaA03/13MaA04/07DiA01 **−1**. Trimming 10MaA01 on the 1-based extent
dropped its title page and kept the index's first page. Read `page_offset`, do not infer it.

**Links re-keyed in place, never rebuilt.** `_maa01/relink_10MaA01.py` and
`_maa02/relink_11MaA02.py` load `_fnprobe/relink_rebuilt.py` and swap its two volume lists rather
than copying it, so there is one implementation. 188 and 249 ordinals re-keyed, **0 mismatches**;
6 and 4 unnumbered paragraphs placed once each; every visible unnumbered paragraph is in the
reverse map. **Only `09Ma01.links.json` and the two `.rev.json` moved — every other links file is
byte-identical to its backup.** `build_links.py` was NOT re-run.

### 8. `tops` CANNOT MIX A LITERAL WITH A PATTERN

`subtree` reads a `re:` top only when `tops` is a list of ONE. So 10MaA01's
`['Ganthārambhakathā', 'Nidānakathā', VAGGA]` silently made both vaggas children of the
Nidānakathā and the builder REFUSED on the order check. The two vaggas are NAMED instead, as
07DiA01's thirteen suttas are. **Do not widen `subtree` for this** — it feeds every volume's tree.

**And the Majjhima commentary's top level is the VAGGA, not the sutta** (12MaA03's refusal,
2026-07-27ah). The rule holds underneath — a commentary book takes the structure of the text it
comments on — but the Dīgha comments on a nikāya whose SUTTAS are the top level and the Majjhima
on one of five vaggas of ten. **The two mātikās say so themselves, and differently:** in the
Dīgha the CENTRED group head is the SUTTA and the dotted entries are its sub-kathās; in the
Majjhima the centred head is the VAGGA and the dotted entries are the suttavaṇṇanās. 13MaA04's
goes further and expresses depth by INDENT — its seven `…ratanavaṇṇanā` sub-kathās sit at indent
7 against the numbered entries' 1, and `Nigamanakathā` sits at the numbered entries' own column,
so it is a SIBLING of the suttavaṇṇanās and had to be named at level 1.

### 9. `matika_drop` FOR A TITLE STACK A TWO-PAGE MĀTIKĀ CANNOT FILTER

`matika_headers` identifies a mātikā's running header as "a line that opens three or more of its
pages". **11MaA02's mātikā is TWO pages**, so the rule can never fire and `Dutiyabhāga` — the
second line of the title stack — entered the entry list; one unresolvable entry is enough to make
`matika_gate` unusable. Its first line `Mūlapaṇṇāsaṭṭhakathā` slipped the `fold(title)` filter
too, because the node is labelled with its BHĀGA as the standing rule requires.

**The general rule the page seems to state was tried and REJECTED.** "Nothing above the
`Mātikā … Piṭṭhaṅka` column head is an entry", measured over every volume declaring a mātikā
(`_maa02/matkolumn.py`): it removes **31 entries across the layer and several are REAL** —
33Abhi05's five book heads and four `1. Paṇṇattivāra-uddesa`, 37Abhi09's four
`2. Paccayapaccanīya 1. Vibhaṅgavāra` pair-lines, 15An01's three `1. Paṭhamapaṇṇāsaka` — and
16An02 GAINS one. So the two lines are NAMED in `matika_drop`, which is what that key is for.
(38Abhi10 carries the same `Tatiyabhāga` artefact and is `matika_gate: False`, so it has never
been visible there.)

### 10. !!! A NEW CORPUS-WIDE DEFECT, SIZED AND NOT FIXED — THE PEYYĀLA MARK

**The line-end-hyphen join treats the edition's `-pa-` as a word break.** Where the mark falls at
the end of a printed line its closing hyphen is stripped and the next line glued on:

```
printed   … so dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ -pa-
          parisuddhaṁ. Evaṁ desento …
rendered  … so dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ -paparisuddhaṁ. Evaṁ desento …
```

Measured over both layers that hold text (`_diaA/peyyala.py`), with the guard that a hyphen
preceded by whitespace cannot be a compound's internal hyphen — without it the scan also claims
`aññamañña-paccayena` and `nāma-padena`, which are correct:

```
the CORPUS          0 occurrences        — the corpus keeps -pa- intact
the SIDE-MAPS   2,647 occurrences in 46 files
                verse/29Abhi01 322 · 32Abhi04 183 · 30Abhi02 177 · 38Abhi10 170
                37Abhi09 167 · 39Abhi11 156 · 35Abhi07 124 · 13Sam02 118 · 14Sam03 111 …
```

**It is pre-existing and it is in the CANON, not the commentary** — and for a canon volume the
reader draws `verse/`, so 29Abhi01 renders `phasso hoti -paavikkhepo hoti -pa-` where the edition
prints `-pa- avikkhepo`. **The body gate cannot see it**: it strips line-end hyphens on both
sides, so the parser and its checker share the blind spot — the same shape as the graphic
footnote rule (2026-07-26ak).

This session's roles add exactly ONE instance (07DiA01 7 → 8; 08DiA02 12 → 12, 09DiA03 12 → 12,
12MaA03 7 → 7), because a false heading had been splitting that one run; the alternative was
keeping the false heading. **NOT TOUCHED.** The join happens at six separate sites in
`build_khu_volume.py`, all `x.endswith('-')`, so a real fix is one predicate applied at all six
plus the standing measurement over every volume. **It is now the largest open defect known in the
canon render.**

### 11. TWO STANDING FIGURES CORRECTED

* **`check_shape`'s prose-as-verse total is 227 in 19 volumes without this session's work, not
  the 219 the file records.** The extra 8 are in volumes untouched here; 07DiA01 contributes 5 and

  **243 in 23**; 12MaA03's own contribution is **unchanged at 7** old-vs-new — the same 7 blocks,

* **`check_shape`'s apparatus assertion fired on its own defect class, unprompted.** After

  ratio **7.80** against a corpus maximum of 0.75 — the 07DiA01 shape it was written for (94.0).
  `rebuild_apparatus --write` took it to 0.07. **A check written the previous night for a defect
  a USER found paid for itself on the first volume it could apply to.** 11MaA02 fired the same

The two deferred items are unchanged and still wait for every corpus to be final: **(a)** the

## 12MaA03 BUILDS AND GATES CLEAN ON THE FIRST PASS; ITS NAV IS CORRECTLY REFUSED (2026-07-27ah)

```
SPEC        one book, Majjhimapaṇṇāsaṭṭhakathā, printed p7-315, ords 0-354
            katha + heads_by_form + pada_runon   (453 display lines, 179 with a comma,
            so the volume prints gāthā and `no_verse` is not arguable)
build       printed units 354 / corpus ¶ 354   [OK] on the FIRST run — no errata, no
            colofix, no splices
body gate   (6 314, 0-354)  0 / 2 / 0 / 0   — the 2 are chunking artefacts
            (PDF-lines-missing is 0)
layout      ok, 354 ¶ — the whole volume, because its link coverage is 100%
regress     55/55; the SPEC addition is additive and moves nothing
```

The booktitle ordering trap fired again and the nav's own report caught it: headings 109 -> 108
across the rebuild, the dropped one being the title page's series line `Majjhimanikāya`. **Fourth
occurrence.** Build body, write booktitle, REBUILD body.

### THE NAV REFUSED, AND IT WAS RIGHT TO

```
REFUSED — the top level does not appear in printed order; stopped at 're:\d+\.\s+.*sutta$'
   1. Gahapativagga   107 children
```

**The Majjhima commentary does NOT take the Dīgha's tops.** Its top level is the VAGGA, not the
sutta: `1. Gahapativagga`, `2. Bhikkhuvagga`, … with `N. Xsuttavaṇṇanā` under it and sub-kathās
(`Kāmādīnavakathāvaṇṇanā`) under those. The rule still holds underneath — a commentary book takes
its structure from the text it comments on, and 10Ma02 is five vaggas of ten suttas — but the
Dīgha volumes comment on a nikāya whose suttas ARE the top level, and this one does not. So
`tops` is `re:\d+\.\s+.*vagga$`, three levels deep.

### AND THE HEADS STREAM SHOWS TWO ROLE DEFECTS, BOTH INVISIBLE TO ALL THREE GATES

1. **`Papañcasūdaniyā Majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya` — the RUNNING FOOTER — is read as a heading**,
   roughly fifty times, once per page turn. It is not body text, so suppressing it deletes
   nothing; but it must go through `headskip`, and the standing question applies: **ask what a
   suppressed line BECOMES before suppressing it.**
2. **Two quoted verse lines read as headings** — `Tānīdha khettāni supesalānī”ti–` (p63) and
   `Ko me imaṁ puttamakāsi evan”ti–` (p65). These ARE body text and must become body, not vanish.
   Same class as the five roles corrected this morning by `unnum_reclass`, and as the batch named
   for 03VinA03/04VinA04/01VinA01.

Neither moves a single word, so the body gate is 0/2/0/0 and `check_layout.js` is `ok` with both
present. **The heads-stream diff is the only thing that finds them** — the standing rule, holding
for the ninth volume running.

Nothing of 12MaA03 is written to the nav; its side-maps, booktitle and gates ARE written.

## THE READING-MODEL CHANGE IS **NOT** CONTAINED — SCOPED, AND THE ANSWER IS NO (2026-07-27ah)

Proposed: make a commentary volume ALWAYS its own spine, drawn from the corpus with `fmtBold`,
with the links used only for jumping between layers. That would make `check_layout.js` examine
100% of every volume instead of the link-coverage fraction, and put bold through the whole layer.
Timeboxed and scoped before touching anything. **It does not survive the measurement.**

### !!! AND IT CORRECTS AN ERROR I MADE EARLIER TODAY

I wrote, in the entry on the sections path, that *"4 printed lines the corpus lacks now sit in
`verse.after` and are invisible in the reader"*. **That figure is wrong.** It counted only the
lines held by the `verse.after` of the UNNUMBERED anchors. The verse map of a `katha` volume holds
a full printed-stream reconstruction of the body — `add_prose` puts every unit's own prose into
`after` — so the real figure is the whole map. Measured across the eight built commentary volumes:

```
vol         visible ¶   verse-map lines   NOT held by the corpus
01VinA01        159          1210               57
02VinA02        239          1272              103
03VinA03        738          1771              148
04VinA04        300          1810              456
06VinSg06       326          2776              109
07DiA01         330          1383               86
08DiA02         345          2087               91
09DiA03         293          1284              244
                                          ------------
                                             1,294 printed lines
```

**Rendering a commentary volume from the corpus alone would drop ~1,300 printed lines** — the
1–9% line-join residue every one of these corpora carries. 04VinA04 loses 456 and 09DiA03 loses
244. That is a trade this project does not make: bold and a whole-volume gate are not worth
deleting printed text.

### WHAT THE RIGHT CHANGE LOOKS LIKE, AND WHY IT IS LATER

**Reduce the verse map to only what the corpus does NOT hold, and render corpus + residue.** That
is the same rule that fixed the unnumbered prose this morning — *the printed stream supplies only
what is missing, checkable per line rather than assumed* — applied to the numbered units too. It
loses nothing, gains bold everywhere, and makes the body gate and the reader model the same
render.

It is not a contained edit: it changes `kat_build`'s `add_prose`, the reader's `block()`, and
`verify_render_vs_pdf.py`'s `render_parts` together, and it needs the standing treatment across
every volume. **So the fallback stands: continue building the Aṭṭhakathā volumes, and take this
with the links at the end**, when the corpora are final and the ordinals have stopped moving.

One consequence to keep in view while building: until it is done, a commentary volume's
presentation verdict covers only its link-coverage fraction (46% for 06VinSg06, 64% for 03VinA03,
100% only for the three Dīgha volumes), and its body gate certifies the printed-stream render
rather than the one the reader draws.

## THE PARAGRAPH NUMBER *IS* THE JOIN KEY — TESTED AT LAST, AND IT IS NOT SUFFICIENT ALONE (2026-07-27ah)

The project instructions list this as **unverified**: *"Paragraph numbers. Reportedly shared across
Tipiṭaka, Aṭṭhakathā and Ṭīkā… This is unverified — test it on samples across all three layers
before designing around it."* Tested.

### IN THE ELEVEN ONE-TO-ONE GROUPS THE NUMBER RANGES COINCIDE EXACTLY

```
canon     commentary   canon n-range | commentary n-range | shared | content confirms
06Di01    07DiA01          1-559     |      1-559         |  322   | 62%
07Di02    08DiA02          1-441     |      1-441         |  344   | 72%
08Di03    09DiA03          1-360     |      1-360         |  293   | 64%
10Ma02    12MaA03          1-485     |      1-485         |  354   | 66%
11Ma03    13MaA04          1-463     |      1-461         |  306   | 55%
24Khu07   43KhuA24         1-210     |      1-210         |  209   | 91%
27Khu10   45KhuA26         1-170     |      1-170         |  119   | 78%
20Khu03   32KhuA13         1-663     |      5-657         |  480   | 71%
30Abhi02  49AbhiA02        1-1044    |      1-1030        |  325   | 56%
29Abhi01  48AbhiA01        1-1616    |      1-1577        |  269   | 42%
25Khu08   44KhuA25         1-211     |      1-161         |  144   |  0%
```

**The claim holds.** Random unrelated pairs share >=2 distinctive words 3% of the time; the
shipped `direct` in-group links score 67%. A number join at 55-72% is in the same class as the
best thing in the repo, and it is principled and reproducible where the shipped map is neither.
(55-72% is not a defect rate: a commentary glosses a lemma and often explains it in other words.)

### THREE COMPLICATIONS, EVERY ONE PREDICTED BY THE PROJECT'S OWN CONCORDANCE

1. **THE RELATION IS MANY-TO-MANY AT VOLUME LEVEL.** Eleven of the twenty-two groups are not 1:1
   — two Jātaka volumes to seven commentary volumes, Abhidhamma 31-40 sharing one
   Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā. **41,672 canon paragraphs have more than one work claiming their
   number.** A bare N cannot choose; content must break the tie, and it does so cheaply (take the
   best-overlapping candidate).
2. **SOME WORKS DO NOT USE THE CANON'S NUMBERING AT ALL.** 50AbhiA03 against its ten canon
   volumes: hundreds of number matches, **0%** content agreement. 25Khu08 -> 44KhuA25: 144
   matches, 0%. 29Abhi01 -> 48AbhiA01: only 269 of 1,616 numbers shared. This is a per-work fact
   to be MEASURED, not assumed, and where the numbering is the commentary's own the join must
   REFUSE rather than emit junk.
3. **"NO NUMBER = NO COMMENT" WOULD DROP EXACTLY WHAT WAS RECOVERED THIS SESSION.** The
   Ganthārambha and the Bāhiranidāna — 26 and 78 printed pages — ARE commentary and carry no
   number. They need the unnumbered-anchor rule built today: the canon paragraph of the unit they
   precede.

### THE DESIGN THAT FOLLOWS

**The number proposes, the content confirms, and where the content disconfirms the answer is "no
comment here" rather than a guess.** Self-verifying, which is the project's first working
principle, and it replaces `resolve_old` — the fallback that takes `cand[0][1]`, an arbitrary
paragraph with the same id, and manufactures the 32,052 evidence-free edges measured above.

Corpus-wide, number + content confirmation yields **17,238** commentary links carrying evidence.
That is fewer than the shipped map's 49,435 canon paragraphs "with a link", and that is the point:
the shipped figure counts a third of a graph that is indistinguishable from random.

**IT DOES NOT FIX THE READING MODEL.** Even with perfect links, clicking a linked row shows a
slice filtered to ONE host canon volume with `fmtText` and no bold, while clicking an unlinked row
shows the whole work standalone. That is a separate defect and it should be settled first.

## THE P/A/T LINKS AUDITED — A THIRD OF THE GRAPH IS NOISE, AND A COMMENTARY VOLUME RENDERS TWO DIFFERENT WAYS (2026-07-27ah)

Asked whether the links between Pāḷi, Aṭṭhakathā and Ṭīkā work. Measured rather than answered.
**98,652 link edges. The direct, in-group ones are real. A third of the rest is indistinguishable
from random.**

### 1. DO LINKED PAIRS SHARE ANYTHING? — sampled 400 per class, against a random-pair control

A commentary paragraph explains a canon paragraph by QUOTING it, so a real pair shares distinctive
(>=8 character) words. Random unrelated pairs share >=2 such words **3%** of the time.

```
class                          edges    share >=2 words   mean shared
in-group  state=direct         28,662        67%              3.4     REAL
OUT-of-group state=direct       4,945        28%              1.6     mixed
in-group  state=covered        32,966        13%              0.6     expected: a `covered`
                                                                      link asserts a RANGE,
                                                                      not a quotation
OUT-of-group state=covered     32,052         2%              0.1     !!! BELOW THE CONTROL
```

**32,052 edges — a third of the whole graph — carry no evidence of any relation.** They are
dominated by one volume: `21KhuT01` is pointed at from all six Khuddaka canon volumes, 21,332
edges (21Khu04 4,841 · 20Khu03 4,428 · 19Khu02 3,650 · 23Khu06 3,621 · 22Khu05 2,957 ·
18Khu01 1,835). 37.5% of all edges are out-of-group across 231 (canon, target) pairs; 3,567 edges
are non-monotonic, the target going BACKWARDS as the canon advances.

**A CORRECTION TO THIS SESSION'S EARLIER ENTRY.** I stopped the `build_links.py` re-run because it
dropped `21KhuT01` to zero everywhere and called that an unpredicted shape. It is now measured:
on those edges **the builder was right and the shipped map is manufacturing them** — `resolve_old`
converts an old link by `(id, n)` and, with no exact match, takes `cand[0][1]`, an ARBITRARY
paragraph carrying that id, under a comment that says "so coverage never regresses". The two maps
still disagree in BOTH directions (20Khu03 -> 32KhuA13 goes 709 -> 4,293 the other way), so
`build_links.py` is not simply correct either and the hold stands — but the reason for the hold is
now "both are wrong in different places", not "the shipped map is right".

### 2. HOW MUCH OF THE COMMENTARY CAN A READER ACTUALLY REACH?

The reader draws a commentary volume through its links, so an unlinked paragraph is in the corpus,
searchable, and on no page.

```
commentary     18,988 of 24,716 visible paragraphs reachable = 76%   (2 volumes at 0%)
subcommentary   4,061 of 10,004 visible paragraphs reachable = 40%   (3 volumes at 0%)
```

The five at 0% are the Visuddhimagga and its Ṭīkā (51Vism01, 52Vism02, 25VsmT01, 26VsmT02) —
which comment on no canon volume, so they have nothing to hang off — and 09DiT02. Worst of the
rest: 05Kankha 10%, 10DiT03 16%, 26KhuA07 21%, 05ViT05 23%, 18AnT01 24%.

### 3. !!! AND THE SAME VOLUME RENDERS TWO DIFFERENT WAYS, DECIDED BY WHICH ROW YOU CLICK

`openKey()` branches on whether the CLICKED paragraph has a canon counterpart. With one, it opens
the CANON spine filtered to this work. Without one, it opens the volume STANDALONE as its own
canon spine. Driven in jsdom (`_fnprobe/openprobe.js`), both routes on the same volume:

```
03VinA03  738 ¶, 471 with a counterpart
   click ¶0  (linked)   -> spine 02Vin02, filter=03VinA03   278 paragraphs   2,294 bold lemmata
   click ¶6  (unlinked) -> spine 03VinA03, standalone       738 paragraphs       0 bold lemmata

06VinSg06 327 ¶, 149 with a counterpart
   click ¶20 (linked)   -> spine 04Vin04                     89 paragraphs
   click ¶0  (unlinked) -> spine 06VinSg06, standalone      327 paragraphs
```

**Click one row and you get 38% of the work WITH its lemma structure; click another and you get
100% of it with NONE.** The standalone route renders through `block('canon', …)`, which uses
`fmtText` — no spans — where the linked route uses `fmtBold`. And the linked route is filtered to
ONE host canon volume, so a work hosted by several (06VinSg06 is a target of all five Vinaya
volumes) is only ever shown a slice at a time.

**104 of the 112 commentary and Ṭīkā volumes have every nav row unlinked**, so today almost all of
them open standalone — unbolded but complete. The 8 that are MIXED are exactly the 8 built this
week: 03VinA03 (249 linked / 135 not), 04VinA04 (133/34), 06VinSg06 (17/21), 02VinA02 (61/10),
01VinA01 (77/7), 08DiA02 (154/2), 07DiA01 (141/1), 09DiA03 (156/1). **Building a volume is what
makes it inconsistent**, because that is when its rows acquire counterparts.

### WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE ORDER OF WORK

The commentary layer's remaining 43 volumes are worth less than fixing this: every volume built
adds a work that renders one way from one row and another way from the next. **The reading model
has to be settled first** — most plausibly: a commentary volume is ALWAYS its own spine, drawn
with `fmtBold` and its own side-maps, and the links are for JUMPING between layers rather than for
deciding what is on the page. That also removes the reachability question entirely, and it is the
same conclusion the gate mismatch pointed at (`verify_render_vs_pdf.py` models the canon render;
the reader does not perform it for this layer).

## THE THREE ASSERTIONS ARE WRITTEN — ALL THREE DEFECTS WERE FOUND BY A USER, NOT BY A GATE (2026-07-27ah)

The three content gates ask whether every printed WORD is present, once, in the right order.
None of them can see a wrong SHAPE, because a wrong shape leaves every word in place. These
three are the shapes a reader of the page caught this session.

### 1. A NIKĀYA'S NODE COUNT AGAINST THE PRINTED VOLUME COUNT — `_navdup.js`

**A volume of the COMMENTARY or ṬĪKĀ layers contributes exactly ONE top-level node.**
Layer-scoped, because it is a fact about those layers: 01VinA01–04VinA04 are four bhāgas of one
work and their inner books are the first TREE level (2026-07-27ae), whereas a canon volume
legitimately carries several books of the piṭaka (18Khu01 five, 15An01 four). In the canon the
invariant is only that every volume the manifest lists has a node — which also catches a volume
whose node is silently dropped by a rebuild.

`_navdup.js` PASS: 118 volumes carry a nav node, 172 top-level nodes in all, 18,169 rows checked.

**ELEVEN VOLUMES STILL FAIL IT AND ARE NAMED, not tolerated by a widened rule** — every one still
carries the old font-heuristic tree from `build_nav.py` and has never been built: 18AnA02,
19AnA03, 50AbhiA03, 03ViT03, 07ViT07, 15MaT03, 19AnT02, 20AnT03, 22AbhiT01, 23AbhiT02, 24AbhiT03.
Each comes off `MULTITOP_PENDING` when its volume is built. 24AbhiT03 currently shows **ten**.

### 2 & 3. `pipeline/check_shape.py`

**APPARATUS PROPORTIONATE TO THE PARAGRAPH — and stated without a tuned constant.** A note is a
marker PRINTED in the paragraph's own text, so **a paragraph cannot carry more notes than it has
words.** Measured over all **22,854** anchored paragraphs: the corpus maximum is **0.75**
notes/word (18Khu01 ord1864, 6 notes on 8 words), and **0 paragraphs fail**. The defect it is
written for — 07DiA01 ord0 holding **94 notes on a 26-character, 3-word paragraph** after its
corpus was rebuilt under it (2026-07-27af) — scores **94.0**, a hundred and twenty times the
corpus maximum. Replayed synthetically and the rule fires: **a check that has never seen its own
defect is untested.** It also flags a note anchored past the end of the corpus.

**A GĀTHĀ BLOCK THAT IS PROSE.** The reader draws a `gatha` block with a `<br>` between lines, so
every printed line becomes a verse line — right for a pāda, wrong for a paragraph. The
discriminator is the MEASURE. Over all **6,802** gāthā blocks of three lines or more, the median
line is **31** characters, p90 **46**, p99 **63**; the Bāhiranidāna's restored prose sat at ~70.
So the threshold is the measured distribution, not a guess: median line ≥ 58. The sentence test is
reported beside it (a pāda ends in `,` at least as often as in `.`, so a run of lines each closing
a sentence is prose twice over).

**219 blocks in 19 volumes to judge against the printed page**, and they are NOT all defects —
this is a report, not a gate:

```
06VinSg06  129 of 162      02Vin02   16 of  79      08DiA02  13 of 43
04VinA04    12 of  25      01Vin01    9 of  42      09DiA03   7 of 16
03VinA03     7 of  25      02VinA02   7 of  21      12Sam01   6 of 295
```

**06VinSg06 at 129 of 162 is the finding.** Its `verse.after` blocks are canon quotations set at
the full body measure — which is the class START HERE already names ("A DISPLAY BLOCK IS NOT
ALWAYS VERSE… what separates them is PĀDA PUNCTUATION") and which `display_prose` is the existing
per-volume key for. The assertion rediscovered it independently and, for the first time, sized it.
12Sam01's six are likely false positives — real gāthā whose median is pulled over the line by a
few long pādas — which is exactly why the report names the block and quotes its first line.

## THE UNNUMBERED-PROSE DECISION IS REVERSED, BOTH HALVES IN ONE CHANGE (2026-07-27ah)

`hide`-the-unnumbered (2026-07-27v) is withdrawn. Unnumbered corpus PROSE now renders from the
corpus, and the printed stream no longer restores what the corpus already holds. Both halves are
one edit, because landing either alone duplicates every line.

### THE MECHANISM: A RUN THAT PROVES ITSELF

`unnum_runs(items, paras, cands)` aligns each unnumbered corpus paragraph against a CONTIGUOUS
run of printed items and requires the run's joined text to EQUAL the paragraph's, normalised for
whitespace. Nothing is guessed: a paragraph the printed stream does not reproduce exactly is
reported (`unnum_unaligned`) and left hidden. **A line-end hyphen is joined either way** — the
corpus keeps `…sakadāgāmi- anāgāmi…` with the hyphen AND the space, the body gate strips it — so
both candidates are tested against the paragraph and the paragraph decides. **47 of 47 aligned**
across the two volumes.

What the run's item kinds then decide:

| the run is | the paragraph | why |
|---|---|---|
| any `popen`/`pcont`/`cand` | **VISIBLE**, an anchor; its items suppressed | body prose, and the corpus is its home |
| only `vline` | hidden, restored as `gatha` | the render needs the printed LINE BREAKS |
| one `head` / `colo` / `homage` | hidden | it IS a heading, a colophon, the homage |
| in `booktitle`'s stack | hidden | `booktitle/` draws the title page |

**A VISIBLE UNNUMBERED PARAGRAPH IS AN ANCHOR, exactly as a numbered unit is** — so the headings
printed above it land in ITS `sections` entry. Carried forward to the book's first numbered unit
they were drawn BELOW the 26 pages of text they head. `sections/07DiA01.json` now reads
`3: [Ganthārambhakathā, <gāthā>, Nidānakathā]`, `4: [Paṭhamamahāsaṅgītikathā]`,
`8: [1. Brahmajālasutta, Paribbājakakathāvaṇṇanā]` — the printed page, in order.

**`ords` SERVED TWO JOBS AND THEY HAVE PARTED COMPANY.** `pair_ords` (numbered only) is what the
printed units pair 1:1 against and what `seq` walks; `ords` is what the corpus renders. In every
volume with no unnumbered prose the two are the same list, so the 1:1 count keeps exactly the
meaning it has always had.

**AN UNNUMBERED ANCHOR GETS NO `groups` KEY.** Both the reader and `verify_render_vs_pdf.py` take
the verse branch — rendering `before + after` and NOT the corpus text — for any entry that HAS a
`groups` key, even an empty one. Its body IS the corpus text, so its entry carries only what the
print adds around it, and is omitted when the print adds nothing.

### MEASURED OVER EVERY SPEC VOLUME, AND ENUMERATED

Built twice (`.preunnum2` vs current) and the five side-maps diffed:

```
46 of 49 volumes with a corpus: ALL FIVE MAPS BYTE-IDENTICAL
moved: 01VinA01, 07DiA01 (intended) and 05Kankha (hide only; it still FATALs, and was NOT written)
```

Then line by line, not counted (`_fnprobe/unnumenum.py`): every printed line the OLD side-maps put
on the page must still be carried OR be provably inside a now-visible corpus paragraph.

```
07DiA01   side-map lines 2271 -> 1580   683 distinct removed   0 unaccounted   0 added
01VinA01  side-map lines 4384 -> 1422  2932 distinct removed   0 unaccounted   0 added
```

### WHAT IT CORRECTED ON THE WAY

* **01VinA01's body gate 15/11/26/0 -> 7/4/15/0.** 07DiA01 unmoved at 4/7/8/0. `regress.py check`
  55/55. `_navdup.js` PASS on 18,169 rows.
* **Five misread roles**, each a printed line the extraction had put INSIDE a paragraph — which is
  the evidence that it is body text, since the extraction breaks at headings. They are drawn as
  the verse lines they are (`unnum_reclass`): 01VinA01 `Tato ca bhāsantarameva hitvā` (one of the
  three hyphen-heads), `Bhaddanāmo ca paṇḍito.`, `Dīghasumano ca paṇḍito.`; 07DiA01
  `Desanāsāsanakathā-bhedaṁ tesu yathārahaṁ.`, `Sikkhāppahānagambhīra-bhāvañca paridīpayeti–`.
  **A run that IS one structural item keeps its role** — 01VinA01 ord68 is the whole colophon
  `Vinayadharassa ca lakkhaṇādikathā.` and stays one.
* **Navs rebuilt.** 07DiA01 15 tops / 141 keys (was 142 — the reclassified head). 01VinA01
  4 tops / 78 sections / 82 keys, with the Bāhiranidānakathā now carrying its three councils.

### ONE CORPUS DEFECT, FLAGGED NOT CORRECTED

`unnum_spanning`: 01VinA01 ord14 spans the printed heading `Bāhiranidānakathā` (p18) — the
extraction did not break on it. The heading cannot be drawn where the page sets it, so it is drawn

**!!! `build_links.py` DOES NOT REPRODUCE THE SHIPPED `linksk/`. DO NOT RE-RUN IT.** Measured:
