## THE SECTIONS PATH CARRIED NO BOLD, AND A TARGET'S FRONT MATTER WAS DRAWN ONCE PER CANON ORDINAL (2026-07-27ah)

Two reader defects, both surfaced by the reversal above.

### 1. `layerFront(ts[0].key)` — THE FIRST TARGET'S FRONT MATTER AND NO OTHER

Where one canon paragraph points at several commentary paragraphs — which is now every volume
opening with unnumbered prose, 06Di01 ¶1 owning 07DiA01 ¶3–¶9 — the headings anchored to ¶4…¶8
were built, written to `sections/` and never drawn. `check_layout.js` reported
`sections-not-rendered`. Front matter is now drawn PER TARGET.

**Blast radius enumerated over every links file, not sampled:** `_front` fires only for the 2nd
and later DRAWN target under one canon ordinal. Corpus-wide that is **27 targets, of which 18
carry front matter, in exactly two volumes — 01VinA01 and 07DiA01.** Nowhere else in the 118 does
a canon ordinal own two drawn targets. Confirmed empirically by running `check_layout.js` under
both readers (`OSBCT_READER=` now selects the file): 02VinA02, 03VinA03, 04VinA04, 06VinSg06
report identically; 08DiA02, 09DiA03, 18Khu01, 29Abhi01, 06Di01, 01Vin01 all `ok`.
07DiA01 is `ok` again; 01VinA01 PART at 87% (was 64%) with 0 layout issues.

### 2. `fmtText` TAKES NO SPANS

Everything rendered from `sections/` was unbolded, because that path was written for a four-pāda
opening gāthā and never asked to carry a lemma. A sections entry's text is the PRINTED stream, so
the ordinal-keyed corpus spans cannot address it and translating their offsets would be guesswork.
It is aligned against the SAME render-mode signature instead — `extract_bold.py --sections-only`,
writing `bold/<VOL>.sect.json` keyed `"<ord>:<index>"`, touching no `.bold.json`.

**MEASURED OVER THE WHOLE CORPUS: 17 such entries in 12 volumes, all 17 align, and exactly ONE
carries bold** — 07DiA01 `3:1`, the Sumaṅgalavilāsinī's opening gāthā, 8 spans / 82 characters
(`Sugataṁ`, `dhammaṁ`, `ariyasaṁghaṁ`, `Dīghassa`, `āgamavarassa`, `Aṭṭhakathā`, `Visuddhimagge`,
`Visuddhimaggo`). So the fix is provably inert on 16 of 17 — `gathaHTML` with no spans is the old
expression character for character.

Backups: `site/reader/reader2.html.preunnumfront`, `.presectbold`;
`pipeline/check_layout.js.prereaderenv`.

### !!! AND A GATE THAT MODELS THE WRONG RENDER

`block()` takes the verse branch only when `kind==='canon'`. **For a commentary or Ṭīkā volume the
reader draws `fmtBold(corpus text)` and ignores `verse/` and `uddana/` entirely.**
`verify_render_vs_pdf.py` models the CANON path, so a commentary volume's 4/7/8/0 certifies a
render the reader does not perform. It has not mattered while the printed stream and the corpus

## USER-REPORTED: THE BĀHIRANIDĀNA'S PROSE IS RENDERING AS VERSE — AND MY `hide` DECISION IS THE CAUSE (2026-07-27ag)

`Paṭhamamahāsaṅgītikathā` and its neighbours draw as centred gāthā lines. They are prose.
Diagnosed, and it is a straight consequence of the decision I took on 2026-07-27v.

**What the data says.** `sections/07DiA01.json` and `sections/01VinA01.json` store whole slabs of
narrative with `k: 'gatha'`:

```
07DiA01 ord9   GATHA 'Paṭhamamahāsaṅgīti nāma cesā kiñcāpi Vinayapiṭake tantimārūḷhā,
                      nidānakosallatthaṁ pana idhāpi evaṁ veditabbā. …'
01VinA01 ord19 GATHA 'Tissopi kho mahābrahmā brahmalokato cavitvā Moggalibrāhmaṇassa
                      gehe paṭisandhiṁ aggahisi, …'
```

The reader draws a `gatha` entry as `<div class="gatha pali">` with `<br>` between lines — so
every printed line break becomes a verse line. 07DiA01 has 6 such entries and 01VinA01 has 10,
and between them they hold most of the Ganthārambha and the whole Bāhiranidāna.

**WHY, AND IT IS MY REASONING THAT WAS WRONG.** On 2026-07-27v I hid unnumbered corpus
paragraphs from the render, reasoning that "the kathā path already draws that text from the
printed stream, so rendering it from the corpus as well would draw it twice." The first half is
true. **The second half is where I stopped too early: the printed stream restores that text into
`sections`, and `sections` has exactly one shape for restored printed material — `gatha`,
display verse.** That is right for a four-pāda opening gāthā, which is all it had ever been asked
to carry. It is wrong for 26 pages of narrative.

So the design question I raised on 2026-07-27t — **does unnumbered printed prose live in the
corpus or in the side-maps?** — I answered "side-maps" on the strength of the mechanism already
existing, without checking what shape it gave the text. The evidence now says side-maps can only
render it as verse, so the answer has to be **the corpus**.

**THE FIX IS THE REVERSE OF WHAT I DID, and it has two halves that must land together:**

1. Do NOT hide unnumbered corpus paragraphs — render them, as the prose they are.
2. Do NOT restore into `sections` what the corpus already holds — the printed-stream restoration
   should supply only what is missing, which is checkable per line rather than assumed.

Landing half of it duplicates every one of those lines, which is precisely what `hide` was
avoiding. **Both halves, measured together, or neither.**

Affected: **01VinA01 and 07DiA01** — the two volumes whose corpora were rebuilt and which open
with long unnumbered prose. 02VinA02, 03VinA03, 04VinA04, 06VinSg06, 08DiA02 and 09DiA03 have
only short restored material (a homage, an uddāna, a real gāthā) and are not affected; their
`gatha` entries were checked and are verse.

**No gate sees this.** The body gate finds every printed line present, contiguous and once —
which it is. The presentation gate has no rule that prose is not set as verse. That rule is
writable: a `gatha` block whose lines carry sentence-ending punctuation mid-block, or whose
average line length matches the body measure rather than a pāda, is prose. **It belongs with the
two other assertions this session's user reports have called for** — nav node count per volume,
and apparatus proportionate to paragraph length.

## USER-REPORTED: 07DiA01 OPENED AS A WALL OF FOOTNOTES — TWO REAL DEFECTS BEHIND IT (2026-07-27af)

A screenshot of the volume's first pane showed the heading and then nothing but footnote
markers — `1 Khu 1. 21 →`, `2 Aṁ 1. 439 →`, `4 Evameva (Ka)` — several pages' apparatus in one
block and no readable text. Two separate faults, both mine, both from this session.

### 1. A COMMENTARY VOLUME'S OWN `hide` MAP WAS NEVER APPLIED

The canon spine skips hidden ordinals — `if(HIDE[String(i)])return ''` — but that `HIDE` is the
CANON volume's, indexed by canon ordinal. **Nothing anywhere consulted the TARGET volume's.**
So 07DiA01 rendered as body paragraphs:

```
ord0   hidden=True   'Sīlakkhandhavaggaṭṭhakathā'        a leaked heading, 26 chars
ord4   hidden=True   'Paṭhamamahāsaṅgīti nāma cesā…'    25,625 characters, printed pages 19-42
```

— the title line, the homage, and a 25,000-character unnumbered slab, each with its whole
apparatus attached. Fixed in `targetsFor()`, which now drops a target whose ordinal the target
volume hides. **This only became reachable when unnumbered paragraphs entered the corpus
(2026-07-27s/v): before that there was nothing in a commentary corpus for `hide` to hide.**

07DiA01 314 ¶ rendered → 313, and the volume now opens as the page does: `Dīghanikāya` /
`Sīlakkhandhavaggaṭṭhakathā` / the homage / `Ganthārambhakathā` / its gāthā / `Nidānakathā`.
All three Dīgha volumes still `ok`; canon re-checked unchanged; `regress.py check` 55/55.

### 2. THE APPARATUS OF THE THREE REBUILT VOLUMES WAS ANCHORED TO THE OLD ORDINALS

I wrote this consequence down when I rebuilt those corpora and then did not act on it. The maps
were keyed to ordinals that no longer exist, and the pile-up was visible in one line:

```
07DiA01    ord0 carried  94 notes      01VinA01   ord0 carried 40
08DiA02    biggest block 28            (never rebuilt — the sane shape)
```

Rebuilt all three with the covering-first anchoring rule (2026-07-27w):

```
07DiA01   1163 anchored (was 1297 stored)   unanchored 0   111 xref lines
01VinA01   414 anchored (was  282)          unanchored 0
05Kankha   510 anchored (was   20)          unanchored 1     8 xref lines
```

05Kankha going 20 → 510 is the measure of how much apparatus was lost while 96% of its text was
missing from the corpus. **This is the first use of `rebuild_apparatus --write` on any volume.**
The hold stands for the other 115: these three were rebuilt because their maps were already
broken by a corpus change, not as the start of the 118-volume pass, which still waits on the
ordinal-level diff.

**A LESSON I SHOULD HAVE TAKEN FROM MY OWN NOTES.** "Their `linksk` and `apparatus` maps are now
stale" was written into HANDOFF and two project docs on 2026-07-27s, and I then built three
volumes on top of them without acting on it. Writing a consequence down is not the same as
handling it, and a user reading the page found it before any gate did — **no gate tests that a
paragraph's apparatus is proportionate to its length**, which is what 94 notes on a 26-character
paragraph would have failed instantly.

## THE SIDEBAR SHOWED NINE VINAYA-AṬṬHAKATHĀ NAMES WHERE THE EDITION PRINTS SIX — USER-REPORTED (2026-07-27ae)

**Corrected: six nodes, one per printed volume.**

I had declared `separate_books` on 03VinA03 and 04VinA04, which gives every inner book its own
top-level node — three for 03VinA03, two for 04VinA04, so nine names for six volumes.

**That was the wrong invariant for these volumes, and my own doc already said so.**
`separate_books` exists for 31Abhi03, where the Dhātukathā and the Puggalapaññatti are two of the
Abhidhamma's SEVEN BOOKS and nesting one under the other would invent a book the edition does not
print. **01VinA01-04VinA04 are the opposite case: four bhāgas of ONE work, the Samantapāsādikā** —
03VinA03's own cover says it, `Samantapāsādikā nāma / PĀCITYĀDI-AṬṬHAKATHĀ` — and their inner
divisions mirror the canon's Vinaya divisions rather than standing as separate works.

So they take `label` and keep their inner books as the first tree level, which is the shape
36Abhi08 already uses (`Paṭṭhānapāḷi (Paṭhamo bhāgo)` > `Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi`):

```
01VinA01   Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā (Paṭhamo bhāgo)    1
02VinA02   Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā (Dutiyo bhāgo)     1
03VinA03   Pācityādi-aṭṭhakathā                        3   Pācityādi / Bhikkhunīvibhaṅgavaṇṇanā / Mahāvagga
04VinA04   Cūḷavaggādi-aṭṭhakathā                      2   Cūḷavaggādi / Parivāra
05Kankha   Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī-aṭṭhakathā                   0
06VinSg06  Vinayasaṅgahaṭṭhakathā                     37
```

`_navdup.js` PASS on 18,171 rows, 172 nav nodes (was 175).

**Why no check caught it.** `_navdup.js` tests for DUPLICATE labels and adjacent repeats; nine
distinct correct names are not duplicates. Nothing anywhere asserts that a nikāya's node count
matches the number of printed volumes, or that a volume contributes exactly one. **A user
counting names in the sidebar is currently the only test for this**, which is the same way the
Abhidhamma's "Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi three times" was found. That assertion belongs in `_navdup.js`.

**One cosmetic consequence, left alone deliberately.** 01VinA01 and 02VinA02 now show a single
child repeating the parent's name (`Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā` under
`Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā (Paṭhamo bhāgo)`) — a redundant rung. It is exactly how 36Abhi08
renders in the canon, so it is left consistent rather than special-cased here; if it is to
change it should change for both layers at once.

## 05Kankha NEEDS A READER THAT DOES NOT EXIST YET — READ FROM THE PAGE, NOT GUESSED (2026-07-27aa)

Two guesses about this volume have now been disproved: first that its corpus was a fragment
(19% — it is 96% once extracted properly), then that its SPEC page ranges were wrong. **Both
withdrawn. Here is what the page actually shows.**

Printed p103, the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī's Nidānavaṇṇanā:

```
84                    Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī-aṭṭhakathā
                            Nidānavaṇṇanā
    Tattha pātimokkhanti pa-atimokkhaṁ atipamokkhaṁ atiseṭṭhaṁ ati-
uttamanti attho. Iti iminā vacanatthena ekavidhampi sīlaganthabhedato
duvidhaṁ hoti. …
```

**Continuous prose under a centred kathā heading, with no numbered unit anywhere.** Across the
whole volume:

```
pages  20- 55   Bhikkhupātimokkhapāḷi        220 numbered ¶   printed scan finds 304
pages  56-101   Bhikkhunīpātimokkhapāḷi      304 numbered ¶
pages 102-311   Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī-aṭṭhakathā      5 numbered ¶   printed scan finds 0
pages 312-376   Bhikkhunīpātimokkhavaṇṇanā     5 numbered ¶   printed scan finds 0
```

**The `katha` reader pairs printed numbered units against corpus paragraphs. This volume has
five units in 210 pages, so there is nothing to pair** — and in books 1-2 the mismatch runs the
other way, 304 printed against 220 corpus, because the pātimokkha's sikkhāpada numbers are being
read as unit numbers.

None of the three page-readers fits: `verse` wants pādas under a number, `niddesa` wants a lemma
plus prose, `katha` wants a number opening prose. **What this volume wants is HEADING-DELIMITED
PROSE — the structure carried entirely by the centred kathā titles, which is what `sections`
already records and what the unnumbered-paragraph rule (2026-07-27v) already keeps out of the
render's way.** That is a fourth reader, small but real, and it is a design decision rather than
a SPEC fix. **Do not write more SPEC for this volume until it exists.**

### AND THE VOLUME IS HALF MIS-FILED

`manifest.json` places 05Kankha in the **commentary** layer, but its first two books —
`Bhikkhupātimokkhapāḷi` p20-55 and `Bhikkhunīpātimokkhapāḷi` p56-101, 46% of its printed body —
are the **canonical pātimokkhas**, each with its own homage title page. They are not commentary
on anything; they are the text the other two books comment on. Whatever reader is built, the
layer question should be settled first: a nav that lists canonical Pāḷi under "Aṭṭhakathā" is
wrong however well it renders.

**THE VINAYA-AṬṬHAKATHĀ IS FIVE OF SIX.** 01VinA01, 02VinA02, 03VinA03, 04VinA04 and 06VinSg06
are built, gated and navigable. 05Kankha is the sixth and it is not a matter of finishing —
it is the one volume in the block that the machinery was never designed for.

## THE TWO `duplicate-heading` DEFECTS WERE ONE DEFECT, AND IT WAS MINE (2026-07-27x)

03VinA03's `Catuvaggakaraṇādikathā` and 04VinA04's `Anissitavaggavaṇṇanā` are the same fault.
Neither is duplicated in any side-map — each appears exactly once. The second copy came from
**`emitHead`, which draws the corpus `book` / `vagga` fields**, and in this layer those are
RUNNING HEADERS, not structure (the scout said so plainly: "the corpus `book` field is unusable —
it alternates with the running header `Vinayapiṭaka` 118 times in 02VinA02's 240 paragraphs").

```

04VinA04 ord258   vagga='Anissitavaggavaṇṇanā'     ...and sections ord258 carries the same title
```

The canon path has always made this choice — `hasSec ? secmap(i) : (emitHead(...) + secHead(i))`
— and the `layerFront` I added on 2026-07-27p drew the sections map but left `emitHead` running
unconditionally beside it. **Where a volume has a sections map, that map is the authority and the
corpus fields are not consulted.** Fixed in `reader2.html`.

## THE APPARATUS ANCHORING CHANGE IS WRITTEN AND IS NEVER WORSE; ITS PAYOFF IS NOT YET MEASURED (2026-07-27w)

The rule HANDOFF has named four times is now in `pipeline/rebuild_apparatus.py` (backup
`.preanchor`): **a note belongs to the paragraph that COVERS its page, not to the first one
STARTING on it.**

The old candidate set was every paragraph starting within ±3 pages, and the note went to the
first of them carrying that marker number. Marker numbers restart on every page, so several
candidates in a 7-page window routinely carry the same digit — which is how `Visuddho (Syā)`,
printed ONCE on p20, ended up stored at both ord22 and ord28. The covering set is the paragraphs
that START on the page plus the ONE that started earlier and is still running through it.

**COVERING-ONLY WAS NOT A WIN, AND THE MEASUREMENT SAID SO BEFORE IT LANDED:**

```
             covering-only          old window
06Di01       173 anchored, 2 lost   175, 0      <- WORSE
07Di02       416, 0                 416, 0
08Di03       409, 0                 405, 5      <- better
09Ma01       395, 0                 395, 0
```

The two 06Di01 losses are **`pdf_page` drift** — it runs up to ~3 pages out in places (12Sam01
is off by +2 throughout), and where it drifts, "covers" is computed from the wrong pages. That
is what the ±3 window was compensating for all along.

**So the window is KEPT, BEHIND the covering set.** `hit` takes the first candidate carrying the
marker, so a genuine covering paragraph always wins and the window only rescues what drift put
out of reach. Result — never worse than the old rule, better on one of four:

```
06Di01  175 anchored, 0 unanchored    (old 175, 0)
07Di02  416, 0                        (old 416, 0)
08Di03  409, 0                        (old 405, 5)   <- five notes recovered
09Ma01  395, 0                        (old 395, 0)
```

### !!! WHAT THIS DOES NOT YET SHOW, AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT

Equal anchored COUNTS do not mean equal anchored ORDINALS. The change's purpose is to put each
note on the RIGHT paragraph, and three of these four volumes anchor the same number of notes
under both rules — which is consistent with every note moving, or with none moving.

**The measurement still to do, before any volume is rebuilt: dump the ord-per-note mapping under
both rules and diff it.** Expected shape, from `claude/apparatus_question_settled.md`: notes
should move OFF the paragraphs that merely shared a marker digit and ONTO the covering one, and
the 405 unexplained extra copies across six volumes should be the bulk of what moves. If instead
almost nothing moves, the anchoring was never the mechanism and that document's diagnosis needs
re-opening.

**NOTHING HAS BEEN REBUILT.** `rebuild_apparatus` has still not been run with `--write` on any
volume, and it should not be until that diff is read. The hold stands; what has changed is that
the rule it was waiting for now exists.

## THE BUILDER CHANGE IS IN, AND IT IS THREE LINES, NOT A REWRITE (2026-07-27v)

**The design in the previous entry was wrong about the hard part, and the reason matters.** I
expected to have to teach the walk to EMIT unnumbered corpus paragraphs. It already emits that
text — from the PRINTED stream, through `pend_before` / `add_prose`, as the following unit's
`before`. That is exactly why 01Vin01 gates 0/0/0/0 while `extract.py` had dropped 28 of its
paragraphs.

So rendering an unnumbered corpus paragraph would draw those lines **twice**. The correct change
is the opposite of the one I planned:

```python
for o in range(o0, o1):
    if str(o) not in hide and paras[o].get('n') is None:
        hide[str(o)] = 1
```

**Unnumbered corpus paragraphs are hidden from the render and kept in the corpus.** The reader
draws them from the print; the corpus is what makes them searchable, linkable and citable. Two
consumers, two sources, and the corpus is no longer required to be a subset of what the page
numbers.

**Inert on everything already built, by construction and then by test.** Of the 45 SPEC volumes
with a corpus only 01VinA01 and 05Kankha have a visible unnumbered paragraph, so `hide` gains
nothing anywhere else. Rebuilt as controls: **01Vin01 and 02VinA02 — all five side-maps
byte-identical**; `regress.py check` 55/55. 06VinSg06's `sections` changed at ord0 only, and not
from this edit: it lost `{"l": "Vinayapiṭaka", "k": "gatha"}`, the title-page series line, because
that volume gained a `booktitle` map after its sections were built — the same correction
02VinA02 took. Its body gate is still 0/0/0/0.

### 01VinA01 BUILDS

```
Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā KATHĀ  printed units 138 / corpus ¶ 138  [OK]
   verse 138 | sections 58 | uddāna 51 | hidden 37 | incipits 1

body gate (14 358, ords 0-175):
   PDF-lines-missing 15 | chunks-missing 11 | render-not-in-PDF 26 | rendered-too-often 0
```

**`rendered-too-often` is 0**, which is the number that decides whether hiding was the right
call: nothing is drawn twice. 15 missing lines across 345 printed pages puts it in the same
class as 04VinA04, and the shape looks the same — compound words broken across a line and
rejoined differently. The volume that was called unbuildable now builds, renders and gates.

### 05Kankha DOES NOT — ITS BOOK RANGES ARE WRONG, NOT ITS CORPUS

```
Bhikkhupātimokkhapāḷi       FATAL 304 printed units != 242 corpus ¶
Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī-aṭṭhakathā   printed units 0 / corpus ¶ 1
Bhikkhunīpātimokkhavaṇṇanā  printed units 0 / corpus ¶ 1
```

Books 3 and 4 find NO printed numbered units in their declared page ranges, so the ranges in
`SPEC['05Kankha']` are wrong — they were written from the title-page scan without the per-book
unit scouting every other volume got. **This is a SPEC error, not a corpus error**: the corpus is
96% of the printed body and its page anchors are monotonic. It needs the ordinary treatment —
`scout_volume.py` per book, the geometry measured, the ranges read off the page.

### WHAT THIS OPENS

The same three lines unblock **07DiA01** once its corpus is rebuilt (26-page unnumbered opening,
body p17-354, index from p355). And they settle the question for the whole layer: unnumbered
printed prose lives in the CORPUS for search and in the PRINTED STREAM for the page, and never in
both at once.

Backup: `pipeline/build_khu_volume.py.preunnum`.

## THE BUILDER CHANGE: SCOPED, AND THE FIRST HALF IS PROVABLY INERT (2026-07-27u)

The blocker is one line in `kat_build`:

```python
rec['printed_units'] = len(printed)
if len(printed) != len(ords):
    rec['FATAL'] = 'printed numbered units %d != corpus paragraphs %d'
```

`ords` is the book's VISIBLE corpus ordinals and it serves two jobs at once — it is the list
paired 1:1 against the printed numbered units, **and** it is the walk (`seq = iter(ords)`) that
emits the body. Those two jobs part company the moment the corpus holds a paragraph with no
number: an unnumbered paragraph must be WALKED but must not be PAIRED.

**So the change is to separate them:** pair against `[o for o in ords if paras[o]['n'] is not
None]`, keep the walk over all of `ords`, and emit an unnumbered paragraph in place.

**THE FIRST HALF IS PROVABLY INERT, and this is the measurement that says so.** Across **all 45
SPEC volumes that have a corpus**, the only visible paragraphs carrying no number are in the two
volumes rebuilt this session:

```
01VinA01    37 of 175
05Kankha   398 of 932
    ...and NONE in any of the other 43
```

So `pair_ords` cannot change a single existing volume — there is nothing in them for it to
change. The 1:1 count that has verified every volume built to date keeps exactly the meaning it
has always had, because in every one of those volumes the two lists are the same list.

**The second half — emitting an unnumbered paragraph in the walk — is the real work**, and it is
NOT inert by construction: it touches the loop that draws every book's body. The standing
treatment applies to that half and none of it is done yet: build every SPEC volume twice, diff
the five side-maps, ENUMERATE what changes, stop on any shape not predicted in advance.

**The 07DiA01 measurement that decided the order.** Of the three Dīgha-Aṭṭhakathā volumes, two
need none of this and one needs all of it:

```
08DiA02   shipped corpus 99% of the printed body   corpus starts p10, body starts p10   BUILDABLE NOW
09DiA03   shipped corpus 96%                       corpus starts p10, body starts p10   BUILDABLE NOW
07DiA01   shipped corpus 89%                       corpus starts p43, body starts p17   SAME WALL
```

07DiA01 opens with a 26-page unnumbered Ganthārambha and Bāhiranidāna — the same shape as
01VinA01's 78 pages, smaller. So the builder change unblocks **07DiA01, 01VinA01 and 05Kankha**
together, and settles the corpus-vs-side-map question for the whole 78-volume layer.

## I WAS WRONG: THE CORPUS IS REPRODUCIBLE FROM THE PDF, AND 01VinA01 AND 05Kankha ARE NOW 99% AND 96% (2026-07-27s)

**CORRECTION TO A CLAIM I PUT ON THE CRITICAL PATH TWICE.** I wrote that the corpus "is not
reproducible from the repo" because `site/*.json` paragraphs carry `key`, `covers`, `n_to` and
`peyyala`, "none produced by `pipeline/extract.py`, none produced by anything in the repo", and
that the extractor fix therefore "cannot be applied until the missing generator stage is
reconstructed". **That was never tested. It is false.** All four fields are plain derivations:

```
key      = '<VOL>#<ordinal>'
n, n_to  = the paragraph's own printed number, and the second half of a range ("182-3.")
covers   = list(range(n, n_to+1))
peyyala  = n_to > n
```

Checked over **118 volumes and 83,752 paragraphs**: zero mismatches except two paragraphs of
18Khu01 where the shipped value is `None` and the derivation gives `[]`.

And the extractor itself reproduces the corpus. `extract.py` run on the PDF, plus those four
derived fields, diffed field by field against the shipped file:

```
01Vin01     662 ¶   byte-for-byte
06Di01      559 ¶   byte-for-byte
20Khu03    4461 ¶   byte-for-byte
29Abhi01   1780 ¶   byte-for-byte
02VinA02    240 ¶   byte-for-byte  (needs PARA to admit "182-3.", which is inert on the four above)
```

Five volumes, 7,702 paragraphs, four piṭaka divisions. **The blocker was imaginary, and it held
back the whole commentary layer for two sessions.**

### WHY 01VinA01 REALLY STOPPED AT PRINTED p93

Not a corrupt corpus and not a missing generator. **`extract.py` opens a paragraph only on a
`NN.` marker and has no `else`**, so text outside a numbered paragraph is dropped. 01VinA01's
first numbered unit is `1. Idāni` on printed **p93**; everything before it — the
Ganthārambhakathā and the whole Bāhiranidāna, the account of the councils, pages 15-92 — is
**unnumbered running prose**, and it simply never opened a paragraph. The "78-page run missing
from its start" is that, exactly.

Rebuilt from the PDF with the missing `else` restored (`_fnprobe/rebuild_corpus.py`):

```
01VinA01   138 -> 163 ¶   429,631 -> 694,193 chars   pdf_page 93..359 -> 15..401
05Kankha   534 -> 861 ¶   107,872 -> 610,594 chars   pdf_page 21..368 -> 20..412
```

Measured against the printed body text: **01VinA01 69% -> 99%, 05Kankha 19% -> 96%.** Both are
now in the same band as the four volumes that built cleanly. Old corpora in
`_fnprobe/corpus_pre/`.

### !!! THE FIX MUST NOT BE APPLIED TO A VOLUME ALREADY BUILT, AND THIS IS WHY

Run against shipped volumes the same fix is **not** inert: 01Vin01 gains 28 unnumbered
paragraphs (+41,877 chars) and 06Di01 gains 6 (+17,972). But **26 of 01Vin01's 28 are already
on the page** — `build_khu_volume.py` restores them from the printed page into `uddana`,
`sections`, `incipit` and `verse`. That is why 01Vin01 gates 0/0/0/0 with an incomplete corpus.
Adding them to the corpus as well would render each twice and the gate would report
`rendered-too-often`.

So the architecture, stated plainly for the first time: **the corpus holds NUMBERED UNITS; every
other printed line is restored into a side-map at build time.** A corpus-vs-print character
ratio therefore measures *how much of a volume is unnumbered prose*, not how much is
unrecoverable — which is why my 69% / 19% screen led me to call two volumes unbuildable when
their text was in the PDF all along. **The body gate is the arbiter; I wrote that myself and
then used a cheap screen anyway.**

01VinA01 and 05Kankha are the right scope for the fix precisely because nothing has been built
for them: no side-map exists to duplicate.

### CONSEQUENCES TO CARRY FORWARD

* **Their `linksk` and `apparatus` maps are now stale** — both were keyed to the old ordinals
  (01VinA01: 63 apparatus entries, 117 reverse links; 05Kankha: 9 and 101). They must be rebuilt
  when those volumes are built. `rebuild_apparatus` stays held until the anchoring change.
* Neither volume has a SPEC, a body build or a nav yet. **Nothing is blocking that now.**
* The 78 pages recovered for 01VinA01 are running narrative, not headings — they belong in the
  corpus, which is where they now are, not in `sections/`.

## THE COMMENTARY LAYER'S FRONT MATTER AND HEADINGS WERE BUILT, WRITTEN TO DISK, AND NEVER DRAWN (2026-07-27p)

**`titleHTML`, `incHTML` and `canonHead`→`secmap` all read `cache[state.canonVol]` — and for a
commentary or Ṭīkā volume `state.canonVol` is the CANON BOOK THE WORK HANGS OFF, not the work
itself.** So a commentary volume's own title page, its homage and every one of its section
headings were anchored, generated, saved, and then silently dropped at render time. 02VinA02
has 74 headings across 60 anchors; **the reading pane drew none of them** and ran its 240
paragraphs together with nothing between them. No gate said a word — `check_layout.js` reported
only `incipit-not-rendered`, and only because 02VinA02 is the one volume in the layer that has
an `incipit/` file.

**Fixed in `reader2.html` (backup `.prelayerfront`) with `layerFront(key)`**: for a non-canon
spine, read `btl` / `inc` / `sec` from the TARGET volume's cache, keyed by the TARGET
ordinal. 02VinA02's opening now reproduces printed p7 line for line:

```
Vinayapiṭaka                                    <- head bookseries
Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā                        <- head booktitle
Namo tassa Bhagavato Arahato Sammāsambuddhassa. <- incipit
3. Tatiyapārājika                               <- head section
Tatiyaṁ tīhi suddhena, … (4 pādas)              <- gatha
Paṭhamapaññattinidānavaṇṇanā                    <- head section
162. Tena samayena Buddho Bhagavā …
```

**A SECOND DEFECT THE FIX IMMEDIATELY EXPOSED — and it would have shipped.** Several canon
paragraphs routinely point at ONE commentary paragraph. The block is deduped (`if(dedup &&
t.key===lastA) return`), the head was not, so every such heading drew TWICE with the single
paragraph between the two copies — `Ānāpānassatisamādhikathā` above 02VinA02 ¶165 and again
above ¶167. **`duplicate-heading` cannot see it**: that rule tests two heads with NOTHING
between, which is the artifact it was written for. The head now obeys the same dedup as the
block. *Found by reading the rendered stream, not by a gate.*

**A THIRD, in the data, fixed by the builder itself.** `sections/02VinA02.json` held
`{"l":"Vinayapiṭaka","k":"sutta"}` at ord0 — the title page's series line captured as a section
heading, which with `booktitle/` now drawing that same line put "Vinayapiṭaka" on the page
twice. The volume was built before it had a booktitle map. Rebuilt: **one change across all six
side-maps — that entry, gone.** `verse`, `uddana`, `hide`, `incipit`, `booktitle` byte-identical.
No hand-editing of a generated map.

**NEW GATE — RULE 6, `sections-not-rendered`.** Every heading group anchored on a paragraph
that is ON SCREEN must be ON SCREEN. **Proved against the defect it was written for:** with
`reader2.html.prelayerfront` swapped back in it reports `51 of 51 anchored heading group(s) on
rendered paragraphs are absent (first ord 0)`; with the fix, zero. That is the assertion that
closes this whole class — a side-map that is built, saved, and never drawn.

**!!! DO NOT READ THE LAYER-WIDE SILENCE AS A PASS.** Rule 6 is quiet on 77 of the 78 volumes
because **they have no `sections/` file at all** — their bodies have not been built. Absence of
data is not absence of defect. Every one of them will have to pass this rule once built.

**Sweeps after the change.** All 40 canon volumes re-run and diffed line by line against the
pre-change output: **identical, all 40.** The whole commentary + sub-commentary layer re-run:

```
21 ok · 52 PART · 0 FAIL · 5 REFUSED     (was 21 · 51 · 1 · 5)
```

Exactly one volume moved — 02VinA02, FAIL → PART, `incipit x0` → `incipit x1`. Nothing else in
the layer changed by so much as a paragraph count. `regress.py check` 55/55.

### AND AN ERROR IN SHIPPED WORK: FOUR OF THE SIX VINAYA COMMENTARY NAV LABELS NAME THE WRONG BOOK

The commentary nav is a placeholder from an early automatic pass. Read against the printed
title pages (`pdftotext -f 1 -l 1`):

| vol | nav label today | the title page prints |

| 02VinA02 | `Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā IV` | `PĀRĀJIKAKAṆḌA-AṬṬHAKATHĀ (Dutiyo bhāgo)` |
| 03VinA03 | `Mahāvagga-aṭṭhakathā` | `Samantapāsādikā nāma` / `PĀCITYĀDI-AṬṬHAKATHĀ` |
| 04VinA04 | `Cūḷavagga-aṭṭhakathā` | `CŪḶAVAGGĀDI-AṬṬHAKATHĀ` |
| 05Kankha | `Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī-aṭṭhakathā` | `KAṄKHĀVITARAṆĪ-AṬṬHAKATHĀ` ✓ |

03VinA03 and 04VinA04 are labelled with the names of **Vinaya canon divisions**, not of the
works they contain. 01VinA01 carries **14 book nodes** where the edition has one book: three

`Ākāsaṭṭhakathā` …) promoted to book level. The roman numerals are nobody's — the edition
distinguishes the two Pārājikakaṇḍa volumes by **bhāga** (`Paṭhamo` / `Dutiyo`), which is also
what keeps two nav nodes from sharing a label. **None of the six commentary navs has any

volume's INNER title page and there says only `Vinayapiṭaka / Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā` — so

form with the bhāga belongs in the NAV label, where it does the disambiguating the edition
itself intends. If the reading pane should carry the bhāga too, that is a decision to take
explicitly and record — not to slip in.

## THE PRESENTATION GATE NOW COVERS THE WHOLE COMMENTARY LAYER — AND THE REVERSE-LINK MAP HAD BEEN STALE SINCE THE LINKER WAS REBUILT (2026-07-27o)

`check_layout.js` walks a commentary volume once per HOST canon volume and grades the union.
All 78 commentary and sub-commentary volumes have now been through the presentation gate for
the first time. **Nothing in the layer fails a layout rule.** One volume fails, on the front
matter the user asked for; five refuse; the rest pass on what the reader can reach.

**THE THING THAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG WAS NOT THE CHECKER.** `linksk/*.rev.json` — the map from
a commentary paragraph back to its canon paragraph — was written 2026-07-23 **16:58**. The
forward links were rebuilt by `build_links_bynum.py` at **23:42–23:54** the same day and
`build_reverse.py` was never re-run. Every rev file in the repo was five to seven hours older
than the links it inverts. Measured before touching it, then confirmed against the actual
regeneration:

| | predicted | actual |
|---|---|---|
| files differing | 68 | 68 |
| entries added | +9,562 | +9,562 |
| entries pointing at a different canon paragraph | 3,169 | 3,169 |
| entries dropped | 4,401 | 4,401 |
| files gained | 4 (05Kankha, 36KhuA17, 37KhuA18, 38KhuA19) | same |
| files orphaned | 1 (09DiT02) | same |

Consequences while it was stale: the reader's **↩ Canon** button sent you to the wrong canon
paragraph in 3,169 cases and was simply absent for 10,943 more; and `openKey` resolved a
commentary volume's host canon volume from it, so **02VinA02 opened 02Vin02 and showed 45 of
its 240 paragraphs when 146 of them hang off 01Vin01.** Regenerated with `build_reverse.py`;
old copies in `_revbak_20260727/`, the orphan moved to `_to_delete/rev_orphan_20260727/`.
**A derived file with no freshness check is a wrong answer waiting to be believed** — nothing
in the pipeline notices that rev is older than links.

**A commentary volume is not reachable through one opening.** `openKey(k,'A')` resolves the
paragraph to its canon counterpart and opens THAT canon volume with `state.filter` set, so one
opening shows the slice hanging off one canon volume. 02VinA02's 240 paragraphs hang off four
(146 · 01Vin01, 43 · 02Vin02, 15 · 05Vin05, 3 · 04Vin04); 22AbhiT01 and 50AbhiA03 hang off
twelve. `hostsOf()` reads the rev map, takes the first paragraph per host, and the checker
opens each in turn — clearing `state.curbook` first, since it survives an earlier click and
clamps `render()` to one book's BOOKSPAN.

**THREE CORRECTIONS TO THE CHECKER ITSELF, each caught by a control:**

1. **The PARTIAL marker was crying wolf on five shipped canon volumes.** Coverage was
   `mine / corpus`, but the reader deliberately does not draw the `hide` map — 40Abhi12 hides
   714 of its 2,413 paragraphs by design. 36Abhi08 read "1348 of 1091 = 92% PARTIAL". The
   denominator is now corpus − hidden. **Enumerated, not counted:** 15 canon volumes changed
   their paragraph number and **all 15 now equal `corpus − hidden` exactly**, as do the other
   25 that did not move. Every canon volume renders 100% of what it is meant to render.
   (Two side-effects of the same fix: the count is now the volume's OWN paragraphs, so
   restored `plain` uddāna blocks — `.para.canon` with no id — are no longer counted as
   corpus text; and 28Khu11 drops 364→258 because 106 of what was counted were those blocks.)
2. **`prose-number-stacked :: 207` on 02VinA02 was a false positive — all 207 correct.**
   That rule describes the CANON renderer, where `block()` hands the number into the first
   `.gatha`/`.gatha-after`. A commentary paragraph is built by `fmtBold`, which returns inline
   html: the `<span class="pn">` is followed directly by a `<b>` and there is nothing for it
   to be inside. Read the actual `outerHTML` before believing the rule. The rule now branches
   on `.para.canon` and asserts for the other layers what it actually means — the number must
   be followed by inline content, which `reading:'outline'` would break.
3. **Four volumes reported `host-rendered-nothing` because the render-wait loop waited for
   2,000 characters.** A host contributing one commentary paragraph never reaches that, so the
   loop burned 6.3s and declared the host empty. It now waits for *this volume's* paragraphs.
   **Enumerated:** exactly four volumes changed (26KhuA07, 27KhuA08, 28KhuA09, 39KhuA20), all
   from FAIL to PART/ok, and **all four kept an identical paragraph count** — the false alarm
   went away without a single paragraph going quiet with it.

Also `w.close()` per volume: without it the run holds every JSDOM window it ever made and node
dies of heap exhaustion in the middle of the Khuddaka — which looks exactly like a checker that
found nothing wrong with the volumes it never reached.

**THE SWEEP — 78 volumes, `_fnprobe/check_layout_AT.log`:**

```
21 ok  ·  51 PART  ·  1 FAIL  ·  5 REFUSED
```

* **1 FAIL — 02VinA02, `incipit-not-rendered`.** Real, and it is the thing the user asked for:
  `incHTML` and `titleHTML` are drawn on the CANON spine only, so a commentary volume's homage
  and its cover title (`PĀRĀJIKAKAṆḌA-AṬṬHAKATHĀ (Paṭhamo bhāgo)`) never reach the page even
  when the side-maps hold them. 02VinA02 is the only volume in the layer with an `incipit/`
  file, so it is the only one that can report this yet — **the other 77 will fail the same way
  the moment they get one.** Fixing it is a reader change, not a data change.
* **5 REFUSED — 09DiT02, 25VsmT01, 26VsmT02, 51Vism01, 52Vism02** have no reverse map at all:
  no canon paragraph links to them, so the reader has no route into them. Vism/VsmT are the
  Visuddhimagga and its ṭīkā, which comment on no single canon text — expected. 09DiT02 is not:
  it HAD 80 rev entries before the by-num rebuild and now has none.
* **NOT ONE volume in the layer failed `homage-as-body`, `verse-number-stacked`,
  `duplicate-heading`, `opens-with-uddana` or `rule-leaked-into-body`.**

**THE REAL RESULT IS THE COVERAGE NUMBER, AND IT IS NOT GOOD: the reader can reach 23,016 of
the layer's 32,265 paragraphs — 71%.** 21 volumes ≥95%, 24 at 70–94%, 11 at 40–69%, and
**17 below 40%**: 07ViT07 5%, 10DiT03 16%, 05Kankha 18%, 26KhuA07 22%, 05ViT05 24%, 18AnT01
25%, 04ViT04 27%, 17AnA01 28%, 20AnT03 28%, 19AnA03 32%. A paragraph no canon paragraph links
to cannot be displayed at all — the link map is the reader's only route into the layer, so
**link coverage is a hard ceiling on presentation coverage, and no amount of checker work
raises it.** That, not the checker, is now the top commentary-side item. Note also that
`build_links_bynum` joins on the paragraph NUMBER, which is why 22AbhiT01 spreads over twelve
canon volumes — the number collides across volumes and the "keep the existing target volume"
carry is doing all the disambiguation. Whether those wide spreads are right is untested.

**Gates run:** `check_layout.js` over all 40 canon volumes (before and after, diffed line by
line) and over all 78 commentary/sub-commentary volumes twice; `regress.py check` 55/55 after
every edit. Body and apparatus gates untouched — this entry says nothing about content.
Backup: `pipeline/check_layout.js.prewalk`.

## `check_layout.js` FIXED — IT CAN REACH A COMMENTARY VOLUME, IT REFUSES WHEN IT CANNOT, AND IT NO LONGER PASSES OFF A FIFTH OF A VOLUME AS A VERDICT (2026-07-27n)

### The three faults

1. **`openKey(key, layerkind)` TAKES A SECOND ARGUMENT AND THE CHECKER PASSED
   ONE.** Without it a COMMENTARY volume resolves to
   `state.active={canon:true}` and the reader renders that volume's CANON
   COUNTERPART. The checker then selected `.para.canon` — exactly what was on
   screen — and graded those canon paragraphs against the COMMENTARY's verse
   map. Every id missed, so every numbered paragraph containing a gāthā was
   flagged: **`FAIL 02VinA02 / verse-number-stacked :: 127`**, while
   `check_layout.js 02Vin02` PASSED on the identical render. Same pixels,
   opposite verdict, decided only by which verse map was loaded.
2. **THE SELECTOR IS LAYER-SPECIFIC.** Canon paragraphs carry `.para.canon`,
   commentary `.para.l-A`, subcommentary `.para.l-T`. The checker only ever
   knew the first.
3. **`openKey` OPENS ONE SLICE OF A COMMENTARY VOLUME, NOT THE BOOK.**
   02VinA02 renders **45 of its 240 paragraphs**, and that was being reported
   as a whole-volume verdict.

### The fix

* `layerOf(vol)` reads the volume's layer from `nav.json`; `LAYERKIND` and
  `LAYERSEL` give the right `openKey` argument and the right selector.
* **THE ONE-LINE ASSERTION THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT ALL OF THIS:** the rendered
  paragraphs must BELONG to the volume asked about (`id` contains `-<VOL>-`).
  If none do, **REFUSE** with the offending id rather than grade. *A checker
  that cannot reach its subject must refuse, not grade* — the same lesson as
  `_vinnavverify.js` reporting "292 of 292 rows clicked" for a 156-row volume.
* **NO SILENT PARTIAL CHECKS.** Coverage is computed against the volume's
  corpus paragraph count and printed when below 95%:
  `PART 02VinA02  45 ¶ … [PARTIAL: 45 of 240 ¶ = 19% examined]`, and the
  summary line now counts PARTIAL separately from clean.

### Proved inert on the canon

Old vs new on the same volumes, byte-identical verdicts and counts. Twenty-four
canon volumes re-run under the new file, **all `ok` with unchanged paragraph
counts** — 01Vin01 661, 02Vin02 1242, 03Vin03 478, 04Vin04 454, 05Vin05 500,
06Di01 559, 07Di02 441, 08Di03 360, 09Ma01 512, 10Ma02 486, 11Ma03 464,
12Sam01 517, 13Sam02 722, 14Sam03 598, 15An01 952, 16An02 498, 17An03 426,
19Khu02 3657, 20Khu03 4461, 24Khu07 210, 26Khu09 404, 29Abhi01 1819.
Backup `pipeline/check_layout.js.precommentary`.

### What it now says about 02VinA02 — REAL findings, on 19% of the volume

    FAIL 02VinA02  45 ¶, incipit x0  [PARTIAL: 45 of 240 ¶ = 19% examined]
        - incipit-not-rendered :: 1 anchored, 0 rendered
        - prose-number-stacked :: 45 prose unit(s)

These are no longer artefacts, but they are **not a whole-volume verdict**
either, and the incipit one may simply be that the opened slice does not
contain ord 0. **02VinA02 remains unverified on presentation.** Making the
checker walk a whole commentary volume — several `openKey` calls, one per
canon section it maps onto — is the next piece of this work.

## PILOT — 02VinA02 IS THE FIRST COMMENTARY VOLUME TO PASS THE BODY GATE, AND IT FAILS PRESENTATION (2026-07-27n)

**`SPEC['02VinA02']` written and built. Body gate `6 317 0 240`: 0/0/0/0 at
minw 4 AND 1.** Apparatus parsed: 480 stored / 424 printed cells / 0 spliced /
4 variants / 2 xrefs. `regress.py check` 55/55. Side-maps WRITTEN.

**This settles the pilot's first question: the corpus front-matter loss is NOT
universal.** 02VinA02 loses nothing its render needs, where 06VinSg06 loses its
whole Ganthārambhakathā. So the shortlist is worth building volume by volume.

Its mātikā diff is canon-scale — 69 entries, 75 headings, and the residue is
one erratum (`4. Nissaggiyakaṇḍa` mātikā vs `4. Nissaggiyakaṇṭa` body), the
title-stack line `Vinayapiṭaka`, the running formula
`Samantapāsādikāya Vinayasaṁvaṇṇanāya`, `Dutiyabhāga` (the mātikā's own
subtitle), and two mātikā entries the body splits in two.

### !!! `check_layout.js` CANNOT DRIVE A COMMENTARY VOLUME — ITS "FAIL 02VinA02 / 127" IS AN ARTEFACT, AND IT REPORTS IT AS A CONFIDENT FAILURE

**RESOLVED 2026-07-27n. 02VinA02's presentation is UNVERIFIED, not failed.**

The mechanism, established from the render (`_fnprobe/vnprobe.js`,
`_fnprobe/navrow.js`), not inferred:

* Of the 21,245 nav rows the reader renders, **ZERO carry a `02VinA02#` key**
  by either mechanism the checker tries (`data-k` prefix, `onclick` substring)
  — the commentary layer's rows are not exposed the way the canon's are, even
  though `nav.json` holds four such keys.
* So the checker falls through to its own fallback, `w.openKey(vol+'#0')`,
  which **opens the CANON counterpart 02Vin02** (the A-layer is shown beside
  its canon text).
* It then grades those 1,242 **02Vin02** paragraphs — ids `p-02Vin02-244` … —
  against **02VinA02's** verse map. Every id misses, `e` is undefined, so
  `isProse` is false for every one, and every numbered paragraph containing a
  gāthā is counted. Hence 127.
* **`check_layout.js 02Vin02` passes on the identical render.** Same pixels,
  opposite verdict, decided entirely by which verse map was loaded.

**IT DOES NOT SAY "not driveable headlessly" — IT SAYS FAIL.** That is the same
false-signal class as `_vinnavverify.js` reporting "292 of 292 rows clicked"
for a 156-row volume (2026-07-27). **A checker that cannot reach its subject
must REFUSE, not grade.**

**CONSEQUENCE: no commentary volume can be presentation-gated until this is
fixed**, and any `check_layout.js` verdict on a commentary volume — pass or
fail — is meaningless. The fix has two parts: make the checker able to open a
commentary volume (or refuse loudly), and make it assert that the rendered
paragraph ids actually belong to the volume it was asked about. **That second
assertion is one line and would have caught this immediately.**

### (superseded) the original note

**NOT DIAGNOSED, AND NOT WORKED AROUND.** What is established: the volume's
verse map has **ZERO units with verse groups** (0 of 239), so these are not
prose-drawn-as-verse in the 27Khu10 sense. The check's branch that fires is the
one for a paragraph that is NOT `isProse` — and `isProse` is
`Array.isArray(e.groups) && e.groups.length===0`, which is FALSE when the
paragraph has no verse entry `e` at all. So the 127 are rendered paragraphs
with no verse entry that nonetheless contain a `.gatha` with the unit number
outside it.

Whether that is a real visual defect or a check that mis-handles a volume whose
rendered paragraph count (1242) far exceeds its verse entries (239) **is not
established, and must not be assumed either way** — read the rendered HTML.
**02VinA02 is therefore NOT clean and must not be listed as done.**

### The pilot's standing instruction

Build the shortlist one volume at a time and let the gates speak. The screens
cannot certify a volume; the body gate can, and the presentation gate is the
one that just caught something no content gate could see — again.

## THE COMMENTARY HEADING RULE IS IN — 38 OF 39 VOLUMES INERT, AND IT CORRECTS A SHIPPED ONE; BUT THE FRONT MATTER IS MISSING FROM MOST OF THE LAYER (2026-07-27m)

### THE RULE, AND IT SHIPPED

**A display line whose SUCCESSOR begins lowercase is mid-sentence, and a
heading is never continued by one.** Under `heads_by_form` `kat_is_head` asks
only for a capital, six words or fewer, no comma and no terminal stop — and the
commentary quotes canonical kammavācā PROSE at a display indent constantly:

    06VinSg06 p114   9| Sammato saṁghena itthannāmo vihāro kappiyabhūmi khamati
                     6| saṁghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṁ dhārayāmī”ti.

THE SIGNAL IS THE CAPITAL — the measurement this file already carries
("every heading, colophon, homage, title and pāda opens with one"). `wrap_display`
uses it for the line ITSELF; this uses it for the line BELOW. `headfix` wins.

**MEASURED OVER ALL 39 SPEC VOLUMES, A SHIPPED CANON VOLUME RUN FIRST AS A
CONTROL** (`_fnprobe/headnext.py`): **THIRTY-EIGHT BYTE-IDENTICAL.** Two move:

* **06VinSg06** — 31 quoted-formula lines demoted (the target).
* **15An01** — TWO RUNNING HEADERS demoted, **and that is a CORRECTION**,
  checked on the page: 0-based p292 sets the real stack `3. Tatiyapaṇṇāsaka /
  (11) 1. Sambodhavagga / 1. Pubbevasambodhasutta`, while p294 and p298 repeat
  `(11) 1. Sambodhavagga` as the PAGE HEADER above body text continuing
  mid-sentence. The real heading is kept. **p296 is a THIRD such running header
  and SURVIVES** — its successor opens with a capital — a pre-existing defect
  the rule neither fixes nor worsens. Recorded, not worked around.
  15An01 rebuilt and re-gated: body `32 611 0 952` **0/0/0/0** at minw 4 and 1,
  `check_layout.js` ok, nav rebuilt (559 keys), `_samspan.js` 555 rows 0 empty
  spans, `_navdup.js` PASS. `regress.py check` 55/55.

**With the rule plus a handful of named literals, 06VinSg06's heads stream is
CLEAN** — 37 headings against 35 mātikā entries, ZERO spurious, and the single
unresolved mātikā entry is the edition's own `Adhiṭṭhāna`/`Adhiṭthāna` erratum.
The literals: `colofix` for the section closing formula
`Iti Pāḷimuttakavinayavinicchayasaṅgahe` (33 printings, one literal) and its
variant; `headskip` for four lines, each checked on its page. **That is
canon-scale treatment, which is the point — the class went from unmanageable to
ordinary.**

### !!! BUT 06VinSg06 IS NOT WRITTEN, AND THE REASON IS A NEW FINDING

Body gate `5 472 0 327`: **PDF-lines-missing 51.** Every one of them is the
**GANTHĀRAMBHAKATHĀ** — the homage, the four opening verses, and the verse
listing the 34 topics. The corpus simply does not have them: it opens at
`1. Tattha divāseyyāti…`, and `Vatthuttayaṁ namassitvā`, `Divāseyyā parikkhāro`
and `Namo tassa` are all absent from it.

**THE COMPLETENESS CENSUS CANNOT SEE THIS.** 51 lines is ~0.5% of the volume,
so 06VinSg06 scores **99%** and looks sound. Tested directly instead — does the
corpus contain the volume's FIRST BODY PAGE? —

    01Vin01    CANON control   corpus picks up at word 76   (after title + homage) OK
    51Vism01   commentary      corpus picks up at word  7                          OK
    01VinA01 02VinA02 03VinA03 04VinA04 06VinSg06 07DiA01 17AnA01
    19AnT02  25VsmT01          FIRST BODY PAGE NOT IN THE CORPUS AT ALL

**Nine of eleven volumes sampled are missing their opening page** — including
02VinA02 at "97%" and 06VinSg06 at "99%". So the front-matter loss is
widespread and is INDEPENDENT of the ratio. **Run this test, not the ratio,
before calling any commentary volume buildable.** The census's SOUND list is
therefore optimistic and must be re-screened this way.

### A REJECTED HYPOTHESIS ABOUT `extract.py` — DO NOT RETRY IT

`extract.py` starts a corpus paragraph only at `PARA = ^\s*(\d{1,4})\.\s+`, a
NUMBERED line, so the obvious explanation for the lost front matter is that the
dropped regions carry no numbered units — the Ganthārambhakathā is unnumbered
verse, and that would explain 06VinSg06 exactly.

**MEASURED, AND IT IS NOT THE CAUSE.** Numbered-unit lines per page, lost
region vs kept region of the same volume:

    01VinA01   lost p14-91   0.83/pg   kept p92-359   1.20/pg
    20KhuA01   lost p19-120  1.40/pg   kept p121-234  1.86/pg
    05Kankha   lost p216-375 2.53/pg   kept p19-215   3.65/pg

The numbers ARE there in the lost regions, at comparable density. So the loss is
not "no numbers, no paragraph" and `extract.py` needs a real investigation —
page-range handling, book-boundary truncation, or something else. **Budget it as
work, not as a one-line fix.** (`PARA` requiring `\s+` after the period is still
worth fixing on its own account — it is the same trap that hid 09Ma01's
`42.Tassa` — but it is not this.)

### THE SCREENS HAVE A FLOOR, AND THE CONTROLS FOUND IT — STOP SCREENING, START BUILDING

Three corpus-side screens were built to decide which commentary volumes are
worth a SPEC. Measured against SHIPPED CANON VOLUMES as controls:

* **ratio** — good for gross loss (condemned 25 of 78), **blind below ~5%**;
  06VinSg06 loses its whole Ganthārambhakathā and still scores 99%.
* **edge test** (is the first/last printed body page in the corpus?) — good for
  contiguous end-loss, and it caught SIX volumes the ratio passed as sound
  (03ViT03, 10DiT03, 14SamA01, 17AnA01, 43KhuA24, 46KhuA27). Biggest finds:
  05Kankha missing its LAST 159 pages, 20KhuA01 its first 102, 07ViT07 its
  first 94, 36KhuA17 its first 82, 01VinA01 its first 78. Controls: 01Vin01
  0/1, 06Di01 1/1, 29Abhi01 0/0 — one page at either end is NORMAL.
  **Blind within a page**, which is where 06VinSg06's loss sits.
* **line-level test — ABANDONED.** Printed body lines whose first six words are
  absent from the corpus: **15An01, shipped and gating 0/0/0/0, scores 3.3% —
  worse than 06VinSg06's 0.8% with its known 51-line loss.** 01Vin01 0.9%,
  06Di01 1.2%, 29Abhi01 0.1%. The noise floor exceeds the signal, because
  printed lines break words mid-token.

**NO CHEAP CORPUS-SIDE SCREEN CAN CERTIFY A VOLUME.** The only instrument that
found 06VinSg06's 51 lines is the BODY GATE, which compares the page against
the RENDER — where broken lines are rejoined — not against raw corpus text.

**So the next session should BUILD, not screen further.** The screens have done
their job: the hopeless volumes are identified. **28 volumes pass both
surviving screens** and are the shortlist:

    02VinA02 03VinA03 06VinSg06 08DiA02 09DiA03 11DiT04 11MaA02 12DiT05
    12MaA03 13MaA04 14MaT02 15MaT03 15SamA02 16SaT01 16SamA03 17SaT02
    18AnA02 18AnT01 19AnA03 19AnT02 20AnT03 25VsmT01 26VsmT02 38KhuA19
    47KhuA28 49AbhiA02 51Vism01 52Vism02

**A SHORTLIST, NOT A WARRANT** — 06VinSg06 is on it and is known to be short.
Expect failures of the same shape: small, and at the FRONT.

**THE LESSON, EARNED THREE TIMES IN ONE DAY.** The encoding census reported 384
of 403 pages contaminated; the per-page probe reported 295 of 396 pages absent;
the line test ranks a shipped volume worst of six. Every one looked convincing
until a known-good volume went through it. **RUN THE CONTROL FIRST, NOT AFTER.**

### WHERE THIS LEAVES THE LAYER

* The reader now FITS — that was the open question and it is answered.
* **`pipeline/extract.py` is now unambiguously the blocking work**: 25 volumes
  fail the ratio, and most of the rest lose their front matter.
* **Still nothing written to `site/reader/` for any commentary volume.**
  `SPEC['06VinSg06']` is complete and correct except for what the corpus lacks.

### Files

* `pipeline/build_khu_volume.py` — the successor rule in `kat_items`;
  `SPEC['06VinSg06']` gains `colofix` and `headskip`. Backups `.preheadnext`,
  `.previnA`.
* `_fnprobe/headnext.py` — the 39-volume measurement, re-runnable.
* 15An01 side-maps and nav rewritten.

## THE WHOLE COMMENTARY LAYER IS CENSUSED — ENCODING IS UNIFORM, BUT A THIRD OF IT CANNOT BE BUILT FROM ITS CORPUS (2026-07-27l)

All 78 volumes swept — 52 Aṭṭhakathā, 26 Ṭīkā. Full table:
`claude/commentary_layer_census.md`; raw data `_fnprobe/census78.json`.

### ENCODING — SETTLED FOR THE ENTIRE LAYER

**Every one of the 78 shows exactly 2 pages / 9 characters of legacy residue**,
the Burmese alphabet tables on pages 1-2, byte-identical to shipped canon
volumes. Not one differs. **Open question 2 of the project instructions is
answered for the Aṭṭhakathā AND the Ṭīkā: same VZTimes table, no second
mapping.**

### COMPLETENESS — THE FINDING THAT DECIDES THE NEXT PROJECT

Two independent measures, and BOTH are needed:
* **ratio** — corpus chars / printed body chars. *Is the TEXT there?*
* **¶/pg** — corpus paragraphs per printed page. *Is the STRUCTURE there?*
  Side-maps map printed lines onto CORPUS ORDINALS, so a volume with almost no
  paragraphs has nothing to anchor to even where its text is complete.

    SOUND   (ratio >=95%, >=0.25 ¶/pg)   34   buildable
    MIDDLE                               19   look first
    UNUSABLE or DOUBTFUL                 25   upstream work needed

Worst: **07ViT07 22 ¶ over 529 pages (0.04 ¶/pg, ratio 2%)** and **01ViT01 23 ¶
over 520 pages** — those are stubs, not corpora. Then 05Kankha 19%, 29KhuA10
35%, 33KhuA14 37%, 20KhuA01 43%, 01VinA01 69%.

**23KhuA04 is why both columns are read: 97% of the text and 0.19 ¶/pg** — 92
paragraphs over 478 pages. A ratio-only screen would pass it, and it has no
ordinals to hang a side-map on.

**So the corpus gap is SYSTEMIC, not two unlucky volumes.** The reader fix
(the heading rule, 2026-07-27k) unlocks the 34 sound volumes and probably much
of the 19 middle; the other 25 need `pipeline/extract.py`, whatever the reader
does.

### TITLES — the cover is the label, and the Ṭīkā covers need their own rule

Page 0 gives the work's name in capitals plus the bhāga where split, e.g.
`PĀRĀJIKAKAṆḌA-AṬṬHAKATHĀ (Paṭhamo bhāgo)` / `(Dutiyo bhāgo)` — **this is what
the nav must use**, because the INNER title page omits the bhāga and two
volumes of one work labelled alike collide under `_navdup.js` (user-raised,
2026-07-27k). The all-caps scan found a title on all 52 Aṭṭhakathā and on
**none of the 26 Ṭīkā** — their covers are laid out differently; the bhāga
parenthesis is found, the name is not.

### !!! AN INSTRUMENT THROWN AWAY, AND THE CONTROL THAT KILLED IT

The census's first version also asked, per printed page, whether three six-word
phrases from it occur in the corpus, calling the page ABSENT when all three
missed. It reported "295 of 396 pages absent" for a volume whose ratio was 97%.

**Measured against a CONTROL — 01Vin01, shipped, gating 0/0/0/0 — only 27% of a
printed page's six-word windows occur verbatim in its own corpus**, because
printed lines break words, carry inline footnote digits that normalisation
strips, and hyphenate. Rates: 01Vin01 27%, 06VinSg06 29%, 07DiA01 17%,
19AnT02 15%, 22AbhiT01 9%. **A measure on which a perfect volume scores 27%
cannot call a page missing**, so the column was dropped entirely.

01VinA01's finding stands only because it was corroborated THREE ways — a 69%
ratio, a CONTIGUOUS 78-page run, and reading its ord0 against printed p15.
Nothing was claimed for the Ṭīkā on the probe's word alone.

**Second instrument error of the session** (after the encoding census that
counted `ñ` as legacy residue). Both were caught by reading what the probe
PRINTED rather than its total. **Put a known-good volume through any new
corpus-wide measure before believing it.**

## THE VINAYA-AṬṬHAKATHĀ IS SCOUTED, AND TWO OF ITS SIX VOLUMES CANNOT BE BUILT — THE CORPUS DOES NOT HOLD THE TEXT (2026-07-27k)

**Nothing has been written for any of the six.** The scout found something that
changes what this block of work is, so it was reported rather than built
through. Full scout: `claude/next_session_vinaya_atthakatha.md`; the finding:
`claude/vinaya_atthakatha_corpus_gap.md`.

### THE FINDING: THE COMMENTARY CORPUS IS INCOMPLETE, AND THE CANON'S RULES DO NOT COVER IT

Corpus characters against PRINTED BODY characters — footnote blocks removed
with `fnblock.fn_start`, running header dropped, both sides normalised — then
three six-word probe phrases per printed page looked up in the corpus:

    volume      corpus/printed   body pages   wholly absent   verdict
    06VinSg06        99%             468            —         BUILD
    02VinA02         97%             312            —         BUILD
    03VinA03         97%             437            —         BUILD
    04VinA04         91%             265            21        BUILD, gap recorded
    01VinA01         69%             346           101        DO NOT BUILD
    05Kankha         19%             357           264        DO NOT BUILD

**01VinA01's absent pages are mostly ONE CONTIGUOUS RUN — 0-based 14–91, i.e.
78 pages from the start.** Its corpus ord0 is `1. Idāni Tenāti-ādipāṭhassa…`
while printed p15 opens with the `Ganthārambhakathā` and its prologue verses,
none of which is in the corpus. **05Kankha is a fragment** — 264 of 357 body
pages wholly absent, in runs of a hundred pages at a time.

**EVERY CANON VOLUME'S CORPUS WAS FAITHFUL TO THE PRINTED PAGE.** Every defect
this project has chased was about ROLE — a pāda read as a heading, a homage
lifted from the wrong place — and the fix was always a side-map. **Here the
text is not there**, and the governing rule ("never edit the corpus; build
side-maps and map onto corpus ordinals") has nothing to map onto. This is a
CONVERSION problem and it belongs upstream in `pipeline/extract.py`.

**`docs/verify_report.md` HAS BEEN SAYING THIS ALL ALONG** — 01VinA01 86%,
05Kankha 85% with 6,604 lines missing — and those rows were read as "not yet
built" when they were in fact saying "the corpus is short". **Read the
percentage column before planning a volume.**

### ENCODING — SETTLED, and my first census was wrong

**The Aṭṭhakathā volumes use the SAME VZTimes table.** Residue on the legacy
source side is **nine characters on pages 1–2 of every volume, byte-identical
to what shipped 01Vin01 carries** — the Burmese alphabet tables §3 says to
skip. Open question 2 of the project instructions is answered.

**My first census reported residue on 384 of 01VinA01's 403 pages** and I was
about to report the encoding unresolved. It was wrong: I had built the "legacy"
set from BOTH columns of the mapping table, so `ñ` and `Ñ` — legitimate Pāḷi
*output* — counted as residue, and every sample line the probe printed was
perfectly good Pāḷi. **The samples are what exposed it, in one look. A
self-verifying check is only self-verifying if the alphabet it checks against
is right.**

### !!! AND THE `katha` + `heads_by_form` READER DOES NOT FIT THIS LAYER — 66 OF 106 HEADINGS WRONG

`SPEC['06VinSg06']` was written and built as the cheapest proof that the
commentary builds at all: one book, a flat 36-entry mātikā, 99% corpus. **It
pairs 326 printed units against 326 corpus paragraphs on the FIRST run — and
that is not success.**

**66 of its 106 headings are quoted kammavācā PROSE.** The commentary quotes
canonical formulas at a display indent constantly, and `kat_is_head` under
`heads_by_form` asks only for a capital, six words or fewer, no comma and no
terminal stop:

    p114   9| Sammato saṁghena itthannāmo vihāro kappiyabhūmi khamati
           6| saṁghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṁ dhārayāmī”ti.
    p339   8| Dinno saṁghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṁ
           4| āpattīnaṁ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṁ ekāhaparivāso, khamati saṁghassa,

The opener sits 2-4 columns DEEPER than its own continuation and the sentence
runs straight on. **THE 1:1 UNIT COUNT CANNOT SEE THIS AND NEITHER CAN THE BODY
GATE** — every word is present and in order. The MĀTIKĀ DIFF found it, as it
has found every wrong role in this project.

* **`display_prose` does not reach it** — that key acts at the verse-run stage,
  after the per-line classification where the heading is claimed.
* **`headskip` does not scale** — 66 literals in the EASIEST of 52 Aṭṭhakathā
  volumes.

**So the reader needs a rule, and the rule is shared machinery on the branch
nineteen canon volumes depend on.** The discriminator the page offers is that a
quoted line's SUCCESSOR sits at a SHALLOWER indent and completes its sentence,
where a heading's successor opens a new one — but that must be built twice and
diffed over every SPEC volume, ENUMERATING what changes, before it can ship.
**Nothing was written to `site/reader/` for any commentary volume**, and
`SPEC['06VinSg06']` is kept only as the thing to re-build against once the rule
is measured.

**The lesson is the one this file keeps paying for: a 1:1 count that comes out
right on the first run is not evidence that the volume is right.** It was the
`--show` listing and the mātikā diff that said otherwise, and they said it
immediately.

### THREE COMPLICATIONS TO SETTLE BEFORE ANY SPEC IS WRITTEN

1. **THE CORPUS `book` FIELD IS UNUSABLE HERE.** It alternates with
   `Vinayapiṭaka` — the running header — dozens of times per volume (02VinA02
   flips 118 times in 240 paragraphs). The title pages and `n` resets are the
   witnesses. Same lesson as the Aṅguttara, worse.
2. **03VinA03's MIDDLE BOOK BOUNDARY HAS NO `n` RESET.** Its three books show
   one book-scale reset (ord463, the Mahāvagga); the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga at
   printed p184 continues the numbering, and the printed unit at p185 is **660**
   where the corpus sits near **1228** — the two numbering systems do not
   correspond across that seam at all.
3. **NUMBERED UNITS SIT AT INDENT 1–2**, not the canon's 3–6, in all four
   buildable volumes. `_kat_cols`' `body + 3` floor was measured on the canon.

### THE SHAPE — ELEVEN NIPĀTAS OVER THREE VOLUMES

The most books per volume in the canon: four, three and four, each with its own

### !!! A NARRATIVE HOMAGE WAS BEING DELETED FROM THE BODY AND OVERWRITING THE BOOK'S INCIPIT — AND IT REACHED TWO VOLUMES ALREADY CALLED DONE

`kat_items` classified EVERY line matching `HOMAGE` as kind 'homage'; the
consumer writes each one to the SAME key — the book's first visible ordinal —
so **the LAST one won**, and the branch's `continue` meant **the line never
reached the body at all**. In a book that QUOTES the homage in its narrative
that is text loss plus a wrong incipit.

    10Ma02   incipit[0] held the NARRATIVE comma-form from p346 instead of the
             title page's, and Brahmāyu's threefold homage was MISSING from
             verse[387]                                        (SHIPPED)
    12Sam01  uddana[186] held ONE of the Dhanañjānī brahmin's THREE lines
                                                    (built 2026-07-27i, by me)
    15An01   incipit[323] held the Ārāmadaṇḍa quotation; body gate reported
             `render-not-in-PDF 1`
    16An02   incipit[0] held the narrative `Namo Tassa` form

**THE DISCRIMINATOR IS POSITION AND NEEDS NO VOCABULARY:** a book's own homage
stands on its TITLE PAGE, BEFORE that book's first numbered unit; every
narrative one is quoted after it. **MEASURED OLD-vs-NEW OVER ALL 39 SPEC
VOLUMES** (`_fnprobe/homagepos.py`): **thirty-five byte-identical**, and the
only four that move are the four above, each a correction. All four rebuilt;
10Ma02 re-gated (`6 444 0 485` — still `0 lines / 1 chunk`, its own known open
chunk, unmoved) and 12Sam01 re-gated **0/0/0/0**.

**I called 12Sam01 clean last session and it was losing two printed lines.**
The body gate did not report it, and I did not look for it — the finding came
only from building a nikāya that quotes the homage more often.

### !!! THE EDITION MISPRINTS THE HOMAGE ITSELF, AND THAT HID A WHOLE BOOK

17An03's DASAKANIPĀTA title page (0-based 279) prints **`Namo tassa Bhagavatā
Arahato Sammāsambuddhassa.`** — *Bhagavatā* for *Bhagavato*. `HOMAGE` could not
match it, so `scout_volume.py` reported only THREE homage pages for a FOUR-book
volume and the line was never lifted: it stayed in the body, was classified
`gatha`, and the reader drew its built-in fallback homage above it. 17An03
built with THREE incipits for FOUR books.

**MEASURED over all 40 canon volumes**: the whole-line form occurs in 17An03 x1
and **18Khu01 x1** and nowhere else. **18Khu01 is SHIPPED and is NOT affected —
checked directly rather than assumed**: its `incipit/18Khu01.json` already
carries the misprint verbatim at ord705 (Suttanipāta), because that volume is
built by `build_suttanipata.py` and never consults this pattern. **38 of 39
SPEC volumes byte-identical** (`_fnprobe/homagediff.py`); only 17An03 moves.
The printed spelling is preserved verbatim.

### `head_paren` — WITHOUT IT HALF THE VAGGAS ARE NOT HEADINGS AT ALL

From the second paṇṇāsaka on, the edition numbers a vagga TWICE and prints the
outer number in PARENTHESES: `(6) 1. Brāhmaṇavagga` (15An01 0-based p185).
`kat_is_head` requires the core to open with a CAPITAL, so every such line fell
through. **The Tikanipāta showed FIVE vaggas for eighteen, and its second and
third paṇṇāsakas carried ~52 suttas each as DIRECT children of the paṇṇāsaka.**
Same key and same cause as 32Abhi04's `(10) 1. Parūpahārakathā`. Headings after:
Duka 22->32, Tika 164->180, Catukka 288->311, Pañcaka 278->299, Dasaka 209->226.
**Found by building the NAV, not by any content gate** — the 1:1 unit count was
right before and after, and the body gate was 0/0/0/0 both ways.

### ALSO FOUND BY THE MĀTIKĀ DIFF AND THE COLOPHON SCAN

* **Three COLOPHONS read as HEADINGS, two shapes.** 15An01 closes two vaggas
  with a PARENTHESIS — `Vaggo sattamo. (Etadaggavaggo niṭṭhito.)` — and 17An03
  closes one with NO TERMINAL STOP AT ALL, `Dānavaggo catuttho`. `kat_is_colo`
  requires `endswith('.')`, so none of the three could be reached. Named in
  `colofix` after reading each page.
* **Three PĀDAS read as HEADINGS in 16An02, one root cause: a line ending in a
  STOP FOLLOWED BY A PRINTED MARKER does not `endswith('.')`** — a footnote
  asterisk (`Kammaṁ daḷhaṁ karomi dānīti.*`) or the edition's own verse number
  (`Kāyassa bhedā nirayaṁ vajanti tā. (1-3)`). **MEASURED over all 40 canon
  volumes: 728 display lines end that way in eight volumes** — but the question
  is which are actually CLAIMED, and that was checked against the SHIPPED heads
  streams rather than inferred: **not one** of 05Vin05's, 27Khu10's or
  29Abhi01's appears in its `sections/` map (theirs sit at indent 9-10, below
  their own display gate), and 18Khu01/22Khu05/23Khu06/25Khu08 do not use this
  reader. The class is 16An02's alone, and it is three lines — so `headskip`,
  not a rule.
* **`6. ( )1` (15An01 p453) is the EDITION'S OWN** — an unnamed sutta with a
  footnote marker, which its mātikā simply omits. Kept.

and presentation, and all three navs are written.** 12Sam01 and 13Sam02 are

    13Sam02   Khandhavagga + Saḷāyatanavagga             `18 584 0 722`  0/0/0/0    2 nodes, 735 rows
    14Sam03   Mahāvagga                                  `18 432 0 598`  1/1/2/0    1 node,  717 rows

Body at minw 4, 2 AND 1, each volume as ONE range. `check_layout.js` ok on all
three. Apparatus PARSED and deliberately **NOT REBUILT**, as for the Dīgha and
Majjhima: 12Sam01 616 stored / 558 printed cells / 0 spliced / 23
variants-not-stored, 13Sam02 452 / 428 / 0 / 8, 14Sam03 267 / 236 / 0 / 2.

### THE SHAPE, AND WHAT IT COST

Five books over three volumes, numbering restarting per book, and **three
levels beneath the book** — saṁyutta, vagga, sutta — where the Majjhima has two
and the Dīgha one. `books` takes two entries on 12Sam01 and 13Sam02;
`n_scope: 'book'`; `pada_runon` on all three (12Sam01 is the most verse-dense
text in the canon, 1,895 of 3,039 display lines carrying a comma).

**Two scouted facts were WRONG and are corrected here.** 12Sam01's mātikā is
0-based 13-38 and the reported "hole at 26" is **a BLANK LEAF** between the two
books' mātikās, not a missing page — measured, then LOOKED AT. And the homage
page at 1-based 201 is the Dhanañjānī false positive the scout already named;
the real boundaries are the title pages at 1-based 282 and 254.

### !!! A UNIT NUMBER IS NOT ALWAYS A SINGLE NUMBER — IT CAN BE A RANGE

The peyyāla sections number ONE printed unit for several suttas at once:
14Sam03 0-based p39 sets `42-47. Sace vo bhikkhave…` at indent 5 under the
heading `2-7. Saṁyojanappahānādisuttachakka`, and the corpus holds it as one
paragraph with n=42. `VERSE = ^(\d+)\.` could not see it, so **94 printed
units were invisible to the page reader** — 13Sam02 337/361 and 345/361,
14Sam03 544/598 — which reads exactly like a corpus overrun and is nothing of
the kind. `HEADNUM` has admitted the same form for HEADINGS since the Apadāna's
`3-1.`; this is that form on the unit side.

**MEASURED OLD-vs-NEW OVER ALL 36 SPEC VOLUMES BEFORE APPLYING**
(`_fnprobe/rangediff.py`): **34 byte-identical** on all five side-maps with
printed-unit and colophon counts unmoved; only 13Sam02 and 14Sam03 move.
12Sam01 is inert — it prints no range.

### TWO MORE MACHINERY CHANGES, EACH MEASURED THE SAME WAY

* **A LINE THAT OPENS WITH A UNIT NUMBER IS NOT A COLOPHON BY THE GENERIC FORM
  TEST.** The HEADING branch of `kat_items` has always said so; the COLOPHON
  branch runs FIRST and carried no such guard. 13Sam02 p200/p202 print the
  peyyāla instruction `251-274. (Dutiyavagge viya catuvīsati suttāni
  pūretabbāni.).` as a UNIT at indent 4 — six words, terminal stop, no comma —
  and `kat_is_colo` took both, so the Khandhavagga paired 359 against 361 and
  REFUSED TO BUILD. Guard added inside `kat_is_colo` (one call site, so the
  wrapper in `_fnprobe/colonumdiff.py` IS the branch guard); `colofix` still
  wins. **35 of 36 volumes byte-identical.**
* **!!! `Tassudānaṁ` — ONE `d` — IS THE EDITION'S OWN MISPRINT, AND IT REACHES
  A SHIPPED VOLUME.** 14Sam03 p233 centres it above the Balakaraṇīyavagga's two
  mnemonic pādas; unmatched by `UDDLBL` it fell to the heading test and became
  a HEADING, stranding its pādas in `verse[...]['before']`. Measured over all
  40 canon volumes the whole-line form occurs in 14Sam03 x1 and **20Khu03 x2**
  and nowhere else. **In 20Khu03 — SHIPPED — the label was sitting as the FIRST
  LINE of the uddāna block with `label: null`** at ord1412
  (Sakacintaniyavagga) and ord3133 (Ekapadumiyavagga). Same wrong role, shipped.
  **34 of 36 byte-identical; the only two that move are these.** The printed
  spelling is PRESERVED verbatim, exactly as `PROSEOPEN` already does for
  "Ittaṁ sudaṁ" and "abhiāsitthāti".
  **20Khu03 rebuilt and re-gated:** body `20 464 0 4461` **0/0/0/0** at minw 4
  and 1, apparatus 1016 / 1041 / 0 / 1, `check_layout.js` ok. The correction
  moved a ROLE, not a word — which is why no gate ever saw it.
  **`regress.py` FAILED on exactly one map, `20Khu03 uddana`, and nothing else**
  — the predicted shape, confirmed before acting. That ONE baseline snapshot
  was then deliberately advanced (`_regress/base/20Khu03.uddana.json`, backup
  `.preuddlbl2`); note that `regress.py baseline` regenerates from the FROZEN
  `.preniddesa` builder and so cannot carry an intended change — the snapshot
  has to be advanced by hand, and that fact is worth knowing before the next
  time.

### WHAT THE MĀTIKĀ DIFF FOUND, WHICH IS WHAT IT IS FOR

Zero spurious headings remain in all three volumes. Before the fixes it found:

* **12Sam01 p83 `Dukkaraṁ vāpi karonti (Kāmadāti Bhagavā)` — A PĀDA READ AS A
  HEADING, and the only one in the canon.** Under `heads_by_form`
  `kat_is_head` asks only for a capital, no comma, no terminal stop and six
  words or fewer. Its own sibling four lines below, `Dullabhaṁ vāpi labhanti,
  (Kāmadāti Bhagavā)`, is safe ONLY because the edition happened to set a comma
  there. **Measured over all 40 canon volumes: a centred line carrying a
  parenthesised speaker tag with no comma and no terminal stop occurs EXACTLY
  ONCE.** So it is NAMED in `headskip`, not ruled — one literal against
  widening a shared form test.
* **The collective-number headings.** The peyyāla headings end not at `sutta`
  but at the numeral collective that counts the run —
  `23-112. Sāragandhādidānūpakārasuttanavutika`,
  `36-40. Rūpa-appaccupalakkhaṇādisuttapañcaka` — and `HEADTXT` anchors the
  stem at the END. Enumerated from the page over all three volumes and added to
  each volume's own `stems`; `dasaka` covers `ekādasaka`/`dvādasaka` and
  `tiṁsaka` covers `ttiṁsaka`, because the stem matches as a SUFFIX.
* **Errata, every one COUNTED ON BOTH SIDES before `errata` was chosen.**
  12Sam01 two, 13Sam02 five, 14Sam03 ten — including a misprinted NUMBER, not a
  name: the mātikā runs `1. Veḷudvāravagga`, `10. Rājakārāmavagga`,
  `3. Saraṇānivagga` where the body heads it `2. Rājakārāmavagga`.

    vaggo vitthāretabbo.) (Yadapi Maggasaṁyuttaṁ vitthāretabbaṁ, tadapi

it touches **12 volumes and 44 `before` entries, eight of the twelve SHIPPED**.

**REFUSED.** That is a regression, not a correction, and it is a shape I did
not predict — which is the stop condition. 14Sam03 is honestly `1 line /

### !!! THE CLICK-EVERY-ROW SWEEP DOES NOT WORK ON THIS SIDEBAR

`_vinnavverify.js`'s row loop takes `b.parentElement.querySelectorAll('.row')`,
which on the current nav is **EVERY row in the tree (15,441)**, not the
volume's own — so sweeping one Saṁyutta node means clicking the whole nav and
it does not finish. It also asserts ONE nav node per volume, which is false for
both two-book volumes. **A sweep that silently swept the wrong rows is exactly
the false pass that file was fixed for on 2026-07-27**, so it was not used.
`_samspan.js` was written instead: it reproduces `render()`'s own span
arithmetic (reader2.html ~line 295) in flat document order and asserts the
invariant the three shipped SPAN bugs violated. **2,038 rows checked, 0 empty
spans, every key in range.** Its first version reported `PASS — 0 rows checked`
because the children live under `tree`, not `kids`; it now REFUSES when a node
has no children, which is the only reason that vacuous pass was caught. A DOM
sweep scoped to the volume's own subtree is still worth writing.
