## THE APPARATUS DUPLICATION QUESTION IS SETTLED — THE STORE DUPLICATES, AND `rebuild_apparatus` IS RIGHT (2026-07-27h)

**Answered by the test this file has been asking for: for a note text stored N
times, is it PRINTED N times?** Read-only, using `verify_apparatus`'s own
`printed_notes()` / `stored_notes()` / `norm()` (`_fnprobe/appdup.py`).

    volume    extra copies   explained by printed cell count   UNEXPLAINED
    06Di01         12                 1                            11
    07Di02        103                 4                            99
    08Di03         73                 1                            72
    09Ma01         64                 7                            57
    10Ma02        100                 4                            96
    11Ma03         83                13                            70
    TOTAL         435                30                           405

**405 of 435 extra copies are NOT justified by the printed page.** Compared
against printed CELL count, not distinct pages, because a reading can
legitimately appear twice on one page under two markers — that fairer test
still leaves 405 unexplained.

**A measurement artefact was ruled out first:** `stored_notes()` reads BOTH
`apparatus/<VOL>.appk.json` AND the uddāna map's `app` fields, so a note in
both would be double-counted by the TEST rather than by the data. **The uddāna
`app` fields are empty in all six volumes (0 notes) and no text occurs in both**
— the duplication is entirely within `appk.json`.

### THE MECHANISM, SEEN DIRECTLY

    'Visuddho (Syā)'                     PRINTED once, p20 marker 2
                                         STORED at ord22 AND ord28
    'Uttarenābhimukho (Syā) uttarenamukho (Ka)'
                                         PRINTED once, p21 marker 1
                                         STORED at ord28 AND ord30

**One printed note attached to EVERY candidate paragraph carrying that marker
number**, instead of the single paragraph that actually carries it. That is the
old anchoring rule — candidates widened by a page either side — and it is
exactly the change this file has named three times: **anchor a note to the
paragraph that COVERS its page, not the first one STARTING on it.**

### WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT

* **`rebuild_apparatus` is DE-DUPLICATING, not losing.** 07Di02's `504 stored
  -> 416 anchored` is now explained: ~104 duplicates within the store, of which
  the rebuild removes ~88 while keeping the genuine repeats (416 exceeds the
  ~400 distinct texts). **The rebuild is safe to run on these volumes**, and
  **the 78-volume commentary rebuild is unblocked** — it was held only on this
  question.
* **IT DOES NOT prove the rebuild's ANCHORING is right.** This settles that the
  extra copies are unjustified; which paragraph each note belongs to is the
  separate anchoring change above, and it should be made BEFORE the 78-volume
  rebuild rather than after, or the whole corpus is re-anchored twice.
* **The six volumes are still UNREBUILT** — deliberately. Running it now would
  bake in the current anchoring. Do the anchoring change first, then rebuild
  once.

## THE `pada_runon` AUDIT — ONE MORE SHIPPED VOLUME WAS WRONG, AND THE COMMA CLAUSE IS WHY IT COULD NEVER BE FIXED (2026-07-27g)

**Audited every built volume for the 2026-07-27f class. The answer is: one
more, and it is 31Abhi03.**

**First, a correction to the audit I wrote in 2026-07-27f.** The "label-less
single-line uddāna block" query fires on 25 volumes and is USELESS as a general
test — its closing-formula list is far too narrow. `Paṭhamapīṭhavimānaṁ
paṭhamaṁ.`, `Sāriputtattherassāpadānaṁ paṭhamaṁ.` and `Uddesavāro.` are all
COLOPHONS; the edition closes sections with an ORDINAL (`paṭhamaṁ`, `paṭhamo`)
or with a bare vāra name in the nominative, and neither is in the pattern.
**Do not use that query.** The precise question is the one below.

### THE RIGHT QUESTION: which volumes are `katha` + `heads_by_form` WITHOUT `pada_runon`?

`pada_runon` only bites where display lines are classified BY FORM, so the
`verse` and `niddesa` readers are irrelevant however much gāthā they print
(19Khu02 has 3,460 display lines carrying a comma and does not need the flag).
Ten volumes qualified: 29Abhi01, 30Abhi02, 31Abhi03, 33Abhi05, 34Abhi06,
35Abhi07, 37Abhi09, 38Abhi10, 39Abhi11, 40Abhi12.

**Tested by forcing the flag on and diffing the five side-maps
(`_fnprobe/prprobe.py`): NINE ARE INERT, byte-identical, colophon counts
unmoved. Only 31Abhi03 changes.**

### !!! 31Abhi03 — HANDOFF HAS CLAIMED SINCE 2026-07-26 THAT THIS WAS FIXED

This file records `pada_runon` as having "corrected FOUR shipped volumes —
31Abhi03 (11), 32Abhi04 (45), 33Abhi05 and 36Abhi08 (8)". **32Abhi04 and
36Abhi08 carry the flag; 31Abhi03 and 33Abhi05 never did.** 33Abhi05 turns out
not to need it (inert). **31Abhi03 needed it and went eleven months of sessions
with the note claiming otherwise** — the eleven lines were never corrected.

They are all second pādas of the Dhātukathā's mnemonic couplets:
`Itthipumaṁ jīvitaṁ nāmarūpaṁ.`, `Dhātūsu satta dvepi ca indriyato.`,
`Anārammaṇaṁ no cittaṁ cittena vippayuttaṁ.` and eight more, read as COLOPHONS.

### WHY IT COULD NOT BE SET, AND THE ONE-LINE FIX

Turning the flag on ALSO demoted a REAL colophon — `Ekakaṁ.` (p110, indent 38),
which closes the Ekaka-uddesa with a rule and `2. Duka-uddesa` directly after
it. Cause: `pada_runon`'s second clause asked whether THE LINE ABOVE ends in a
comma, and the line above `Ekakaṁ.` is the list item `54. …paṭipanno,` at
indent **6**. A comma thirty-two columns away said nothing about this line.

**A couplet's two pādas sit at the SAME indent** — 09Ma01 p239 sets all fourteen
at 18 — so the clause now requires the comma to be a NEIGHBOUR's,
`abs(lines[_li-1][0] - ind) <= 2`.

**Proven inert: byte-identical on ALL THIRTEEN volumes that already carry
`pada_runon`** (01Vin01, 02Vin02, 03Vin03, 04Vin04, 05Vin05, 06Di01, 07Di02,
08Di03, 09Ma01, 10Ma02, 11Ma03, 32Abhi04, 36Abhi08). With it, 31Abhi03 demotes
**exactly the eleven pādas and keeps `Ekakaṁ.`** — which is the correction this
file always claimed.

**31Abhi03 re-gated:** body `7 191 0 890` **0/0/0/0** at minw 4 and 1;
apparatus **0 / 0 / 0**; `check_layout.js` ok; nav rebuilt and **every node in
the file byte-identical, 118 of 118**; `_navdup.js` PASS; `regress.py check`
55/55. Backups `.precomma`.

**The lesson repeats today's:** a note in this file saying a thing was fixed is
not evidence that it was. The flag's ABSENCE was checkable in one line.

## RESOLVED — IT WAS A MISSING `pada_runon` ON ALL SIX VOLUMES I BUILT, AND IT HAD TORN 38 GĀTHĀ APART (2026-07-27f)

**The classification count settled it in one pass, and the answer was neither
of the two instruments I had costed.** Of the 388 label-less single-line uddāna
blocks, position separates them cleanly: **130 sit at a vagga or sutta END**
(real uddāna, correctly stored and correctly placed) and the rest reduce to
**39 DISTINCT MID-TEXT ORDINALS** — 07Di02 7, 08Di03 22, 09Ma01 2, 10Ma02 6,
11Ma03 2, 06Di01 **0**.

Then one case read end-to-end gave the cause. 09Ma01 ord279 is Brahmā's
fourteen-pāda request, and the render drew SEVEN of them — the even-numbered
ones — in a block of their own AFTER the verse:

    [after] 'Pāturahosi Magadhesu pubbe,'      [udd] 'Dhammo asuddho samalehi cintito.'
    [after] 'Apāpuretaṁ1 amatassa dvāraṁ,'     [udd] 'Suṇantu dhammaṁ vimalenānubuddhaṁ.'
    [after] 'Sele yathā pabbatamuddhaniṭṭhito,'[udd] 'Yathāpi passe janataṁ samantato.'

**The printed page sets ALL FOURTEEN AT ONE INDENT (18).** The split is not
geometric at all — it is the edition's couplet PUNCTUATION: first pāda a COMMA,
second a FULL STOP. That is precisely what **`pada_runon`** exists for, and
this file already says so: *"A COLOPHON IS DECIDED BY FORM UNDER
`heads_by_form`, AND SO IS EVERY SECOND PĀDA OF A COUPLET… whenever a new
volume prints gāthā, run the measurement over EVERY volume."*

**I did not. `pada_runon` was missing from ALL SIX volumes I built** — 06Di01,
07Di02, 08Di03, 09Ma01, 10Ma02, 11Ma03 — while 03Vin03 and 05Vin05 have carried
it since the Vinaya. That is the whole defect, and it is my omission of a rule
this file states explicitly.

### WHAT IT WAS DOING, AND WHAT THE CORRECTION IS

Every second pāda fell to the form test, was read as a COLOPHON or a `centre`
line, and was flushed to the uddāna map. Colophon counts were wildly inflated:

    volume    colophons before -> after     gāthā blocks
    06Di01        31 ->  25                  11 -> 13
    07Di02       113 ->  40                  74 -> 66
    08Di03       212 ->  22                  62 -> 62
    09Ma01        99 ->  88                  10 -> 12
    10Ma02       116 ->  62                  40 -> 31
    11Ma03       116 ->  64                  31 -> 27

**08Di03 was carrying 212 "colophons" for a volume with eleven suttas.** The 22
that remain are exactly the real ones — the bhāṇavāra ends and the sutta
colophons, checked in the `--show` listing.

**Mid-text uddāna ordinals: 39 -> 1.** The one that remains is 10Ma02 ord455,
the case already known to be a different shape (a numbered verse unit whose
opening pāda hangs left at indent 6, meeting its own continuation) — and it is
still the volume's single open chunk.

### GATES, ALL RE-RUN AFTER THE REBUILD

* **body** — 06Di01, 07Di02, 08Di03, 09Ma01, 11Ma03 all **0/0/0/0** at minw 1;
  10Ma02 `0 lines / 1 chunk / 0 / 0`. Printed-unit counts unchanged in every
  volume (559, 441, 360, 511, 485, 462), so no unit moved.
* **presentation** — `check_layout.js` ok on all six.
* **nav** — all six rebuilt and **EVERY nav node in the file is byte-identical**;
  118 of 118 volumes unchanged. Heading counts did not move, so the trees could
  not. `_navdup.js` PASS.
* **apparatus** — unchanged, and still unrebuilt for the standing reason.
* `regress.py check` **55/55**.
* **Both corpus-wide reports re-run** with fresh caches (`_vcache18`,
  `_appcache10`), each until the count stopped rising: body **33/118**,
  apparatus **15/118** — both unchanged, which is the point: the correction
  moved 38 gāthā into the right role WITHOUT moving a single volume's gate
  verdict, because no gate could see the defect in the first place.

### THE LESSON, AND IT IS ABOUT THE PROCESS, NOT THE CODE

Three gates and two nav checkers all read clean on 08Di03 while 190 of its
lines sat in the wrong role. **A wrong ROLE leaves every word present**, which
is why this file already carries the `--show` rule and the mātikā diff — and
neither of those catches it either, because a second pāda is not a heading and
does not appear in the mātikā.

**What DID catch it was refusing to fix 10Ma02 with a named literal.** The
cheap fix would have made that volume read 0/0/0/0 and left 38 torn gāthā
across five volumes, two of them shipped. The rule that saved it is the one
added the same day: *enumerate what a change silences, and stop when any of it
is a shape you did not predict.*

**The standing instruction now has teeth: when a volume prints gāthā, CHECK
`pada_runon` ON EVERY VOLUME, including the ones already called done.**

## (superseded by 2026-07-27f) THE UDDĀNA-BLOCK CLASS IS NOT ONE LINE, AND IT REACHES TWO VOLUMES ALREADY CALLED COMPLETE (2026-07-27e)

**Measured before choosing an instrument for 10Ma02's one open chunk, and the
measurement killed the cheap option.** The plan was a named literal
(`headfix`/`colofix`/`headskip` family) for the single pāda 10Ma02 renders as an
uddāna. First check: how many label-less SINGLE-LINE uddāna blocks exist in the
six built Dīgha/Majjhima volumes, and how many are NOT a closing formula
(`niṭṭhit|samatt|bhāṇavār|pariccheda|niyutt|vagga|paṇṇāsak|uddān`)?

    06Di01     6      09Ma01    10
    07Di02    74      10Ma02    55
    08Di03   190      11Ma03    53      — 388 in all

**So the class is not one line, and 07Di02 and 08Di03 are volumes this file
already calls COMPLETE with their navs written.** At least some are
demonstrably BODY gāthā, not uddāna: 07Di02 ord70 `Ye sotavanto pamuñcantu
saddhaṁ. / Dhammaṁ paṇītaṁ manujesu brahme”ti.` is Brahmā's invitation verse in
the middle of the Mahāpadānasutta, and 08Di03 ord28/ord30 `Amaññi kotthu
migarājāhamasmi.` is the jackal's verse in the Cakkavattisutta. Neither closes
anything.

**WHAT IS NOT YET ESTABLISHED, and must be before anyone acts:** the 388 are a
MIXTURE. A vagga's or book's own uddāna really is VERSE and really does belong
in that map — 06Di01 ord558 `Soṇakūṭamahālijālinī. / Lohiccatevijjā terasāti.`
is the Sīlakkhandhavagga's mnemonic listing its thirteen suttas, correctly
stored and correctly rendered last. The distinguisher is POSITION, not form: an
uddāna sits at the end of a vagga or book, right after a colophon; a body gāthā
sits mid-text. **Nobody has separated the two yet, and the count of real
defects is therefore UNKNOWN — somewhere between the handful named above and
388.**

**Consequences, stated plainly:**
* **The named literal is the WRONG instrument** — it was chosen on the belief
  that this was one line in one volume. It is not.
* **`docs/verify_report.md`'s clean 33/118 does not cover this class.** A wrong
  ROLE leaves every word present, so the body gate reads 0/0/0/0 either way;
  10Ma02's single chunk surfaced only because it happened to fabricate a
  mismatched chunk as well. **The other instances are invisible to all three
  gates and to the nav checks.**
* **The Dīgha's "COMPLETE" needs qualifying** until the separation is done.
  Its bodies, presentation and navs are gated and sound; this is a fourth thing
  none of those gates measures.

**NEXT STEP, and it is a measurement, not a fix:** classify each of the 388 by
POSITION — is the anchoring paragraph the last of a vagga/book (uddāna, keep)
or mid-text (body gāthā, defect)? That number decides everything: a handful
means named literals after all; a large number means the display-run grouping
is wrong and the ±2 tolerance (174 merges across six volumes, already measured)
is the real fix. **Do not touch either instrument before that count exists.**

`check_layout.js` ok on all three. `regress.py check` 55/55 after every edit.

### !!! 09Ma01's CORPUS WAS SHORT BY TWO UNITS, AND THE FIRST READING WAS WRONG

`scout_volume.py corpus` reports `n ends at 513` over **511** paragraphs with a
single discontinuity `41 -> 44`, and a search of the printed pages for
`^\s*4[123]\.\s` found only `41.`. **That reading — "the edition skips 42 and
43" — was WRONG, and the regex is why:** the edition sets both numbers with **NO
SPACE AFTER THE PERIOD**, `42.Tassa` (0-based p36) and `43.Tassa` (p37), so a
pattern requiring whitespace could not see them. The printed side is RIGHT (513
units, 1-513 unbroken); the CORPUS is short by two, both welded into ord40, the
paragraph carrying n=41.

**Fourth and fifth embedded unit number in the corpus** (05Vin05 p32
`39.Eḷakalomāni` was the third). Fixed with `kat_splices`, marks taken from the
page and not retyped — *a mark is the text that RENDERS, so it must be the
printed unit's whole first line*. 511/511 after.

**The lesson is about the instrument, not the volume: a numbering gap found by
a regex is not a numbering gap until you have looked at the page.**

### !!! THE HOMAGE GUARD WAS INSPECTING THE COMPLEMENT OF ITS OWN WINDOW

`verify_render_vs_pdf.py`'s structural guard flags a `Namo tassa…` rendered as
body text instead of as an incipit, with an exception for a homage QUOTED in
the narrative. The exception read

    p[:max(0, p.find('amo tassa') - 60)]

which is everything up to SIXTY CHARACTERS BEFORE the homage — **precisely
excluding the sixty characters the test exists to look at.** A narrative homage
is introduced immediately before it (`tikkhattuṁ udānaṁ udānesi “namo tassa…`),
so the marker always fell in the excluded window and the guard fired on the
quotation. 09Ma01 ord287 is where it surfaced.

**MEASURED over every corpus volume before changing it:** 22 paragraphs carry
the homage; the old window flags **20**, the corrected window flags **16**, and
**all four changed verdicts are OLD-ONLY** — nothing is newly hidden, so the fix
cannot mask a defect the old test caught. The four are 09Ma01 ord287, 10Ma02
ord387 and ord472, and **12Sam01 ord186** (Saṁyutta, not yet built), every one a
character in the story uttering the homage. Backup `.prehomage`.

### !!! RESOLVED 2026-07-27d — THE LOOK-AHEAD IS IN, AND THE ONE REPORT IT REFUSED TO SILENCE IS A REAL DEFECT

**`display_openers()` added to `verify_render_vs_pdf.py`** (backup
`.prelookahead`): a line at indent >= 8 whose predecessor sits AT THE BODY
COLUMN opens a display block, so the line above it is terminated and the
chunker can no longer glue prose to a gāthā.

**MEASURED OLD-vs-NEW OVER ALL 34 BUILT VOLUMES BEFORE APPLYING** (`_fnprobe/
chunkdiff.py`, which enumerates every report that changes, not just counts):
**31 volumes show NO movement at all, and NOTHING APPEARED ANYWHERE.**
09Ma01 0->0, 11Ma03 **5->0**, 10Ma02 **2->1**.

**THE FIRST VERSION OF THE RULE WAS TOO LOOSE, AND THE STOP CONDITION CAUGHT
IT.** Written as `prev < 8` it also silenced 10Ma02 p413, which is NOT prose
meeting a display block:

     6| 456. Tesaṁ vo ahaṁ byakkhissaṁ, (Vāseṭṭhāti Bhagavā)
    11| Anupubbaṁ yathātathaṁ.

— a numbered VERSE unit whose opening pāda hangs left because the number pushes
it there, meeting its OWN continuation. Measured over the seven junctions: all
six genuine cases have a predecessor at indent **0** and this one at **6**, so
the rule stops at the body column. **The tightened rule preserves that report,
and preserving it was right:**

    ord455 [after] 'Tesaṁ vo ahaṁ byakkhissaṁ, (Vāseṭṭhāti Bhagavā)'
    ord455 [after] 'Jātivibhaṅgaṁ pāṇānaṁ, aññamaññāhi jātiyo. …'
    ord455 [udd]   'Anupubbaṁ yathātathaṁ.'

**10Ma02 renders the second half of unit 456's first couplet as an UDDĀNA
BLOCK, out of order, after the rest of the verse.** A pāda pulled out of its
gāthā and given the wrong role AND the wrong position. **STILL OPEN** — one
chunk, `10Ma02 6 444 0 485` reads `0 lines / 1 chunk / 0 / 0` at minw 4, 2 and
1.

**DIAGNOSED 2026-07-27d, NOT FIXED.** The page sets the couplet's second pāda
ONE SPACE DEEPER than its siblings:

     6| 456. Tesaṁ vo ahaṁ byakkhissaṁ, (Vāseṭṭhāti Bhagavā)
    11| Anupubbaṁ yathātathaṁ.
    10| Jātivibhaṅgaṁ pāṇānaṁ, aññamaññāhi jātiyo.
    10| Tiṇarukkhepi jānātha, na cāpi paṭijānare.

A display run is grouped by EXACT indent equality, so the line at 11 forms a
run of ONE, is classified `centre`, lands in `pend_centre` and is flushed to the
UDDĀNA map (`uddana/10Ma02.json` ord455, `label: null`) — which renders it last.

**TWO INSTRUMENTS RULED OUT, so do not reach for them:**
* **`verse_indent` is a FLOOR**, the size of the gap between prose-list runs and
  gāthā runs. It says nothing about grouping two runs one space apart.
* **`wrap_display` keys on a continuation that CANNOT open a line** — no
  capital. `Anupubbaṁ` has one, so it is not a wrap by that test.

**The fix is a TOLERANCE in display-run grouping** (`lines[_j2][0] ==
lines[_i2][0]` and the same equality in the `centre` path). That is shared
machinery feeding every volume's side-maps, so it needs the corpus-wide
measurement FIRST — how many runs merge in each of the 34 built volumes, and is
every merge a genuine one-block gāthā. `_fnprobe/chunkdiff.py` is the harness to
copy: enumerate what changes, do not count it.

**AND THE BLAST RADIUS IS ALREADY MEASURED — it is NOT small.** One-line
display runs sitting within 2 of an adjacent display run, per volume:
09Ma01 **23**, 10Ma02 **62**, 11Ma03 **25**, 06Di01 **24**, 07Di02 **17**,
08Di03 **23** — **174 across these six alone**, against 594-740 one-line
display runs each. A ±2 tolerance would merge all of them. So this is NOT a
one-line change to make casually: every one of those 174 has to be a genuine
single gāthā before the tolerance can ship, and the six Saṁyutta/Aṅguttara
volumes are not even measured yet. **Consider instead naming the ONE line per
volume**, as `headskip` and `colofix` do — one literal against 174 merges is a
very different risk. The lesson is the one the entry below already states in its own way: **a
gate that goes quiet is not the same as a volume that is correct**, and the
acceptance condition — enumerate what disappears, stop if any of it is a shape
you did not predict — is what turned a convenient silence into a finding.

**09Ma01 and 11Ma03 are now 0/0/0/0 at minw 4, 2 and 1.**

### (superseded, kept for the diagnosis) THE RESIDUAL — 7 CHUNK DIVERGENCES, NO TEXT LOST, AND THE FIX IS NOT A HACK

10Ma02 (2) and 11Ma03 (5) report `PDF-chunks-missing` at minw 4, 2 AND 1 — the
same count at every threshold, so it is not short-chunk noise. **No text is
lost: `PDF-lines-missing 0`, `render-not-in-PDF 0`, `rendered-too-often 0`**,
i.e. every printed LINE is in the render.

Diagnosed, not assumed. Every one of the seven is a PROSE line running into the
FIRST PĀDA OF A DISPLAY VERSE:

    yaṁ kho no āvuso bhagavā saṁkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ
    avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho ATĪTAṀ NĀNVĀGAMEYYA

The prose line ends `…vihāraṁ paviṭṭho` with no sentence punctuation, so the
chunker glues it to the display line below and fabricates a chunk that exists
nowhere in the render — where the two are correctly a paragraph and a gāthā
block. **This is exactly the fabrication `display_lines` already prevents for
HEADINGS**, and the docstring there describes it in those words.

**Why it does not fire here:** the terminator asks whether the line ITSELF is
display-class (`norm(t) in disp`); `display_lines` collects only CENTRED SHORT
**UNPUNCTUATED** lines, and a verse pāda ends in `,` or `.` so it is never in
that set. The gluing line is the PROSE one above it. **The fix is a LOOK-AHEAD:
terminate a body-column line whose SUCCESSOR sits at display indent.**

**NOT DONE, deliberately.** That is shared machinery on the gate that every
volume is measured by, and it needs the corpus-wide measurement first — how
many chunks does it change in each of the 31 volumes now reading clean, and
does any of them lose a real report. Do that before touching it. Until then
these two volumes are honestly `0 lines / N chunks`, and **they must not be
called 0/0/0/0.**

### `headfix` NOW BEATS THE COLOPHON TEST — a one-line change, proved inert

`headfix`'s stated meaning has always been "a line NAMED here IS A HEADING
WHEREVER IT SITS", but the colophon branch runs FIRST and claimed the line
before the heading branch could honour it. 06Di01 p149 heads a section

colophon; the mātikā lists it at printed p131 immediately after `Tisso vidhā`,
which IS read as a heading, and unit 343 opens directly beneath it. **No content
gate can see a wrong ROLE** — the volume read 0/0/0/0 either way; only the
mātikā diff found it.

Inert wherever `headfix` is empty, which is every volume but three, and none of
those three names a line this branch would claim. **Proved, not asserted:**
`regress.py check` 55/55 and BUILDER-vs-BUILDER **135/135 maps byte-identical
over all 26 other SPEC volumes**, against a baseline generated by reverting
exactly that line (`_fnprobe/inert.py` now takes `BASELINE` and `SKIP`).

### !!! `_vinnavverify.js` GAVE A FALSE PASS (rule 5)

Asked for 07Di02's rows it reported **"292 of 292 clicked" for a 156-row
volume** — because it clicked a HARDCODED `Vinayapiṭaka` and then the first
sidebar row carrying the volume's title, and **`Mahāvaggapāḷi` is BOTH 03Vin03
(Vinaya) and 07Di02 (Dīgha)**. It swept the Vinaya Mahāvagga and called it a
pass. The title collision is legitimate data — two different works the edition
really does give the same name, which is why `_navdup.js` scopes its
no-duplicate-title rule to ONE nikāya — so the checker had to handle it, not
the data. Fixed three ways: the lookup now searches every nikāya (its CHECKS
were always generic; only the lookup named the Vinaya), the nikāya to click is
derived from the volume, and the row is chosen from **the span between that
nikāya's row and the next**, since the DOM row carries no key attribute to
disambiguate by. It now prints which nikāya it resolved. Backup `.prenikaya`.
**The Vinaya volumes' earlier sweeps were genuine** — they were in the
hardcoded nikāya — and 01Vin01, 03Vin03 and 05Vin05 re-pass 9/9 under the fix.

are already stored. **The first hypothesis was wrong**: it is not a

## THE VINAYA IS COMPLETE — 05Vin05's NAV IS WRITTEN, AND `headskip` WAS THREE DEFECTS IN ONE ROOT CAUSE, ONE OF THEM A SILENT APPARATUS LOSS IN TWO SHIPPED VOLUMES (2026-07-26ak)

**All five Vinaya volumes now have bodies, apparatus, presentation AND navs.**
05Vin05's tree is written: **19 tops / 253 rows, 21/21 mātikā centred group
heads, 13/13 printed colophons, all 253 rows clicked.** 03Vin03 was rebuilt with
it and is **292 rows** (it was 293; the row that went is the false heading below).
`node _navdup.js` PASS on 12,759 rows / 185 nodes. Of the 118 volumes' nav nodes,
**116 are byte-identical to the pre-session backup and exactly two changed.**

### THE ROOT CAUSE HAS FOUR CONSUMERS, NOT ONE

2026-07-26aj diagnosed it correctly and scoped it too narrowly. The edition
separates body from apparatus with a horizontal rule; pdftotext emits it as a
line of underscores on almost every page, and `_{10,}` is how the pipeline finds
it. Where the rule is drawn as a GRAPHIC there is no line to find — and **FOUR
separate places were looking for it**, each failing in its own way:

| consumer | what it does | how it failed |
|---|---|---|
| `build_khu_volume.page_lines` | cuts the page | cells entered the PRINTED stream |
| `verify_render_vs_pdf.pdf_lines` | stops the body comparison | cells entered the PDF side of the gate |
| `rebuild_apparatus.page_notes` | parses the block | returned `{}, []` — **the cells were stored NOWHERE** |
| `verify_apparatus.printed_notes` | reads the printed cells | the gate could not see them either, so the loss was INVISIBLE TO ITS OWN GATE |

(a fifth, `verify_render_vs_pdf.running_headers`, derives the header set and was
counting footnote lines on those pages; corrected with the rest.)

**THE APPARATUS LOSS IS THE PART NOBODY HAD SEEN.** ~17 variant readings and
cross-references, printed in the edition, were held by no layer at all — only
by the body stream, as bogus headings and stray prose. The body gate read
0/0/0/0 throughout and the apparatus gate reported 05Vin05 `0 spliced / 1 / 0`,
because rows three and four of that table fail TOGETHER: the parser and its
checker share the blind spot, so the missing cells were missing from both sides
of the comparison and cancelled out. **Two checks that share an input are ONE
check** — the same lesson 19Khu02 taught, in a new place.

### `fnblock.py` — MEASURED OVER ALL 118 VOLUMES, IN BOTH pdftotext MODES

    05Vin05   0-based 51 54 67 110 119 121 140 330 331 382   (10)
    03Vin03   0-based 340                                    ( 1)
    07Di02    0-based 154 155 157                            ( 3)

and NOTHING else. The LOOSE test — any trailing run of cell-shaped lines on a
rule-less page — fires on **95 pages in 37 volumes**, and the other 81 are
numbered BODY units ("145. Yattha rūpakkhandho nirujjhittha -pa-."). What
separates a footnote block from them is the **VARIANT SIGLUM**: at least one
cell ending in `(Sī)`, `(Ka)`, `(Sī, Syā)`, `(?)`, or an XREF cell carrying
`piṭṭhe`. The `-layout` and plain readings agree on all 14 pages, which matters
because the builder reads the one and the body gate the other.

**IT REFUSES RATHER THAN GUESSES, AND THAT EARNED ITS KEEP ON THE FIRST RUN.**
Where the cells are NUMBERED, every number must be matched by a footnote MARKER
printed above it (`samatittikaṁ1`, `uccāraṁ2`, `uyyokhajja3`) — 12 of the 14 are
backed that way, the other 2 being xref-only lines that carry no number. A block
with the siglum evidence but WITHOUT the backing is reported and NOT cut. On its
first sweep that refusal stopped three commentary volumes' printed WORD INDEX
pages from being cut — 36KhuA17 p594, 37KhuA18 p458, 38KhuA19 p579, where
`33 (ādipiṭṭhesu)` looked like an xref. `piṭṭhe` is now evidence only inside a
`*`/`+` cell, so the two defences stay independent.

**INERT BY CONSTRUCTION:** `fn_start` returns None the moment the page carries a
`_{10,}` line, so every rule-bearing page in the corpus is untouched. Proved,
not assumed: `regress.py check` **55/55**, and BUILDER-vs-BUILDER over **all 25
other SPEC volumes, 125/125 maps byte-identical** (`_fnprobe/inert.py`).

### WHAT A SUPPRESSED LINE BECOMES — the question 2026-07-26aj left open

**A footnote cell becomes A FOOTNOTE.** Not "deleted". The page is cut where the
rule would have been, so the cell never enters the printed stream in any role.
But the builder and the gate agreeing is CIRCULAR — nothing would then check
that the drop was legitimate. It is sound only because the cells are now
provably IN the apparatus, which is a different gate with a different input.
That was checked before the body was cut, not after: **all 19 recovered cells
and xrefs were confirmed present in `apparatus/*.appk.json` and `xrefs/*.json`.**
Had they not been, the right move was to stop — cutting them out of the body
while nothing else held them would have deleted printed text from the edition.

**A verse line misread as a heading becomes BODY TEXT.** Nothing is suppressed;
only the ROLE changes. So the body gate is unmoved BY CONSTRUCTION — which is
exactly why it never saw this class, and why the surfaces that move are
`check_layout.js`, the reader and the NAV, where a false heading takes real
sections as its CHILDREN.

**These are two different answers, so `headskip` is TWO keys, not one.**
2026-07-26aj's "a `headskip`-style named literal would close all three at once"
is WRONG: a named literal in the body would have hidden the footnote cells
without ever storing them, which is the one outcome worse than the defect.

* **`fnblock.py`** (no SPEC key — it is self-verifying and refuses) closes the
  footnote cells.
* **`headskip`**, a per-volume tuple of literals, closes the false headings:
  05Vin05's seven Palibodhapañhābyākaraṇa pādas (p324-325, whose parenthesised
  ANSWER NUMBER leaves them with no terminal stop) and 03Vin03 p23's
  `Aññātāro bhavissantī”ti.]`. **Every declared literal must be met as a heading
  or the build REFUSES** — tested by declaring a line that is not printed.
  The literals were taken from the build's own `--show` listing, not retyped.

### THE CORPUS HAS THE SAME BLIND SPOT, AND TWO WRONGS WERE HOLDING EACH OTHER UP

The original extraction also ran the graphic-rule blocks into the body, so the
corpus carries the cells as numbered paragraphs — `ord146 n=1
'1. Desanārocanā ceva (Sī, Syā)'`, and `ord147 n=3` with the whole of p55's
opening verse welded on behind `3. Acelakānupakhajja (Ka)`. **While the PRINTED
side was also wrong these PAIRED**, and the 1:1 count check read 505/505. Cut
the page correctly and exactly five printed units go with it, so the count
breaks 500/505 until the same five corpus paragraphs are hidden. Counted per
page, not assumed: 05Vin05 p54 x2, p119, p140, p382; 03Vin03 p340 x3.

    05Vin05  backmatter [227] -> [146, 147, 225, 227, 238, 495]   500/500
    03Vin03  backmatter (none) -> [291, 292, 293]                 476/476

### !!! THE SCOUTED MĀTIKĀ PAGE RANGES WERE WRONG FOR ALL FIVE VOLUMES

2026-07-26ai recorded `01Vin01 14-22`, `02Vin02 4-14`, `03Vin03 4-14`,
`04Vin04 4-11`, `05Vin05 4-14`. Every one is shifted by **+1**: measured from
the pages that actually carry the `Piṭṭhaṅka` column, they are **13-22, 3-13,
3-13, 3-10, 3-13**. Each scouted range DROPS the mātikā's first page — the one
carrying the volume's opening top level — and includes one page of title or
body instead. On 01Vin01 that first page holds `Verañjakaṇḍa`, the whole
`1. Pārājikakaṇḍa` opening and pārājikas 1-3: eight of the 57 centred group
heads the gate runs on. **Measure the range; do not take it from a note.**

### THE GATE THIS PIṬAKA NEEDED — `matika_centred_gate`

`matika_gate` must indeed be FALSE here, exactly as scouted: every Vinaya
mātikā lists analytic entries the body never heads (`Paṭhamapaññatti`,
`Anupaññatti`, `Sikkhāpadavibhaṅga, padabhājanīya`), so on 01Vin01 only 75 of
243 entries resolve. But that leaves the tree gated on the colophons alone, and
with every level declared as a PATTERN `check_colophons` has only the five top
names to look for — five tests for a 90-row tree.

**The mātikā's CENTRED lines are a different witness and they are 1:1 with the
body's structural headings.** New per-volume key `matika_centred_gate`: every
centred group head must resolve in the tree or the build REFUSES. It found a
real divergence on its first run (below) and it is what now gates all five.

`matika_lines()` returns `(entry, is_centred)` and `matika()` is a thin wrapper
over it, so nothing else moved. **Proven inert: all twelve Abhidhamma volumes
rebuild with byte-identical trees AND byte-identical reports** (`_navprobe.py
old|new`, which runs every volume into its own copy of nav.json under both the
old and the new file and diffs 24 keys).

### THE OTHER NEW SPEC KEYS, each gated per volume and each proven inert

* **`centred_indent`** (default 18). A centred head's indent is a function of
  its LENGTH, so 18 is not a constant: 03Vin03 sets `3. Vassūpanāyikakkhandhaka`
  at 17 and 05Vin05 `Samuṭṭhānasīsasaṅkhepa` at 16, and at 18 the 03Vin03 gate
  saw 8 of its 10 khandhakas. Measured at 14 over every volume that prints a
  mātikā: it adds exactly those three lines in the Vinaya and would add ~130 in
  the Abhidhamma (the printed TWO-COLUMN pair-lines, which are not group
  heads), so it is declared per volume and left at 18 everywhere else.
* **`head_skip`** — a division's name reprinted over each of its parts where
  the fold test cannot see it. `subtree` already skips an ancestor reprint (27
  of them in 01Vin01, the vagga name over each of its ten sikkhāpadas), but
  02Vin02 prints `Bhikkhunivibhaṅge` — locative, short i — over five of the
  seven kaṇḍas whose division's title page reads `Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga`, and
  04Vin04 reprints three section names in the locative over each of their
  sub-blocks. Named per volume rather than reached by normalising ī to i.
  **Every declared literal must actually be printed, or the build refuses** —
  so the list cannot rot.
* **`nowrap`** on a book — a book the edition does not NAME gets no node.
* **`matika_drop`** — a line of the mātikā's own furniture that
  `matika_headers` cannot see because it opens one page.

### WHAT THE TREES ARE, AND WHY

* **01Vin01** — tops the five kaṇḍas; `[pārājika, vagga]` / `[sikkhāpada]`;
  `level_memo` REQUIRED (a sikkhāpada is one rung down under the Saṁghādisesa-
  and Aniyatakaṇḍa and two under the Nissaggiyakaṇḍa). `pairsides` NOT needed,

  bhāṇavāra / `Idaṁ …mūlakaṁ` blocks; declaring them is WRONG.** Declared, each

* **04Vin04** — tops the twelve khandhakas; one numbered level; the unnumbered

* **05Vin05** — tops the nineteen chapters, UNNUMBERED and exactly the mātikā's

**FOUR of 05Vin05's printed "headings" are FOOTNOTE CELLS**, and in the tree
they take real sections as children (`1. Rathiyāya vā (Ka)` acquires eight):

    0-based p67   '1. Samatitthikaṁ (Ka)'
    0-based p121  '1. Rathiyāya vā (Ka)'

**The cause is `page_lines` in `build_khu_volume.py`**, which cuts the page at
`FNRULE = ^\s*_{20,}\s*$`. On EIGHT pages of this volume the edition's footnote
rule is a GRAPHIC and pdftotext emits no text line for it — 0-based **51, 54,
67, 110, 119, 121, 140, 382** — so the cells enter the printed stream.

**MEASURED, so the fix can be scoped:** 05Vin05 is the ONLY volume where this
happens. The other four Vinaya volumes have **zero** such pages (79 / 120 / 134
/ 140 rule-bearing pages each), and over all 27 SPEC volumes no other volume has
a head-classified line ending in a variant siglum — 4 hits, all here.

**AND THE SPEC'S OWN LIST OF CONTAMINATED CORPUS PARAGRAPHS IS SHORT BY TWO.**
`SPEC['05Vin05']` records "five more corpus paragraphs have the same shape
(ord146, 147, 225, 238, 495)". The same measurement finds **ord133** (p51's
cell) and **ord208** (p110's `* Aṁ 3. 311 piṭṭhepi` xref cell) with the same
shape and not listed.

**A `head_skip` in the nav would only hide it** — the reader still draws those
four lines as centred headings, and `verify_render_vs_pdf.py` models the
reader, so the defect lives in both. The fix belongs with the BODY and needs
its three gates. Until then the tree is built and read but not written, which
is the choice this volume's side-maps already got in 2026-07-26ah.

**This is the same open finding as 05Vin05 p325's verse-line-as-heading, and
that one is bigger than recorded too: 2026-07-26ai names ONE line, `Cīvare
niṭṭhite cīvarapalibodho chijjati. (2)`. There are SEVEN, all at ord432,

closing the editorial insertion opened on p20, read as a heading and now a nav
row in a written volume. **A `headskip`-style named literal would close all

## THE VINAYA IS COMPLETE — 05Vin05 DONE, AND A LABEL FILTER THAT WAS DELETING PRINTED LINES IN A SHIPPED VOLUME (2026-07-26ai)

**05Vin05 (Parivārapāḷi) is done on all three gates, and the fix that finished
it corrected 32Abhi04, which has been shipped and reading 0/0/0/0 since
2026-07-26z.**

### The defect

The tidy pass at the foot of `build()` read:

```python
uddana[k] = [b for b in uddana[k] if b.get('lines') or b.get('head')]
```

with the comment "an uddāna block with a label but no lines is a stray label".
It is not. **An uddāna label is a PRINTED LINE.** It has no lines of its own
whenever the verses it labels are not centred lines, and the edition does that
in two different ways:

* **the verses are a numbered UNIT** — 05Vin05 p171 sets
  `Samuṭṭhānassuddānaṁ` and then unit 268, "Aniccā sabbe saṅkhārā, dukkhānattā
  ca saṅkhatā."; and
* **the uddāna is set as PROSE**, which the corpus absorbs into the preceding
  paragraph — 32Abhi04 does this at the end of most vaggas (p240:
  "Gihissa arahā, saha upapattiyā arahā, …" runs on as prose under its
  `Tassuddānaṁ`).

In both shapes the block ended with a `label` and no `lines`, and the filter
deleted it, so the printed label never rendered.

### Why the body gate could not see it

**Because the same word renders elsewhere in the same volume.** 32Abhi04 prints
`Tassuddānaṁ` **27** times and was rendering **4** of them. The forward check
asks whether a PDF line is present in the render — not how often — so 23 lost
labels read as 0 missing. 05Vin05 showed only because
`Samuṭṭhānassuddānaṁ` occurs exactly once in the volume.

This is the same class as the pāda-as-colophon defect of 2026-07-26ah: a
content gate cannot see a duplicate line go missing. **When a fix touches
shared machinery, measure the shape over EVERY volume — it is the only thing
that finds this.**

### The measurement, before the change

`_udd_probe.py` loads a copy of the builder whose tidy filter RECORDS what it
removes, and ran over all 27 volumes in `SPEC`:

| volume | label-without-lines blocks dropped |
|---|---|
| 05Vin05 | 1 |
| 32Abhi04 | 24 |
| the other 25 | 0 |

`_udd_diff.py` then built every volume with `build_khu_volume.py.preuddlabel`
and with the current file and compared all five maps byte-for-byte: **25
identical, 2 changed (`uddana` only)** — exactly the two the probe named.

After the change 32Abhi04 renders `Tassuddānaṁ` **27 times, matching the
printed count exactly**, plus its one `Paṇṇāsakuddānaṁ`; and its body gate
still reads 0/0/0/0 at minw 4, 2 and 1, so nothing was double-rendered.

`_abhi04verify.js` → 277 passed, 0 failed. `regress.py check` → 55/55.

### The reader

`uddanaHTML()` drew `<div class="udd-verse"></div>` unconditionally, which
under a label with no lines is a blank band. It is now emitted only when the
block has lines. `verify_render_vs_pdf.py` already modelled the label
correctly and needed no change.

### 05Vin05 — the gates

* **body** `python3 pipeline/verify_render_vs_pdf.py 05Vin05 14 403 0 519` at
  minw 4, 2, 1 → **PDF-lines-missing 0 | render-not-in-PDF 0 |
  rendered-too-often 0** at all three; chunks 0 / 1 / 1.
  The one chunk is NAMED and is not a drop: `na ca vi`. Printed p332 ends its
  body column with "…nissitajappī ca, na ca" and carries the footnote
  "* Vi 5. 287 piṭṭhepi." below the rule; the continuation
  "bhāsānusandhikusalo hoti…" is the first line of p333. The chunk cutter reads
  the page in stream order and so MANUFACTURES a run that spans the
  body/footnote join — text the page never sets in that order, and which the
  render is right not to contain. Two PDF-reading-order artifacts are reported
  and named the same way (ord146, and one at the same p332/333 join).
* **apparatus** `rebuild_apparatus.py 05Vin05 --write` then
  `verify_apparatus.py 05Vin05` → **stored 176 | printed cells 182 | spliced 0
  | variants-not-stored 1 | xrefs-not-stored 0**, up from 119 stored / 3 lost /
  21 xrefs lost. The single loss is RECORDED, NOT GUESSED: p30 note 1
  "Odātānaṁ ante ante (Sī), odātānaṁ ante (Syā)" cannot be anchored because the
  body reads "thokaññeva odātaṁ ante 1 ādiyitvā" — the note's lemma is not the
  body's wording, so no anchor exists to match. Needs a lemma-form rule, not a
  wider match.
* **presentation** `node pipeline/check_layout.js 05Vin05` → **ok, 505 ¶,
  incipit x1**.

### A SECOND defect, found in the gate itself and fixed

`verify_render_vs_pdf.py` had

```python
    if fwd_chunk:
        ...
        order_chunks = [c for c in fwd_chunk if c not in _li]
        fwd_chunk = _keep
    order, order_chunks = [], []      # <-- clobbers what was just computed
```

so every chunk the reclassification named was **discarded and reported
nowhere**, undercounting the PDF-reading-order column. It never hid a real
failure — those go to `_keep` and are still reported as MISSING-CHUNK — but the
diagnostic was silently lossy. The initialisation now happens BEFORE the block.
05Vin05 went from 1 reported reading-order artifact to 2 on that change alone;
**other volumes' reading-order counts may rise for the same reason and that is
the fix working, not a regression.**

### Still open on 05Vin05 — RECORDED, NOT FIXED

**53 uddāna labels are rendered as colophon lines, not as labels.** `UDDLBL`
requires the label to end at the word (`\d*$`), and 05Vin05 sets
`Tassuddānaṁ.` **with a full stop** 53 times. Those lines are classified
`colo`, so each renders as its own centred italic block above its verses
instead of as that block's `udd-label`. **Content and printed order are
correct** — nothing is missing or moved — and the difference is one of ROLE and
styling. Measured across every built volume: **05Vin05 is the only one
affected** (all 27 uddāna maps scanned for the period form). Left alone
deliberately: widening `UDDLBL` changes `kat_items` classification for every
volume and buys styling only.

### A THIRD defect: `colofix` HAS BEEN UNREACHABLE ON EVERY `heads_by_form` VOLUME

Scanning every volume's heads stream for a heading that says a section has
ENDED (`niṭṭhit|samatt`) found **three colophons printed WITHOUT a full stop**,
each read as a HEADING — present, contiguous, and in the wrong role, which
every content gate reports as 0:

| volume | printed line | printed page |
|---|---|---|
| 01Vin01 | `Pārājikapāḷi niṭṭhitā` | the volume's own closing line, p404 |
| 02Vin02 | `Sañciccasikkhāpadaṁ niṭṭhitaṁ sattamaṁ` | p212 |
| 05Vin05 | `Ekuttarikaṁ niṭṭhitaṁ` | p265 |

`colofix` is exactly the mechanism for naming such a line — **and it did
nothing**, because `kat_is_colo` opened with

```python
    if SPEC[VOL].get('heads_by_form'):
        return (t.endswith('.') and ...)
```

and RETURNED before the `colofix` test below it. Every `heads_by_form` volume —
all five Vinaya volumes, 31Abhi03, 32Abhi04 and the rest — could declare a
`colofix` literal and see no effect and no error. The named literals are now
checked FIRST, which is what "named" is supposed to mean. `regress.py check` →
55/55 both before and after.

                          **25 of the 39 are ONE editorial excursus** — see below
              presentation  check_layout ok, 454 ¶, incipit x1
              extent      declared 1-based 12-519, which the measured extent
                          reproduces exactly; gate 0-based `11 518`
              inert       regression 55/55; the 55 side-maps of the eleven
                          other kathā volumes rebuild byte-identical; body
                          sweep 26/118 -> **27/118**, none dropped

The diagnosis below was written before the fix; both are kept because the
measurement is what scoped the fix.

### AN UDDĀNA THAT CHANGES COLUMN AT A PAGE BREAK

The Senāsanakkhandhaka's closing uddāna runs over three printed pages:

    p344   'Vihāraṁ Buddhaseṭṭhena, apaññattaṁ tadā ahu.'      indent 0
    p345   'Khuddake kuṭṭapādo ca, ovassati saraṁ khilaṁ.'     indent 6
    p346   'Kālañca sāmaṇerañca, sikkhāpaccakkha-antimaṁ.'     indent 0

`_kat_cols` measures the body column PER PAGE. On p344 and p346 the uddāna IS
the whole page, so the body column measures 0 and its lines sit AT it — they
are classified `pcont`, ordinary prose. On p345 the same block sits at 6, three
or more above that page's body column, so the same lines are classified
`vline`, verse.

**One printed block, classified two ways, and then emitted in two different
places** — `pcont` joins the running prose string in `after`, `vline` opens a
gāthā block — so the render reads p344 straight into p346 and the p345 half
turns up elsewhere. Nothing is LOST, which is why `PDF-lines-missing` is 0 and
only the ORDER check catches it: `render-not-in-PDF` at ord327 word 118/235 and
ord380 word 129/288, both exactly at a page boundary inside an uddāna.

### THE MEASUREMENT, so the fix can be scoped rather than guessed

Pages that are a solid run of comma-bearing couplet lines (12 or more), by
where those lines sit:

    01Vin01   2 at the BODY column,  2 at a display indent
    02Vin02   0                      0
    03Vin03   0                     14
    04Vin04   8                     17

So 04Vin04 is the first volume where BOTH shapes occur, which is why it is the
first to break: a block only goes wrong where it CROSSES from one to the other.
01Vin01 has two of each and passes all three gates, so its uddāna do not
straddle a flip — checked, not assumed.

### WHAT THIS IS NOT

It is not `disp_only` — that fires only when a page has NOTHING at the body
column, and on p344 the uddāna itself is at the body column. It is not
`pada_runon` or `verse_indent`, which decide whether a display run is verse;
here the question is prior to that, namely which column the block is IN.

**DO NOT FIX IT BY WIDENING THE DISPLAY GATE.** The body column is measured
per page for good reason and every shipped volume depends on it. The shape to
recognise is a BLOCK THAT SPANS A PAGE BREAK: an uddāna opened by
"Tassuddānaṁ" and closed by its khandhaka colophon is one block wherever its
lines happen to sit, and the page it starts on should decide the whole of it.
That is a change to `kat_items`' page loop, which is shared machinery, so it
needs the same treatment as everything else — gate it per volume, measure it
over all of them, and prove the shipped ones byte-identical.

### THE FIX — `udd_run`: the LABEL decides the block, not the page

The edition marks the block itself: **"Tassuddānaṁ" opens it and the section's
own colophon closes it.** So the label decides the whole run wherever its lines
happen to sit, and that state is carried ACROSS the page break — the only
thing in `kat_items` that is. A numbered unit or a heading ends the run too;
those cannot occur inside an uddāna and are the safety net if a colophon is
ever missed.

The closing line is recognised WITHOUT an indent test, for the same reason the
pādas are: on a page the uddāna fills, the colophon sits at the body column too
("Senāsanakkhandhako niṭṭhito." on p346 was arriving as prose). It must NAME a
section and say it is finished — `kat_is_colo`'s own strictest form.

**The per-page body measurement was NOT touched.** It is load-bearing for every
shipped volume and this is a fact about one BLOCK, not about the page. Gated
per volume; 04Vin04 is the only volume that declares it, and the eleven other
kathā volumes rebuild byte-identical with it in the file.

### !!! THE EDITION PRINTS A WHOLE ALTERNATIVE RECENSION BELOW THE RULE

04Vin04's apparatus reports 39 variants not stored, where the other Vinaya
volumes report one to three. **Twenty-five of the 39 are a single editorial
excursus spanning printed p187-p189.** Footnote 1 on p188 says the navaka
appears in the old manuscripts in the *avisukkhi* form conflated with the
third, that the editors separated it, and that the Sīhaḷa and Syāma manuscripts
have it in the *visuddhi* form — "Taṁ panevaṁ veditabbaṁ–" — and then prints
the ENTIRE alternative section below the rule, under its own centred heading
**"10. Mūlāyavisuddhinavaka (Sī, Syā)"**, with its own numbered unit 183 running
over three pages.

So these are not lost word-variants: they are an alternative RECENSION of a
section, carried in the apparatus. `verify_apparatus` counts them as printed
cells because they are below the rule, and cannot store them as notes because
they carry no marker. **This is substantive for the project** — §2 of the
instructions treats the variant apparatus as the most valuable single output,
and this is a kind of apparatus entry no volume has shown before. FLAGGED, not
forced into the note model. The body is unaffected: it is all below the rule,
and the body gate reads 0/0/0/0.

**A first attempt to census how often the edition does this was WRONG and its
figure must not be quoted** — it matched any numbered footnote cell beginning
with a capital, so it "found" 71-218 pages per volume, which is simply the
ordinary apparatus. Whether the excursus shape occurs elsewhere is UNKNOWN.

that everything under `site/reader/` has passed its gates. The SPEC stays in
the builder and is correct as far as it goes.

**THE MISSING LINE, and its cause is known.** Printed p171 sets

    Samuṭṭhānasīsasaṅkhepa        <- head
    Samuṭṭhānassuddānaṁ           <- udd  (the label)
    Aniccā sabbe saṅkhārā, …      <- a NUMBERED UNIT

The label opens an uddāna block, but the verses it labels ARE the numbered unit
that follows — so the block ends with a `label` and NO `lines`, and the tidy
pass at the foot of `build()` drops exactly that shape ("an uddāna block with a
label but no lines is a stray label"). The label never renders. That filter is
right in general — it is what keeps 28Khu11's paired headings — and what it
cannot see is a label whose verses are a UNIT. **The fix belongs with the
filter, is SHARED machinery, and must be measured over every volume first.**

## THE UDĀNA FALLBACK WAS PRINTING TWICE — 03Vin03 DONE (2026-07-26ag)

    03Vin03   body        14 524 0 490 {4,2,1} -> 0/0/0/0
              apparatus   397 anchored, 413 printed cells -> 0 / 3 flagged / 0
              presentation  check_layout ok, 481 ¶, incipit x1
              pairing     479 / 479, 0 n-mismatches
    THE FIX WAS IN THE READER, and `verify_render_vs_pdf.py` had the same bug
    inert     ALL 26 body-clean volumes re-run: 26/118, none dropped;
              check_layout re-run on all 26, all ok; every per-volume checker
              re-run (see below); regression 55/55

### THE CAUSE — a fallback that assumed there was a verse to introduce

`block()` in `reader2.html`, for a verse entry with NO `before`:

    else { const mt=pr.text.match(/^([\s\S]*?udāna\S*\s+udānes[iī][–-])/);
           pre=mt?fmtText(mt[1]):''; }

That lifts the narrative lead-in ("…imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi–") out of the CORPUS
paragraph so it stands above the gāthā the side-map supplies. It was written
for the Udāna and it is right there.

**A PROSE UNIT HAS NO GĀTHĀ TO INTRODUCE, AND ITS WHOLE BODY ALREADY COMES FROM
`after`**, drawn from the printed stream. So on a kathā volume the fallback
printed the lead-in a SECOND time, inside the paragraph that already held it —
one text node in the `.para.canon` and another in the `.gatha-after` nested
inside it. Both now require a non-empty `groups`.

MEASURED over every volume with a verse map: **seven paragraphs in all are
affected and every one is in 03Vin03**; and NOWHERE does a prose unit have an
empty `after` for which this fallback was the only source, so requiring a verse
cannot blank anything. The body gate had reported only **two** of the seven —
the other five are masked by the Vinaya's own formulaic repetition, which is
also why the first count taken here (125 of 479 openings appearing more than
once) was not a defect count: **91 of those 125 are the edition repeating
itself**, e.g. "Idha pana bhikkhave bhikkhusaṁghena tajjanīyakammakato…" ten
times.

### !!! `verify_render_vs_pdf.py` MODELS THE READER, SO IT MODELLED THE BUG

The gate does not run the reader; `_plist` and the block around it reproduce
`block()` in Python. That is why it could see the symptom and never the cause,
and why patching only `reader2.html` left the gate still reporting 2. **When a
render defect is found, look for it in BOTH.** Backups: `reader2.html.bakvinaya`,
`verify_render_vs_pdf.py.preudana`.

### WHY 03Vin03 WAS RIGHT TO BE WITHDRAWN, and right to come back

2026-07-26af held the volume out rather than shipping it on a gate result that
was not understood. The mechanism turned out to be a defect in shared code, not
in this volume — which is exactly the case where shipping on "probably fine"
would have buried it. The side-maps were restored from
`_to_delete/03Vin03_unverified/` unchanged; nothing about the volume's own
build needed to change.

### `head_words` — THE WORD CAP IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A CONSTANT

Under `heads_by_form` a NUMBERED line is a heading only when it is centred AND
short AND unpunctuated within. "Short" has been **2** since 36Abhi08 measured it
there, and every Abhidhamma volume since has agreed. 03Vin03's section titles
are three and four words — "Āpattiyā adassane ukkhittakavatthūni", "Saṁghe
bhinne cīvaruppādakathā" — so four of them were read as numbered UNITS.

MEASURED on that volume: of its 769 numbered printed lines, **282 are ≤4 words
with no internal period and centred at body+14 or beyond, and every one is a
section title**; the 473 that are longer are all units; and of the 14 that are
short but sit LOW, the six ending at a heading stem are titles whose own length
pushed them down (the recurring "a centred line's indent falls as its name
grows") and the rest are units the stem test correctly refuses. So
`head_words: 4` here, defaulting to the 2 every shipped volume was measured at.

### `pada_runon` WIDENED TO THE WHOLE RUN — and a fourth shipped volume fixed

01Vin01's couplets alternate comma / stop, so looking one line back reaches
them. **03Vin03 prints long gāthā in which every pāda ends in a stop** and only
some carry a comma at the caesura, and there the line above says nothing. What
the page says is that they are ONE BLOCK: a maximal run of display lines at a
single indent. If any line in that run carries a comma, the run is verse and
none of it is a closing line.

**THE ONE EXCEPTION IS THE EDITION'S OWN STRICT COLOPHON FORM** — a line that
both NAMES a section and says it is FINISHED. 31Abhi03 p94 sets "Asaṅgahitena
sampayuttavippayuttapadaniddeso terasamo." at the SAME indent as the six gāthā
lines above it. Measured over every kathā book with a SPEC: the run test
reclassifies 476 lines and the strict form rescues **exactly that one**.

**32Abhi04 had 45 pādas drawn as colophons** — "Tayassu dhammā jahitā
bhavanti.", "Sīlabbataṁ vāpi yadatthi kiñci." and 43 more — and a false
colophon also CUT the block it stood in, so the volume drew 35 gāthā blocks
where it prints 44. Fixed and re-gated. **26Khu09, 27Khu10 and 28Khu11 were
suspected on the same evidence and CLEARED**: the form test fires there but the
classification never reaches it. That makes **four** shipped volumes corrected
by this class in two sessions (31Abhi03, 32Abhi04, 33Abhi05, 36Abhi08).

### !!! WHY 03Vin03 IS NOT WRITTEN — an unexplained RENDER duplication

The body gate reports **2 chunks rendered twice, printed once**, both in the
Mahākhandhaka's opening (printed units 4 and 5, "Atha kho Bhagavā sattāhassa
accayena tamhā samādhimhā vuṭṭhahitvā …"). Established so far, by measurement:

  * the phrase is printed ONCE, is in the corpus ONCE, and appears in exactly
    ONE side-map entry;
  * the RENDER contains it TWICE — two distinct text nodes, one in the
    `.para.canon` itself and one in a `div.gatha-after` INSIDE it;
  * 476 of the 479 verse entries have an `after` that repeats their own corpus
    paragraph's opening, which is how the kathā path is supposed to work (it
    draws the body from the PRINTED stream), so that alone is not the fault;
  * **01Vin01 and 02Vin02 pass the same gate at `rendered-too-often 0` with the
    same builder and the same reader**, so this is specific to this volume;
  * a count of "units whose 70-character opening appears more than once in the
    render" gives 125 of 479, but **91 of those are explained by the Vinaya's
    formulaic openings** ("Idha pana bhikkhave bhikkhusaṁghena tajjanīyakammakato
    …" occurs 10 times), so that figure is NOT evidence of 125 defects and must
    not be quoted as one.

What is NOT yet known is the mechanism, and therefore whether the remaining ~34
are real. **FLAG RATHER THAN GUESS**: the side-maps are withdrawn rather than
shipped on a gate result that is not understood. `03Vin03` also carries
commentary links (`ATp.3 ⧉` renders immediately before the duplicated text),
which 01Vin01 and 02Vin02 have far fewer of — that is the first thing to test.

**THE VINAYA IS THE KATHĀ PAGE AGAIN** — a numbered unit IS prose and the
number opens it at indent 4-5, continuation returning to the body column —
so `heads_by_form` and the kathā reader carry straight over. What does NOT
carry over is that these volumes PRINT GĀTHĀ, in quantity, where the whole
Abhidhamma prints almost none; that is where all the new work was.

### THE METADATA MERGES TEXT AND INDEX ON BOTH, and the tail must be MEASURED

01Vin01 and 02Vin02 say "[23 pages of content, 405 pages of text **and
index**]", so `declared_range` correctly refuses them. Measured from the page:
01Vin01 is 1-based 24-404 (p405 is a blank leaf, the index opens at p406) and
02Vin02 is 15-484.

**!!! `docs/verify_report.md` HAS BEEN CARRYING THE WRONG RANGE FOR BOTH** —
`23–404` and `14–485`, i.e. one and two pages of INDEX read as body text. That
is where part of their old 138 and 310 missing-line counts came from.

### `pipeline/scout_volume.py` — the scouting is now a REPO TOOL

The same four measurements have been hand-rolled as session scratch three times
(33Abhi05, 34Abhi06, 35Abhi07). `extent` / `corpus` / `geometry` / `pair` /
`page`, and `pair` is the one that matters: it aligns the printed unit stream
against the corpus with `difflib` and NAMES every divergence with its page,
where a count alone only says that a book does not pair. Moved into the repo
for the same reason `regress.py` was on 2026-07-26w.

**It found two of its own bugs immediately**, both about where a volume's text
ENDS, and both would have put index pages into the body:
  * **the index's own title is not spelt the same in every volume** — 05Vin05
    heads it "anukkama**n**ikā" with a dental n, 02Vin02 "anukkamaṇik**a**"
    with a short final a;
  * **a blank leaf before the index is not text** — 03Vin03 closes on p525 and
    leaves p526 blank.
With both fixed the tool reproduces the declared extent exactly on the three
Vinaya volumes whose metadata is usable.

### `pada_runon` — A PĀDA THAT FINISHES THE LINE ABOVE IT IS NOT A COLOPHON

Under `heads_by_form` a colophon is decided by FORM alone: ends in a stop, no
comma, six words or fewer. In a book that prints gāthā that is also the shape
of every SECOND pāda of a couplet —

    Na dukkaraṁ viriyamathopi maccuno,      <- a candidate
    Bhāyāvuso vippaṭisāri sammā.            <- read as a COLOPHON

— so eighteen of 01Vin01's uddāna were being cut in half and their even pādas
drawn as centred closing lines. **0/0/0/0 from the body gate on every one.**

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE EDITION'S OWN PUNCTUATION: the line above ends in a
COMMA, so it is mid-sentence, and a closing line never follows one. MEASURED
over every kathā book with a SPEC: it reclassifies 75 lines and **not one of
them carries a closing word** (`niṭṭhita`, `samatta`, an ordinal).

**A rule keyed on "shares its indent with a neighbour" was tried first and
REJECTED on measurement** — it loses real colophons in 31Abhi03, 32Abhi04,
33Abhi05, 35Abhi07 and 40Abhi12, all of which print two adjacently at one
indent.

### !!! THE SAME DEFECT WAS ALREADY SHIPPED IN TWO ABHIDHAMMA VOLUMES

Found by running the measurement over every volume rather than only the new
one, and NOT noticed when either was built:

  * **31Abhi03 — 11 pādas** drawn as colophons ("Sattindriyā asaññābhavo
    ekavokārabhavo.", "Itthipumaṁ jīvitaṁ nāmarūpaṁ." and nine more);
  * **36Abhi08 — 8**, all in its opening mātikā ("Dukaṁ tikañceva tikaṁ
    dukañca." / "Cha anulomamhi nayā sugambhīrāti.", p44-p47).

Both now carry `pada_runon` and both were re-run on all three gates and on
their own checkers (`_abhi03verify.js` 49/49, `_abhi08verify.js` 1323/1323).
**26Khu09 and 27Khu10 were suspected on the same evidence and CLEARED** — the
form test fires there but the classification does not reach it, so neither
volume has the defect. Checked, not assumed.

### `wrap_display` GENERALISED, and it too was already shipped broken

The rule added on 35Abhi07 required the wrapped remainder to sit at the SAME
indent as the line above. That is true of that volume's two and false
everywhere else, because a CENTRED line's remainder is centred too and lands
somewhere else entirely — and the line above need not be a display line at all
(02Vin02 p286 sets the recitation formula at the body column and centres only
its remainder). Both conditions dropped; what is being recognised is a line
that CANNOT begin anything, and the capital says so.

Re-measured: SEVEN instances in all seventeen volumes with a SPEC, every one a
genuine wrap. **33Abhi05 p207 and p227 and 36Abhi08 p160** are two more shipped
instances — a parenthetical editorial note rendering as two paragraphs — now
fixed with the same flag and re-gated.

### Three more one-line shapes, each NAMED after a census

  * **`split_literals` x4.** A census over all five Vinaya volumes finds SIX
    centred pair-lines `split_centre` cannot read; three are in 02Vin02 and one
    in 01Vin01 (the rest are in 05Vin05, not yet built). Two are the
    single-space slip already known from 37Abhi09 and 33Abhi05. The third,
    01Vin01 p36 "1. Paṭhamapārājika       Sudinnabhāṇavāra", is a THIRD
    pair-line shape — numbered|UNNUMBERED, where `split_centre` reads
    numbered|numbered and `split_unnumbered` reads unnumbered|numbered.
    Exactly one line in the whole Vinaya has it, so it is named.
  * **A LIST OF NUMBERS, not just a range.** 02Vin02 p472 heads three
    sikkhāpadas together "8-9-10. Aṭṭhama navama dasamasikkhāpada", and
    `\d+(?:-\d+)?\.` does not match that at all — so the strip left a leading
    digit, `kat_is_head` refused it for want of a capital, and the pair took a
    unit's ordinal. Widened to `(?:-\d+)*` in `_is_double_head` and
    `_starts_double_head` ONLY: both are reached solely from the kathā path, so
    no verse-mode volume can see it.
  * **A TITLE STACK OF ONE IS A STACK.** The derivation wanted two lines
    because 40Abhi12's twenty title pages all set a naya above the book name;

    derivation aborted for the WHOLE volume, so that book had no stack — and
    `kat_build` filters the title line out of the body on the understanding
    that `booktitle/` will draw it, so **the line vanished from the page**.
    The body gate found it: one PDF line missing.

### 34Abhi06 — the piṭaka's SECOND embedded unit number, exactly where predicted

Printed p78 sets **"24.Yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca…"** with no space after the
number, so the extraction saw no boundary and unit 24's whole text arrived
inside ord185, the paragraph carrying n=23. 2026-07-26m's census of all
eighteen Abhidhamma volumes found exactly two of these and named this one three
sessions before it was built; `kat_splices` took it with no argument.

**!!! AND THE MARK IS NOT ONLY A KEY — IT IS THE TEXT THAT RENDERS.** Declared
as `'24.Yattha kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca'` — the unit's opening words,
which is all the check asks for — every one of the three tests passed, and the
page then read "…paṭighānusayo ca **diṭṭhānusayo** ca…" with `mānānusayo ca`
gone, because the printed continuation lines were joined onto a truncated
opening. **The mark must be the printed unit's WHOLE FIRST LINE.** The body gate
caught it (1 chunk missing, 1 not in the PDF), which is exactly what that gate
is for; 36Abhi08's declaration happens to be a whole first line and so never
exposed the requirement.

### 34Abhi06 — and 35Abhi07 — PRINT NO GĀTHĀ AT ALL, and it is SHOWN

The same test 29Abhi01 used, and the strongest form of it: **a pāda carries
commas, and not one display line in either volume has one.** 34Abhi06: 175
display lines over 316 text pages, every one a heading, colophon, homage or
title. 35Abhi07: 224 over 330. So `no_verse`, and four blocks of the
Saṅkhārayamaka's catechism and nine of the Indriyayamaka's stop being drawn as
italic verse. **33Abhi05 could not use the flag** — it prints one real mnemonic
gāthā and needed `verse_indent: 10`. Three volumes of one work, two different
answers, because it is a fact about the PAGE and not about the book.

### 34Abhi06 — the edition's own misprint, preserved

Printed p211 numbers a unit **277** between 226 and 228. Kept exactly as
printed; the corpus carries the same number, so the pairing is unaffected and
`_abhi06verify.js` asserts the page still shows it.

### 34Abhi06's ANUSAYAYAMAKA prints every vāra's name TWICE

Once over its anuloma half and once over its paṭiloma half, and its mātikā does
the same — but the COLOPHONS settle it: "Anusayavāre anulomaṁ.", "Anusayavāre
paṭilomaṁ.", then "Anusayavāro." closing both. **ONE node with six children.**
Splitting it would also put two adjacent siblings of the same name in the tree,
which `_navdup.js` refuses.

### !!! `matika_reprints` — AND WHY 57 ENTRIES WERE MEASURED FROM THE WRONG PLACE

The mātikā reprints an ancestor's name exactly as the body does, and the tree
has no node for a reprint. The entry scan's pointer is FORWARD-ONLY, so an
unrecognised reprint is searched for AHEAD — **and in a book that says the same
thing twice, it is found, in the next section.** 34Abhi06's Cittayamaka prints
an Uddesa and a Niddesa with IDENTICAL entry lists and reprints
"1. Suddhacittasāmañña" over each of its three vāras; the first unrecognised
one sent the pointer out of the Uddesa and into the Niddesa, and all 57 entries
after it were measured from there. **Nothing was missing and the tree was
right — the CHECK was wrong**, which is the exact failure that scan's own
comment has warned about since 36Abhi08.

Two shapes, both keyed on the chain of the LAST MATCHED node and both read OFF
THE TREE rather than from a list typed in the file:

  * the entry IS an ancestor's name -> a reprint, skipped, pointer held;
  * the entry OPENS with one -> the pair-line "2. Pavatti  2. Nirodhavāra",
    where the tree holds one "2. Pavatti" with three children.

**This REPLACES `matika_prefixes`**, added earlier the same day for 33Abhi05's
pair-lines, which was that list typed by hand. 33Abhi05 reads identically
without it (141 entries, 4 compound, 0 out of order) — corrected in the
2026-07-26ac entry above.

### 35Abhi07 — A WRAPPED DISPLAY LINE IS NOT A COLOPHON (`wrap_display`)

Printed p83 sets two catechetical statements too long for the measure:

    Na somanassaṁ na somanassindriyaṁ. . Na somanassindriyaṁ na
    somanassaṁ.

The remainder, alone at the display indent, is ONE WORD ENDING IN A FULL STOP —
a colophon by every test this file has — so two centred closing lines rendered
in the middle of a vāra. **0/0/0/0 from the body gate**, because every word is
present and in order; the `--show` listing is the only thing that could see it.

**The signal is the capital.** In this edition every heading, colophon, homage,
title and pāda opens with one, and a wrapped remainder does not. MEASURED over
all twelve Abhidhamma volumes: **10,789 display lines, and a display line
beginning lowercase directly under another at the SAME indent occurs EXACTLY
TWICE — these two.** So 33Abhi05 and 34Abhi06 are confirmed unaffected rather
than assumed to be, and there is nothing to correct in them.

### !!! 35Abhi07 — AN ERRATUM IN THE BODY IS NOT AN ERRATUM IN THE MĀTIKĀ

Printed p328 heads the Pariññāvāra's fourth vāra **"4. Paccuppannātītivāra"** —
*-īti-* for *-īta-* — where the other four printings (p28, p50, p71, p229) and
the volume's own mātikā all set "4. Paccuppannātītavāra". Preserved verbatim.

`errata` cannot express this: it rewrites a mātikā entry GLOBALLY, which is
right when the misprint occurs once on each side (31Abhi03) and wrong when the
same heading is printed five times and only ONE printing is misspelt. Rewritten
globally, all five mātikā entries matched only the misprinted node — and the
forward-only pointer jumped **195 sections into the next book**, stranding 71
entries. So the alternative belongs on the TREE side: `body_errata` makes the
misprinted label ALSO fold as the form the mātikā uses, through the same slot
`head_prefixes` already uses, and the four correct printings keep matching
literally.

### 35Abhi07's level table — and why `Anuloma` needed a rung of its own

33Abhi05 could put the six vāras and `Anuloma`/`Paccanīka` at the SAME declared
level, because under its Pariññāvāra the six carry nothing. Here they each
carry an Anuloma and a Paccanīka — so with both at one level, `level_memo`
handed the pair the depth it had just given the vāra and they rendered as its
SIBLINGS. Declared one rung down they clamp to depth 2 under a vāra wherever
that vāra itself sits, which is what the page shows in all three branches.
(Pariññāvāra came out with 18 children instead of 6; the tree listing showed it.)

### What these two volumes print that no other does

  * **The Dhammayamaka closes with a BHĀVANĀVĀRA**, not a Pariññāvāra —
    "Bhāvanāvāro." on p81 — and the edition sets it as one section with nothing
    under it.
  * **The Indriyayamaka's Pavatti holds ONLY the Uppādavāra.** No Nirodhavāra,
    no Uppādanirodhavāra; its own mātikā goes straight on to the Pariññāvāra.
    The short branch is the page's, not a drop, and it is asserted as such.
  * **The Cittayamaka's Niddesa stops its third vāra at the fifth** where the
    Uddesa runs all fourteen — again the mātikā's own reading.

**BOTH COUNTS THAT WOULD NOT PAIR WERE ON THE PRINTED SIDE, exactly as
2026-07-26ab predicted — and neither was where that entry expected to look.**
The nine hidden ordinals were all genuine and the hide-map never moved.

### Āyatana: TWO PRINTED LINES READ AS UNITS — `split_literals`

The pair **"2. Pavatti   N. …vāra"** is printed nine times in this volume.
SEVEN separate the halves with three spaces, which `split_centre` reads; printed
**p142 ("2. Pavatti 2. Nirodhavāra") and p180 ("2. Pavatti 3.
Uppādanirodhavāra") use ONE**, so those two lines stayed whole and — starting
with a number — were classified as numbered UNITS. That is the whole of
Āyatana's 256-against-254. The same shape as 37Abhi09 p316; the same answer,
because widening the rule to one space would split ordinary unit text at its
first internal number. **Census over all 284 pages: exactly these two.**

### !!! Sacca: THE DECLARED EXTENT IS ONE PAGE SHORT AT THE END TOO

2026-07-26ab found that `declared_range('33Abhi05')` starts one page early and
**corrected only the head**. It is wrong at BOTH ENDS, and for one reason: the
metadata declares "content 10 + text 265" where the front matter is **eleven**
pages, so the declared text LENGTH is right and the whole range is shifted by
one. The text runs 1-based **12-276**, not 11-275.

Printed **p276** carries the Saccayamaka's last numbered unit (**170**, under
"6. Atītānāgatavāra"), its "Pariññāvāro." and its "Saccayamakapāḷi niṭṭhitā.";
the printed word index opens at 277. Cut at 275 the book came out 169 printed
against 170 corpus — the missing unit was simply off the end of the range.

**SO THE BODY GATE IS 0-based `11 275`. The `11 274` given in 2026-07-26ab is
WRONG and that entry's Sacca diagnosis ("its printed stream is missing one real
unit") was right about the symptom and wrong about the cause.**

`verify_all_volumes.page_range()` now prefers `build_khu_volume.SPEC`'s
hand-measured extent over the metadata wherever the volume has one. That is a
second reading of the same question rather than a table typed by hand, and it
was MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS TRUSTED: over the twenty volumes SPEC covers the two
agree on nineteen and differ only here. Without it the corpus report keeps a
permanently dirty row (4 lines / 3 reversed) for a volume that is clean — which
is precisely the trap the 22Khu05/23Khu06 caveat records.

### 21 OF THE 23 GĀTHĀ BLOCKS WERE THE BOOK'S OWN CATECHISM — `verse_indent`

The Yamaka asks its questions **one statement per printed line** —
"Sotaṁ sotāyatanaṁ, sotāyatanaṁ sotaṁ." — each a complete sentence with a comma
at its centre. That is a run of lines sharing one indent above the body column,
which is a gāthā's own shape, and `display_prose`'s pāda test cannot separate
them either because every line ends in a full stop. The body gate reads 0/0/0/0
on all of it, because every word is present.

**MEASURED OVER THE WHOLE VOLUME, not chosen:** the runs fall at indents 4, 6,
7, 8 and 9 — twenty-six of them, every one catechism — and at **12**, two of
them, both the SAME two-line mnemonic

    Mūlaṁ hetu nidānañca, sambhavo pabhavena ca.
    Samuṭṭhānāhārārammaṇā, paccayo samudayena cāti.

printed once to close the Mūlayamaka's Uddesavāra (p17) and again to close its
Niddesavāra (p26). **NOTHING at 10 or 11**, so `verse_indent` is the size of
that gap. `no_verse` is not available here — it would draw that mnemonic as
prose. 21 blocks -> 2.

### THE NAV — five yamakas, ONE bhāga, and the first NON-UNIFORM level table

The title page prints "Abhidhammapiṭake / YAMAKAPĀḶI / (Paṭhamo bhāgo)", so this
is **one node labelled as the edition labels it** with its five inner yamakas as
the first tree level — the shape `group_abhidhamma_volumes.py` already gave
volumes 33-40. NOT `separate_books`: the five yamakas are divisions of the
Yamaka, which is ONE of the seven books, where 31Abhi03's two really are two of
the seven.

**"2. Pavatti" is the LEFT half of a printed pair-line**, so by the standing
rule it stands one level above its three vāras. It is ONE node and its second
and third printings are ANCESTOR REPRINTS — which is also what keeps
`_navdup.js`'s adjacent-sibling rule satisfied; three sibling "2. Pavatti" tops
would have failed it.

**!!! THE KHANDHAYAMAKA'S THIRD IS PRINTED WITHOUT ITS LEFT HALF.** p67 sets a
bare "3. Uppādanirodhavāra" where the volume's own mātikā (p6) sets the pair.
The edition's asymmetry, followed rather than smoothed; the heading still lands
under "2. Pavatti" because that is the level it is declared at, and
`_abhi05verify.js` asserts exactly that.

Three machinery changes, each gated per volume and each proved inert by
rebuilding all nine shipped Abhidhamma navs to a byte-identical nav.json:

  * **`level_memo` — A DECLARED LEVEL KEEPS THE DEPTH IT WAS FIRST GIVEN UNDER
    ITS TOP.** `levels` is a table of DEPTHS and every shipped book has a
    uniform one, so `min(hit, len(stack))` never actually clamps there. **This
    is the first book whose two halves are not the same depth:** the six vāras
    "1. Paccuppannavāra" … "6. Atītānāgatavāra" sit THREE rungs down under
    "2. Pavatti" (Pavatti > Uppādavāra > Paccuppannavāra) and TWO rungs down
    under "3. Pariññāvāra", which has no middle rung at all. Declared at the
    deeper level the first Pariññāvāra vāra clamps correctly and the next five
    nest INSIDE it, six deep; declared at the shallower one Pavatti's vāras
    become siblings of their own parent. So the clamp is REMEMBERED, cleared at
    every new top and truncated above whatever level was just placed.
  * **~~`matika_prefixes`~~ — THE MĀTIKĀ REPRINTS AN ANCESTOR'S NAME TOO**, and
    the tree does not. It sets all three Pavatti vāras as pair-lines, so only
    the first folds equal to two adjacent tree labels. This is the mirror of
    `head_prefixes` on the body side; the literal fold is still tried FIRST, so
    nothing that matched before can stop matching. **SUPERSEDED THE SAME DAY BY
    `matika_reprints` (2026-07-26ad), which reads the reprint off the TREE
    instead of from a list typed by hand, and which 34Abhi06 needed for a
    second and worse shape of the same thing. This volume reads identically
    under it — 141 entries, 4 compound, 0 out of order.**
  * **A MĀTIKĀ RUNNING HEADER MAY CARRY A ROMAN FOLIO.** This mātikā runs eight
    pages over five books and heads each with that book's name, so
    `matika_headers`' "opens three or more pages" test cannot see them; the odd
    pages set the folio at the FAR margin ("Khandhayamakapāḷi        iii"),
    which `CENTRED` then read as an entry. A dotted entry always ends in an
    ARABIC number, so requiring no leaders keeps every real one.

### SANDHI AGAIN, and it cost two headings on the first run

`Suddha` + `āyatana` is printed **Suddhāyatanavāra**, so a level pattern
spelling `Suddha` matches the Khandha, Dhātu and Sacca yamakas and NOT the
Āyatana one — whose two vāras then fell through the level table to the
catch-all and hung under the previous section. **The stem ends at `Suddh` and
the vowel belongs to what follows** — the same trap the Paṭṭhāna hit at
`tika`/`tikādi` (2026-07-26v), and it was caught by READING THE TREE LISTING,
not by any gate: 487 sections either way.

### What the edition does here that no other volume does

  * **FIVE title pages and five homages in one volume**, one per yamaka, all
    five now rendering (`incipit x5`).
  * **The Dhātuyamaka is abridged by the edition itself** — "(Dhātuyamakaṁ
    paripuṇṇaṁ peyyālena.)" and "(Yathā Āyatanayamakaṁ vibhattaṁ, evaṁ
    Dhātuyamakampi vibhajitabbaṁ, sadisaṁ kātabbaṁ.)" — so it holds 19 units
    where the Āyatanayamaka holds 254, its Pavatti has ONE vāra and its
    Pariññāvāra none. Its own mātikā (p9) lists exactly that, so the short tree
    is the page's and not a drop.
  * **The Mūlayamaka's Uddesavāra and Niddesavāra are never printed as
    headings** — the edition names them only where they CLOSE ("Uddesavāro
    niṭṭhito."). So its four printed headings stand at the top of that book and
    the asymmetry is REPORTED rather than filled in with a heading the page does
    not set.
