## YAMAKA I — 33Abhi05 SCOUTED AND PART-BUILT, NOTHING WRITTEN (2026-07-26ab)

**SUPERSEDED BY 2026-07-26ac, WHICH FINISHED THE VOLUME — and TWO STATEMENTS
BELOW ARE WRONG, kept because the reasoning that produced them is worth
reading.** (1) "The body gate for this volume is 0-based `11 274`" — it is
`11 275`; the declared extent is shifted by one at BOTH ends, not just the
head. (2) "Sacca's printed stream is MISSING one real unit" — the classifier
was not missing it; unit 170 is printed on p276, off the end of the range that
same paragraph set. The Āyatana diagnosis below was right: two printed lines
are not units, and they are the two `split_literals` names.

`declared_range('33Abhi05')` gives 0-based 10-274, i.e. 1-based 11-275. **But

just the metadata, when a volume's first book will not pair.**

Both diverge at the same shape and it is a LEAKED HEADING: the corpus captured

`_is_double_head` requires BOTH halves to be heading-shaped, and on a CORPUS
paragraph the form test is unavailable (no indent evidence), so the stem list is
what decides: "Uppādavāra" ends at `vāra`, "Pavatti" ended at nothing. Adding
`pavatti|paññatti` to this volume's stems made the scan hide nine paragraphs
(148, 203, 329, 432, 512, 586, 615, 677, 726) — **but the two counts did not
move**, so the arithmetic is now the other way round and needs measuring rather
than another guess:

  * Sacca is 1 printed UNDER, which is the mirror case and probably a printed
    unit the classifier is missing rather than an over-hide.

Each was read back out of the corpus and every one is a leaked heading PAIR of

### 31Abhi03 — TWO BOOKS OF THE PIṬAKA, AND I GAVE THEM ONE NODE

The Dhātukathā and the Puggalapaññatti are two of the Abhidhamma's SEVEN books
that happen to share a physical volume. The nav builder writes ONE node per
volume, so it produced one node with the Puggalapaññatti nested inside the
Dhātukathā — inventing a book the edition does not print, which is exactly what
`group_abhidhamma_volumes.py` exists to undo in the other direction.

**`_abhigroupverify.js` caught it immediately** — "the Abhidhamma should list 13
volume rows; got 12" and "missing book row: Puggalapaññattipāḷi" — which is the
first time one of these checkers has caught a defect in the same session that
created it. `separate_books: True` now writes one nav node per book and the
splice's count assertion follows it. THE INVARIANT IS ONE NODE PER BOOK; a
volume node is not the unit.

### Three defects in the shared machinery, each found by a pairing count

  * **A UNIT AT THE LEFT MARGIN.** The Puggalapaññatti's mātikā sets every unit
    on its own line at indent 0-1 with no continuation at all, so the page's
    body column measures 0 and the `body + 3` floor read all 22 of them as prose
    (350 printed against 372 corpus). `heads_by_form` already lifts that floor —
    it is the escape 36Abhi08 needed for its two flush-left units.
  * **A CENTRED LINE'S INDENT FALLS AS ITS NAME GROWS**, and two separate
    indent floors assume otherwise. 31Abhi03 centres fourteen "-padaniddesa"
    section heads and the four longest land at indent 12-13, below the
    `body + 14` heading floor, so that book came out 522 printed against 518
    corpus. And its ELEVENTH padaniddesa COLOPHON —
    "Saṅgahitena sampayuttavippayuttapadaniddeso ekādasamo." — sits at indent 7
    where the other thirteen sit at 20+, below the `body + 8` colophon floor,
    and was rendering as ordinary prose. Both now let the WORDS be decisive:
    a heading that is two words or fewer with no internal period AND ENDS AT ONE
    OF THE VOLUME'S OWN STEMS is a heading wherever it sits; a colophon that
    both NAMES a section and says it is finished needs no indent, which is what
    `kat_is_colo`'s own docstring has claimed since it was written — the caller
    was refusing the line before the function could apply it.
    **Proved inert: 29Abhi01, 30Abhi02 and 36-40 all rebuild byte-identical.**

### 31Abhi03 — TWO MISPRINTS AND A HOMAGE VARIANT, all preserved verbatim

  * the BODY heads the fifth Niddesa section **"5. Pañcakapaggalapaññatti"** —
    *paggala* for *puggala* — where the volume's own mātikā and its printed word
    index both set *puggala*. The mātikā check found it; named in the nav
    builder's `errata` so the two are known to be one section.
  * the fourth padaniddesa's colophon reads **"…saṅgahitapasaniddeso
    catuttho."** — *pasaniddeso* for *padaniddeso*. This is why the colophon
    check reports that one section as not testable rather than failing on it.
  * **THE TWO HOMAGES DIFFER FROM EACH OTHER AND FROM EVERY OTHER VOLUME'S.**
    The Dhātukathā prints "Namo tassa … Sammāsambuddhassa" WITH NO TERMINAL
    STOP; the Puggalapaññatti prints "Namo Tassa" with a capital T — the form
    38Abhi10 also uses and the reason `HOMAGE` matches either case. Both kept
    as printed and asserted.

### 32Abhi04 — a heading form no other volume has (`head_paren`)

The Kathāvatthu heads every one of its 280 kathās with TWO numbers: the kathā's
number in the whole book, in parentheses, then its number within its vagga —
**"(10) 1. Parūpahārakathā"**, and "(106-108) 1-3. Tissopi-anusayakathā" where
three run together. `kat_is_head` requires the core to open with a capital, so
without stripping that parenthetical every one of them fell through. The LABEL
keeps both numbers exactly as printed; only the test needs the name.

`heads_by_form` is not merely convenient here but necessary: the 280 kathā
headings share no stem beyond `kathā` itself — the vaggas, the anuyogas,
"1. Vādayutti", "1. Suddhasaccikaṭṭha", "1. Nasuttasādhana" share none — and a
stem list would silently drop whichever it missed. **MEASURED SAFE:** of the
display lines at indent 8-17 that the form test would call a heading, ALL
EIGHTEEN are headings (long names centred low BECAUSE they are long), and the
176 comma-bearing display lines are rejected by the comma test before it.

**35 of its 37 display blocks are genuine quoted gāthā; TWO are the book's own
DIALOGUE** set at the same indent, both opening "Attheva suttantoti, āmantā."
(*Is there such a sutta? — Yes.*). `display_prose` catches one (its second line
runs on); the other has both lines ending in a full stop, so the formula decides
it — named, as in 27Khu10, not generalised.

### 32Abhi04's NAV — BUILT 2026-07-26aa, following the page rather than smoothing it

**THE DECISION WAS THE USER'S** (asked and answered): the first vagga has no
printed heading, so its ten kathās stand at the top level beside the
twenty-two named vaggas. That is exactly what the page sets — and what the
volume's own MĀTIKĀ sets, which lists the first vagga's kathās as its own group
heads and only then begins "2. Dutiyavagga". The asymmetry is the edition's.

A first row taken from that vagga's closing colophon ("Mahāvaggo." at ord305)
was the alternative and was REJECTED, on the user's point: **"Mahāvagga" is a
BOOK title elsewhere in this canon** — 03Vin03 and 07Di02 both print
Mahāvaggapāḷi, and three commentary volumes echo it — so a bare row of that name
inside the Kathāvatthu would read as one. THE BOOK IS Kathāvatthupāḷi, off its
own title page, and nothing in the nav changes that.

### What the mātikā check found once it could read the mātikā at all

`MAT` could not see an entry whose absolute number is set in parentheses, so it
was reading **45 of ~255 entries**. With the optional `(\d+)` prefix — kept IN
the entry text, because the body keeps it too, so the two fold equal — it reads
255, and then reported six real divergences between the two printed pages, all
named in `errata` and each page keeping what it prints:

    mātikā  3. Brahmacariyakathā (ka)      body  3. Brahmacariyakathā
    mātikā  3. Odhisokathā (kha)           body  3. Odhisokathā
    mātikā  15. Pannārasamavagga           body  15. Pannarasamavagga
    mātikā  (16) 7. Cittiṭṭhitikathā       body  (16) 7. Cittaṭṭhitikathā
    mātikā  (106-8) 1-3. Tissopi-…         body  (106-108) 1-3. Tissopi-…
    mātikā  (175) 10. …dinnaṁ mahapphal…   body  (175) 10. …dinnaṁmahapphal…

and ONE MISSING HEADING, which is the part that matters: **the body's longest
heading is centred at indent 7**, below the display gate, and was rendering as
ordinary prose. 0/0/0/0 from the body gate either way, because the line is
present — the mātikā check is the only thing that could see it.

**LETTING MEASURED CENTRING STAND IN FOR THE DISPLAY GATE WAS TRIED AND
REJECTED.** It moves EVERY `heads_by_form` volume (29Abhi01, 30Abhi02, 31Abhi03
and 36-40 all shift), and even confined to this volume it took 44 of the
edition's starred cross-reference lines as headings — six words, no comma, no
terminal stop, and `head_body` strips the `*` before the form test — while still
missing the line it was written for. So the line is NAMED in `headfix`, and
`headfix` now applies wherever a line sits rather than only above the gate.

### Superseded — what the nav needed before the decision

The tree is 23 vaggas x ~10 kathās, and the vagga name is REPRINTED at the head
of every kathā ("2. Dutiyavagga" eleven times), which the nav builder's
ancestor-reprint rule already handles. **THE PROBLEM IS THE FIRST VAGGA: the
edition prints NO opening heading for it.** The book opens straight into
"1. Puggalakathā", and the vagga is named only where it CLOSES —
"Mahāvaggo." at ord305, after which "2. Dutiyavagga" is reprinted at every kathā
of the second. So an ordered top level cannot be read off the printed headings
alone, and inventing "1. Paṭhamavagga" would be invention.

Two honest options, and this is a judgement about the book rather than about the
machinery, so ASK BEFORE BUILDING:
  (a) take the first vagga's node from its CLOSING colophon, labelled
      "Mahāvagga" as the edition names it there — the colophons are a printed
      witness and the other 23 agree with the headings;
  (b) leave the first vagga's kathās directly under the book and start the vagga
      level at the second, reporting the asymmetry.
Its mātikā (0-based pages 3-13) is a real ordered list and can gate whichever is
chosen. **NOTE the 24 vagga colophons for 23 vaggas** — "Kalyāṇavaggo paṭhamo."
at ord191 closes something inside the first vagga; that needs reading before the
tree is built.

Two apparatus variants stay FLAGGED, NOT GUESSED: p307's note is a two-witness
variant whose printed cell spans a line break, and p357's is an editorial remark
carrying no reading.

### !!! `page_lines(pages, i)` TAKES A 1-BASED PAGE NUMBER

A scout written with 0-based pages read one page early throughout: it picked up
the last two entries of the MĀTIKĀ ("1. Rūpaduka … 452", "2. Lokiyaduka … 452")
as numbered units and reported 1046 printed against 1044 corpus, with printed
numbers 1 and 2 occurring twice. The pairing check is what exposed it. This file
already says the builder counts pages 1-based and the body gate 0-based; the
same is true one level down, inside `page_lines`, and it is worth stating
because a scout is the first thing written for every new volume.

### THE GEOMETRY, and the one flag that had to be invented (`verse_indent`)

Body column 0, unit openers at indent 3-8 (mostly 4-5), display at 13 and up.
**NO page is a hanging list and NO printed line carries a 3+ space run**, so
none of `split_centre`'s machinery applies — the first Abhidhamma volume where
the edition never sets two headings on one line. Headings by form on 29Abhi01's
evidence: 192 distinct display lines, NONE longer than six words, 127 with no
terminal stop and 65 with one.

**BUT `no_verse` COULD NOT BE CARRIED OVER, AND WITHOUT IT THE BUILD DREW 45
GĀTHĀ WHERE THE EDITION PRINTS THREE.** The Vibhaṅga sets its enumerations one
item per printed line — "Duvidhena vedanākkhandho–atthi sahetuko, atthi
ahetuko." / "Tividhena vedanākkhandho–…" — which is a run of candidates sharing
an indent, a gāthā's own shape. 29Abhi01 met exactly this and answered it with
`no_verse`; that is not available here, because this volume DOES print gāthā.
And `display_prose`'s pāda test cannot see it either: every item is a complete
sentence ending in a full stop.

**MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN.** Over the whole volume the verse runs fall at indents
**4-7 (42 of them, every one a prose list) and 10-14 (three, every one a gāthā
checked against the printed page)** — with NOTHING at 8 or 9. `verse_indent: 8`
is the size of that gap: a run, or a numbered unit's pādas, counts as verse only
at `body + 8` or beyond. Per volume; the 55-map regression does not move.

The three gāthā, all confirmed against the page: printed p439 (4 pādas, indent
14), p453 (2 pādas, indent 13), and **p441, which is a NUMBERED UNIT that is a
gāthā** — "1029. Ukkhittā puññatejena, kāmarūpagatiṁgatā." with its remaining
seven pādas at indent 10. So `units_may_be_verse: True` is needed too, and it is
safe here ONLY because `verse_indent` stops it reading a unit followed by a
prose LIST as verse. Result: 2 gāthā blocks + 1 verse unit, zero one-line blocks.

### ERRATUM — the edition's own, PRESERVED VERBATIM

Printed p453 closes the last of the eighteen vibhaṅgas **"Dhammahadayavibhaṅgo
niṭṭhoto."** where the other seventeen all read *niṭṭhito* — 'o' for 'i'. It
needed no `headfix` (the colophon test recognises it by its section name and
terminal stop), so the `ERRATA` entry exists only so that a later change cannot
silently correct it.

**Its mātikā is a REAL ORDERED LIST of the body's own headings** — three levels
deep, vibhaṅga -> bhājanīya -> section — so `matika_gate` is TRUE here, which it
cannot be anywhere in the Paṭṭhāna (an abbreviating index). Second volume in the
piṭaka to earn the hard gate.

Levels are the edition's own sets: a vibhaṅga divides into bhājanīyas and a
Pañhāpucchaka (fourteen do), or into a mātikā and a niddesa per numerical group
(the Ñāṇa and Khuddakavatthu vibhaṅgas), or into ten vāras (the Dhammahadaya).
**THE NUMBERING IS NOT UNIFORM AND MUST NOT BE NORMALISED**: the Indriyavibhaṅga
prints no Suttantabhājanīya, so its two divisions are numbered "1.
Abhidhammabhājanīya" and "2. Pañhāpucchaka" — a pattern reads both, a literal
list would not.

**FOUR MĀTIKĀ ENTRIES NEEDED `errata`, and the check is what found them.** The
Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅga's Abhidhammabhājanīya prints the four catukkas TWICE —
its own mātikā (1-4) and the niddesa (5-8), the body numbering them continuously
1..8 — and the printed mātikā disambiguates the second run by adding
"(niddesa)". The body heads them with the bare names. Listed rather than handled
by stripping parentheses generally, which would let a genuinely missing heading
through.

### TWO ASSERTIONS OF MINE WERE WRONG BEFORE THE VOLUME WAS

Worth recording because both looked like defects in the build:

  * `Pañhāpucchaka` occurs **fourteen** times, not twelve — twelve numbered "3."
    and two numbered "2." in the vibhaṅgas that print no Suttantabhājanīya.
  * the sixth vibhaṅga's colophon is **"Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅgo1 niṭṭhito."** —
    the edition ABUTS A FOOTNOTE MARKER to the word it marks, so a regex without
    `\d?` reads 17 vibhaṅga colophons and looks like a dropped one.

### !!! AND THE BODY SWEEP'S CACHE WAS EXISTENCE-ONLY TOO — worse, its docstring said otherwise

`verify_all_volumes.py` says in its own header that it "only re-checks volumes
whose cache entry is missing or older than the volume's own data". **It did no
mtime comparison at all.** Found the plain way: 30Abhi02 was rebuilt, the sweep
re-run, and the report still showed its pre-rebuild 1/2/4 — because the CORPUS
file had not changed, only the SIDE-MAPS, which is how every rebuild in this
project works. So the standing advice in START HERE ("pass a fresh `--cache DIR`
whenever a volume's data has moved") was not a precaution, it was the only thing
holding the sweep together.

Now an entry is stale if any input the render depends on is newer than it: the
corpus file, all six side-maps (`verse`, `sections`, `uddana`, `hide`,
`incipit`, `booktitle`), the PDF, and either harness. Backup
`pipeline/verify_all_volumes.py.precache`. **Editing the sweep itself
invalidates every entry, which is correct and costs six budgeted runs.**

### !!! `verify_apparatus.py --all` HAD NO CACHE INVALIDATION AT ALL

This file records the `verify_all_volumes.py` stale-cache trap twice. The
apparatus sweep had the same trap in a worse form:

  * the cache path was **hardcoded** to `/tmp/osbct/appcache` with no `--cache`;
  * an entry was reused **if the file merely EXISTED** — no mtime comparison,
    where the body sweep at least re-checks a volume whose data is newer.

`/tmp/osbct/appcache` was found holding **118 entries from an earlier session**,
so `--all` would have rewritten the report from those in under a second and
reported the four stale fixes as still outstanding. (This file says
`/tmp/osbct/...` is not writable on the device; it is — that note is wrong, and
the directory being writable is exactly why the stale cache was there.)

Fixed: `--cache DIR` for parity with the body sweep, defaulting to
`_appcache/` inside the repo, and an entry is STALE if any of that volume's own
inputs is newer than it — its corpus file, `apparatus/`, `xrefs/`, `uddana/`,
its PDF, or either harness. Backup `pipeline/verify_apparatus.py.precache`.

### What the fresh apparatus numbers say, and what they do NOT

The improvement is the accumulated effect of three fixes made for single volumes
— the measured per-volume page offset, the multi-witness variant parser, and the
two marker forms — never before measured across the corpus. **But the REPORT

## NETTI + PEṬAKOPADESA — 27Khu10's VERSE/PROSE DEFECT FIXED, AND TWO MORE FOUND WITH IT (2026-07-26w)

    units drawn as verse   66 of 271  ->  20
    frame prose as verse   23 lines   ->   2   (both named below)
    gāthā blocks           280        -> 305   (quotations no longer merged)
    one-line gāthā blocks  ?          ->   0
    body        verify_render_vs_pdf.py 27Khu10 6 346 0 271 {4,2,1} -> 0/0/0/0
    apparatus   verify_apparatus.py 27Khu10 -> 4 spliced / 0 / 0, UNCHANGED
                (the same four at ord270, same recorded structural cause)
    presentation check_layout.js 27Khu10 -> ok, 271 ¶, incipit x2
                _nettiverify.js 42/42 (37 + 5 NEW on this classification)
    regression  55/55 byte-identical after each edit; baseline re-taken after
    unchanged   `sections`, `uddana`, `hide` and `incipit` are byte-identical
                to what shipped, so the nav, the mātikā check and the apparatus
                anchors cannot have moved.  ONLY `verse/27Khu10.json` changed.

### The discriminator is the BOOK'S OWN IDIOM, because the geometry has none

The reason this waited three entries is that the printed page does not separate
the two cases at all. p15's genuine verse unit and p203's prose unit are set
identically — number at indent 4, the lines below at a greater indent — and
neither carries the citation dash that decided 28Khu11. Measured here: `'hanging'`
test (b) is not merely unhelpful but WRONG on this volume, because unit 95's
genuine gāthā is followed by "Idaṁ vāsanābhāgiyaṁ suttaṁ." at indent 20 — a
candidate at a still greater indent — so (b) would call it prose.

What does decide it is that **the Netti and the Peṭakopadesa are CATECHETICAL**:
they ask a question and answer it with a quotation. Four printed formulae, and
they are the whole of it:

    Tattha katam…   43   (Tattha katamo / katamā / katamaṁ / katamāni X.)
    Tatthimāni       1   "Tatthimāni suttāni."
    Tatridaṁ         1   "Tatridaṁ niyyānaṁ–"  (also caught by the dash test)
    Manopubbaṅgamā   1   "Manopubbaṅgamā dhammāti gāthā."

46 of the 66, and **the other 20 were checked against the page one at a time** —
every one is a gāthā whose FIRST PĀDA carries the unit number (`14. Sabbo samādhi
ñāṇamūlako…`, `44. “Ye keci sokā paridevitā vā,`). `units_may_be_verse:
'formula'` applies the dash test and not the hanging test; `prose_openers` names
the four. **A NAMED FORMULA, NOT A WIDENED RULE**: any rule loose enough to catch
the 46 also catches the 20.

Two of the 46 were worse than a misdrawn verse: "Tatridaṁ niyyānaṁ–" and
"32. Tattha katamaṁ suttādhiṭṭhānaṁ." are followed by PROSE, not verse at all —
a printed list and a run of compounds — so those were prose drawn as italic
verse throughout.

### ...and fixing it exposed the same formula printed WITHOUT a number

The same opener occurs unnumbered wherever the answer to the previous question
runs on — "Tattha katamā jarā.", "Tattha katamaṁ neyyaṁ.",
"Tattha katamaṁ lobhādhiṭṭhānaṁ." — and two of them side by side make a run of
two, which the verse-run rule reads as a gāthā. Three blocks opened with one.
`prose_openers` now applies to unnumbered display candidates too.

### A WHOLE PAGE AS ONE ITALIC BLOCK — nine pages of it (`display_centre`)

A page with no body column at all is read as ENTIRELY DISPLAY, and on such a
page `run` is forced true, so every line becomes a verse line. **27Khu10 has
nine such pages, and on them the edition frames each quoted gāthā with its own
centred prose** — "Tattha katamo assādo–" above, "Ayaṁ assādo." below. Printed
p6 was arriving as a SINGLE 24-line italic block holding six quotations and
their twelve frame lines. 0/0/0/0 from the body gate: every word present,
contiguous, in order.

**MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN.** Over those nine pages the indents fall in two clusters
— **6-15 (196 pāda lines) and 19-35 (34 frame lines), with NOTHING at 16, 17 or
18**. So the split is the page's own largest gap and the rule refuses to fire
unless there is one (gap >= 4 and the upper band at 18 or more).

!!! **THE SAME BAND DOES NOT EXIST ON AN ORDINARY PAGE, and that was measured
too.** Over the whole volume the display indents run 5..36 CONTINUOUSLY, with
genuine pādas at 21 and frame prose at 19 — they interleave. So no global
threshold is available and none was invented; on ordinary pages the frame lines
are separated by the run rule and the formula instead.

### A prose quotation drawn as verse, and a sharper pāda test

`display_prose` is now ON for this volume — the comment where that flag was
written predicted it would be needed here, and it is: printed p41 sets a PROSE
quotation ("Ayuñjantānaṁ vā sattānaṁ yoge…" running on into "So pamādo /
duvidho taṇhāmūlako…") with exactly a gāthā's geometry.

The test itself is sharper by one line: it checked every line but the LAST for
pāda punctuation, and a gāthā's final pāda ends in a full stop while a prose
quotation's last line runs on into the paragraph below — which is the clearest
tell of the two. **Measured over the eleven regression volumes, requiring the
last line as well moves NOTHING except 27Khu10** — 28Khu11, the volume the flag
was written for, is byte-identical. That is the only change here that is not
gated per volume, and that is why.

### The quotation's own first line hangs LEFT of its pādas (`hanging_quote`)

Once the question is prose, the quotation it introduces is printed

    26. Tattha katamo adhippāyo.                   (indent 4)
     + “Dhammo have rakkhati dhammacāriṁ,          (indent 5)
         Chattaṁ mahantaṁ yatha vassakāle.         (indent 9)

so the marker line is a run of ONE and would be drawn as a prose paragraph with
the rest of the gāthā as a separate block below it — the same split, one line
further down. **What marks it is the edition's own apparatus**: the citation
marker (`*`, `**`, `+`) and/or the opening quote are set to the LEFT of the
pādas, which is WHY the line hangs. Requiring that keeps an ordinary one-line
prose paragraph out of the gāthā below it — p176 sets "Aṭṭhimā Ānanda
dānupapattiyo ekuttarike suttaṁ, ayaṁ jāti." immediately above one, and it is
prose. The following run may be a single pāda: the edition sets plenty of
two-pāda quotations and both of ord54's and ord158's are that shape. The hanging
line and its pādas are ONE run, so the pāda test sees the whole quotation.
**Result: zero one-line gāthā blocks in the volume.**

### KNOWN, NAMED, NOT GUESSED — the two frame lines that remain

  * **ord116** — one "Idaṁ saṁkilesabhāgiyaṁ suttaṁ." sits inside a gāthā block
    at the pādas' own indent, so neither the band nor the run rule separates it.
  * **ord121** — the block `["Dānakathā sīlakathā saggakathā puññakathā
    puññavipākakathā”ti.", "Idaṁ vāsanābhāgiyaṁ suttaṁ."]` is prose plus its
    frame; both lines end in a full stop, so the pāda test cannot see it.

And one that is the EDITION'S OWN and should not be touched: **ord138** sets a
pāda and its frame on ONE printed line — "Raṭṭhaṁ sānucaraṁ hantvā”ti. . Idaṁ
dhammādhiṭṭhānaṁ." — so the block is genuinely mixed on the page. Separating it
would be an editorial act, not a repair.
`_nettiverify.js` asserts the NUMBER (2), which is the only honest form for a
residue: if it moves in either direction, read this entry.

### `pipeline/regress.py` — the regression now lives IN THE REPO

It was `/tmp/mp/regress.py` with the session directory hardcoded as `ROOT`, so
the check this file calls essential was one `rm -rf` from being lost and would
have failed with a path error in any later session before that. Moved to
`pipeline/regress.py`; `ROOT` derives from the file's own location and the
snapshots live in `_regress/` inside the repo. **`python3 pipeline/regress.py
baseline` then `check`, still ~3 seconds.** Update the START HERE reference when
next editing it.

**THE PAṬṬHĀNA IS COMPLETE: all five bhāgas, 36Abhi08-40Abhi12, on all three
gates with their nav trees built and every row clicked.**

### The crossed book, and why `split_centre` was left alone

The open question was how to separate the two levels of a CROSSED book —
Tikatika crosses a tika with a tika, Dukaduka a duka with a duka — when a `re:`
pattern for the top level necessarily matches both. The distinction the edition
prints is POSITIONAL:

    printed p1        1. Kusalattika   1. Vedanāttika
                 1. Sukhāyavedanāyasampayuttapada    1-7. Paṭiccādivāra
                          Paccayacatukka-hetu

**THE RULE THE PAGE STATES IS GENERAL AND IT WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: ON A
TWO-HEADING LINE THE LEFT HALF STANDS ONE LEVEL ABOVE THE RIGHT.** It holds for
the crossed pair (outer tika | inner tika), for the pure books (tika | vāra),
for Dukatika (duka | tika) and for the pada | vāra pairs — every one of the
volume's 696 pair-lines.

The handoff's suggested fix was to have `split_centre` mark which half a
heading came from. **That was not done, and should not be**: `split_centre`
feeds every volume's `sections/` and `uddana/` files, so marking it changes the
heading stream the whole corpus reads and would need the 55-map regression to
carry a data change rather than prove there is none. The same evidence is free
downstream — `build_abhidhamma_nav.py` already reads the PDF — so the pair-lines
are read there and aligned against the heads stream.

**THE ALIGNMENT IS STRICT LOCKSTEP, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT A CHECK.** The next
printed pair-line must be the next same-ordinal adjacent pair in the stream;
a forward search would always find something. Over the volume's declared text
extent: **696 printed pair-lines, 696 aligned, none left over** — two readings
of the same edition agreeing entirely. The builder REFUSES and names the page if
one cannot be found. `pairsides` is per volume: it is ON for 40Abhi12 only,
because it WOULD move 36Abhi08, whose page sets "Pucchāvāra  1. Paccayānuloma"
on one line while that volume's measured level table puts Ekamūlaka between the
two — and 36Abhi08 is shipped and gated. 29Abhi01, 36Abhi08, 37Abhi09 and
38Abhi10 rebuild **byte-identical** through all of this session's changes.

Adjacency ALONE is not enough and the measurement says so: 40Abhi12's first
book has 90 same-ordinal adjacent head pairs and only 44 printed pair-lines.
Reading the page is not optional here.

### !!! 39Abhi11 SHIPPED WITH DUPLICATED TOP NODES — 22 and 52 of them

Where the top level is an open (`re:`) set, `subtree` tested the pattern BEFORE
the ancestor-reprint rule. The Paṭṭhāna reprints the outer section's name at the
head of every inner one, so each reprint opened a NEW top:

    Dukatikapaṭṭhānapāḷi   "1. Hetuduka" x22, "100. Saraṇaduka" x22
    Tikadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi   "1. Kusalattika" x52, 19 labels repeated in all

The sidebar showed "1. Hetuduka" twenty-two times. **NOTHING COULD SEE IT.**
The body and apparatus gates do not read `nav.json`; `_navdup.js`'s three tests
are all about BOOK nodes; and `_abhi11verify.js`'s row sweep passed 2061/2061
because a duplicated row still opens text. Found here only because the fix for
40Abhi12 forced a reading of what the pattern branch does with a reprint.

Corrected: **the reprint test runs before the top test wherever the top level is
a pattern.** Dukatika 129 tops -> 87 with "1. Hetuduka" now carrying its 22
crossed tikas as children; Tikaduka 94 -> 44. 2058 nav keys -> 1966.

**44 IS RIGHT AND 22 WOULD BE WRONG, which is worth stating because it looks
like a remaining duplicate.** The Tikaduka book makes THREE passes — all 22
tikas crossed with the first duka, then the first tika with all the remaining
dukas, then all 22 tikas with the last duka — so 22 of its top labels occur
twice. Those passes are NOT CONTIGUOUS, and a nav node's span is one contiguous
slice, so each pass needs its own node. What must never happen is two ADJACENT
siblings sharing a label, and that is now asserted over the whole nav.

### ASSERTED: `_navdup.js` gained the rule that would have caught it

**No two adjacent siblings anywhere in any tree may share a label** — 10,972
tree rows checked, clean. Two adjacent repeats are the EDITION'S OWN and are
named rather than admitted by loosening the rule: 25Khu08's two bare
"Pārāyanavagga" (the vagga's text, then its niddesa) and 39Abhi11's
"Paccayacatukka-hetu" printed for the Paṭiccādivāra block and again for the
Pañhāvāra block with no heading between, which `check_layout.js`'s
duplicate-heading rule already records as the edition's.

### 40Abhi12 has NO SECTION MĀTIKĀ — and its ONE mātikā page checks the books

Its four pages of front matter are the cover, the imprint, the Pāḷi alphabet
table and a single mātikā page, and that page lists the TWENTY BOOKS grouped
under their four nayas with the printed pages each occupies, and nothing below
them. So:

  * the entry-level mātikā check has nothing to run on and says so rather than
    reporting 1,262 body headings as unlisted;
  * a new **book-level** check reads that page and requires the tree's twenty
    book nodes to match it entry for entry, in order — 20/20;
  * and it compares every book's PRINTED PAGE RANGE against the SPEC's. **That
    check earned its keep immediately: it caught a typo of mine** (I recorded
    Dhammapaccanīyānuloma Tikatika as 403-424 where the page prints 403-423).
    Printed page 1 is 0-based pdf page 4 throughout, and the only divergences
    are blank leaves absorbed at a book's end (pdf 66, between books 2 and 3).

A THIRD printed witness to the same division: seven of the twenty books are
closed by a colophon naming both naya and paṭṭhāna ("Dhammānulome
Tikatikapaṭṭhānaṁ niṭṭhitaṁ."), and each falls inside the ordinals of the book
it names. The test runs FROM the colophons the edition prints, never demanding
one it does not.

### The level tables, and a SANDHI trap that cost a tree

The twenty books are the same six shapes four times over, so the level tables
are written once (`_SHAPE` in the nav builder) — but every book's tree is
printed by the build and was read. A gocchaka is a NAMED GROUP OF DUKAS and the
edition sets it at the duka's own level, abbreviating a run
("20-54. Saññojanādichagocchaka"), so the duka pattern admits it.

**"Vipākattika" + "ādi" is printed "Vipākattikādi", not "Vipākattika-ādi."** A
pattern ending `tika(ādi)?` therefore does not match it, and the heading fell
through the level table and was nested UNDER ITS OWN SIBLING — visible only in
the printed tree, since the row still opened text. The stems now end `tik`/`duk`
and the vowel belongs to the suffix.

## THE PDFs AND THE READER ARE NOT THE SAME DELIVERABLE (2026-07-26u)

Asked whether the site could be uploaded to Cloudflare. The answer turns on a
distinction worth stating once, because it decides what can ship when.

**THE PDFs DEPEND ONLY ON THE `/ToUnicode` INJECTION, AND THAT IS CLEAN.** A
character census over the full text of six volumes spanning all three layers
(01Vin01, 12Sam01, 36Abhi08, 01VinA01, 14SamA01, 01ViT01 — 4.6 million
characters) puts EVERY character outside the Pāḷi alphabet on **0-based page 2**,
the PĀḶI ALPHABET table that §3 says is Burmese script in the same font and must
not be converted, plus `¥`/`©` on the cover and imprint. From page 3 to the end
the only non-alphabet characters are ordinary punctuation and `‘`. So the
injection holds over the body, and the PDFs are a FINISHED deliverable that owes
nothing to the corpus work. **Sampled, not exhaustive — run the same census over
all 118 before publishing.**

**THE READER DEPENDS ON THE CORPUS AND SIDE-MAPS, AND THOSE ARE 16 OF 118.**
24 canon volumes are still raw corpus (the three Majjhima are ~500 missing lines
EACH) and all 52 commentary + 26 subcommentary volumes have never been rebuilt.
Publishing the reader as finished would put 102 volumes of unverified text in
front of readers with nothing to tell them apart — which working principle 4
(attribute provenance; the reader must be able to tell) forbids.

**Recommendation was: ship the PDFs, hold the reader.** **DECIDED OTHERWISE —
NOTHING IS PUBLISHED UNTIL EVERYTHING IS READY (user, 2026-07-26).** A
`publish/` folder was started and removed; no deployment has been made and none
should be until the corpus work is finished. The deployment facts below stand
and are worth keeping — they are what a future deploy has to get right, and two
of them are traps rather than preferences.

### Deployment facts, measured

  * `site/` is the deployable root; the PDFs are NOT in it — `downloads.html`
    serves them from R2 (`pub-825764a1…r2.dev`, custom domain
    `files.buddha-dhamma.net` noted in the file).
  * **FIVE OF SIX PAGES LINK TO THE WRONG READER.** `about`, `downloads`,
    `errata`, `search` and `demo-links` all point at `reader/reader.html` — the
    23 July file, 25 KB, carrying NONE of `uddanaHTML`, `VAGGASPAN`, `proseOne`
    or the incipit fallback. Only `index.html` points at `reader2.html`, which
    is the 76 KB reader every gate in this project has been run against. Settle
    this before any upload: repoint the five, or rename reader2 -> reader and
    fix the one link in `index.html`.
  * 420 MB / 1319 files, of which **40 MB / 180 files are backups**
    (`nav.json.bak*`, `*.pre19build`, `reader2.html.bakpn`) that should not
    ship. Excluding them: 352 MB / 1139 files.
  * `site/index/` is 191 MB of that — the search index, `terms.compact.json`
    alone 17 MB. Under Cloudflare Pages' limits (20,000 files, 25 MB/file) but
    it is most of the payload.
  * External dependency: Gentium Plus and Inter from `fonts.googleapis.com`.

## THE DOWNLOADS PAGE NAMED EVERY VOLUME AFTER ITS COMMENTARY GROUP — USER-REPORTED (2026-07-26t)

The user saw five consecutive rows reading **"Vinaya — Samantapāsādikā +
subcommentaries"** where they should read Pārājikapāḷi, Pācittiyapāḷi,
Mahāvaggapāḷi, Cūḷavaggapāḷi, Parivārapāḷi.

**It was not the PDFs.** Their `/Title` and XMP `dc:title` both carry correct
per-volume names (`Parajikapali`, `Saratthadipanitika_01`, ASCII, no
diacritics). The label came from `site/downloads.data.json`, whose `work` field
held the CONCORDANCE GROUP — the canon→commentary→subcommentary relation, which
is MANY-TO-MANY (§5 of the project instructions says so plainly), so all five
Vinaya volumes, all their aṭṭhakathā and all their ṭīkā shared one string. 118
of 118 rows were labelled this way.

**Fixed at the source: every label is now read off that volume's own printed
COVER PAGE.** One rule covers all three layers — take the block above the first
rule, drop the `(… bhāgo)` parenthetical, prefer the CAPITALISED lines (the
edition sets the work's own name in caps and the locator/author lines in title
case), fall back to the last line otherwise, then normalise per WORD so a cover
naming several books keeps them all:

    18Khu01   Khuddakapāṭha Dhammapada Udāna Itivuttaka Suttanipātapāḷi
    31Abhi03  Dhātukathā Puggalapaññattipāḷi
    01VinA01  Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā (Paṭhamo bhāgo)
    01ViT01   Sāratthadīpanīṭīkā (Paṭhamo bhāgo)

Split on spaces only, never on hyphens — "PĀRĀJIKAKAṆḌA-AṬṬHAKATHĀ" is ONE name
and must come out "Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā".

The old value is preserved as a new `group` field, so the concordance
relationship is not lost and the page can show it again if wanted.
`downloads.html` needed no change — it renders `it.work`. Backup
`site/downloads.data.json.bakwork`. Rendered under jsdom: 118 rows, and the
only repeated label is **Mahāvaggapāḷi x2**, which is the EDITION — the Vinaya's
(03Vin03) and the Dīgha's (07Di02) genuinely share a name, and the code column
tells them apart.

### !!! A LEGACY GLYPH THE §3 MAPPING TABLE DOES NOT LIST: `¥` = Ṁ

The cover pages are still set in the legacy font, and four titles came out as
`SA¥YUTTAṬṬHAKATHĀ`, `MAHĀVAGGASA¥YUTTAPĀḶI`, `BUDDHAVA¥SAṬṬHAKATHĀ`. **U+00A5
`¥` is uppercase Ṁ** — the capital of the `ṁ` the table gives as `Ñ`.

This is exactly the check §3 of the project instructions asks for, so it was run
as a census rather than patched one title at a time: **over all 118 cover pages
the only characters outside the Pāḷi alphabet and ordinary punctuation are `¥`
(8 occurrences, in 12Sam01, 13Sam02, 14Sam03, 21Khu04, 34KhuA15, 14SamA01,
15SamA02, 16SamA03) and a legitimate pair of curly quotes in 06VinSg06.**
Nothing else is unmapped on any cover.

**The §3 table in the project instructions should gain this row** — `¥` -> Ṁ.
It has not been added there; recorded here so it is not lost. Whether the body
text of any volume also carries `¥` has NOT been checked — the census above
covered cover pages only.

for every naya x paṭṭhāna pair; this volume carries the last two of the
Dhammānuloma (Tikatika, Dukaduka) and all six of each of Dhammapaccanīya,
Dhammānulomapaccanīya and Dhammapaccanīyānuloma. All twenty pair 1:1.

**THE CORPUS `book` FIELD IS WRONG HERE** and cannot be used for the
boundaries: it labels pdf 174 — still inside Dhammapaccanīya Dukaduka — as
Dhammānulomapaccanīya Tika. The boundaries were taken from the edition
instead: the twenty pages carrying a HOMAGE, cross-checked by finding each
book's first printed unit in the corpus BY CONTENT, then walked back over the
leaked headings that precede it (a book's own section headings belong to that
book). Page boundaries from the homage pages, ordinal boundaries from the
content match — two independent readings that agree.

**ERRATUM, preserved:** the title page at 0-based 176 reads
**"Abhidhammapiṭika"** for Abhidhammapiṭaka. It is in `booktitle/40Abhi12.json`
verbatim.

### `split_literals`: a heading pair whose second half has no full stop

    printed p48   "1. Hetuduka    19-53 Saññojanādiduka"

A census over the volume's text extent finds exactly one. Making the stop
optional in the general rule would split ordinary unit text at its first
internal number; naming the line does not.

### The title map held 9 stacks for 20 books — derived from the printed pages

`build_booktitles.py` found nine of the twenty title pages, so eleven books
would have rendered with no title at all — and the builder's re-key step,
which refuses to guess, correctly reported rather than invented:

    BOOKTITLE NOT re-keyed: 9 entries for 20 book(s), and at least one sits on
    a hidden ordinal — REPORTED, not guessed

The edition states each stack plainly, so the missing ones are now READ OFF THE
PAGE: the centred lines above the rule on that book's first page, homage
removed, refusing if a page does not open with a stack of 2-4 lines. All twenty
derived and printed line by line in the build output — including the
"Abhidhammapiṭika" misprint, which is what proves they come from the page and
not from a table.

### Still open on this volume: the NAV

`build_abhidhamma_nav.py`'s `books` mechanism (added for 39Abhi11) takes a
`re:` PATTERN for an open top level, and that is not enough here. **A CROSSED
book puts two of the same kind on top of each other** — Tikatika crosses a tika
with a tika, Dukaduka a duka with a duka — so the same pattern matches BOTH
levels and every second-level head would open a new top, flattening the tree.
The printed pair "1. Kusalattika   1. Vedanāttika" carries the distinction only
in its POSITION on the line, which `split_centre` already knows and then
discards.

The fix is probably to have `split_centre` mark which half a heading came from
(first or second) and let a level match on that, but it is a change to the
heading stream that every volume reads, so it needs measuring first. **Do not
guess at it.** Everything else on 40Abhi12 is done and gated.

### Leaked headings recognised AGAINST THE PRINTED STREAM

Books 2 and 3 came in 36 and 52 units short. The cause is a leak shape the stem
test cannot see: the extraction joined TWO CONSECUTIVE centred lines into one
paragraph with a single space —

    1-7. Paṭiccādivāra          (printed on its own line)
    Paccayacatukka-hetu         (printed on the next)
    -> corpus "1-7. Paṭiccādivāra Paccayacatukka-hetu"

— and the result ends in "hetu", which is no heading stem, so **88** of them
stayed visible and took 88 units' ordinals. There is no need to guess at it:
the book's own printed heading stream is already in hand, so a paragraph that
reproduces a RUN OF CONSECUTIVE PRINTED HEADINGS is those headings. Matched as
a run of up to three, exactly as the nav's mātikā matcher handles the edition's
compounded entries. After it, all three books paired 1:1 first try.

`split_unnumbered` also learned the range form `1-7.` (it already knew `\d+\.`),
which the Tikaduka book needs for "Nahetupada    1-7. Paṭiccādivāra".

### A line-end hyphen is never a paragraph boundary

Printed p76 sets a parenthetical whose EVERY line is indented, so each read as
a new paragraph — including "…dassanenapahātabbahetukaduka-" and its
continuation "sadisā." — and the compound came out as two words in two blocks.
The hyphen settles it, and it is the same rule the body gate already applies
before comparing.

### `check_layout.js`'s duplicate-heading rule was comparing the wrong thing

It compared successive `.head` elements and ignored the body between them, so
it reported the edition's own repetition: p357-358 sets "Paccayacatukka-hetu"
for the Paṭiccādivāra block and again for the Pañhāvāra block, several
paragraphs apart, with no heading between because a parenthetical carries the
Pañhāvāra. The artifact it exists to catch is two heads with NOTHING between,
and that is what it tests now. Re-run over all 118 volumes: only the known
pre-existing 02Vin02 finding remains. Backup `check_layout.js.predup`.

### A book's title page belongs above THAT BOOK's first paragraph

`build_booktitles.py` keys the stack by a page estimate, and on a multi-book
volume the estimate lands in the WRONG BOOK: 39Abhi11's second title page was
keyed to ord654 — six paragraphs before the book it heads begins, and itself a
hidden leaked heading, so the stack never rendered at all. Now aligned per book
to that book's first VISIBLE ordinal, reported on every move, and it refuses
unless there is exactly one entry per book:

    BOOKTITLE re-keyed: ord655 -> ord660 (that book's first visible paragraph)
    BOOKTITLE re-keyed: ord2265 -> ord2268 (that book's first visible paragraph)

(The first version of this loop abandoned the whole map at the first key that
was NOT hidden, so a volume with three title pages kept none of the re-keys.)

### The nav builder now takes several books, and a PATTERN top level

`build_abhidhamma_nav.py` gained a `books` key — one subtree per inner book,
each with its own tops and levels — and tops may be a `re:` pattern. Books 2
and 3 cross a duka with a tika, so their top level is an open set the edition
names one by one (111 and 77 of them); which of the two is on top is the whole
difference between the books and is read off their names. 29Abhi01, 36Abhi08,
37Abhi09 and 38Abhi10 all rebuild identically through the new code. A
multi-book volume is NOT wrapped in a further node — doing so produced a single
inner book "Dukapaṭṭhānapāḷi" spanning the whole volume, which
`_abhigroupverify.js` caught. Backup `build_abhidhamma_nav.py.prebooks`.

### THE BUILDER'S `p1` IS INCLUSIVE — and 37Abhi09 was one page over

`kat_items` runs `for pg in range(p0, p1 + 1)`, so a SPEC book of `(…, 7, 612)`
reads 1-based pages 7-612 and swallowed the first INDEX page: six of the eight
`render-not-in-PDF` findings were the volume's own word index rendered as body.
Correct is `(…, 7, 611)`, gated `6 610`.

**37Abhi09 had the same error** — SPEC `(28, 521)` for text ending at 520 — and
it did NOT show, because 0-based page 520 there is the volume's declared BLANK
page. Both SPECs are now tightened and both volumes re-gated: 37Abhi09 is
0/0/0/0 over `27 519`. The rule, worth stating once: **SPEC `p1` = the last
text page, 1-based, INCLUSIVE; the body gate's `p1` = that minus one.**

### A printed unit the corpus does not hold at all (`kat_missing`)

Printed unit 1 — "1. Hetuṁ dhammaṁ paṭicca hetu dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā.
Alobhaṁ paṭicca adoso amoho…" — is **in no corpus paragraph anywhere in the
volume**; the corpus opens at unit 2. This is a different defect from
36Abhi08's splice, where the text was present but merged, and the two are told
apart by mirrored checks: **a splice requires the text to be PRESENT in the
declared host, an absence requires it to be present NOWHERE**, and both must
match exactly one printed unit at that (number, page). With unit 1 dropped
every remaining unit pairs 1:1 with **zero `n` mismatches**, which is the
evidence that this is the whole divergence.

It is not lost from the page: the kathā path draws the body from the PRINTED
stream, so the unit is emitted into the FOLLOWING unit's `before` — which
`block()` draws above that paragraph, i.e. where the edition prints it — as a
numbered prose block carrying its own number. `_abhi10verify.js` asserts it
renders above unit 2.

### Three more leaked-heading shapes, all found by counting

  * **`split_literals` again** — one heading pair set with no space after the
    second number: "1. Paccayānuloma      1.Vibhaṅgavāra" (printed p87). A
    census over the volume's text extent finds exactly one; 36Abhi08 and
    37Abhi09 have none.
  * **`split_centre` now accepts the RANGE form** `\d+(?:-\d+)?\.` that the
    rest of the file already uses (HEADNUM does). "27. Ganthaniyaduka
    1-7. Vārasattaka" was left joined by the narrower pattern.
  * **`_starts_double_head`** — a corpus paragraph that BEGINS with two centred
    headings and RUNS ON into the material printed under them. A census finds
    exactly three in the whole Paṭṭhāna (38Abhi10 ord640 and ord1170,
    40Abhi12 ord190) and none elsewhere in the Abhidhamma. Left visible each
    takes a unit's ordinal AND carries the heading's number, desyncing the
    pairing to the end of the book.

And one erratum: **the edition misspells "Saṅkhyāvāra" as "Saṅkhyāvara"** (short
a) on printed p159. Named in `headfix` and preserved verbatim — no stem list
should be widened to admit it.

### The `head_order` split was filtering BY VALUE, and dropped a heading

`check_layout.js` reported `duplicate-heading :: 50. Parāmāsaduka`. Printed
p341 sets "50. Parāmāsaduka  5. Saṁsaṭṭhavāra", prose, then "50. Parāmāsaduka
7. Pañhāvāra". The trailing head-run was recovered with
`[h for h in pend_heads if h['l'] in keep]` — a VALUE test, so a label
occurring on both sides of the split was kept twice and "5. Saṁsaṭṭhavāra" was
dropped from the page entirely. Now positional: the run is the last *n* entries
of `pend_heads`. **No content gate could see this** — the heading is still
printed elsewhere and nothing is spliced. `_abhi10verify.js` now asserts no
ordinal carries the same heading twice.

### The homage is capitalised in two volumes

`HOMAGE` required "Namo tassa"; 38Abhi10 prints **"Namo Tassa"**. Unrecognised,
the line was never lifted into `incipit`, so it stayed in the body AND the
reader drew its built-in fallback above it — the homage twice on the page. A
census over the Khuddaka and Abhidhamma finds the capital form in exactly two
volumes: **38Abhi10** (its only homage) and **31Abhi03** (one of its two, not
yet built). Matched either way now; the incipit keeps the printed capital.

### The gate learned to name a PDF reading-order artifact

Seven rendered paragraphs came back `render-not-in-PDF` and one chunk missing,
and all eight are the FILE's fault. This gate reads the PDF in content-stream
order (`pdftotext` with no `-layout`), which is the right model of reading
order almost everywhere; on this volume the stream puts a short continuation
line BEFORE the line it continues — printed p319 reads "…vipāke ekaṁ -pa-
avigate / dve." and the stream emits "dve." first. `-layout` reconstructs by
POSITION and has all eight contiguous.

So `verify()` now consults the `-layout` reading of the same pages and reports
those separately as **PDF-reading-order**, in both directions: a rendered part
contiguous there but not in the stream, and a chunk the stream MANUFACTURES by
joining two lines the page does not. Agreeing with `-layout` is not circular —
the disagreement is between two readings of the same PDF, and the one that
reflects the printed page wins. **It can only RECLASSIFY an existing failure,
never create one**, so no clean volume can move; re-run over 36Abhi08,
37Abhi09, 29Abhi01, 19Khu02 and 22Khu05 to confirm, and the 118-volume sweep
after. Backup `verify_render_vs_pdf.py.preorder`.

`split_centre` wants three or more spaces, so each line stayed whole and —

**PAGE ARGUMENTS: the builder counts pages 1-BASED, the body gate 0-BASED.**
`SPEC['36Abhi08']['books']` is `(…, 30, 493, …)` and the gate for the same
extent is `29 492`. Run with `30 493` and the gate reads the four-page index in
and the volume's first two units out, and reports 9 missing lines and 2
render-not-in-PDF that are pure argument error. The declared extent settles it:
`Subject: [497 pages = content 29 + text 464 + index 4]`, so text is 1-based
30-493 and the index 494-497. Every earlier volume was run the same way
(29Abhi01 SPEC 20/317, gate `19 316`) — worth stating once because it costs an
hour to rediscover.

### The corpus splices two printed units into one paragraph (`kat_splices`)

Pairing came in at printed **1001** vs corpus **1000**. The whole divergence is
ONE paragraph. Printed p344 sets unit 41 as

    41.Nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammaṁ paṭicca

with **no space after the number**. The extraction's unit splitter wants
`NN. `, so it saw no boundary and unit 41's entire text arrived inside ord831,
the paragraph carrying n=40. **Nothing is lost** — ord831 is 1299 characters and
holds both units — and `site/*.json` is not edited. Skipping printed unit 41
gives 1000/1000 with **zero n mismatches over the whole volume**, which is the
evidence that this is the only divergence.

A census of all eighteen Abhidhamma volumes for an embedded `NN.` unit number
found **exactly two**: this one and **34Abhi06 ¶185 (unit 24)**, which is not
built yet — expect it there.

So `kat_splices` is a NAMED LIST, not a rule: a rule would swallow a genuinely
missing unit, which is the one thing this pairing exists to catch. Each entry
must satisfy three tests or the build refuses — the host paragraph carries the
declared `n`, the host text really contains the printed unit's opening words,
and the printed stream offers exactly one unit at that (number, page). The page
is part of the key because unit numbers repeat across vāras; n=41 occurs four
times in this book. The unit is not dropped from the page either: its opening
is emitted into the current unit's prose exactly as printed, number and all, so
the reader sees it begin where the edition begins it. Every build prints

    CORPUS SPLICE (recorded, not corrected): printed unit 41 at p373 is inside
    corpus ord831, the paragraph of unit 40 — 'Nevavipākanavipāka…'

### Two more wrong-role defects, both invisible to a unit count

Pairing was 1000/1000 and the body gate still read 3 missing chunks at minw 4
and 25 at minw 1. Both causes are printed ORDER, not missing text — the seventh
and eighth members of the class that has now shipped six times.

**1. `head_order` — heading, its prose, then another heading, then the unit.**
`pend_heads` and `pend_before` are two lists; the unit branch empties the first
into `sections` (drawn above the paragraph) and the second into `before` (drawn
below it). Printed p92 sets

    Tika                                    <- heading
    Ārammaṇapaccayā hetupaccayā …           <- its own text
    (Yathā hetumūlakaṁ, evaṁ gaṇetabbaṁ.)
    Adhipatiduka                            <- heading
    299. Adhipatipaccayā …                  <- the unit

and replaying the two lists put BOTH headings above BOTH paragraphs, so "Tika"
lost its own text to "Adhipatiduka". This is the same defect `pend_seq` already
fixed for 28Khu11 p115 (Ācariyaguṇa / Upāsakaguṇa) — but that repair fires only
when a COLOPHON arrives, and here no colophon comes. The repair reuses the
colophon path: everything up to the LAST RUN OF HEADINGS goes to the previous
unit's uddāna stream, which `block()` draws after that paragraph, i.e. exactly
where the page sets it; only the trailing headings stay in `sections`. When the
headings are all at the front — the ordinary shape — the split point is 0 and
nothing moves, which is why the 55-map regression does not budge.

**2. `head_order` again — prose printed BETWEEN two colophons.** Printed p110
closes the Nissayavāra as

    337. Nahetupaccayā … (Saṁkhittaṁ.)
    Nissayavāre paccanīyānulomaṁ.                     <- colophon
    (Paccayattaṁ nāma nissayattaṁ, nissayattaṁ …)     <- prose
    Nissayavāro.                                      <- colophon

`after` is drawn BEFORE the uddāna blocks that hold the colophons, so that line
jumped above both of them. Once a colophon is queued the unit is closed, so
what follows joins the same stream in printed order.

**3. `split_unnumbered` — an unnumbered head sharing its line with a numbered
one.** `split_centre` required BOTH halves to start `NN.`, so printed p9's
`Pucchāvāra    1. Paccayānuloma` and `Ekamūlaka    1. Kusalapada` each rendered
as ONE heading with a run of spaces in the middle. Gated per volume: the
numbered form is what every shipped volume was measured against.

All three flags are per-volume SPEC keys — `head_order`, `split_unnumbered` —
so no shipped volume can move, and none did.

### The one remaining chunk is the GATE's artifact, not the render's

    MISSING-CHUNK: pucchāvāra ekamūlaka        (minw 2 and 1; 0 at minw 4)

`pdf_lines` splits a two-column heading block COLUMN-MAJOR — Pucchāvāra,
Ekamūlaka, 1. Paccayānuloma, 1. Kusalapada — where the render reads it
ROW-MAJOR: Pucchāvāra, 1. Paccayānuloma, Ekamūlaka, 1. Kusalapada. **The
edition's own mātikā decides it against the gate**: p2 sets "Pucchāvāra
1. Paccayānuloma" on one line and centres "Ekamūlaka" beneath it, with the
numbered padas listed under that. So the render is right and the gate's model
of a two-column heading is what is approximate. Recorded rather than tuned
away: changing `pdf_lines` would move the instrument every shipped volume was
measured with.

### Still open on this volume

`build_abhidhamma_nav.py` gained arbitrary DEPTH (`levels`) and
ancestor-reprint suppression — the Paṭṭhāna nests four deep and prints 1477
headings, so the two-level `mids` shape would have left ~1400 of them in one
flat list under their vāra, which is precisely the sidebar the user reported.
29Abhi01 rebuilds identically through the new code (5 top / 141 sections /
mātikā 134, unchanged). 36Abhi08 now gives 8 tops — the two uddesas, the
Pucchāvāra and the five tikas — with the seven vāras under each, 1292 sections,
51 ancestor reprints skipped. **It still REFUSES on five mātikā entries and the
nav has NOT been written:**

  * `Paṭṭhānapāḷi`, `Paṭhamabhāga` — the mātikā's own title-page lines, read as
    entries. Needs a filter; the existing one only knows the book title
    `Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi`.
  * `Dukādi` — listed in the mātikā, **printed nowhere in the body** (0 hits
    over pages 30-493). An edition-level discrepancy to record, not to fix.
  * `Gaṇanā hetumūlakā`, `Na-anantara nasamanantara` — both ARE printed as
    headings (p57, p63) and both ARE in `sections/36Abhi08.json`, so the cause
    is the forward-only pointer in the mātikā matcher, not a missing heading.
    Note that `Gaṇanā hetumūlakā` is printed TWICE — p56 as a heading and p57
    with a terminal stop as a colophon.

Then: `_navdup.js`, `_abhigroupverify.js`, a per-volume jsdom row sweep, and
`verify_all_volumes.py` with a FRESH cache dir.

### The mātikā cross-check does not transfer to the Paṭṭhāna — SETTLED

Three of the five nav refusals were the instrument, not the volume:

1. **The mātikā's own running header was being read as entries.** `Paṭṭhānapāḷi
   paṭhamabhāga` heads every mātikā page and does not contain the BOOK's name
   (`Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi`), so the `fold(title)` filter never saw it. Now measured
   from the pages themselves — a line opening three or more of them is the
   header, and its individual words go too, which takes out the title page's
   own two lines. 29Abhi01 drops two phantom entries this way (134 -> 132) and
   still passes.
2. **The body names the naya, the mātikā does not:** body `Anuloma hetu`,
   `Paccanīya nahetu` where the mātikā lists plain `Hetu`, `Nahetu`. Handled as
   an alternative fold on the BODY side (`head_prefixes`), not as `errata` —
   the body also prints a bare `Hetu` elsewhere, so a global map would send the
   matcher to the wrong one.
3. **One forward-only pointer was answering two questions.** The mātikā reuses
   bare paccaya names at every one of ~40 vāra sections, so a single mismatch
   did not merely miss — the pointer landed on the NEXT section's copy and
   everything after was measured from the wrong place. That is how six entries
   were reported absent while sitting in `sections/36Abhi08.json`. Now: search
   from the pointer, then from the start; a hit behind the pointer counts as
   OUT OF ORDER and does not move the pointer; only a hit found nowhere is
   missing.

**After all three, 560 of 607 entries resolve and the remaining 47 are the
mātikā's own abbreviations, not tree defects:** `-ādi` lines standing for a run
of headings the page prints in full (`Nahetudukādi`, `Ārammaṇadukādi`, `Dukādi`,
`Gaṇanamūlaka`), two-column mātikā lines captured whole, and three
`…ghaṭanā (n)` entries the body prints under a longer name. The out-of-order
count is 459 of 607, which says nothing about the book — it is what a
repeated-name index does to any positional matcher.

**DECISION (user's, asked and answered): demote the mātikā to a REPORTED NUMBER
on this volume (`matika_gate: False`) and gate the tree on the colophons
instead.** The mātikā check earned its place on 29Abhi01, where the mātikā is a
plain ordered list of the body's own headings; the Paṭṭhāna's is an
abbreviating index, and forcing 1:1 there means adding rule after rule until
the check can no longer fail — worse than no check. 29Abhi01 keeps the hard
gate and is unaffected.

**THE COLOPHON CHECK RUNS FROM THE COLOPHONS, NOT FROM THE TREE, and that
direction is the whole point.** "Is every node closed?" fails on sections the
edition simply never closes — it prints no colophon for a Vibhaṅgavāra or a
Saṅkhyāvāra, and demanding one measures your own assumption. "Does every
section the edition CLOSES exist in the tree?" cannot be satisfied by an
assumption: if the book says `Paṭiccavāro.` and no Paṭiccavāra node exists, a
printed section has been dropped. 36Abhi08: **191 colophons printed, the
edition closes 16 of the 28 declared sections, and all 16 are in the tree.**
The other 12 are named in the output as not testable this way.

`colophons()` reads BOTH side-maps — `uddana/` for colophons after a numbered
unit and `sections/` k:'gatha' for ones before a book's first unit, which is
where `Paccayuddeso.` lives. Reading only the first made the check report the
volume's own opening section as never closed.

### The nav tree itself

`build_abhidhamma_nav.py` gained arbitrary DEPTH (`levels`) and
ancestor-reprint suppression. The Paṭṭhāna nests four deep and prints 1477
headings, so the two-level `mids` shape would have left ~1400 of them in one
flat list under their vāra — precisely the sidebar the user reported. Levels
are closed sets of names the edition reuses at that depth, so the same table
should serve 37-40 (**measure, do not assume**). 29Abhi01 rebuilds identically
through the new code.

Ancestor reprints: the Paṭṭhāna reprints the tika's name at the head of every
vāra (`1. Kusalattika  1. Paṭiccavāra`, then `1. Kusalattika  2. Sahajātavāra`),
so the name occurs seven times. Taken as sections the six extra copies each
open a duplicate row inside their own parent. They stay in the body where the
page prints them; they are simply not nodes. **51 skipped, 1351 printed
headings -> 1300 nodes**, and `_abhi08verify.js` asserts both that count and
that no row repeats an ancestor.

### The splice had to be made VISIBLE, and that took a reader change

Emitting unit 41's opening into unit 40's prose was not enough: `fmtText`
strips a leading `NN.` — that is how every ordinary paragraph number reaches it
— so the number vanished off the page and only the words survived. The body
gate could not see this (it normalises digits away). A new `after` entry shape
`{n, t}` carries the number explicitly and `proseOne` draws it as a `.pn`,
which is what the printed page does. `add_prose` gained an optional `num`, and
its continuation branch now joins into either shape; `_plist` in
`verify_render_vs_pdf.py` models it. Reader BUILD `2026-07-26n-splice`;
backups `reader2.html.bakabhi08`, `verify_render_vs_pdf.py.presplice`. All 55
regression maps and every other volume's presentation gate re-run clean after
it: `check_layout.js` all volumes, `_abhi01verify.js` 69 + 55,
`_milindaverify.js` 69, `_abhigroupverify.js` 77 + 76, `_navdup.js` 185.

### `_abhi08verify.js` — no expansion pass

Opening the volume renders its WHOLE tree; all 1300 rows are in the DOM at
once. The expansion loop copied from `_abhigroupverify.js` clicked each row to
expand it at ~18ms of re-render, i.e. 24 seconds before a single assertion ran,
which is why the first three attempts hit the 45s device cap with no output.
Dropped. Rows run in slices of ~170.

### I TRIGGERED THE verify_all_volumes.py TRAP AGAIN — and `--help` does it too

`python3 pipeline/verify_all_volumes.py --help` is not a help flag. There is no
argument parser: unknown flags are ignored, so it ran as a no-arg invocation,
reused the stale default cache and rewrote `docs/verify_report.md` from old
entries as **clean 0/118** in under a second. The report was wrong until
regenerated. `--budget` is the way to work within the 45s device cap: pass
`--cache <fresh-dir> --budget 33` and re-run until the count stops rising
(five runs for 118 volumes). The cache dir must be inside the repo —
`/tmp/osbct/...` is not writable on the device.

## DHAMMASAṄGAṆĪ — 29Abhi01 DONE END TO END, ALL THREE GATES (2026-07-26k)

**The first Abhidhamma volume, and the first outside the Khuddaka to be rebuilt
from the printed page.** `docs/verify_report.md`: **clean 12/118**.

    body          verify_render_vs_pdf.py 29Abhi01 19 316 0 1780 {4,2,1} -> 0/0/0/0
                  (baseline over the same extent: 1 line / 2 chunks / 10 rev / 0 dup)
    apparatus     verify_apparatus.py 29Abhi01 -> 0 spliced / 0 variants / 0 xrefs
                  (was 0 / 1 / 0; 69 printed notes, 69 anchored, 0 unanchored)
    presentation  check_layout.js 29Abhi01 -> ok, incipit x1
                  _abhi01verify.js  data 53/53 · rows 39/39
    nav           build_abhidhamma_nav.py (NEW, generic over the piṭaka) ->
                  5 top / 141 sections, checked against the volume's own MĀTIKĀ
                  (134 entries, all present and in order); `_navdup.js` 199 clean

**THE KATHĀ PATH FIT WITH NO ARGUMENT: 1780 printed numbered units against 1780
corpus paragraphs, `n` agreeing on every one, first try, no errata.** Body
column 0; the mātikās are read as hanging lists by the machinery 26Khu09
already needed.

**HEADINGS BY FORM, AND A STEM LIST WOULD HAVE BEEN WORSE (`heads_by_form`).**
This volume sets **247 distinct display lines and not one carries a comma;
none is longer than six words; 99 have no terminal stop and 148 do.** That is
the Netti's rule and nothing else is needed: A HEADING IS A TITLE AND CARRIES
NO TERMINAL STOP, and its colophon echoes it with one — `Tika` / `Tikaṁ.`,
`Catukka` / `Catukkaṁ.`, `Hetugocchaka` / `Hetugocchakaṁ.`, `Suddhikapaṭipadā`
/ `Suddhikapaṭipadā.` Enumerating stems would have meant silently dropping
whichever of the 99 headings the list missed, into the body as prose — the
wrong-role failure no gate can see. The form test cannot reach body text here
because the body column is 0, paragraph openers sit at 4-6 and display at 8+.
!!! IT MUST NOT BE APPLIED TO CORPUS PARAGRAPHS. The leaked-heading scan calls
`kat_is_head` on paragraph TEXT, which has no indent evidence, and the form
test claimed **36 of the Dukamātikā's own paragraphs** ("101. Vijjābhāgino
dhammā. (1303) Avijjābhāgino dhammā. (1304)") as leaked headings — which would
have hidden them and broken the 1:1 pairing. `kat_is_head(core, printed=False)`.

**A VOLUME WITH NO GĀTHĀ AT ALL (`no_verse`), SHOWN NOT ASSUMED.** A pāda
carries commas and no display line here has one; the only verse in the file is
in the Nidānakathā front matter, which the declared extent excludes. It matters
because **the Rūpakaṇḍa sets its lists ONE ITEM PER PRINTED LINE** at a
paragraph indent ("Atthi rūpaṁ upādā, atthi rūpaṁ no upādā."), which the
verse-run rule reads as a gāthā — and `display_prose`'s pāda-punctuation test
does NOT save it, because every one of those items is a complete sentence
ending in a full stop. Three runs, 29 printed lines, would have been drawn as
italic verse.

**THE DEFECT CLASS THIS VOLUME SHARES WITH THE PAṬṬHĀNA, fixed here where it
occurs ten times rather than in 36Abhi08 where it occurs 155.** The corpus
glues a printed heading onto the tail of the previous paragraph and drops what
stands between: p147/148 sets "Evaṁ duvidhena rūpasaṅgaho." / "Dukaṁ." /
"Tika" / "Tividhena rūpasaṅgaho–", and the corpus kept the first and last of
those RUN TOGETHER and dropped the middle two. Repaired by the PDF-first build.

**AND THE ASSERTION FOUND AN ORDERING DEFECT THE BODY GATE COULD NOT.** The
Rūpakaṇḍa's eleven divisions (Ekaka, Duka, Tika … Ekādasaka) each have a
heading, an opener, a list and a colophon but **NO NUMBERED UNIT OF THEIR OWN**
— the next "N." does not come until the following division. Without
`orphan_sections` the whole list landed in the NEXT unit's `before`, i.e. below
the colophons that close it and below the following division's heading: printed
order destroyed, 0/0/0/0 from the body gate throughout, because every word was
still present. This is the third volume to need that flag and the second piṭaka;
it is no longer a Milindapañha peculiarity.

**A HARNESS FIX, AGAIN AFFECTING ALL 118 VOLUMES.** Backup
`pipeline/verify_render_vs_pdf.py.present`. `pdf_lines` terminates the page's
FIRST body line with a '.' sentinel so a heading cannot glue to the content
below it and fabricate a chunk. That was enough while the only offender was a
page-top running header; **29Abhi01 sets 99 headings MID-page** ("Tika" above
"Tividhena rūpasaṅgaho–"), and the whole Abhidhamma is built this way. New
`display_lines(vol)` reads `-layout` and terminates every CENTRED, short,
unpunctuated line — printed geometry, not a guess. Trade-off recorded: a short
BODY line wrongly included loses nothing at the line level and only breaks the
chunk comparison there, which is the weaker of the two. **All eleven Khuddaka
volumes re-run after it: still 0/0/0/0 at minw 4 and 1.**

**NAV — `pipeline/build_abhidhamma_nav.py` (NEW, and deliberately GENERIC over
the piṭaka)**, one SPEC entry per volume: the ordered top level, and which
second-level entries are groups. Two things it has to do that no earlier nav
builder did:
 1. **THE TOP LEVEL IS AN ORDERED SEQUENCE, NOT A SET.** 29Abhi01 prints
    "Mātikā" twice — the volume's own opening mātikā (a top) and the
    Rūpakaṇḍa's (a group under it). Matching by label put the second at the top
    of the tree. The sequence is consumed in printed order and the builder
    refuses to write if it does not appear in order.
 2. **THE MĀTIKĀ CHECK IS COMPOUND-AWARE.** The printed mātikā runs a section
    head together with its first subsection where they share a page —
    `Dukanikkhepahetugocchaka` for the body's `Dukanikkhepa` + `Hetugocchaka`,
    `Kāmāvacarakusalapadabhājanī` for `Kāmāvacarakusala` + `Padabhājanī`, and
    nine more. An entry is matched against one body heading or a run of up to
    three. Requiring 1:1 would report eleven defects that are not defects;
    ignoring the compounds would let a genuinely missing heading pass.

    Dhammasaṅgaṇīpāḷi
      Mātikā                 Tikamātikā, Dukamātikā -> 13, Suttantikadukamātikā
      1. Cittuppādakaṇḍa     68 sections
      2. Rūpakaṇḍa           Uddesa; Mātikā -> 11; Rūpavibhatti -> 12
      3. Nikkhepakaṇḍa       16 sections
      4. Aṭṭhakathākaṇḍa     15 sections

**ERRATUM — the edition's own, preserved verbatim.** The mātikā (p69) compounds
its group head with the first subsection as **"Tebhūmakakāmāvacarakusala"** but
writes the head WITHOUT its own `-kusala`, where the body (p88) sets
**"Tebhūmakakusala"** then **"Kāmāvacarakusala"**. Listed in the nav builder's
`errata` rather than absorbed by loosening the compound matcher, which would
let a genuinely missing heading through. One body heading the mātikā does not
list is kept and reported ("Cattāri arūpajhānāni soḷasakkhattukāni").

**BUILDER CHANGE THAT IS NOT PER-VOLUME, and is safe:** the title page's own
stack is now taken from `booktitle/<VOL>.json` instead of the constant
`(title, 'Khuddakanikāya')`, which was the whole Khuddaka and nothing else —
29Abhi01's page sets "Abhidhammapiṭaka" above its book name and that line was
arriving as a heading of the body. The booktitle map already holds the printed
stack for all 40 canon volumes.

## THE PDFs DECLARE THEIR OWN TEXT EXTENT — and the sweep now reads it (2026-07-26j)

**Every one of the 118 files states where its text begins and ends, in the PDF
`Subject` field**, and nothing in this project had ever looked at it:

    29Abhi01   [327 pages = content 19 + text 298 + index 10]
    01Vin01    [23 pages of content, 405 pages of text and index]

That is the publisher saying where the front matter stops and the back-matter
index starts — exactly what `verify_all_volumes.page_range()` has been GUESSING
from the corpus `pdf_page` anchors plus a back-matter marker, and getting wrong
often enough to need two standing caveats in this file.

**VALIDATED BEFORE BEING TRUSTED**, against the eleven Khuddaka ranges this
project measured by hand over ten sessions: the declared extent reproduces
**ten of them exactly**, and the eleventh differs only because the hand range
ran one page past the end of 18Khu01's text onto a BLANK page (its text ends at
idx 479, the index starts at 481). So where it exists it is not merely as good
as the measurement — it is one page better.

116 of 118 volumes give it directly. Seven state it in a second wording
("23 pages of content, 405 pages of text, 148 pages of index"), which the
regex now accepts; and two of those seven — **01Vin01 and 02Vin02** — merge
text and index into a single figure, so their tail cannot come from the
metadata and they still fall back to the measured method, which is why that
method is kept. `declared_range(vol)` in `verify_all_volumes.py`; backup
`pipeline/verify_all_volumes.py.preextent`.

**WHAT THIS RETIRES.** The sweep no longer overshoots into 22Khu05's and
23Khu06's printed word index (they now stop at 425 and 382, the hand-verified
values), so the caveat below about not chasing those two rows is spent. It also
retires the class that inflated 24Khu07's baseline to 140 lines when the true
figure over its own text was 65.
