**MEASURING THE GEOMETRY IS WHAT SAVED THIS VOLUME, AND IT ALSO EXPOSED A
DEFECT IN A SHIPPED ONE.** 28Khu11 looks exactly like 27Khu10 — prose units
with heavy quoted gāthā — so the obvious move was `units_may_be_verse: True`.
Measured, that is WRONG here: **eleven units are followed by a line at a
greater indent and only ONE of them is a gāthā** (the opening "1. Milindo nāma
so rājā, Sāgalāyaṁ puruttame." and its ten pādas). The other ten are PROSE that
ends in the citation dash and then quotes a verse — "4. Bhante Nāgasena
bhāsitampetaṁ Bhagavatā–". The flag as it stood would have rendered each of
those questions as a verse line, glued the quotation's first pāda to it, and
left the rest of the quotation as a separate block.
`units_may_be_verse: 'hanging'` adds the two things the page itself says, and
both are needed: **(a) the citation dash** — a pāda never ends in "–", so a
unit whose own line does is prose whatever follows it (this alone decides all
eleven correctly); **(b) a display quotation's first line hangs LEFT of its own
body**, so a run followed by another run at a still greater indent opens a
block of its own. 258 printed units against 258 corpus paragraphs, `n` agreeing
on every one.

**!!! THE SAME SHAPE IS MIS-READ IN SHIPPED 27Khu10. NOT FIXED HERE. MEASURED
EXTENT: 66 of its 271 units carry a `groups` array, and AT LEAST 34 of those
are prose.** Verified case by case against the printed page: 27Khu10 p29 sets
"26. Tattha katamo adhippāyo." — a prose question — followed by a four-pāda
quoted gāthā, and `verse/27Khu10.json` ord51 stores
`[["Tattha katamo adhippāyo.", "+ “Dhammo have rakkhati dhammacāriṁ,"]]`,
i.e. the question is drawn as a verse line WITH the gāthā's first pāda, and the
gāthā's remaining three pādas become a separate block below it. The same holds
for every "Tattha katamo/katamaṁ X." unit (ord54, 67, and the long run through
the Peṭakopadesa), for "Tatthimāni suttāni.", "Tatridaṁ niyyānaṁ–" and
"Manopubbaṅgamā dhammāti gāthā.". Its body gate is 0/0/0/0 throughout — every
word is present, contiguous and unique. **WHY IT IS NOT FIXED IN THIS CHANGE:
there, unlike here, the printed page does not separate the two cases
geometrically at all** — 27Khu10 p15's genuine verse unit "14. Sabbo samādhi
ñāṇamūlako…" and p203's prose unit "26. Tattha katamaṁ ñāṇaṁ." have IDENTICAL
geometry (number line, then pādas at a greater indent), and the citation dash
is absent from both. Deciding them needs a judgement about 66 units, one at a
time, against the page. `units_may_be_verse` is per BOOK, so 27Khu10 keeps
`True` and its output is byte-identical — proved by the 9-volume regression.
**This is the next thing to do in this file's list.**

**FIVE MORE WRONG-ROLE DEFECTS, ALL CAUGHT BY THE `--show` REVIEW OR BY THE
ROW SWEEP, NONE BY A GATE.**
 1. **A DISPLAY BLOCK IS NOT ALWAYS VERSE.** This edition indents long PROSE
    quotations from the suttas with exactly a gāthā's geometry — a run of lines
    sharing one indent above the body column — and 28Khu11 sets nine of them
    (printed p139, p140, p212, p360, p368, p386, p389 and two more). Every one was
    being emitted as a `{"gatha": …}` block, i.e. drawn as italic verse with
    the printed line breaks kept. The separator is PĀDA PUNCTUATION, not
    indent: a gāthā breaks at the end of each pāda, so every line but the last
    ends in a comma or a full stop, while a prose quotation breaks wherever the
    measure runs out. `display_prose` (per volume). A run of ONE — only
    possible on a page with no body column at all, which is read as entirely
    display — must itself be a pāda, which is how p23's lead-in "Tenāhu–"
    stopped being drawn as the first line of the gāthā it introduces.
 2. **TWO PRINTED HEADINGS ON ONE LINE, SET IN THE BODY COLUMN.** p231 sets
    "1. Buddhavagga        1. Dvinnaṁ Buddhānaṁ anuppajjamānapañha" at indent
    5, not centred as the same shape is on p24 and p103, so the display test
    never saw it and it was read as the Anumānapañha's first NUMBERED UNIT.
    That is worse than a wrong role: it took an ordinal, so every unit after it
    paired with the wrong paragraph — and the 1:1 count check is what refused
    to build on it (259 printed against 258 corpus). The signal is the
    edition's own typography and needs no indent: a run of 3+ spaces separating
    two halves that are BOTH heading-shaped (`_is_double_head`).
 3. **SECTIONS WITH NO NUMBERED UNIT OF THEIR OWN, and there are four.** The
    Dhutaṅgapañha (printed p330-342), the Opammakathā mātikā (p343-348), the
    Meṇḍakapañhārambhakathā with its six parts (p95-102) and the Nigamana
    (p407-408) are each headed, run for many pages, and carry no "N." unit.
    `pend_heads`/`pend_before` attach everything to the NEXT unit, so **489
    printed lines were piling up in ord194's `before`** — rendered as 489
    ONE-LINE paragraphs below a stack of five headings that the page sets in
    two groups seventeen pages apart. The tell that a heading has no unit is
    that a COLOPHON arrives while it is still pending. Such material now goes
    into the uddāna stream of the PREVIOUS unit, in printed order — `block()`
    draws uddāna blocks after `before`/`groups`/`after`, which is exactly where
    the page sets them, and `render_parts` models that stream in full, so
    nothing leaves the body gate's sight. `orphan_sections` (per volume).
 4. **…and the printed ORDER between headings and text was not recorded at
    all.** p101 sets "Ācariyaguṇa", its prose, then "Upāsakaguṇa" and its
    prose; replaying `pend_heads` and then `pend_before` put both headings
    above both paragraphs, so the first heading lost its own text to the
    second. `pend_seq` is now the ordered record and is what gets replayed.
 5. **`uddana` DROPPED EVERY HEAD-ONLY BLOCK.** The tidy pass at the end of
    `build()` deleted any block with no `lines` — right for a stray label,
    wrong for a heading immediately followed by another heading, which is how
    this book sets "Meṇḍakapañhārambhakathā / Aṭṭhamantaparivajjanīyaṭṭhāna"
    and "Ācariyaguṇa / Upāsakaguṇa". It was silently deleting the first of each
    pair; the body gate saw one of them only because a later colophon repeats
    its wording.
 Also: a `plain` block's head was drawn at ONE weight, `vatthu` (13px), because
 until now the only thing that carried one was a Dhammapada vatthu title. These
 are real section heads, so the block now carries `hk` and the reader uses the
 same CLS map the `sections` path uses.

**A HARNESS DEFECT FOUND HERE THAT AFFECTS ALL 118 VOLUMES.** Backup
`pipeline/verify_render_vs_pdf.py.prehyph`. `pdf_lines` appends a '.' sentinel
to the first body line of each page so that a page-top heading cannot glue to
the content below it — **but it appended it AFTER A LINE-END HYPHEN**
("…Gaṅgāyamunā-."), which then defeated the line-end rejoin twenty lines
further down, so both halves of the hyphenated compound were reported missing
AND the render block that correctly holds it whole was reported not-in-PDF.
28Khu11 printed p355 and p403. A hyphenated line cannot glue a heading to content
anyway — it is a word continuing onto the next line, which is exactly what must
NOT be broken. **RE-RUN AFTER IT: all ten previously-done Khuddaka volumes are
still 0/0/0/0 at minw 4 and 1.**

node whose NEIGHBOUR shares its ordinal; a LAST child inherits its PARENT's end
instead, and that can equal its own start. Here the vagga's sixteenth pañha
begins at #110 and the next section its parent knows about —

**THE WORST CORPUS IN THE KHUDDAKA SO FAR: 409 missing printed lines / 224
chunks / 32 rev** over the true extent, against 25/18/12 for the
Paṭisambhidāmagga and 65/55/21 for the Mahāniddesa. Almost all of it is the
QUOTED GĀTHĀ these two works cite on nearly every page; the corpus kept the
prose around them and dropped the verse. All of it is restored from the PDF.

**TWO BOOKS IN ONE PHYSICAL VOLUME.** Nettipāḷi ord 0-150 (pdf 1-166, ending
"Nettipakaraṇaṁ niṭṭhitaṁ."), Peṭakopadesapāḷi ord 151-270 (pdf 167-341, ending
"Peṭakopadesapakaraṇaṁ niṭṭhitaṁ."). Each prints its own title page, its own
homage and its own mātikā, so each gets its own nav node — the standing rule —
and `_nettiverify.js` asserts in BOTH directions that neither bleeds.

**THE KATHĀ PATH FITS, WITH ONE ADDITION: `units_may_be_verse`.** Here a
numbered unit is SOMETIMES A GĀTHĀ and sometimes prose, and the two interleave
in one printed series — which is exactly why the corpus `n` descends twice
inside the Netti (4 -> 1 at ord4, 26 -> 5 at ord30: prose 1-4, then the sixteen
hāra verses 1-26, then prose 5 on). Pairing BY POSITION is blind to that, and
must be; what it cannot be blind to is the SHAPE, because a verse unit rendered
as prose loses its line breaks. The discriminator needs no word list, only the
printed geometry: **a numbered unit is verse when the line after it is set at a
STRICTLY GREATER indent than the number**, since a prose unit's continuation
returns to the body column and a gāthā's pādas do not.
271 printed units against 271 corpus paragraphs, `n` agreeing on every one.

**THE BODY COLUMN IS NOW MEASURED PER BOOK, NOT PER PAGE.** `kat_book_body()`.
27Khu10 p133 sets one numbered unit and eleven quoted verse lines and has NO
line at the left margin at all, so the per-page measurement returned the VERSE
indent as the body column — after which that page's own numbered unit sat to
the LEFT of it and was read as prose continuation. It lost exactly one of the
Netti's 151 units, and the 1:1 pairing check is what refused to build on it. A
page keeps its own column only when it is a genuine HANGING LIST, and what
tells a list from an all-verse page is that a list has many numbered lines and
an all-verse page has one or two. 26Khu09's mātikās are still read as lists;
its output is unchanged.

**!!! A DEFECT IN 26Khu09, SHIPPED EARLIER TODAY AND FOUND BY A CHANGE MADE FOR
THIS VOLUME.** Widening the colophon test uncovered **32 section-end colophons
of the Paṭisambhidāmagga that were rendering as ORDINARY BODY PROSE** —
"Sallekhaṭṭhañāṇaniddeso sattatiṁsatimo.", "Āsayānusayañāṇaniddeso
navasaṭṭhimo." and thirty more. CAUSE: `NIDCOLO` names the ordinals only up to
twenty and that volume runs to seventy-three, so every colophon above the
twentieth fell through. Its body gate reported 0/0/0/0 throughout — the text
was present, contiguous and unique — and the mātikā check could not see it
either, since a colophon is not a mātikā entry. FIX: recognise the ordinal by
its ENDING rather than by a word list; every Pāḷi ordinal above the fourth ends
in -ma, so the nominative ends -mo / -mā / -maṁ. 26Khu09 rebuilt and re-gated:
body still 0/0/0/0 at minw 4 and 1, apparatus still 0/0/0, check_layout ok,
`_patisambhidaverify` 41/41, mātikā check still 133/133. **Its uddāna anchors

**FOUR MORE WRONG-ROLE DEFECTS, ALL CAUGHT BY THE `--show` REVIEW OR THE MĀTIKĀ
CHECK, NONE BY A GATE.**
 1. **The Netti closes a vāra with the bare name** — "Saṅgahavāro.",
    "Uddesavāro.", "Niddesavāro." — which says neither "finished" nor "Nth" and
    which `kat_is_head` matches perfectly, so all three would have OPENED their
    sections instead of closing them. What separates them from the headings
    they echo ("1. Saṅgahavāra") is the rule this edition uses everywhere: A
    HEADING IS A TITLE AND CARRIES NO TERMINAL STOP. `kat_items` now tests
    colophon BEFORE heading.
 2. **…and that test, taken alone, was far too weak**, because a section word
    can fall INSIDE an ordinary word: `vāra` in "nivāraṇaṁ", `bhūmi` in
    "Apāyabhūmiṁ", `gāthā` in "uddānagāthā". It took six quoted verse pādas out
    of the body. Measured, the real bare colophons sit at indent 22-35 and every
    false one at 9-17, so that form must ALSO be centred. The ordinal form is
    deliberately left unguarded, or 26Khu09's colophons at indent 13 are lost.
 3. **The Netti opens with a whole section before its first numbered unit** —
    the Saṅgahavāra's ten gāthā between their heading and their colophon. The
    kathā path folded everything before the first unit into that unit's
    `before`, so the gāthā rendered as its intro prose and the colophon
    rendered AFTER text it precedes. Now `sections` in printed order, the
    mechanism 19Khu02's Nidānagāthā already uses.
 4. **A colophon is not a heading, and the nav builder proved it**: emitted with
    a heading class, "Saṅgahavāro." became a node in the tree. Pre-first-unit
    colophons now go out as `k:'gatha'` — display material in printed order —
    and the nav skips that class.

Clicking "1. Saṅgahavāra" or "2. Uddesavāra" rendered an empty pane. TWO

affecting EVERY tree-shaped volume, and neither visible to any content gate —
the text was present and correct in the data throughout.

 1. **A ZERO-LENGTH SPAN when two siblings share an ordinal.** A node's span
    ended where the NEXT SIBLING starts. The Netti's Saṅgahavāra has NO NUMBERED
    UNIT AT ALL — its ten gāthā are display material printed above the
    Uddesavāra's first paragraph — so both nodes sit at #0 and the first got

    LATER.
 2. **VAGGASPAN WAS KEYED BY THE NODE'S KEY, AND KEYS ARE NOT UNIQUE.** A parent
    and its first child begin at the same paragraph (Paṭiniddesavāra and
    Desanāhāravibhaṅga both at #30), so the child could not record its own span
    and clicking it opened all 121 paragraphs of its parent. `curvagga` is now a
    SPAN ID — the node's path in the tree, unique by construction — while
    `cursutta` keeps the real key, which is what `openKey()` needs. The pane
    title reads `SUTTALABEL[curvagga]` first, so a parent and child that share a
    paragraph still title the pane differently.

    its Paṭhamavagga share #294, and 26Khu09 wherever a kathā and its first

## PAṬISAMBHIDĀMAGGA — 26Khu09 DONE END TO END, ALL THREE GATES (2026-07-26c)

    body          verify_render_vs_pdf.py 26Khu09 9 427 0 405 {4,2,1} -> 0/0/0/0
    apparatus     verify_apparatus.py 26Khu09 -> 0 spliced / 0 variants / 0 xrefs  (was 0 / 6 / 0)

                  node --max-old-space-size=4096 _patisambhidaverify.js -> 40 / 40
    nav           build_patisambhida_nav.py (NEW) -> 3 vaggas / 30 kathās / 122
                  sections, checked against the edition's own MĀTIKĀ (133 entries,
                  all present and in order)

Starting point over the true text extent: **25 lines / 18 chunks / 12 rev / 0 dup**
at minw 4 — this volume's corpus was in much better shape than either Niddesa.
Text extent measured: pdf index 9-427, ending at the closing Uddānagāthā; back
matter from 429. No back-matter paragraph in the corpus this time.

**THE HANDOFF SAID TO CHECK THE GEOMETRY BEFORE REUSING THE NIDDESA PATH, AND
BOTH OF ITS ASSUMPTIONS FAIL HERE.** So `mode: 'katha'` is a third reader of the
page, not a widening of the second.
 1. **THERE IS NO LEMMA.** A niddesa section opens with a display verse and
    comments on it; here the number opens the PROSE ITSELF ("1. Kathaṁ
    sotāvadhāne paññā sutamaye ñāṇaṁ–").
 2. **THE BODY COLUMN IS NOT ALWAYS THE PAGE'S LEFTMOST INDENT.** Three shapes
    are printed and all three are now measured rather than assumed: ordinary
    prose (continuation at the left margin, paragraphs indented); HANGING LISTS,
    where the number is set to the LEFT of its own continuation (the Mahāvagga's
    own mātikā of 73 items, and two further list pages); and the closing
    Uddānagāthā page, which has no body column at all.

**HOW A PROSE UNIT IS STORED, AND THE ONE-CHARACTER SUBTLETY IT RESTS ON.** A
unit has no verse, so its entry is `{"groups": [], "after": [ … ]}`. **`[]` is
TRUTHY in JS**, so `block()` already takes the verse branch, renders
`before + after`, suppresses the corpus text, and — because `groups.length` is 0
— still draws `pr.n` outside the block, which is exactly the prose shape wanted.
No reader change was needed. **`render_parts` DID need one**: Python reads `[]`
as false, so the harness modelled the CORPUS text as rendered where the reader
does not render it. A latent reader/harness divergence that had never fired
because no volume until now has an empty groups list. Mirror the reader with
`if e.get('groups') is not None`.

**HOW VERSE INSIDE THE PROSE IS FOUND, since indent cannot do it.** Measured
over the volume, 1,258 non-numbered lines sit 3-7 columns right of the body and
917 of those are short enough to look like verse — nearly all are prose
paragraph openers. What separates them is what FOLLOWS: a prose opener is
followed by continuation at the body column, a verse line by another line at its
own indent. So verse is a RUN of two or more consecutive lines sharing an indent
above the body column. That gives **24 blocks / 117 lines** in the whole volume,
of which exactly one sits in the ambiguous band (p302's "Adhimokkhe ca paggāhe…")
and it is verse. `--show` lists every block, every heading and every colophon.

**A THIRD HARNESS DEFECT, AND IT IS THE MIRROR OF THE FIRST TWO.** Backup
`verify_render_vs_pdf.py.prehdr2` covers all three.
`running_headers` derives the header set by FREQUENCY, and frequency has a
floor: a form must head at least three pages. **A section shorter than that
never enters the set and its header LEAKS INTO THE BODY**, splitting the
paragraph it interrupts — the other half of the damage that function's own
docstring describes. 26Khu09: "6. Gatikathā" heads two pages, "7. Kammakathā"
and "9. Maggakathā" one each, and all three were being read as body text
mid-sentence. That alone was **11 of the 12 rev findings**. Raising the floor
would let content back in, and the floor is there for good reason — so the fix
is not a threshold at all: `layout_headers()` reads the header from the PAGE'S
OWN GEOMETRY, since in this edition the running header is the line that CARRIES
THE PRINTED PAGE NUMBER, set hard against the opposite margin. `-layout`
preserves that spacing (the plain text `pdf_lines` reads does not, which is why
the frequency heuristic existed at all), so the geometry is read from `-layout`
and matched back onto the plain stream. A page whose first line is not
header-shaped — the first page of a section, where the edition suppresses the
header — is correctly left alone.
**RE-RUN AFTER IT: all nine done volumes are 0/0/0/0 at minw 4 and 1.**

**A SIDE-MAP BLOCK ANCHORED TO A HIDDEN ORDINAL NEVER RENDERS, AND BOTH PROSE
PATHS WERE DOING IT.** Colophons were anchored to `cur - 1` on the assumption
that the previous unit is the previous ordinal. 26Khu09 breaks that: ord351 is a
LEAKED HEADING (see below) and is hidden, so "Paṭisambhidākathā niṭṭhitā." was
attached to a paragraph that both `block()` and `render_parts` skip — present in
the data, invisible on the page, and reported by the body gate as a missing
printed line. Both paths now track the previous unit explicitly. The niddesa
path's output is unchanged (neither Niddesa volume has a hidden ordinal between
units), and it was corrected anyway so the two do not differ on it.

**LEAKED HEADING — ord351.** The corpus captured the printed line
"7. Dhammacakkakathā        1. Saccavāra" — two centred headings typeset on ONE
line — as a paragraph carrying the KATHĀ's number as its `n`. Hidden before the
pairing, as in the verse path, and `split_centre` puts the two headings back.
Left in, it would have taken an ordinal and desynced every unit after it.

**ERRATUM — the edition's own, PRESERVED VERBATIM.** p333 heads the fifth kathā
of the Yuganaddhavagga **"5. Virāgatathā"** where the volume's own mātikā (p8)
sets **"5. Virāgakathā"** — 't' for 'k', the same class as 22Khu05's 'jākaka'
for 'jātaka'. Both pages keep what they print. The builder needs it RECOGNISED
as a heading, and a stem loose enough to do that on its own would be `tathā`,
among the commonest words in this very volume ("tathā avitathā anaññathā"), so
it is listed explicitly in `SPEC['26Khu09']['headfix']` and in `ERRATA`, and the
nav check is told the two spellings are one section via `ERRATUM_SAME`.

**THE MĀTIKĀ CHECK EARNED ITS KEEP IMMEDIATELY.** `build_patisambhida_nav.py`
builds the tree from the headings printed over each section in the BODY and then
requires the front-matter MĀTIKĀ — a different page, set by the editors as their
own table of contents — to appear in it entire and in order. It refused to write
and named **"Mūlamūlakādidasaka"**: the edition prints that heading on p312 and
lists it in the mātikā, but no stem reached it, so it was falling through to the
body and rendering as an ordinary prose paragraph. Present, contiguous, and in
the wrong role — the body gate reported 0 for it. Stem `dasaka` added.
THE CHECK IS A SUBSEQUENCE, NOT AN EQUALITY, and deliberately: the body prints
23 headings the mātikā does not list (the Mahāvagga's own "Mātikā", the
Ānāpānassati chakkas and catukkas, the lettered "Ka./Kha./Ga." sub-niddesas of
the Indriyakathā, the "1. Mātikā" / "2. Niddesa" halves of the Suññakathā). Those
are really printed and belong in the tree; requiring equality would mean either
dropping them or reporting a defect that is not one. Every one is REPORTED.

**THE TREE — all three levels the mātikā prints, MIXED DEPTH, the user's choice.**

    Paṭisambhidāmaggapāḷi
      1. Mahāvagga        Mātikā, then 10 kathās  (Ñāṇakathā 48 sections)
      2. Yuganaddhavagga  10 kathās
      3. Paññāvagga       10 kathās

14 of the 30 kathās are bare leaves, because the mātikā gives them a page and
nothing under them (Gatikathā, Kammakathā, Vipallāsakathā, Maggakathā …). The
Mahāvagga's own "Mātikā" section sits directly under the vagga, since no kathā
is open when it is printed. The generic `tree` branch renders all of it.

### 26Khu09 follow-up — USER-REPORTED: the paragraph number stacked (2026-07-26d)

Reported from a screenshot after the run above called the volume done. The
Mahāvagga mātikā rendered

    1.
    Sotāvadhāne paññā sutamaye ñāṇaṁ.

where the page sets " 1. Sotāvadhāne paññā sutamaye ñāṇaṁ." on ONE line.
CAUSE: `block()` emits `num` and then `body`, and a prose unit's body is a
<div> — block-level — so the number could only stack above it. For a VERSE the
number is handed to the first `.gatha` (`gn=num`) and this never arose; the
prose unit is the first content in the project that has neither a gāthā to
receive it nor inline body text.
FIX: `block()` now arms a `lead` with the number after `before` is rendered and
before `after` is, and the first prose block takes it, exactly as a verse's
first `.gatha` does. `before` is printed ABOVE the number on the page, so it is
rendered first and never takes it. All 404 units now carry the number inline.
!!! WHY NO GATE CAUGHT IT: every word was present, in the right order and
contiguous, so the body harness reported 0/0/0/0 — and check_layout's
verse-number rule skipped the paragraph entirely because the rule opened with
`if(!p.querySelector('.gatha')) continue`, and most prose units quote no verse.
This is the same blind spot recorded for the homage, the leaked Apadāna
headings and the book titles: **content present, in the wrong shape, invisible
to every content check**. It is the fourth round of user-reported presentation
defects and the lesson has not changed — the layout gate only tests what
someone has already thought to assert.
ASSERTED NOW, in the same change: `check_layout.js` gained `prose-number-stacked`
(a prose unit's `.pn` must sit inside its first block), which no longer depends
on the paragraph containing a gāthā; and `_patisambhidaverify.js` asserts that
all 404 units carry it inline and that the first unit reads as one line.

`_jatakaverify` 82/82, `_booktitleverify` 286/286, `_btrender` 18/18,
`_khu01verify` all, `_snverify` all, `_19bleed` no bleed. The body gate is

**check_layout's VERSE-NUMBER RULE WAS TOO BROAD AND IS NOW SHARPER.** It flagged
19 paragraphs here. The rule says a verse number must hang inside its first
`.gatha`; when it was written, every paragraph containing a `.gatha` was a verse
paragraph. A Paṭisambhidāmagga unit is PROSE that quotes verse part-way through,
and there the number belongs outside, beside the prose it numbers. The rule now
reads `verse/<VOL>.json` and exempts a unit whose `groups` is empty — which
keeps it sharp for the volumes it was written for, since a verse paragraph whose
number escaped its gāthā is still flagged even when it opens with intro prose.

**THE BASELINE IN THIS FILE WAS INFLATED, FOR THE REASON THIS FILE ALREADY NAMES.**
It recorded 24Khu07 at 140 lines / 153 chunks / 21 rev and 25Khu08 at 116 / 89 / 14,
from the sweep. Over each volume's ACTUAL TEXT EXTENT the starting figures were
**65 / 55 / 21 / 0** and **116 / 89 / 14 / 0**. 24Khu07's sweep range ran into the
printed word index exactly as 22Khu05's and 23Khu06's do — and here for a second,
compounding reason: **the corpus itself captured two pages of that index as
paragraphs** (see below), so `page_range()` had paragraph anchors inside the back
matter and no marker could stop it. Text extents, measured: 24Khu07 ends at pdf
index 413 ("Mahāniddesapāḷi niṭṭhitā."), 25Khu08 at 311 ("Catuttho vaggo." /
"Cūḷaniddesapāḷi niṭṭhitā.").

**THE THREE OPEN QUESTIONS THIS FILE RAISED ARE ANSWERED, AND TWO OF ITS GUESSES
WERE WRONG.**
 (a) **The low paragraph-per-page count is LEGITIMATE — nothing was merged.** A
     numbered unit here is not a verse: it is one Suttanipāta verse quoted as a
     LEMMA followed by its whole niddesa, frequently five or more printed pages
     of prose, closing "Tenāha Bhagavā–" and the lemma repeated. One printed
     lemma per corpus paragraph, shown two independent ways: the PDF sets 210 and
     161 numbered lemmas against 210 and 161 corpus paragraphs, and the
     Suttanipāta's own Aṭṭhakavagga has 210 verses against 24Khu07's n = 1..210
     with no gap. Had this been read as a merge defect the whole volume would
     have been split wrongly.
 (b) **The 21 and 14 `rev` were NOT splices.** They were mid-paragraph corpus
     DROPS (the paragraph jumps, so the rendered block stops matching partway)
     plus, in 24Khu07, the two back-matter paragraphs. Nothing was spliced in
     either volume — `merged` is empty for both.
 (c) **`n_scope` and the verse machinery genuinely do not apply**, as this file
     suspected. `mode: 'niddesa'` in `build_khu_volume.py` replaces them.

**THE BUILDER'S NEW NIDDESA PATH — `mode: 'niddesa'` on a SPEC book entry.**
Gated per BOOK, so the verse path is untouched BY CONSTRUCTION and the
19Khu02/20Khu03/21Khu04/22Khu05/23Khu06 regression is what proves it (run after
every one of the four edits made here; 5 volumes x 5 maps byte-identical each
time, compared BUILDER-vs-BUILDER against `build_khu_volume.py.preniddesa`).
 * **Lemmas pair with corpus paragraphs BY POSITION, 1:1**, `n` kept only as a
   cross-check — the same choice the Jātaka needed and for the same reason (see
   ERRATA). The two sides are independent (printed lemma lines / corpus
   paragraph array), so the pairing is a real check; the builder refuses to
   build the book if the counts differ.
 * **The commentary becomes `after`, split into the PRINTED PARAGRAPHS**, with
   gāthā quoted inside it emitted as `{"gatha": […]}` blocks — a shape the
   reader's `proseOne()` and the harness's `_plist()` already understood. Result
   1,261 + 969 prose paragraphs and 279 + 199 gāthā blocks where the corpus had
   one run-on paragraph per section and no structure at all.
 * **Geometry, measured not assumed** (`nid_items`): indent base+0..2 is prose
   CONTINUATION, base+3..7 a prose PARAGRAPH OPENER or the numbered lemma,
   base+8 and up is display material. `base` is the page's own leftmost indent,
   and a page with no body column at all (25Khu08's last) is read as entirely
   display — the same rule the verse path uses for a page with no verse number.

**25Khu08 IS TWO HALVES AND THE EDITION'S OWN MĀTIKĀ PRINTS THEM AS TWO BLOCKS.**
Pages 1-21 set the Pārāyanavagga TEXT (Vatthugāthā, the 16 māṇavapucchās,
Pārāyanatthutigāthā, Pārāyanānugītigāthā) as plain verse with no commentary;
only from page 24 does the niddesa begin. The first half is ordinary verse and
uses the ordinary verse path (174/174 mapped). Both blocks are headed bare
"Pārāyanavagga", in the mātikā and in the body, so **the nav has two rows with
the same label** — the edition nowhere distinguishes them and inventing
"text"/"niddesa" or "I"/"II" would repeat the Jātaka mistake in reverse. They are
told apart by their children. **RAISE THIS WITH THE USER if the duplicate label
reads badly in the sidebar; it is a deliberate choice, not an oversight.**

**ERRATUM — the edition's own, PRESERVED VERBATIM.** 25Khu08 p229 opens the
Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa with **"211."** where the sequence requires 121 (the
previous lemma is 120, the next 122). The corpus reproduces it faithfully
(ord294 carries n=211). Pairing by POSITION places it correctly; a number-keyed
map would have seen an ascent to 211 and then a descent to 122, i.e. a false
segment boundary, and desynced everything after it. Recorded in `ERRATA` and
asserted in `_niddesaverify.js` so a later change cannot silently "correct" it.

**24Khu07's CORPUS HOLDS TWO PAGES OF THE PRINTED WORD INDEX AS PARAGRAPHS** —
ord210 and ord211, 15,000 characters each, book field "Mahāniddesapāḷiyaṁ",
n=130 and n=121, i.e. "Saṁvaṇṇitapadānaṁ anukkamaṇikā". Same class as the
14Sam03#598 back-matter paragraph an earlier session DELETED from the corpus.
Handled differently on the user's decision: HIDDEN via `hide/24Khu07.json`,
because the corpus is no longer edited. **Standing caveat: anything reading
`site/24Khu07.json` directly — a search index, an export, the Unicode-PDF plan —
still sees them.** Worth a scan of the other volumes for the same shape; this is
the second instance found.

**TWO HARNESS DEFECTS FOUND HERE, BOTH AFFECTING ALL 118 VOLUMES.** Backup
`pipeline/verify_render_vs_pdf.py.prehdr2`.
 1. **THE RUNNING-HEADER RULE WAS STATED CORRECTLY AND THEN NOT APPLIED, TWICE.**
    This file already says "a running header in this edition is a TITLE… a
    sentence-ending line is content however reliably it falls at a page top".
    The test was `not (re.search(r'[.?!]\d*$', t) and len(t.split()) > 3)` —
    (i) the `> 3` exempted SHORT sentence-ending lines, and a short sentence is
    still a sentence, so the Niddesa formula "…uddhaṁ adho / tiriyañcāpi
    majjhe." and the Pārāyana refrain "Nā'penti'me Gotamasāsanamhā." entered the
    set; (ii) it tested only SENTENCE punctuation, so a verse PĀDA ending in a
    COMMA — "Yaṁ yaṁ disaṁ vajati Bhūripañño," — entered it too. Every page-top
    occurrence of an absorbed line is DELETED FROM THE PRINTED SIDE, so the
    render then holds content the print appears not to have: on 25Khu08 that was
    4 rendered blocks reported not-in-PDF and 2 reported rendered-too-often,
    every one of them correct. **This is the THIRD time recurring content has
    been absorbed into this set** (Udāna's "udānesi–" lines, then the Apadāna
    refrain), and each earlier fix tightened one axis and left the next open.
    Now: terminal punctuation of any kind means content, no length exemption.
 2. **A LINE GLUED TO THE FOOTNOTE RULE LOSES ONE CHARACTER, AND IT IS THE
    HYPHEN.** `pdf_lines` reads PLAIN pdftotext; 25Khu08 p63 ends its last body
    line "pararūpavedanāsaññāsaṅkhāra-", hyphenated across the break, and plain
    mode swallows that hyphen into the rule's glyph run (`-layout` shows it), so
    `norm()` could no longer rejoin it with "viññāṇaṁ." on the next page. Text
    ending in a WORD CHARACTER immediately against the rule is exactly that case
    — a line that genuinely ends before the rule is separated from it by
    whitespace — so the hyphen is restored. Separately, `pdf_lines` now rejoins
    a line ending in '-' with the next FOR THE LINE-LEVEL DIRECTION TOO; the
    chunk and reverse directions read the list as one joined stream where
    `norm()` already did this, and only the per-line test was comparing the two
    halves as if they were whole words.
 **RE-RUN AFTER BOTH: 18Khu01, 19Khu02, 20Khu03, 21Khu04, 22Khu05 and 23Khu06 are
 all still 0/0/0/0 at minw 4 and 1.** `docs/verify_report.md` predates them and

**TWO MORE WRONG-ROLE DEFECTS, EACH CAUGHT BY A REPORT RATHER THAN BY A GATE.**
Both would have shipped at 0/0/0/0 — the text was present and contiguous in each

 2. **A HEADING IS NOT ALWAYS NUMBERED.** 25Khu08 sets three of them bare —

**NAV — `pipeline/build_niddesa_nav.py` (NEW), AND ITS CHECK IS A REAL TWO-INPUT
CHECK.** Shape chosen by the user: book -> vagga -> suttaniddesa, with the

    Mahāniddesapāḷi   1. Aṭṭhakavagga    16 suttaniddesas
    Cūḷaniddesapāḷi   Pārāyanavagga      19 text sections   (the vagga's own text)
                      Pārāyanavagga      19 niddesas, the 19th
                                         (Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa) divided into
                                         four vaggas — MIXED DEPTH, the edition's

The tree is built from the headings printed over each section in the BODY, then

24Khu07's mātikā sets "Cūḷaviyūhasuttaniddesa" and "Tuvaṭṭakasuttaniddesa" where

none (measured gaps between consecutive paragraph starts in 24Khu07: 1 page 103x,

page would fix it; that changes anchoring for all 118 volumes and belongs with
the sweep, not here. **And the reader still does not render `xrefs/` at all** —
24Khu07's 309 cross-reference lines across 190 anchors are stored and invisible,

**!!! THE PREDICTION IN THIS FILE WAS WRONG, AND IT WAS WRONG IN A WAY THAT WOULD
HAVE PASSED EVERY GATE.** This file said `n_scope` "is almost certainly `'vagga'`,
as in the Apadāna — VERIFY that before building." It is not. **`n` resets at every
NIPĀTA**: 22 nipātas numbered 1-22 CONTINUOUSLY across the two volumes (16 + 6),
547 jātakas numbered 1-547 continuously (520 + 27). The `'vagga'` scope segments on
any n-DESCENT, so it would have appeared to work; three separate things put false
descents into the stream and each would have desynced the map silently:
 1. **17 jātaka HEADINGS leaked into 22Khu05's corpus** carrying the JĀTAKA number
    as `n` ("224. * Kumbhilajātaka (2-8-4)") — the same defect as 21Khu04's ord3138
    that left 293 verses unmapped. The existing leak scan missed all 17: it did not
    strip the edition's `*` cross-reference marker and its `(\d+)` suffix could not
    match `(2-8-4)`.
 2. **The edition misprints three verse numbers**, and the corpus faithfully
    reproduces all three (see ERRATA below).
 3. **One of those misprints COLLIDES**: 22Khu05 p304 prints "24." for verse 29
    while verse 24 already exists in that nipāta, so a number-keyed map silently
    drops one of the two — no error, just a verse that loses its structure.
So `n_scope: 'nipata'` keys the map by (nipāta, n) with **a LIST of ordinals per
key, consumed in printed order**, which places repeated numbers correctly. Both
sides of the map are self-verifying and INDEPENDENT — the PDF's printed nipāta
headings and printed verse lines on one side, the corpus `book` field and its
paragraphs on the other. All 22 nipātas pair 1:1, 0 unconsumed, 0 unmapped. That
is a real two-input check, not the 19Khu02 "two checks, one input" trap.

**!!! CORRECTED 2026-07-26, ON THE USER'S REPORT — THE JĀTAKA IS TWO BHĀGAS.**
This nav was first built as ONE Jātakapāḷi row spanning both volumes, by analogy
with the Apadāna, and the user was told "the edition does not make this division".
**That was wrong, and checking the books would have shown it.** Each volume's own
front title page sets

    Chaṭṭhasaṅgītipiṭakaṁ                 Chaṭṭhasaṅgītipiṭakaṁ
    Suttantapiṭake Khuddakanikāye         Suttantapiṭake Khuddakanikāye
    JĀTAKAPĀḶI                            JĀTAKAPĀḶI
    (Paṭhamo bhāgo)   [Pāḷi Series 22]    (Dutiyo bhāgo)   [Pāḷi Series 23]

and each carries its OWN mātikā, every page headed "Jātakapāḷi paṭhamabhāga" /
"Jātakapāḷi dutiyabhāga". A work the edition treated as undivided would not print
two tables of contents under two names. The nav now has two nodes, labelled with
the edition's own Pāḷi — never "I"/"II", which the edition nowhere sets.
WHY THIS IS NOT THE APADĀNA CASE: the Apadāna is printed in two bhāgas too, but
ITS break falls in the MIDDLE of Therāpadāna, between vaggas 42 and 43 of a series
numbered 1-56 straight through, so grouping those two volumes keeps a vagga series
from being cut. The Jātaka's break falls exactly on a NIPĀTA boundary and cuts no
structural unit at all. Both choices are right for their own book.
THE DIVISION DOES NOT RENUMBER, and that is the assertion that matters: the second
bhāga opens at "17. Cattālīsanipāta" / "521. Tesakuṇajātaka", so nipātas run 1-22
and jātakas 1-547 straight through. `build_jataka_nav.py` refuses to write unless
the two trees join up, and `_jatakaverify.js` asserts the join independently.
A CONCRETE GAIN: each bhāga row now OPENS A READING PANE, because its whole tree
lies in one volume. The single-row form could only expand — that is the standing
`render()` limitation, which now applies to the Apadāna alone.
LESSON: when a structural question is about how the EDITION is organised, read the
edition's own front matter before reasoning from another book's shape. The title
page and the mātikā answered this in one look.

**MIXED DEPTH IS THE EDITION'S, AND THE CORPUS `vagga` FIELD LIES ABOUT IT.**
Vaggas exist ONLY in nipātas 1-7 (42 of them: 15/10/5/5/3/2/2). From the
Aṭṭhakanipāta on, jātakas sit directly under their nipāta and no vagga is printed.
22Khu05's corpus `vagga` field sticks on **"Gandhāravaggo dutiyo."** — a COLOPHON,
not a heading — and carries it forward for the rest of the volume; 23Khu06 has no
`vagga` field at all. Driving structure off that field would have invented 15
vaggas the edition does not print. The user chose the edition's own division and
mixed depth, as for the Apadāna; the generic `tree` branch renders any depth.

**ERRATA — the edition's own, all PRESERVED VERBATIM and never corrected.** Recorded
in `ERRATA` in `build_khu_volume.py` and asserted in `_jatakaverify.js` so a later
change cannot silently "fix" them:
 * 22Khu05 p304 prints **"24."** where the sequence requires 29 (and 24 already
   occurs in that nipāta — this is the collision above);
 * 23Khu06 p374 prints **"2324."** for 2342;
 * 23Khu06 p383 prints **"1440."** for 2440;
 * 22Khu05 p105 sets **"271. Udapānadūsakajākaka (3-3-1)"** — *jākaka* for
   *jātaka*. It is the ONLY heading in either volume outside the normal stems, so
   the stem list carries `jākaka` and the label keeps the misprint;
 * 22Khu05 p79 sets **"6. Na taṁ daḷhavagga"** with internal spaces, though its own
   colophon closes it up as "Nataṁdaḷhavaggo chaṭṭho.". A tighter heading regex
   drops it and Dukanipāta then shows 9 vaggas instead of 10.

**NINE CORPUS SPLICES REPAIRED — a defect class worth naming.** The corpus merges
two printed verses into ONE paragraph, leaving the second verse's own number
sitting inside the text ("…matoti. 109.Sobhati maccho Gaṅgeyyo…"). 7 in 22Khu05
(v109, 145, 57, 18, 188, 125, 228), 2 in 23Khu06 (v90, 140). Detected by CONTENT —
the verse's opening words must already be in that paragraph — deliberately NOT by
the stray number, because a footnote marker ("…Yāmuno4. Catuppadoyaṁ…") imitates a
number but cannot imitate the words. Two sub-cases, and the difference matters:
 * within one jātaka: the second verse becomes a second numbered `groups` entry
   with `nums`, as Suttanipāta's merged pairs already do;
 * **across a jātaka boundary** (v109 -> 205. Gaṅgeyyajātaka, v145 -> 223.
   Puṭabhattajātaka): the edition prints a colophon AND the next jātaka's heading
   between the two spliced verses, so folding the second into the first paragraph
   renders it ABOVE ITS OWN HEADING. Those two go out as their own `plain` uddāna
   block carrying the heading as `head`.

**!!! AND THAT FIX CREATED THE EXACT DEFECT THIS FILE KEEPS WARNING ABOUT.** Moving
those two headings out of `sections/` and into the uddāna stream made them render
correctly and **deleted jātakas 205 and 223 from the tree and from ☰ Contents** —
content present, in the right place on the page, missing from the structure. No gate
saw it. What caught it was the nav builder's refusal to write unless it reproduces
the edition's own 1-547: it reported 545 and named the two. `build_jataka_nav.py`
therefore reads heads from `sections/` **and** from `uddana/` plain-block `head`
fields. Prefer a structure the edition asserts over a total from tradition — again.

**FLOATING VERSE NUMBERS.** The edition sometimes sets the number alone on its line
and starts the pādas on the next, at a different indent (22Khu05 p214 v18, p356
v188, p400 v125, p410 v228; 23Khu06 p165 v140). Unfixed, the verse item carried no
text, failed to map, and its pādas were appended to the PREVIOUS verse — every word
still present, so no content gate could fire, while the verse silently lost its
number and its frame. `join_floating()` joins the two lines before classification.

**A HARNESS DEFECT FOUND HERE THAT AFFECTS ALL 118 VOLUMES.**
`verify_render_vs_pdf.pdf_lines()` reads PLAIN (non `-layout`) pdftotext, where a
body line that abuts the footnote rule arrives GLUED to it — 23Khu06 p301 sets the
peyyala "-pa" immediately before the rule. The test was `re.match(r'_{10,}', l)`,
anchored at the start of the line, so it missed the rule entirely and let that
page's ENTIRE apparatus into the BODY comparison, where its variant notes were
reported as missing body content. Now `re.search`, keeping whatever precedes the
rule. Backup `verify_render_vs_pdf.py.prefoot`. **Re-checked after the fix: 18Khu01,
19Khu02, 20Khu03, 21Khu04 all still 0/0/0/0 at minw 4 and 1** — but
`docs/verify_report.md` was built before it and its counts move corpus-wide.

**THE TWO REMAINING LOST VARIANTS ARE FLAGGED, NOT GUESSED** (as 20Khu03's was):
 * 22Khu05 real p423 note 9 "Samappito (Sī, I)": the marker IS printed but the
   edition sets it with a SPACE before the digit ("saramappito 9."). `MARK` requires
   the digit to abut its word, deliberately, so that verse numbers are not read as
   markers. Widening it would catch the inline verse numbers the corpus splices
   leave behind and mis-anchor notes, so it was left alone.
 * 23Khu06 real p59 note 13: the note is printed but the body carries NO marker 13
   at all (the only "13." on the page is verse 13's own number). Same class as
   20Khu03's p378 mismatch — anchoring it means choosing which side of the edition
   is wrong. NOTE both tools label pages 0-BASED, so their "p422"/"p58" are real
   pages 423/59.

**NIPĀTA NAMES ARE NOT UNIQUE ACROSS BOOKS.** Theragāthā (19Khu02) also prints an
Aṭṭhakanipāta, a Navakanipāta and a Mahānipāta, and the sidebar holds every book's
rows in the DOM at once. A nav lookup by bare label therefore opened Theragāthā's
Mahākaccāyanattheragāthā while claiming to test the Jātaka's Aṭṭhakanipāta. Any
jsdom check that finds a row by label MUST scope the search to its own book's
subtree; `_jatakaverify.js` does.

**!!! THE RECORDED BOOK BOUNDARIES WERE WRONG, AND SO WAS THE REASON THEY WERE TRUSTED.**
`docs/19Khu02_structure.json` recorded Theragāthā at ord 1849 and Therīgāthā at ord 3140,
"confirmed TWO independent ways". Both ways shared one dependency — the corpus `book` field.
On a new book's FIRST page the running header prints the NIPĀTA name ('Ekakanipāta'), not the
book title, so a carry-forward keeps those paragraphs in the previous book; and the colophon
check confirmed only the PREVIOUS book's end page, never the new book's first ordinal.
True starts: Theragāthā **1848**, Therīgāthā **3136**. Unfixed, Petavatthu rendered Theragāthā
verse 1, Theragāthā rendered Therīgāthā verses 1-4, and **Therīgāthā lost its own first four
verses**. Sensitivity shown, not asserted, and REPRODUCIBLE: `node _19bleed.js --bad` reinstates the two
wrong ordinals in memory and fails 3 of 4 books (do not rely on `nav.json.bak19` — each nav build
overwrites it).
LESSON: two checks that share an input are one check. The signal that actually works is the
VERSE NUMBER RESETTING TO 1, cross-checked against the edition's own verse totals — the
corrected spans give Petavatthu 814 ¶ / 814 verses, Theragāthā 1288/1288, Therīgāthā 524/524,
exact. `build_khuddaka_nav.py` now snaps every book start back to its n-reset (backup `.prebound`).

**79% COVER WAS NOT LOST EXTRACTION.** The handoff read "79% cover" as "a fifth of the volume is
not being compared". It is not: 19Khu02's PDF is 547 pages and its text ends at 451 — the other
96 pages are the word / name / verse indices and the Sodhanapattaṁ errata. 435/547 = 79.5%.
`cover` has a ceiling well below 100% in every volume; compare it against that volume's own text
extent before reading it as a re-extraction job. Note added to the report generator.

**TWO HARNESS BUGS FOUND, BOTH AFFECTING ALL 118 VOLUMES.**
 1. `verify_all_volumes.page_range()` used the corpus `pdf_page` directly as a pdftotext INDEX,
    so **every volume's first text page was excluded from the sweep** — the page carrying the
    book title, the homage, the opening headings and the first verses, i.e. exactly the material
    the incipit work is about. It also stopped the tail one page early whenever a page's own
    FOOTNOTE contained the word 'anukkamaṇika' (19Khu02's last text page, so its closing
    colophon was never compared). Both fixed; `docs/verify_report.md` re-run over all 118
    volumes: 110 ranges widened, missing lines 79,828 -> 80,502 (90 volumes now show MORE,
    because their opening page is compared at last), rev 2,348 -> 2,159, dup 41 -> 10.
    Clean 1/118 -> 2/118. Backup `verify_all_volumes.py.prerange`.
 2. The apparatus tools had the SAME index/page confusion, but worse: `rebuild_apparatus.py`
    anchored every note a page early, which the +/-3 window then hid by attaching the note to
    whatever earlier paragraph carried the same marker number (19Khu02 put page 19's notes 1
    and 2 onto ords 0 and 3). **The corpus `pdf_page` field does not use one convention across
    volumes** — measured: 19Khu02 / 06Di01 / 09Ma01 need offset -1, 18Khu01 and 12Sam01 need +1
    (12Sam01's known +2 drift). So `vr.page_offset(vol)` now MEASURES it per volume by testing
    which offset puts the most paragraphs' opening words on the page they claim; the winner is
    decisive (400/400 vs <100 for the runner-up). Both tools use it. 18Khu01 re-checked: still
    1 spliced / 7 variants / 0 xrefs, unchanged. Backups `.preoff`.
    **The corpus-wide apparatus sweep in `docs/apparatus_report.md` predates this fix and should
    be re-run** — its 226 spliced / 3,108 variants / 384 xrefs were measured with mis-paged
    anchors, so some of the "splices" are the same artifact that produced 19Khu02's two.

**BODY REBUILD — `pipeline/build_19khu02.py` (NEW, saved).** Whole volume from `pdftotext -layout`,
mapped onto corpus ordinals by verse number; the corpus is never touched. All four books map 1:1
(1031/814/1288/524 paragraphs). What it repaired, all of it corpus defects:
 * dropped printed pāda lines inside verses (v1094 lost "Sukuṇḍalī kappitakesamassu.",
   v1098 lost "Bahussute taṇhakkhayūpapanne." — the same short-line drop as Suttanipāta);
 * every vagga's closing colophon + Tassuddānaṁ SPLICED onto the tail of that vagga's last
   paragraph (ords 155/269/482/631/692) while `uddana/` rendered the same text again;
 * all of Petavatthu's, Theragāthā's and Therīgāthā's colophons and uddāna verses missing outright
   (534 printed lines);
 * Theragāthā's opening **Nidānagāthā** missing outright;
 * three printed section headings captured as corpus paragraphs (ord 388, 390, 857) — now in
   `hide/` and re-placed as headings;
 * no verse structure at all — every verse rendered as run-on prose.
Parser notes worth keeping: a verse start is recognised by its `N.` prefix, NOT by matching the
body indent (the body column shifts as numbers gain digits — that alone dropped ~250 verses); a
page with no verse number on it is a colophon page and is entirely centred material; a centred
colophon or uddāna label OPENS A TAIL, after which body-column lines belong to that tail and not
to the preceding verse (without this the uddāna verses were read as pādas); headings sometimes sit
IN the body column and must be caught by content (`HEADTXT`), which is also how the three leaked
corpus paragraphs were found; two headings can share one printed line (`split_centre`).
DELIBERATE NORMALISATION, recorded rather than silent: the closing formula "Itthaṁ sudaṁ …
abhāsitthāti." is set flush with the verse number on one page and flush with the pādas on the next
(p235 vs p236), so alignment cannot be the authority — it is classified by form and always rendered
as prose in `after`.

**FOUR-LEVEL TREE — the shape the user asked for, and it self-verifies.**
Reader gained a generic `tree` branch (any depth; a node with no `kids` is a clickable leaf at its
own depth; every node gets a VAGGASPAN so clicking a division, vagga or vimāna slices to it; the
BOOK ROW now opens the whole book, which with a four-level tree was otherwise unreachable).
`sections` entries may now carry `k:'gatha'`, display verse the corpus does not hold, needed
because the page interleaves Theragāthā's Nidānagāthā WITH the headings and only `sections`
preserves that order. Build `pipeline/build_19khu02_nav.py`; it REFUSES to write unless each book
reproduces the edition's own totals:
    Vimānavatthu  2 divisions -> 7 vaggas -> 85 vimānas (+36 sub) ; vagga numbering 1-7
                  CONTINUOUS across the two divisions, as the edition prints it
    Petavatthu    4 vaggas -> 51 petas   (the printed vagguddāna says "Vatthūni ekapaññāsaṁ")
    Theragāthā    21 nipātas -> 112 vaggas -> 264 theras
    Therīgāthā    16 nipātas -> 73 therīs
RECONCILED the handoff's open question ("84 vimānavatthu headings found, standard is 85"): the
count is 85. Pāricchattakavagga's fifth member, **Guttilavimāna, contains its own numbered series
of 36 minor vimānas**, and that series' numbers run 1..36 straight THROUGH the vagga's own
expected 6,7,8… — so it cannot be closed by comparing against the vagga counter, which is how it
was read as 36 vagga members and 121 vimānas. What closes it is the numbering DROPPING: the
series ends at 36 and the vagga resumes at 6.

### 19Khu02 follow-up — asked "is Vimānavatthu completely done?", and it was not (2026-07-25an)

**!!! EVERY MULTI-WITNESS VARIANT IN THE CORPUS WAS BEING SILENTLY DISCARDED.**
`parse_variants` split each note on any comma before a capital — which also split INSIDE the
sigla group, so `Padumaṁ (Sī, Syā)` became `Padumaṁ (Sī` + `Syā)` and neither half parsed. The
note text survived; its STRUCTURE did not. The tell was decisive and had been sitting in the data
all along: across all of 19Khu02, 629 notes parsed and **every single one had exactly one
siglum** — impossible for an edition whose commonest form is `(Sī, Syā)`. Since the structured
variant apparatus is the project's stated highest-value output, this was the most costly silent
failure found so far, and note that `verify_apparatus.py` CANNOT SEE IT: it checks that a note's
TEXT is stored and printed, never that the note was parsed. A gate reporting 0/0/0 said nothing
about this.
FIX: scan for sigla groups (`_is_sigla` distinguishes a witness list from an editorial
cross-reference `(Saṁ 1. 188)` and from a bracketed alternative reading) and take each variant's
reading as the text up to its own group. Also recovers notes glued by a failed two-column split
(`Bhāsite (Sī) 3. Khiḍḍaṁ ratiṁ (Syā, I)` → two variants). Backup `.prevar`.
19Khu02 after: **928 of 960 notes structured** (was 629), 1,101 variants, sigla-per-variant
1:765 2:290 3:45 4:1 (was 1:632, 2+:zero). Vimānavatthu alone 300 of 305; the 5 that stay
text-only are correctly so — `( ) Natthi Sī-potthake` and `Pāṭhabhedo natthi` state an ABSENCE
and have no reading to structure.
**EVERY OTHER VOLUME'S APPARATUS IS STILL PARSED THE OLD WAY.** Re-running the corpus-wide
apparatus sweep was already required by the page-offset fix; this makes it urgent. Expect
roughly a third of all stored notes to gain structure.

**Sub-series heading weight.** The tree knew Guttilavimāna's 36 minor vimānas were subordinate;
the reading pane did not — they were emitted at the same weight as the vagga's own members.
`build_19khu02_nav.py` now demotes them to the reader's existing `vatthu` class after building
the tree (the tree is where the sub-series is identified, so that is where the demotion belongs).

**STILL OPEN for 19Khu02 — do not call it finished without saying these:**
 1. `xrefs/19Khu02.json` (53 cross-reference lines, 8 of them in Vimānavatthu) is written but
    **the reader never fetches that file** — `appBlock` renders only the note-level `xrefs`
    field, which is empty for this volume. Same outstanding item as 18Khu01. Stored, invisible.
 2. **The corpus itself is still defective** — 19 Vimānavatthu paragraphs (and more in the other
    three books) still hold spliced or short text in `site/19Khu02.json`. The RENDER is correct
    because the side-map replaces the paragraph, but anything reading the corpus directly — a
    search index, an export, the Unicode-PDF plan — still sees the defect. Same standing caveat

 3. Cross-layer links resolve for all 1,034 Vimānavatthu ordinals, but were built before this

**BUILDER GENERALISED — `pipeline/build_khu_volume.py <VOL> [--write]` (NEW).** Same PDF-first
method as `build_19khu02.py`, driven by a per-volume `SPEC`. Its regression test is the point:
it reproduces 19Khu02's shipped verse/uddana/hide/incipit files EXACTLY, so a change made for a
later volume cannot quietly alter an earlier one. Run that check after any edit to it.

**`n` DOES NOT MEAN THE SAME THING IN EVERY BOOK.** In 19Khu02 the verse number runs continuously
over a whole book; in the Apadāna it RESETS AT EVERY VAGGA, so the same number occurs ~56 times
per book. `SPEC[vol]['n_scope']` selects the behaviour, and the PDF walk mirrors the corpus's
reset counter so the two stay in step. Do NOT reuse 19Khu02's "an n-reset is a book boundary"
rule here — in the Apadāna an n-reset is a VAGGA boundary.

**THREE MORE HARNESS / PARSER DEFECTS FOUND, ALL AFFECTING EVERY VOLUME.**
 1. **A recurring line of CONTENT was being deleted as a running header.** The Apadāna refrain
    "N. Paṭisambhidā catasso -pa- kataṁ Buddhassa sāsanaṁ." closes almost every apadāna, so it
    lands at a page top often; its rarer numberings cleared both the count and the 60% ratio and
    entered the derived header set, DELETING 7 printed occurrences — which then surfaced as the
    render producing that line more often than the edition prints it. Requiring page-top position
    (the earlier fix, for Udāna's "udānesi–" lines) was necessary but not sufficient.
    FIX: a running header in this edition is a TITLE — no terminal sentence punctuation. A
    sentence-ending line is content however reliably it falls at a page top. Backup `.prehdr`.
 2. **A marker can carry MORE THAN ONE printed note**, written "1-1." against the same marker.
    `page_notes` recognised only `^N.`, so every one was dropped — 11 lost variants in 20Khu03,
    2 in 18Khu01. Notes are now a LIST per marker. This was flagged in this file long ago and
    never done; it is done now.
 3. **The marker's period is sometimes not set at all** (18Khu01 p151 prints "3 Anupavādo …").
    Accepted when a capital or bracket follows, so a continuation line starting with a figure is
    not mistaken for a marker.
 18Khu01's apparatus improves 7 -> 4 lost variants on (2)+(3); its remaining 4 are the p111/p217
 book-boundary colophon variants this file already says need doing by hand, plus the ord512 splice.

**REMAINING 20Khu03 VARIANT — AN EDITION NUMBERING MISMATCH, RECORDED NOT GUESSED.** Real p378
prints footnote **5** ("Tasmā (Syā, Ka)") but sets the body marker as **6** ("Kasmā6"), and there
is no footnote 6. The note cannot be anchored by marker. Both readings are preserved; anchoring it
would mean choosing which side of the edition is wrong, so it is left flagged. NOTE the rebuild and
verify tools label pages by 0-BASED index, so their "p377" is real page 378.

**CORPUS DEFECTS REPAIRED (all via side-maps; `site/*.json` is never touched).**
 * 20Khu03: the homage; the printed openers "Atha therāpadānaṁ suṇātha–" and "Atha
   Paccekabuddhāpadānaṁ suṇātha–"; vagga uddānas missing outright or SPLICED onto the tail of the
   vagga's last paragraph (ord662/802/990); no verse structure at all.
 * 21Khu04: 62 printed lines missing; one leaked section heading captured as a corpus paragraph
   (ord3138, "10. Yasodharāpamukha-aṭṭhārasabhikkhunīsahassa-apadāna"). That one mattered out of
   all proportion: it carries the HEADING's number as its `n`, firing a spurious vagga reset that
   desynced the per-vagga counter against the PDF and left **293 verses unmapped**. The leaked-
   heading scan therefore now runs BEFORE the number map is built, not after.
 * Line-end hyphenation is rejoined on the hyphen and nothing else (20Khu03 p342 sets
   "…imā gāthāyo abhi-" / "āsitthāti."). Every wider rule also swallows ordinary line wraps and

 * The edition's own misprints are preserved verbatim but must still be RECOGNISED, or the closing
   formula is read as a pāda and swallowed into the verse: 20Khu03 prints "Ittaṁ sudaṁ" at ord2676.

**APADĀNA NAV — THE EDITION'S OWN DIVISION, ACROSS TWO VOLUMES (the user's choice).**
`pipeline/build_apadana_nav.py` (NEW). The physical split cuts Therāpadāna at vagga 42/43; the

559 / 40 / 35 are the edition's own counts and the builder REFUSES to write unless it reproduces

### 20Khu03 / 21Khu04 — FOUR USER-REPORTED DEFECTS, ALL FIXED (2026-07-25ap)

Reported from screenshots after the run above called both volumes done. Every one
of them passed all three gates. Read that twice before trusting a gate result.

 1. **Four apadānas absent from the tree AND from ☰ Contents** — 3-1 Sāriputta,
    3-2 Mahāmoggallāna, 3-9 Khadiravaniyarevata, 3-10 Ānanda. CAUSE: the edition
    numbers Buddhavagga's third group INCONSISTENTLY — four as "3-1." … "3-10."
    and the other six as "3. 3." … "3. 8.". The heading test matched only `^N.`,
    so the four hyphenated ones fell through to the colophon stream and rendered
    as centred uddāna lines. New `HEADNUM = ^\d+(?:-\d+)?\.\s`. Labels are left
    exactly as the edition sets them, inconsistency and all.
    !!! WHY NO GATE CAUGHT IT: the body harness asks whether the TEXT is present,
    not whether it is in the right ROLE. The lines were present — as colophons.
    This is the same blind spot recorded for the homage, and it will keep
    recurring until presentation rules are asserted per volume.
    !!! AND IT INVALIDATED A "VERIFIED" COUNT: with those four missing, Therāpadāna
    totalled 559, which matches the figure tradition gives — so a check against
    559 PASSED on defective data. The real count is **563**. The check now used is
    the edition's own structure: TEN apadānas to a vagga, with two exceptions the
    edition itself states — Buddhavagga 12, and Yasavagga 11, whose last is
    labelled "Raṭṭhapālattherassāpadānaṁ EKĀDASAMAṀ". That check would have failed
    immediately (Buddhavagga showing 8). Prefer a structure the edition asserts
    over a total from tradition.
 2. **The book's own name rendered small, italic and left-aligned.** It is set at
    its own indent on the title page (20Khu03 p21: indent 11 against a body column
    of 3), so it was classified as neither centred nor body and was swept into the
    opening gāthā block. Now emitted as `k:'booktitle'` and drawn by a new
    `titleHTML()` ABOVE the incipit, in `.head.booktitle` (27px, centred) — larger
    than `.head.sutta`. Printed order title -> homage -> first heading is asserted.
 3. **A book ran on into the next one.** Therāpadāna's 56th vagga swallowed
    Therīapadāna, Buddhavaṁsa and Cariyāpiṭaka: the reader gives a final node no
    upper bound and runs it to the END OF ITS VOLUME. `build_apadana_nav.py` now
    puts an explicit `end` on the last vagga (and last leaf) of each slice, taken
    from the printed book-end colophon. BOOKSPAN never covered these because
    Apadāna's node is registered against 20Khu03, so nothing else bounded them.
 4. **An opener rendered above its own heading** — "Atha therāpadānaṁ suṇātha–"
    printed after "3-1. Sāriputtatthera-apadāna" was landing in the PREVIOUS
    paragraph's uddāna block. A line arriving while a heading is pending now
    belongs to that heading's own verse (`before`), in both the centred and the
    body-column paths.

Assertions for all four: `node _apadanafix.js` -> 16/16. Gates re-run after:

### BOOK TITLES — every book now announces itself (2026-07-25aq)

User-reported, second round: after the title was fixed for the Apadāna volumes it
was still missing for ALL NINE books of 18Khu01 and 19Khu02 — Khuddakapāṭha,
Dhammapada, Udāna, Itivuttaka, Suttanipāta, Vimānavatthu, Petavatthu, Theragāthā,

BUILDER, and 19Khu02's sections had not been rebuilt since, while 18Khu01 is not
built by that pipeline at all (its side-maps are bespoke — build_suttanipata.py
plus hand repairs, do not regenerate them).

`pipeline/add_booktitles.py <VOL> [--write]` (NEW) fixes it for any volume without
touching anything else. It takes each book head from `incipit/<VOL>.json` — which
already marks exactly one ordinal per book — reads the name off that book's
printed title page, and inserts it as the FIRST `sections` entry with
`k:'booktitle'`. Idempotent. It flagged Suttanipāta rather than guessing until the
homage pattern was widened: **Suttanipāta prints "Bhagavatā" where the other books
print "Bhagavato"**, which this file has recorded since the incipit work — the
same variant bit twice.

Result: 18Khu01 x5, 19Khu02 x4, 20Khu03 x1, 21Khu04 x4 — every book that prints a
homage now carries a title at the same ordinal, first in the list, drawn above the
homage in `.head.booktitle`.

**A BOOK ROW NOW OPENS ITS BOOK.** Found while testing the above: in the `nipata`
and `nipatas` branches a book row only EXPANDED, so clicking "Khuddakapāṭhapāḷi"
gave no book and therefore never showed its title page. Only the newer `tree`
branch opened one. All three now behave alike (and set SUTTALABEL so the pane is
titled with the book name).

### BOOK TITLES ACROSS THE WHOLE CANON (2026-07-25as)

User asked what about the other nikāyas and the Vinaya. Answer was: nothing —
only the four Khuddaka volumes had titles. Now **79 book titles across all 40
canon volumes**, read off each book's printed title page.

**THE MECHANISM MOVED, AND THIS IS THE IMPORTANT PART.** Titles were briefly kept
in `sections/`. That is wrong for the canon at large, and this file already says
why in the incipit entry: **a volume that GAINS a `sections/` file switches
`canonHead` to the `secmap` path and silently drops every inline heading it draws
from its `headings` array.** Only 4 of 40 canon volumes have a sections file, so
putting titles there would have broken 36 volumes' headings in order to add a
title. Titles now live in `booktitle/<VOL>.json` = `{ord: "Name"}`, loaded as
`cv.btl`, exactly parallel to `incipit/`. `verify_render_vs_pdf.render_parts` was
taught the new map in the same change — the reader renders it, so the harness has
to model it, or every title becomes a missing printed line.

`pipeline/build_booktitles.py <VOL|--canon> [--write]` (NEW).
 * ANCHORS from `nav.json` (every canon book node carries `first`) plus
   `incipit/<VOL>.json`. Work-level nodes of a cross-volume tree are included;
   NUMBERED tree nodes are not — they are divisions, nipātas and vaggas inside a
   book, and anchoring there put a spurious "Therīgāthāpāḷi" on Therīgāthā's
   second nipāta.
 * The name is READ OFF THE PAGE, never taken from the nav label.
 * ONE TITLE PAGE, ONE BOOK HEAD: several ordinals can resolve to the same title
   page, and the book begins at the earliest; without that 39Abhi11 and 40Abhi12
   each got a book titled twice.
 * Two more places the edition is not uniform, both found here and neither
   assumed: **38Abhi10 prints "Namo Tassa" with a capital T**, and Suttanipāta
   prints "Bhagavatā" for "Bhagavato" (recorded since the incipit work — that
   variant has now bitten three times; the regex allows both).

**9 FLAGGED, NOT GUESSED** — all in 40Abhi12, where the Paṭṭhāna restarts a book
MID-PAGE with no title page at all ("…niṭṭhitaṁ. <Next>paṭṭhānapāḷi" inline).
Those need that volume's book structure, which this file already lists as
outstanding ("clean the Abhidhamma Paṭṭhāna book structure (rough)"). Until then
they stay flagged, and `_booktitleverify.js` excludes 40Abhi12 from the
homage-implies-title rule by name so the exclusion is visible rather than silent.

**A BOOK ROW NOW OPENS ITS BOOK IN EVERY NAV SHAPE.** It only expanded in the
`pdftoc` and default-nested branches, so clicking "Pārājikapāḷi" or
"Mūlapaṇṇāsapāḷi" gave no book and therefore never showed a title. Fixed in all
four branches (`tree`, `nipatas`, `nipata`, `pdftoc`/nested), each also setting
SUTTALABEL so the pane is titled with the book name.

volume has at least one title; every printed homage has a title at the same
ordinal; no title blank or sentence-punctuated). `node _btrender.js` -> 12/12,

        Dīghanikāya                <- was filtered out as noise

        _____
        Namo tassa Bhagavato Arahato Sammāsambuddhassa.

— for all seven collections, not only the four nikāyas asked about; and 38Abhi10
sets THREE lines (Abhidhammapiṭaka / Dhammānuloma / Dukapaṭṭhānapāḷi).

`booktitle/<VOL>.json` values are now the whole printed stack in order,
`{ord: [lines]}` (a bare string is still accepted). The reader draws the last
line as the book — `.head.booktitle`, 27px — and the ones above it as

being flattened to one line. `render_parts` emits every line, so the harness sees
them all.

purpose was to SKIP those lines — I had treated a printed line as noise because it
was not the bit I was looking for. The edition prints it; it belongs on the page.

## STANDING RULE — book boundaries (applies to every Khuddaka book, and any nikāya where several books share one physical volume)
Each book MUST stop rendering at its own end and NOT continue into the next book. Khuddakapāṭha stops at "Khuddakapāṭhapāḷi niṭṭhitā." (does not run into Dhammapada); Dhammapada stops at "Dhammapadapāḷi samattā." (does not run into Udāna); and so on for Udāna, Itivuttaka, Suttanipāta, etc. This is enforced by `BOOKSPAN` (built during nav load) + the `render()` slice `cv.paras.slice(start,end)` — every new book that shares a physical volume must have its own nav node with a correct `first` ordinal so its span is computed. When finishing a book, always verify (jsdom) that the NEXT book's opening text is absent from the render.

 * `xrefs-lost` — a printed `*`/`+` CROSS-REFERENCE line ("* Khu 2. 129 piṭṭhe Petavatthumhipi.") not stored. Counted separately from variants: different loss, different fix. NOTE the apparatus schema has an `xrefs` field but only 85 of 18Khu01's 1,138 notes populate it.

HOMAGE SWEEP DONE (2026-07-25af). New side-map `site/reader/incipit/<VOL>.json` = `{ord: "<printed homage>"}`, built by `pipeline/build_incipit.py` (NEW, saved). The reader loads it as `cv.inc`, renders `<div class="incipit pali">` ABOVE that paragraph's headings (where the page sets it), and `block()` strips the same line off the head of the paragraph body — so a copy the extraction swallowed shows once, in the right role, with the wording the page uses. 18Khu01's five entries were MIGRATED off `sections/` to this map so there is exactly ONE mechanism; the hardcoded lowercase homage survives only as a fallback for volumes with no data.
WHY NOT A `sections/` ENTRY: a volume that gains a `sections/` file switches `canonHead` to the `secmap` path, so a one-line sections file would silently drop every inline heading that volume draws from its `headings` array. Do not do that.
CRITICAL DISCRIMINATOR — the homage is ALSO ordinary body text. It occurs inside narrative when a character utters it ("…tikkhattuṁ udānaṁ udānesi– 'Namo tassa…'", e.g. 09Ma01#287, 10Ma02#387, 12Sam01#186, 15An01#360). My first build anchored those as incipits, which would have been WRONG. The rule now: skip when the preceding 60 chars contain `udān` or an opening quote; require `pāḷi|niṭṭhit|samatt` in that context (the previous book's colophon + the new book's title) unless the homage starts the paragraph; take the WORDING from a standalone printed display line near that page. Applied in both the builder and `check_layout.js`.

VAGGA UDDĀNA RENDERED TWICE — USER-REPORTED, FIXED (2026-07-25ae). Every Suttanipāta vagga opened with the PREVIOUS vagga's closing "Tassuddānaṁ" mnemonic (Mahāvagga opened with Cūḷavagga's, Aṭṭhakavagga with Mahāvagga's, and so on) — visible above verses 224 / 407 / 773 / 982. CAUSE, in `build_suttanipata.py`'s `before` computation: it collected prose from the previous paragraph's tail once it had seen a colophon OR a heading. The stream at a vagga boundary is `verse -> sutta colophon -> vagga colophon -> "Tassuddānaṁ" -> uddāna verse lines -> vagga head -> sutta head -> verse`, so the uddāna prose was picked up by the colophon condition and attached to the NEXT paragraph's `before` — while the `after`/blocks loop had already, correctly, put the same lines in the PREVIOUS paragraph's uddāna block. Rendered twice.
FIX: only a HEADING opens a sutta's intro prose; a colophon closes the previous one (`seen_head` set by 'head', cleared by 'colo'). Prose between a colophon and the next heading is vagga-closing material and belongs solely to the previous paragraph's uddāna block.
!!! THE DUP CHECK HAD A HOLE THAT HID THIS. It excluded kind 'udd' from the occurrence count, so text appearing once as a side-map uddāna block and once as body prose counted as ONE render and never fired. Now only 'head'/'tail' are excluded. With the hole closed the harness reports 19 duplicated lines on the pre-fix data and 0 after — i.e. it would have caught this had the count been right. GENERAL LESSON: an exclusion in a checker is a blind spot; every kind excluded from a count needs a stated reason.

VERSE NUMBER PLACEMENT — USER-REPORTED, FIXED (2026-07-25ad). The paragraph number sat inline beside the verse's first pāda on some verses and on a line of its own above the block on others. It was not random: `block()` only moved the number into the first `.gatha` when the paragraph had intro prose (`hasBefore`) or held several numbered verses (`multi`). So a verse's number moved depending on whether its sutta happened to open with a narrative — and removing the homage from ord705's `before` (see the incipit fix above) would have silently regressed Uragasutta v1 from inline to stacked.
FIX: `else if(!multi && gi===0) gn=num;` (drop the `hasBefore` condition) and suppress the outer number whenever `vmap.groups.length` — i.e. any paragraph rendered as verse hangs its number beside the first pāda, via the existing `.gatha .pn{margin-left:-1.6em}` hanging indent. Pure-prose entries (`groups: []`) keep the number outside, unchanged.

!!! WHY THE HARNESS MISSED IT — READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING A 0/0/0/0. The harness is a CONTENT diff. It asks: is every printed line somewhere in the render (forward), is every rendered block contiguous in the print (reverse), is anything rendered more often than printed (dup). The homage passed ALL THREE — it was present, contiguous and unique. What was wrong was its ROLE and PLACEMENT: body text instead of a display incipit. **A 0/0/0/0 means no text is missing, duplicated or spliced. It does NOT mean the page LOOKS like the printed page.** Presentation is only verifiable in the jsdom layer — `_khu01verify.js` now asserts each book renders exactly one `.incipit`, that Suttanipāta's uses the "Bhagavatā" variant, and that no `.para.canon` contains the homage. Keep adding presentation assertions there; the same blind spot covers headings rendered as body text, wrong heading levels, verse rendered as prose, and ordering within a paragraph.

The earlier claim that "Udāna is missing 2,180 printed lines of prose narrative" was WRONG — my own harness bug, not a corpus defect. `block()` falls back to rendering the corpus text up to the "…udānaṁ udānesi–" marker when a verse entry has no `before`; my rewritten `render_parts` did not mirror that fallback, so every Udāna narrative looked dropped. Udāna's real residual was 6 lines. Lesson: when the harness reports a WHOLE CLASS of content missing, suspect the harness's model of `block()` before believing the corpus lost it.
FOUR MORE render_parts / PDF-filter bugs fixed the same way (all were inflating counts volume-wide):
 * the `udānesi–` fallback above;

 * the derived running-header set was applied GLOBALLY, so it deleted recurring CONTENT — Udāna's 80 "udānesi–" lines among them. Now a form counts as a header only if it appears at a page top on >=3 pages AND >=60% of its total occurrences are at a page top, and it is only stripped when it actually sits in the top 4 lines of that page.
 * a page-top heading with no terminal punctuation glued to the first content line and fabricated chunks that exist nowhere (e.g. "6. Ratanasutta" + a refrain line). A '.' sentinel is now appended to the first body line of each page; `norm()` drops it, so nothing else changes.

HARNESS REWRITTEN — `pipeline/verify_render_vs_pdf.py` is now a two-way tool and is the thing to trust.
 (a) It MIRRORS `block()` in reader2.html (sections heading -> verse.before -> verse.groups OR corpus text -> verse.after -> tail -> uddana block; honours `hide/`; accepts before/after as a string or a list — the old harness iterated a string as CHARACTERS, which silently inflated one volume to 73,693 render parts).
 (b) FORWARD: every PDF line and every >=minw-word sentence chunk must be in the render. Line-level is new and is what found the 27 drops; the old chunk-only mode missed anything shorter than the threshold.
 (c) REVERSE (new): every rendered prose block / verse must appear CONTIGUOUSLY in the PDF — catches splices and fabrication.
 (d) DUPLICATE (new): render occurrences counted against print occurrences — catches a block rendered twice, which NEITHER direction above can see. This caught a real bug in my own first rebuild (a sutta's intro prose landing both in the previous paragraph's colophon block and in its own `before`).
 (e) Running page-headers are now DERIVED from the pages (any line-form recurring at page-top on >=3 pages) instead of guessed by regex. This was the single biggest false-positive source: an unfiltered header is reported as missing content AND splits the paragraph it interrupts. 06Di01 went 290/82/95/1 -> 10/8/3/0 on this fix alone.
 (f) Normalisation fixes: peyyala `-pa-` where the PDF text layer drops the closing hyphen ("-paathāparaṁ", "-pathinamiddhaṁ", "-paBuddho"); intra-word hyphens JOINED not split (corpus "sa- uttaraṁ" vs print "sauttaraṁ", "ekacca-asassatikā" vs "ekaccaasassatikā", "vayo-anuppatto"); `+` and decorative `_____` rules treated as punctuation/skip.
 (g) Phrase lookup is now a word-position index (`WordIndex`), not substring scanning — a full volume went from minutes to well under a second.
 (h) Volumes with no `sections/` file fall back to the corpus `headings` labels (that IS what buildOutline/HEADMAP renders), so pdftoc volumes are no longer flagged for every heading.

- **"Two titles" fix / `sutta`-field normalization (`pipeline/normalize_sutta_field.py`).** Root cause: the extractor captured page running-headers into the per-paragraph `sutta` field, so most suttas carried >1 form — the bare opening-heading title on ¶1 and, on later paragraphs, the running-header form with the MN number ('Kandarakasutta' → 'Kandarakasutta (51)'), plus a handful with a page-variant *spelling* ('Kukkuravatika' → 'Kukkaravatika'). Anything that starts a heading when the field changes therefore printed the title twice. Fix: within each verified sutta span, every non-'X' paragraph's `sutta` label is set to the one canonical (opening-heading, artifact-cleaned) title. **Derived label only — base `text`, `n`, and all other fields untouched** (verified: 09Ma01 text-changed=0, non-sutta-field-changed=0). Relabelled 292/394/369 = **1,055 paragraphs**; afterwards every sutta has exactly one form and emits one heading (50/50/52). Per-volume backups at `site/<VOL>.json.bak`. **Roll this into the other nikāyas' extraction too** — the same running-header artifact is corpus-wide, so Saṁyutta/Aṅguttara/etc. will show it until normalized.

- **Saṁyutta (added):** SN is too big to list suttas in the tree, so (agreed with the user) the tree stops at **saṁyutta** level and the **suttas live in the ☰ Contents** — which is exactly the reader's `pdftoc` behaviour, so no reader change was needed. Builder: `pipeline/build_samyutta_nav.py`. Field mapping differs: `book` = saṁyutta, `vagga` = chapter-vagga but the major-division title ("…vaggasaṁyuttapāḷi") also appears there (used, carry-forward, to segment the 5 major vaggas). Two SN-specific wrinkles handled: (a) **boundary bleed** — the first saṁyutta of the next major vagga also appears at the tail of the previous one because the running-header title lags the content; fixed by a cross-boundary dedup that also hands the earlier start-ord to the next major so sutta spans are right (this had made Sakka show 26/Paṭiccasamuppāda-bled and inflated the last saṁyutta of each non-final major); (b) **sutta dedup must be strict** (exact folded-key only) — the loose proximity+edit-distance rule used for the distinctive saṁyutta names falsely merged real short suttas (Cālā/Upacālā). Result: 5 major vaggas, **56 saṁyuttas** (11/10/13/10/12), 1,691 suttas, all 1,747 nav keys in-range. Verified: 56-saṁyutta set/order/names = canonical SN; A/Ṭīkā links resolve (517/722/599 canon paras, 0 out-of-range → Sāratthappakāsinī + Ṭīkā); paragraph numbers (`n`) exact (they are the literal "247."/"1071." printed at each paragraph). The peyyāla-only saṁyuttas (e.g. Mahāvagga Jhānasaṁyutta) legitimately show 2 compressed range-entries — that is the edition's own compression.
