This affects only the **facsimile "view page" link** for 12Sam01 (Sagāthā/Nidāna) — NOT the paragraph numbers, nav, Contents, or links. 13Sam02/14Sam03 are offset-0. Fix later: recompute 12Sam01's front-matter page offset and re-anchor `pdf_page`; check the other multi-mātikā volumes for the same.

- **Aṅguttara (added):** AN is nipāta (11) → vagga → sutta with thousands of (often unnamed) suttas. Unlike SN, AN's **vaggas do NOT extract reliably**: the Ekakanipāta has an irregular sub-book structure (Aṭṭhānapāḷi, Ekadhammapāḷi, Etadagga's 7 sub-vaggas) that inflates its vagga count (~34 vs 21), and lower nipātas drift ±1–2 from running-header corruption. Only the **11 nipātas are guaranteed correct**. So (decided with the user) the **tree stops at nipāta** — each nipāta is a clickable leaf — and the vaggas + suttas live in the ☰ **Contents** as best-effort structure, keeping the left pane exactly right. Builder: `pipeline/build_anguttara_nav.py`; needed a **new reader mechanism** (`VAGCONTENTS` + a nipāta tree-leaf branch + a Contents branch in `reader2.html`) since this is neither the pdftoc nor the Majjhima-nested shape. Nipāta detection matches the short stem (so `Dukaka·nipātapāḷi` ↔ Duka; without this the Duka front half was absorbed into Ekaka); nipāta anchors snapped to the n=1 paragraph. Result: 11 nipātas (correct names/order/spans, all anchor at n=1), 192 vaggas + 1,307 named suttas in Contents, all 1,489 nav keys in-range. Verified: paragraph numbers exact (n == the number printed in every one of the 1,489 anchor paragraphs, 0 mismatches); Manorathapūraṇī + Ṭīkā links resolve for 100% of AN canon paras (952/497/426), 0 out-of-range. **Update — vaggas now IN the tree.** At the user's request the tree was changed to nipāta → vagga (expandable), suttas still in ☰ Contents. The Ekaka sub-book problem was solved properly: the paragraph `vagga` field actually carries the sub-vagga inline ("Etadaggavagga    1. Paṭhamavagga"), so `parse_vagga` now splits base+sub and renders sub-books as "14.1 Etadaggavagga (Paṭhamavagga) … 14.7 (Sattamavagga)", "15.x Aṭṭhānapāḷi", "16.x Ekadhammapāḷi" — collapsing Ekaka to the correct 21 main vaggas. Reader: nipāta branch is now expandable with vagga leaves; the reading-pane title shows the nipāta name (was wrongly showing the "Paṭhamapaṇṇāsaka" sub-marker); `buildOutline` now drops back-matter (name/word index `anukkamaṇikā`, `Gāthāsūci`, `Nānāpāṭhā`, alphabet markers, page-refs) — it stops the outline at the first index marker, so the volume's index no longer leaks into the reading pane as headings. The pdftoc books (Dī/Saṁ) already avoided this via HEADMAP; the nipāta-style books (Ma/An/Khu) still used the raw path. Fix: `pipeline/build_sections.py` runs `anchor_headings.py` (precise: pairs each heading with the paragraph that follows it in PDF reading order, matched by opening text — reliable despite gibberish heading fonts; clean title from the corpus `headings`) → `site/reader/sections/<VOL>.json` = `{ord:[{l,k}]}`. **Shipped fix = improved `buildOutline` (fast, no new data), applied to all non-pdftoc volumes:** the junk filter now drops closing markers (`/[ṁṃ]\d*\.\s*$/`, `niṭṭhit`) and it dedups the consecutive start/close echo (nkey strips trailing `ṁ.`/`.`), and the anchor loop **spreads** headings that share one printed page instead of stacking them (`ord = max(pageAnchor, lastOrd+1)`). Verified on 18Khu01: Khuddakapāṭha renders Saraṇattaya … Mettasutta clean (no `…ṁ.`, no `_____`, no dups, no pile-up); Dhammapada vatthu titles spread out. **Remaining imperfection:** within-page ORDER can still be slightly off (e.g. Maṅgala before Kumārapañhā) because exact per-heading anchoring needs the PDF re-parse. That precise path IS built — `pipeline/build_sections.py` (→ `site/reader/sections/<vol>.json`, precise) — but anchor_headings is pdfminer-slow (~30–90s/vol) and I couldn't run all 40 in-session (only 01–03Vin done). It's wired in `loadVol` (`cv.sec`) but the `canonHead`/`secmap` render path had a bug and is currently reverted/dead; to switch to precise later, finish the `sections/` build (`build_sections.py <vol>`, per-volume, in background) and re-enable `canonHead`. Marker `SECTIONS-2026-07-24k`.

## ROOT CAUSE for Khuddakapāṭha (deeper than anchoring — the CORPUS TEXT is defective)
Following the TOC links to the actual paragraphs + reading the page images shows the corpus paragraphs themselves are wrong for Khuddakapāṭha (18Khu01), which is why no heading/anchor fix worked:
- **Saraṇattaya (section 1) is MISSING** — 18Khu01 starts at ord0 = "1. Pāṇātipātā…" (Dasasikkhāpada precept 1). The refuge formula "Buddhaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāmi…" (visible on PDF page 26) was never extracted.
- **Dvattiṁsākāra (section 3) is MERGED** into ord9 — its text "Atthi imasmiṁ kāye– Kesā lomā nakhā dantā taco…" is appended to precept 10 (Jātarūpa), not its own paragraph.
Repair (do carefully, verify): (1) insert a Saraṇattaya paragraph (text readable from the page image — I CAN render+read PDF pages via `pdftoppm`→PNG→Read, ornamental font and all); (2) split ord9 into Jātarūpa-precept + Dvattiṁsākāra; (3) re-key ALL 18Khu01-keyed derived data for the shifted ordinals (nav.json Khuddaka nodes, `linksk/18Khu01.*`, `apparatus/18Khu01.appk.json`, `bold/18Khu01.*`, `uddana/18Khu01.json`); (4) re-anchor headings from the TOC links. **This likely affects other Khuddaka books too — audit each for dropped/merged unnumbered sections (Saraṇattaya-type prose, Dvattiṁsākāra-type lists) before trusting the split.** The TOC-link + page-image method (below) is how to find and verify each.

## KEY LEAD (use this — the anchoring breakthrough)
**The PDF's front Mātikā/TOC pages carry clickable LINK ANNOTATIONS with precise destinations** (target page + y-coords), even though the title text is an unextractable ornamental font. For 18Khu01 the TOC links live on PDF pages 14–25 (~300 links; the "Text" part starts PDF page 25 per the bookmark). Verified with pypdf: each `/Link` annot's `/Dest` (or `/A /D`) resolves to `[pageRef, /FitR|/XYZ, …y…]`. Plan that fixes section titles+anchoring cleanly (replaces the slow pdfminer `build_sections.py`):
1. `pypdf`: read link annots on the TOC pages in reading order (sort by -rect_y within each page) → ordered list of exact destinations (target PDF page + top-y).
2. Take the clean titles from the corpus `headings` array in order.
3. **Pair 1:1** (nth link ↔ nth title) — TOC is authoritative for count+order, so this fixes missing/extra/mis-ordered sections at once.
4. Anchor each to the corpus paragraph at (target page, y): map target page → corpus `pdf_page` (watch for a fixed offset, like 12Sam01 had), and for multiple sections per page use the y order vs the page's paragraphs. Only the target pages need a light per-page parse (bounded, fast) if y-precision is needed.
5. Emit `site/reader/sections/<vol>.json` = `{ord:[{l,k}]}` and re-enable the reader's `canonHead`/`secmap` path (currently reverted; `loadVol` already loads `cv.sec`).
Caveat to check first: are the corpus titles and the TOC links in the SAME order and count? Spot-check Khuddakapāṭha (should pair 9 titles ↔ its first 9 TOC links). The background `build_sections.py` (pdfminer) was started but is slow/coarse — prefer this TOC-link method instead.

## Reader mechanics (don't relearn the hard way)
- Production reader: `site/reader/reader2.html`. Loads `nav.json`, `pageindex.json`, `manifest.json`, per-volume `site/<VOL>.json`, `linksk/`, `bold/`, `apparatus/`.
- `nav.json` canon books carry `pdftoc:true`; the tree renders them expandable → numbered suttas; sutta sub-sections render inline in the reader via `HEADMAP` and appear in the ☰ Contents. Reader-pane title uses the clicked sutta name (`SUTTALABEL`).
- Keys are `<VOL>#<ordinal>` (ordinal = index in that volume's `paragraphs`). Link files use the bare ordinal.
- Preview locally over http (it fetches JSON): `cd ~/Documents/OSBCT/site && python3 -m http.server 8000` → open `http://localhost:8000/reader/reader2.html`. Hard-refresh (Cmd-Shift-R) — `nav.json` caches.
- Text is the authentic Sixth-Council (Burmese) edition — **never import external text**; only names/structure come from the authoritative checklist (labels only).

## Verify-before-claiming-done
Every rebuild step was validated against the actual paragraph text, not assumed. Keep doing that: spot-check names/placement against the PDF, confirm keys resolve, and don't report a nikāya "done" until checked.
